News.title: Aston Villa 2.0 are making mockery of the early-season doom merchants
News.content:
In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

He said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

Just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”

News.title: Carrick apology to United fans ominously similar to Solskjaer’s final match
News.content:
There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

News.title: Ebola case confirmed in Nigeria as outbreak spreads through Africa
News.content:
African ministers have been called to an urgent health summit after Nigeria confirmed its first case in the outbreak of the deadly Ebola fever tearing through eastern Congo.

Confirmation of a case in Africa’s most populous nation came days after a cluster was detected in Kenya and has heightened questions about border screening checks designed to stop the virus spreading from its epicentre in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

With cases now found in West Africa, Central Africa and East Africa, the epidemic “has already become the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history,” said Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the continent’s main public health body.

DRC has recorded close to 10,000 cases since an outbreak began in mid-May, with around half of them dying of the haemorrhagic fever.

The Nigeria case meant “Ebola is now affecting three regions of Africa,” warned Dr Kaseya, director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

“The situation demands urgent action and political leadership at the highest level,” he said, convening an online summit for next week.

News.title: One billion children at risk from heatwaves, WHO warns
News.content:
More than one billion children are exposed to increasingly severe heat waves, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned.

1.5 billion children under one experienced a fivefold increase in the number of heat wave days in 2024 compared with the 1986 to 2005 baseline period, jumping from roughly four days per year to a high of over 20, says the health agency. And these periods of high temperature are becoming longer, more frequent and more severe, the WHO warns.

According to the Met Office, this summer was the hottest on record in the UK, with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days where the temperature was above 30 degrees celsius. Europe also saw record-breaking temperatures, and Asia and Africa both experienced their warmest July on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

Four UN agencies, including the WHO, the WMO, Unicef and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), have urged countries to monitor how extreme heat affects pregnant women, newborns and children.

The new framework tracks preterm birth, stillbirths, low birthweight, pregnancy hypertension, child deaths and health facility visits.

“Heat is already affecting our most vulnerable populations, including pregnant women, newborns and children. But what health systems do not count, they cannot respond to,” said Dr Pascale Allotey, director of WHO’s department of maternal and child health.

“By tracking outcomes such as preterm birth, child deaths and illnesses, and health-facility visits alongside heat exposure, countries can identify potential impacts and take action to protect women and children,” she said.

High temperatures are particularly dangerous for pregnant women because the body has to work much harder to cool both the mother and the baby.

Intense heat can cause surface-level blood vessels to dilate, which in pregnant women can restrict blood flow to the placenta and reduce the amount of oxygen and nutrients that reach the foetus. Heat can also put strain on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, dangerously high blood pressure, and pre-eclampsia.

The odds of a preterm birth also increase by 26 per cent during heatwaves: for every one degree rise in heat exposure, the likelihood of giving birth early rise by roughly 4 per cent, according to a systematic review published in Nature Medicine.

The WHO has also urged countries to develop and implement tailored heat-health action plans that account for the needs of pregnant women, newborns and children, as well as strengthening early-warning systems to ensure timely action to heat risks, such as alert systems and personalised public messaging.

“As our world continues to heat up, it creates new risks for health, and older people, pregnant women, newborns and children are among those least able to escape them,” said Bruce Gordon, director of environment and climate change at the WHO.

“Our health systems need the data to recognise this reality and take action – from protecting people during heatwaves to embedding climate risk consideration into everyday health services,” he said.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Second investigation confirmed as Pep Guardiola questioned on legacy
Sports.content:
As the saga around Manchester City's 115 charges continues to rumble on, Mirror Football will be here with all of the latest updates and news

Welcome to Mirror Sport's live blog about Manchester City's 114 guilty charges.

The football world is still reeling from last month's announcement which confirmed the Cityzens had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18.

It was deemed that the club artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through the use of supposed 'sham' sponsorship deals. City continue to insist they are innocent and launched an appeal against the verdict on October 1.

They also maintain there is a "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" that exonerates them, but this is yet to be communicated to the public. In and amongst the saga, the legitimacy of their achievements over the last 20 years have been brought into question.

Sports.content:

Sports.title: Michael Carrick given Man Utd sack verdict as Red Devils confirm decision
Sports.content:
A majority of fans have decided that Manchester United should sack Michael Carrick - but they won't get their wish for now. Carrick, 45, hit a new low on Wednesday as he watched his side produce an abject display and lose 4-1 away to Champions League debutants Como.

It's now seven games without a win for United, who've already been knocked out of the Carabao Cup and are languishing 13th in the Premier League table after a dreadful start to the season. Their woeful form is a stark contrast to the winning run that they enjoyed during Carrick's spell as interim manager last term.

Wednesday's result plunged his future into doubt and it was unknown whether he'd be in charge for Sunday's home match against Bournemouth. It's now been confirmed that Carrick will hold his pre-match press conference as usual on Friday, with the message from Old Trafford being that it's 'business as usual'.

But just 11 games into his first full season, the majority of readers who voted on Mirror Football's poll have seen enough. Fifty-four per cent voted to sack Carrick, with the remainder believing that he deserves more time.

"Ryan Giggs did a lot of big games for Manchester United, Paul Scholes, Ruud Van Nistelrooy… a lot of players. I watched nearly every game of Manchester United 10 years ago, when I was a younger guy and a player.

‌



"I watched not only English football but also Serie A, Primera Division. I wanted to become a professional so it was important to watch games and look at what the best players in Europe do.

"Sir Alex Ferguson had a long and very successful time for Manchester United so it was also interesting to watch him, what he changed from one season to the next.

‌



"I know there will be no fans so that's hard. When there will be fans it will be more of a bigger experience. But if we win the game in the Theatre of Dreams it will be perfect."

View 3 Images Julian Nagelsmann 'watched nearly every game' involving Manchester United in his youth (Image: Vincent Mignott/DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

‌



Sadly for Nagelsmann, his side suffered a 5-0 loss. But his impressive work at Leizpig didn't stop him from being poached by Bayern, who paid €25million (£20.9m) to prise him away from Red Bull's football operation.

Nagelsmann lasted just shy of two seasons in Bavaria, winning the Bundesliga title in his first campaign. His next job was with Germany, leading them to the quarter-finals of a home European Championship in 2024.

‌



That was before the four-time winners were dumped out of this year's World Cup by Paraguay in the round of 32 on penalties. Nagelsmann quit shortly after the defeat, making way for Jurgen Klopp.

View 3 Images Julian Nagelsmann demands that his teams press high (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

‌



United fans may also be interested in some of his tactical comments after Bruno Fernandes criticised how Carrick set the Red Devils up against Como. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball," Fernandes told TNT Sports.

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

‌



Pressing is central to Nagelsmann's philosophy, as he explained in an interview with the Guardian in 2025: "I am not too keen on tackles. I much prefer us to win the ball by pressuring the opponent into a mistake, that we cut off his angles so that he makes a mistake when he tries to find a team-mate with a difficult pass.

‌



"And then, when we get the ball, we need to be quick in order to be able to create a chance and then it's better and the player is fresher when he hasn't had to make five tackles before starting an attack."

Once the hottest prospect in management, Nagelsmann's stock is arguably lower than ever. But at just 39 and with experience of high-pressure roles under his belt, he'll fancy he chances of being the answer to United's problems.

Sports.title: 'I played for Man Utd and under Antonio Conte - he'd be a disaster there'
Sports.content:
'I played for Man Utd and under Antonio Conte - he'd be a disaster there'

Antonio Conte is being linked as a potential replacement for Michael Carrick at Manchester United, though one ex-Old Trafford star has warned it could be a "disaster"

View 2 Images Manchester United have received a warning that Antonio Conte would be a disastrous appointment as manager (Image: Getty Images)

Former Manchester United star Ashley Young has cautioned his old club against appointing Antonio Conte as manager. The Italian is once again being tipped for the job as Michael Carrick comes in for more scrutiny.

‌



‌



United's season went from bad to worse on Wednesday when Carrick's side lost 4-1 away to Como in the Champions League. The club's seventh straight game without a win led to some uncomfortable comments from the manager post-match, suggesting United's players aren't running enough in their efforts to earn results.

‌



That's one specific area in which Young believes Conte, who coached him for 18 months at Inter Milan, would be a poor appointment. The former Juventus, Chelsea and Tottenham chief is renowned as a taskmaster when it comes to conditioning, where some in the current United squad may not meet the grade.

‌



Young appeared on The Overlap Daily, where he was quizzed on whether he felt Conte was a genuine target for United, or the Italian and his team were attempting to orchestrate the move themselves.

"I’d go with the second one," he said. "I think linking himself to the job, saying that big clubs, he wants to get the history back and whatnot.

Man Utd waste no time with sack decisions as Michael Carrick set to face the music READ MORE :

"I’ve worked underneath him at Milan. He’s crazy, by the way. Like he is crazy. He’s a bit like Diego Simeone on the sidelines. Like you hear him non-stop.

‌



"Meetings were long. When I say long, I’m talking, if we lost the game, we could go in and do the meeting after the game and it stops literally everything and you could be there for three, four hours. I think that’s one of the reasons why he doesn’t last long at places because not just the players, he tries to test mentally, but the board as well and the owners."

Young then proceeded to put his former team on high alert as he addressed United's alleged lack of running. "There has been a lot of talk about Man United’s running stats," he added. "If they’re not going to run and Antonio Conte goes in there, it’s going to be a disaster."

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick is under growing pressure to get the boot at United following a grim run of results (Image: AP Photo/Antonio Calanni)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Conte has long held a reputation as having incredibly high standards when it comes to the fitness levels demanded of his players. He's also a keen believer in strict dieting and helped ex-United striker Romelu Lukaku shed weight and improve his conditioning during their time together at Inter.

During his first pre-season in charge of Tottenham in 2022, stories emerged of how Conte and his fitness team were putting the Spurs players through their paces. Reports even claimed one two-hour session in Seoul ended with Harry Kane throwing up, while Son Heung-min collapsed in front of a home audience.

‌

Young - who only retired this year at Ipswich Town, aged 40 - was clearly up to the required standards. The veteran was long regarded as having impressive fitness levels throughout his playing career.

The same might not be said for numerous United players after struggling to keep up with Como's pace in Italy. And it's possible Conte's introduction to the current environment at Old Trafford could either bring the squad onto the next level or end in tears.

Sports.title: Julian Nagelsmann gives Man Utd green light as Michael Carrick replacement identified
Sports.content:
Julian Nagelsmann gives Man Utd green light as Michael Carrick replacement identified

Michael Carrick's job is hanging by a thread after Manchester United suffered a 4-1 hammering against Como in the Champions League, leaving them winless in seven games

View 2 Images Michael Carrick will remain in his post - for now (Image: Stefano Guidi/Getty Images)

Manchester United are set to consider Julian Nagelsmann if they decide to sack Michael Carrick - and the German is open to talks. United chiefs are sifting through the wreckage of Wednesday's woeful 4-1 defeat away to Como in the Champions League which thrust Carrick's future back into the spotlight.

‌



‌



The hammering extended the Red Devils' winless run to seven games, having only claimed victory in two of their 11 matches this season - against newly prompted Ipswich and European minnows Sabah. Carrick apologised to United's travelling supporters at the rainy Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium in scenes reminiscent of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's final act before he was sacked in 2021.

‌



While it's been decided that Carrick will stay in charge for Sunday's game against Bournemouth, the Telegraph report that United will consider appointing Nagelsmann if things don't improve. It's added that the ex-Bayern Munich boss would listen to an approach.

‌



The 39-year-old has been out of work since being resigning as manager of Germany in July. Nagelsmann - who made his name managing Bundesliga side Hoffenheim in his late 20s - has links with Christopher Vivell, United's director of global talent, having worked together at RB Leipzig.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



When Vivell was technical director at Chelsea, they looked at hiring Naglesmann. The report adds that Nagelsmann held concerns regarding Chelsea's structure and recruitment in 2023, so he'd likely demand assurances from the United board over those issues.

Another manager on United's shortlist is Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler, whose side are flying high in the Premier League. Like Nagelsmann, Hurzeler began his managerial career at a young age and he's been tracked for some time by the Old Trafford hierarchy as a future option.

‌



View 2 Images Julian Nagelsmann stepped down as Germany's manager in July (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

Antonio Conte has also been offered to the Red Devils, although the ex-Chelsea and Tottenham manager won't be considered. Nor will Eddie Howe, who's also a free agent after he left Newcastle.

‌



As for Carrick, he was handed a two-year deal by United following an outstanding spell as their interim manager last season. But things have already unravelled, with captain Bruno Fernandes calling out his tactics in a post-match interview.

Article continues below

"It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club," Carrick said after the loss. "It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters. I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

Sports.title: Red Roses’ four-year record gone – but good for women’s rugby?
Sports.content:
November 12, 2022 - the date England's Red Roses last lost a Test match before suffering defeat to Canada in Toronto a week ago, four years on.

Between their galling 2022 Women's Rugby World Cup final defeat to New Zealand at Eden Park and last week, the Red Roses went 41 Tests unbeaten, winning 39 consecutive matches before a draw against Canada in Exeter last month.

England's dominance is even more stark when you take into account that before that 2022 defeat, they had gone on a 30-Test winning run between November 2019 and November 2022.

Before last week in Canada, therefore, England had won 70 of their previous 72 Test matches. Astonishing and remarkable in equal measure.

Image: Canada ended England's 41-game unbeaten run in Toronto last week in a marvellous contest

Some eight Six Nations titles have been won in a row, in near totally dominant fashion too between 2019 and 2026, while a third World Cup triumph to sit alongside 1994 and 2014 was finally clinched on home soil in 2025, after final defeats in 2017 and 2022.

And yet, such monumentally impressive dominance had placed England in a position where Six Nations contests were fast becoming a non-event, competition-wise.

While France and New Zealand had historically competed hard and alongside England at the top of the world game, and Ireland won Six Nations titles in 2013 and 2015, the Red Roses were now consistently blowing those sides away completely.

Canada's rise in recent years can only be a good thing for the sport, as is the apparent resurgence of New Zealand's Black Ferns. They were level with England at 19-19 at Twickenham last month and pushing for a late winner in the final play, only for the Red Roses to snatch victory themselves.

In 2023, England put 50 points and 45 points on Canada in one-sided Test wins. By the 2025 World Cup final at Twickenham, Canada were competitive until England proved too strong and pulled away to glory.

But a year on, Canada have drawn with England in Exeter and now fought back to beat them in Toronto from a position of 21-12 behind. Friday's third Test between the sides in Ottawa is now a genuinely compelling and tantalising prospect. That can only be seen as a good thing for women's rugby.

Image: England being beaten and facing tough contests against Canada and New Zealand in this WXV has been good for women's rugby

Mitchell: Defeat is 'definitely' what Red Roses needed

Red Roses head coach John Mitchell has borderline talked up a defeat for his side in recent months.

Indeed, it appears the 62-year-old anticipated this WXV Global Series block was going to prove testing for his side, and is now relishing the chance to hit back.

"Definitely [it is what England needed]," he said. "I think even before that message we said: 'Come and get us.'

"We have been asking for someone to come and get us and they have done that. Not that we designed that to happen, far from it. We have to respond.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England head coach Mitchell explains why Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench for their third Test against Canada

"The important thing is winning after winning is harder than before. I guess what it does to everyone is it frees us up, which is cool. It allows us all to find more.

"I know this group has definitely got more in it but sometimes it requires the context that we have just received to dig deeper and push for something more.

"Friday is our first chance to respond. Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most and that's on us to fix.

"This week is about getting back to who we are: hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could.

"We've earned a strong period, but nothing about it is owed to us going forward. Friday is an opportunity to apply sustained pressure, learn from what we missed and come out the other side better than we went in."

Image: Mitchell and Jones spoke to media this week as the Red Roses digested a first defeat since November 2022

Jones: I know this will make Red Roses stronger

Red Roses centre Meg Jones has proven an inspirational leader since taking on the captaincy earlier this year, and was so even before the official title came her way.

In this period of pressure and spotlight, so unusual for the Red Roses, her soundbites to media have nearly all been pitch perfect.

"For us the biggest thing is that we stick together," she said this week.

"Games are built on moments, it is not one individual moment, it is multiple. That is the beauty of it and we get to review it, we get to go again, we get to stick together.

"I think it is good for us to reassess this and see where we are at. I think togetherness is the main message to come out of that because it's how you respond when you have had a loss, I think that is the biggest test of character.

"They are lessons at the end of the day, I don't think a loss necessarily changes the way we approach things. You genuinely do learn from it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Red Roses captain Jones speaks about facing Canada again after their remarkable 41-match unbeaten run came to an end when Kevin Rouet’s side beat them 24-21

"I spoke to Burts [Abi Burton] and we said: 'How many games have we lost in our career?' And we had a little chuckle, those are the ones that shape you the most at times. It's the biggest lesson for sure. Teams are coming out to beat us, they are going to put their best foot forward. We need to make sure we have got our best foot forward as well.

"It tests our game a lot, and it shows our character. We've just gained massive amounts of experience, and I know it'll make us stronger going into each game.

"Now we have the opportunity to not be defined by the outcome and really solidify where your two feet are and where you are is the most important. That is where you find courage and bravery to stick where you are in the present moment. That is going to be huge for us this weekend."

'Everything we do this year is to beat England'

And what of Canada? A year ago, they crowdfunded their way to a World Cup final against England at Twickenham, producing one of the tournament's standout performances along the way by beating New Zealand 34-19 at Ashton Gate with a swashbuckling brand of rugby.

Bringing together players from eight of Canada's 13 vast provinces and territories, spread across six time zones, and giving them the best possible preparation for the World Cup prompted a fundraising campaign with a target of C$1m (£535,355). Rugby Canada made its ambitions clear, dubbing it Mission: Win Rugby World Cup 2025.

Pledges reached 95 per cent of the target, helping fund training camps in California, Ontario and Belfast, as well as warm-up Tests in South Africa and Ireland.

Since rugby turned openly professional in 1995, Canada's women's sevens and 15s teams have become the country's flagship sides, surpassing the men's team. But Rugby Canada has lacked the resources to fully contract them.

As a result, world No 2 Canada are not a fully professional outfit like top-ranked England, but the gap between the two sides feels narrower than ever.

In September, Canada scrum-half Olivia Apps told the media that "everything we do this year is to beat England". True to their word, the Canadians have now done just that.

Now, it is England's chance to reply.

Image: Canada, who crowdfunded their way to a World Cup final last year, celebrate after their stunning win over England in Toronto

"When you've done it once, you want to do it twice," Canada head coach Kevin Rouet said this week.

"But to do it twice, you have to be serious. We have to enjoy, but we have to go back to the grind."

Also this week, Rouet signed a new contract with Canada through to 2030 as they build towards the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles and at Women's Rugby World Cup 2029.

"I am very excited for the opportunity to continue coaching this team for the next four years. We have grown so much as a group since I began in 2022, and I am excited to see what our teams and players can achieve as we build towards the 2028 Olympics and the 2029 Rugby World Cup.

Image: Canada head coach Kevin Rouet signed a new contract through to 2030 this week

"I also look forward to continuing to help develop the high-performance pathway for women's rugby in Canada. It's going to be an exciting next cycle."

Sports.title: 'They're not special anymore' - How Man Utd reached their latest low
Sports.content:
Manchester United's 4-1 defeat to Como was the latest chapter in their continued downward trajectory in recent years.

The problems go way beyond what supporters saw on the pitch in Italy. It is the culmination of over two decades of instability, mismanagement and tension.

With there seemingly being no end to Manchester United's fans discontent, Sky Sports News' Chief Correspondent Kaveh Solhekol takes a look at how the club got here and what could happen next.

Players are trying to tell fans something is wrong

I don't have a problem with what Bruno Fernandes said. I think it's quite refreshing. I understand the perspective of it should be kept inside the dressing room. I think these players are just so frustrated with the way the club is being run. They want to communicate to the fans that there is something wrong here.

Lisandro Martinez in his comments was saying there is something wrong upstairs. Especially in the transfer window. Fernandes was letting fans know that there was something wrong in the dressing room.

What was Fernandes supposed to say? What's the point of him talking to the media? This is a bit of a distraction. The big story is, Manchester United have been falling apart since the Glazers bought the club. This is just a symptom of what is going wrong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On Paper Talk, Henry Winter disagrees with Bruno Fernandes for publicly criticising Michael Carrick's tactics after Manchester United lost 4-1 at Como.

He and Martinez are performing a useful role for Manchester United fans by letting them have a little peek in what is going on behind the scenes at the club. Why in football is everyone allowed an opinion but the players?

One thing I will say is, how many of these players are good enough to play for Manchester United? How many would get into the starting XI's of Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City?

It's not Fernandes' fault. He is probably looking around going 'why am I still here?'

There are no positives and they aren't special

The only positives at Manchester United is that their revenue is at record levels even though they didn't play in Europe last season. Apart from that, there are absolutely no positives whatsoever. I don't think anything is going to change at Manchester United unless new owners come in and pay off the debt that the Glazer family have put on Manchester United.

Being owned by the Glazer family has cost Manchester United more than £2bn over the last 20 years. That is during a period of time where others are putting money into their clubs. I even heard from United fans over the past few days that 'it would be good if we were to get relegated. If we were relegated, the owners could sell the club and we can start again.' That is how bad things are. They are saying this team is worse than the team who finished 15th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports reporter Danyal Khan explains who is who in Manchester United's hierarchy

It's not beyond the realms of possibility that this team is going to be stuck in a relegation battle for the rest of the season. Maybe those United fans will get what they are asking for.

Is it the impossible job? I don't think so. I think there are harder jobs in the EFL. I think it is a very difficult job with the ownership structure. Sir Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS have come in and tried their best, but Jim Ratcliffe lives in Monaco. He is only allowed to be in the country for 90 days a year. The Glazer family live in the United States. You have owners that aren't even in the country for the vast majority of the time.

You've got all the debts that have now been put on the club. This was a club that was totally debt free. You have people at the club who have no understanding of the history and tradition of Manchester United. How many Manchester United people are there? 40 per cent of people have been made redundant, fans are getting priced out of season tickets. There is absolutely nothing good to say about Manchester United.

They are not special any more. Brentford are a better club. Brighton are a better club. You are surprised when Manchester United win, not when they lose. If they play Brighton you expect them to lose. If they are playing Brentford, you expect them to lose.

They play Bournemouth at the weekend. That's 50/50. If Bournemouth win, I wouldn't be surprised, that's just where Manchester United are. The fans recognise that about the club. They know what the major problem is. It's not Michael Carrick. It's not the players. It's the ownership model at the club.

Manchester United

Bournemouth Sunday 25th October 12:30pm Kick off 2:00pm

Sir Alex couldn't save this - but he's part of the problem!

You can bring Sir Alex Ferguson back, and nothing would change. United would not win the title again. I'm old enough to remember when he replaced Ron Atkinson. It took him five years to win the title, but he still had some great players and great characters at the club. Also, in those days, Manchester United were richer than anyone else. They had the biggest stadium. They had the biggest support. Their revenue came from matchday income.

That's completely changed. They're not the richest club in the country or one of the richest in the world. They may even drop out of the top 10. Even if Ferguson came back, I don't think he could fix this mess.

Image: Sir Alex Ferguson and Sir Matt Busby are the only two men to have won top tier league titles at Man Utd since World War II

Of all the great things he achieved, if you speak to Manchester United fans who worshipped him, they will say 'he never spoke out against the Glazers.' He was the one person 21 years ago who could've come out and maybe stopped the Glazers buying Manchester United in a leveraged buy out. He didn't do that, he went along with it.

You can go either further back in time in history. The whole story with the horse he owned, Rock of Gibraltar, and the disagreement over the breeding rights that indirectly led to the Glazers starting to buy shares in Manchester United and building up their stake until they owned the club.

What he achieved on the football pitch is incredible, but he himself did play a part in the Glazers becoming the owners of Manchester United and everything that has followed since.

The past is one thing, but what about the immediate future?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Paul Merson reflects on Manchester United's poor form but believes Michael Carrick should remain as United boss

I'm worried about Carrick. I'm worried about his body language as well. I didn't see that much fight in him. There's obviously a problem with his relationship with the players.

He just seems to be demoralised and almost disillusioned. I don't know what his relationship is like with the people above him. Maybe he feels let down because of what happened in the summer transfer window. It just seems to me watching him even on the touchline that the fight has gone out of him.

Other managers in that press conference last night I'd have expected to come out angry and raging. Defiant. He just seemed really flat. I wouldn't be surprised if he lost his job or I wouldn't be surprised if he just threw his towel in and said 'I don't need this in my life. This job is too big.'

Sports.title: McDermott blasts 'harsh' RL World Cup format
Sports.content:
England head coach Brian McDermott has branded the format of the Rugby League World Cup as "harsh" with his side up against it to progress.

Last Saturday's loss to Tonga means England must hope Tonga beat Samoa in their final group game next week in order to stand any realistic chance of reaching the semi-finals.

That scenario would leave England and Samoa to be separated by points difference - a particularly tough ask for McDermott's men given the Samoans started their campaign with a crushing 78-4 win over France.

"The jeopardy is losing one game is so harsh, it's almost like we don't get another chance to straighten things out," said McDermott, whose side face the French in their second group game in Perth on Saturday.

Image: England were thrashed by Tonga in their opening game at the 2026 Rugby League World Cup

"There's still a slim chance that we get through, and that's something we're focusing on, and we're really determined. It's just harsh that we have to take a standing eight count in the first round."

This year's World Cup was reduced to 10 men's teams after France pulled out of hosting the event in 2023, resulting in a complicated, partial cross-group format which means one of the top five nations will be eliminated at the first stage.

In contrast, favourites Australia and New Zealand are effectively guaranteed to reach the last four after being placed in a conventional, four-team Group A alongside Fiji and the Cook Islands.

McDermott added: "New Zealand have lost their first game as well, but they're going to get another go at it and the likelihood is they'll qualify, so their destiny is not lying in other people's hands.

"That's not the position we find ourselves in. There's no frustration, all I'm recognising in that the jeopardy is really harsh. We knew that for us to go through, we had to go and beat Tonga."

Image: McDermott pointed out the differences between England losing their opening game compared to New Zealand

'Lewis has shown humility in camp - we have considered changes'

In his squad to face France on Saturday, McDermott has stuck with the same 19-man group that were thrashed 30-12 by Tonga, with a late alteration seeing Matty Ashton start in place of Zach Eckersley on the wing.

There remains no place for Hull KR star Lewis, who is named a reserve and not in the starting team nor on the bench.

The 25-year-old, who won 2024's Man of Steel, has picked up eight caps so far in his career, but only started three of them.

"He [Lewis] is good, it was a frustrating end to the season for him, but he won a World Club Challenge at the start of the year," McDermott said.

"He's been great round the camp, he knows his role. He's shown a lot of humility in the camp, as have a few other players.

"He's been really good to work with.

Image: Mikey Lewis will not feature for England again as England opt for unchanged squad vs France

"Mikey Lewis is a tremendous player and you've got to wonder whether he'd give us something that we haven't got.

"For sure, it has been considered [change at half-back], but I thought George (Williams) was good against Tonga.

"I think George has been unfairly assessed and I thought Harry Smith was really good. We were co-ordinated both in yardage attack and good ball attack.

"We got held up over the line four times in the game and there was a try-saver from Tonga holding up Herbie Farnworth."

Sports.title: Jarvis leads at Genesis Championship to pressure McIlroy in Race to Dubai
Sports.content:
Casey Jarvis made a strong start to his late bid for Race to Dubai glory by grabbing the early lead at the Genesis Championship, where Ryan Fox also impressed.

Fourth on the Race to Dubai ranking, Jarvis birdied the final hole at Woo Jeong Hills Country Club to regain the outright lead from nearest challenger Sanghun Shin on day one of the final event of the regular season.

Already a two-time winner this season, the 23-year-old is projected to overtake Rory McIlroy and Patrick Reed and enter the DP World Tour Play-Offs in second place behind leader Eugenio Chacarra.

"Felt really good out there," Jarvis said.

"Hit a lot of good-quality iron shots and made some good putts. Been working really hard on the greens and to see it finally paying off a bit is really nice. So yeah, super happy.

"I definitely think the putting has improved a lot. I went through a bit of a dip, so I worked hard with the putter and took some time in the middle of the season to start finding the stroke again. I started with a new putting coach and it seems to be working really well."

The South African made three birdies in a row at the third, fourth and fifth holes before another at the eighth took him to four under alongside early leaders Antoine Rozner and Mikael Lindberg.

A dropped shot at the ninth saw him turn in 33, but after two pars, a brilliant approach from the rough at the 12th helped him regain a share of the lead. He then moved clear with a 32-footer for birdie to reach five under.

Close behind on the other side of the course, Frederic Lacroix converted from two feet for birdie at the sixth, his 15th, to briefly join Jarvis at the top. The Frenchman then gave the shot straight back after missing the green at the par-three seventh before closing with two pars for an opening 67.

Sanghun Shin, who had been part of a four-way tie one shot back, was the next to join Jarvis as the Korean Tour (KPGA) Order of Merit leader birdied his final hole.

After Shin signed for a 66, Jarvis regained the outright lead by holing from seven feet for a closing birdie of his own.

It has been a breakout year for Jarvis, who recorded two top tens before claiming his maiden DP World Tour title in February with a birdie-eagle finish at the Magical Kenya Open presented by absa.

A week later, he won his second DP World Tour title on home soil at the Investec South African Open Championship, securing qualification for both the Masters Tournament and The Open Championship in 2026, where he finished tied sixth.

He almost made it three wins in a row with a tie for second at the Joburg Open, and although he has not maintained that momentum throughout the season, he recently returned to form by finishing tied second at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.
