Sports.title: Carra: Fernandes comments 'disgraceful', but Carrick's time may be up
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has criticised Bruno Fernandes for questioning Man Utd's tactics following their 4-1 defeat to Como, but believes that it could be the end of the line for Michael Carrick.

Fernandes questioned the decision to not press Como man-to-man post-match, while Carrick responded in his press conference by saying "if you don't run back, you ain't going to win".

Fernandes' claims come just over a week after Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy following the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid. Carragher was critical of the Argentine's comments, and shared a similar stance when it came to the Manchester United captain's verdict.

"We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order for calling out the hierarchy," Carragher said on CBS Sports.

"For Bruno Fernandes to do that, it is a disgrace. Last season he was Player of the Year. That was due to Michael Carrick coming in as manager. He wouldn't have got that award without Carrick. He put him back in his right position.

"His attitude and the way he goes about things, it is not right at all. He has reacted like that because he was brought off and he has been embarrassed tonight by the manager.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United boss Michael Carrick admitted his team's performance was 'not acceptable' in their 4-1 loss at Como in the Champions League

"When he talks about pressing, whether it is man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Man Utd can't press.

"He runs all over the place like a kid in the school yard for the supporters. They all think he's working hard, he is not. He is killing the rest of the team by doing it.

"He is not playing in a successful era at Manchester United but years ago there was a captain called Bryan Robson, one of the greatest players to ever play for Man Utd.

"He didn't play for teams that won leagues or European cups every year. He is still seen as one of the greatest players to play for the club. He never threw a manager or the players under the bus. He kept fighting for Man Utd.

"Watching him [Bruno] play every week, throwing his arms up at players constantly, it is a disgrace that he has called out the manager considering how he has performed this season on the pitch. Awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should be.

"How many managers has he had? Every single manager at Man Utd has not had an identity?

"[Como boss] Cesc Fabregas, I think he is the best young thing in managerial terms, but Man Utd is rotten from top to bottom. Everything about the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On Paper Talk, Henry Winter disagrees with Bruno Fernandes for publicly criticising Michael Carrick's tactics after Manchester United lost 4-1 at Como

"This can't go on for a club of this stature. I am glad Michael Carrick came out and said that about Bruno Fernandes. That they don't run, because they don't run.

"I am delighted he brought him off and delighted he had a pop back at him."

'Looks like another Man Utd manager is going to bite the dust'

While Carragher may have been pleased with Carrick's response to Fernandes, he admitted that it might be the final straw for the former midfielder as Man Utd manager.

"It's embarrassing. But the worst thing about it I that I don't think there were many people who thought Manchester United could win tonight," Carragher added.

"So, in some ways it doesn't feel like a shock result. I think the manner of it is the shocking part of it.

"I think it's such a bad result and a bad performance that it could have serious repercussions for the manager, unfortunately for him.

"Good lad, good player for Man Utd, did really well last season, but again It looks like another Man Utd manager is going to bite the dust."

Merse: United should stick with Carrick

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Paul Merson reflects on Manchester United's poor form but believes Michael Carrick should remain as United boss, following their heavy 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

While Carragher thinks Carrick's time might be coming to an end, Paul Merson has suggested that changing the manager will change nothing and that the club should stick with their man.

"It's a bad result. It's a bit like snakes and ladders. They get to the top of the ladder and then get to the snake and go back down again. It's got to get steadied out," Merson said.

"To steady the ship, I think you've got to keep with the same manager. He's proven that he did get results last year. This is what I wanted to see from Michael Carrick last season. When it was going well and people were saying give him the job, it's easy when you're winning every week.

"It's when you're not doing well how the manager reacts. Now is the time to see how you are going to react.

"What do you change the manager for? You could bring in [Carlo] Ancelotti and tell him to win the league but he will fail miserably. But, if you want to come in and start learning how to walk first and go from there...

"It's just bringing managers in and it's the same thing. It's Man Utd, you've got to win the league. You're entitled to get top four. That's not Man Utd any more."

'Carrick's change in tune startling'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan provides insight on three things we learned from Manchester United's embarrassing Champions League loss at Como

Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan:

"I'm still processing what we saw last night and even more incredibly, how Michael Carrick handled that situation.

"After the final whistle blows you see him going to the away fans, really ignoring a lot of the players, hands up apologising to the 100 of the 700 away stand left.

"A completely dejected Michael Carrick. There will be comparisons to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2021 when United were pretty comprehensively beaten by Watford. Carrick was part of that coaching staff and Solskjaer was sacked.

"Then you see Michael Carrick in his post-match press conference. He has defended this team so much after the last few months when they have been targeted with their running, their intensity and their aggression. He couldn't defend any of that.

"His captain, Bruno Fernandes, comes out questioning the tactics and Carrick bit back. The fact that he hasn't broken ranks and turned on the team, but accepted criticism that for the majority of the season has been targeted at his side, was quite startling."

Sports.title: Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max Rushden
Sports.content:
You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago.

And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants”, to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie.

Yes, it’s time to dust down the Manchester United bin-fire article. Read this and compare and contrast. From 11 August 2022: “Reds rinse and repeat: will we ever break the Manchester United crisis cycle?” There are others.

It is some feat to be more newsworthy than Manchester City, even for an evening. The defeat in Como wasn’t surprising. We’re getting to the stage where the large pieces of furniture Barney Ronay keeps comparing Harry Maguire to are fighting back. @19thCenturyArmoir: “mate i’m a hundred and sixty years old, of course my legs have gone.” @CoffinFridge69: “#BeKind Ronay, appliances have feelings too.”

Everyone knows the problems at Old Trafford lie deeper than the defensive line held by Maguire and Matthijs de Ligt on Wednesday.

Perhaps it was only a matter of time before Bruno Fernandes’s constant on-field complaining spilled off the pitch. An exercise in throwing his manager under the bus, where presumably Michael Carrick found Jason Wilcox, still lying in hiding under the 250 to the Trafford Centre after Lisandro Martínez’s post-match intervention in Madrid.

Carrick did push back on the criticism: “Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you aren’t going to win.” But it’s hard to throw someone under the bus when you’re already under the bus you’re trying to throw people under.

Poor Carrick, who may well be gone by the time I finish this tram ride, never mind by the time you get around to reading this. It was one of those funereal press conferences: Carrick being as earnest as it is possible to be, while journalists take it in turn to sound even more earnest, as if they’re questioning a man who’s just failed to blow up the asteroid coming to destroy the Earth.

At this rate, that meteor will arrive long before United have recaptured past glories. Ineos presumably has a big blame pie chart constantly updating on a PowerPoint. Spin the wheel – who’s to blame today? Maybe the players?

56:15 Manchester United bin-fire keeps blazing and Arsenal draw at Bayern | Football Weekly Extra – video

Does anyone genuinely know any more whether any United player is good? I have analysis paralysis when trying to work out whether Fernandes is world class or why Youri Tielemans never lumbered at Aston Villa. How bamboozled will we be when Joshua Zirkzee has 25 goal involvements for Real Sociedad next season?

As for Carrick, while most of us (me included) felt he’d earned the right to manage the side this season, a more ruthless and efficient ownership would have made a different call. It wouldn’t have been popular.

He may turn out to be a world-class manager – he may not. Football decides pretty quickly about these things. But if he is sacked, there is a path to redemption. Daniel Farke has moved beyond “only good in the Championship”. Frank Lampard could reasonably expect an apology from anyone who comments on the game for his achievements at Coventry.

But at this stage it is fair to say Carrick doesn’t have the tactical ability or experience of almost all his competitors in the division.

Above him, is Jason Wilcox good? Perhaps the last time someone yelled at him like Martínez, it was Mike Newell after an overhit cross at Ewood Park in 1991. What will Omar Berrada’s CV look like after the independent panel delivers its punishments?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick’s remaining time as Manchester United head coach may be short. Photograph: Antonio Calanni/AP

It is fair to say that barring the odd All or Nothing documentary, I have almost no knowledge of what happens behind the scenes. But £1bn spent by United to create this squad over the past five years, plus the randomness of Rangnick/Ten Hag/Van Nistelrooy/Amorim/Carrick, gives us limited evidence to suggest high performance.

And at the top, what does Jim Ratcliffe care about? Apart from enjoying the tax rates of Monaco while opining about the fallen British empire. The good old days where you could just colonise and get a pat on the back, eh Jim.

And then there’s the Glazers. Even for someone whose brain shuts down as soon as they hear the words “leveraged debt” the fact they have extracted about £1bn out of the club since the takeover in 2005 is an outrage. Perhaps if they had overseen a period of sustained success, but it is the opposite.

So when you add bad (maybe bad?) players, bad (or at least disrespectful) captain, bad (not great yet) manager, bad technical director, bad chief executive, bad minority owner, bad majority owners – apologies if I’ve missed anyone – it is, well, bad.

So what’s the best plan of action now? Did someone say Antonio Conte? For the wind and the rain make it happen. As Paul Watson said on the latest Guardian Football Weekly, he might resign during his unveiling.

Lots of us who lived through the Fergie success can’t help but enjoy a Manchester United crisis, but it’s possible to laugh and at the same time sympathise with powerless United fans under that dripping roof in the East Stand.

Football is so stupid that Conte, or Eddie Howe, or even Carrick could turn this into a good season. Perhaps everyone’s expectations still cling to a Manchester United that do not exist any more. Perhaps the odd trophy, the occasional foray deep into Europe, may be the new normal. But right now, how many Premier League teams are worse than they are? Did someone say a Manchester derby in the Championship next season? I can hear David Prutton’s excitement already.

Sports.title: Lech Poznan v Sunderland, Juventus v Rennes, and more: Europa League – live
Sports.content:
It’s been a strange start to the season for Sunderland and I’m not just talking about those pink Elvis kits. Yes, that is a real sentence. They’ve had some rotten luck – if they could’ve picked two players to avoid injury, Dan Ballard and Brian Brobbey would probably have been them – and, after last season’s outrageous exploits, they now sit bottom of the Premier League.

However! Making their first foray into Europe in 52 years, they won their first home game then, on their first trip abroad, they conceded a ridiculous opener, equalised, missed a late penalty … and scored an incredible injury-time winner which was also Noah Sadiki’s first goal for the club, all of which combined into one of the great away-end goons. And no, I’m not enumerating it in such detail because my best mate had to cry off late doors due to a work crisis, I promise; by way of compensation, I’ve demanded he furnish us with photos from Poznan.

So, Sunderland’s trip to Poland will form the centrepiece of our early coverage, but that’s not the half of what we’ve got going on. Little more than a decade ago, if someone told us Milan were going to Bournemouth, we’d have assumed it was in holiday and told them not to miss Sega World or Splashdown in Poole. Now, though, they’re visiting for a game of football, one of the biggest ever played in the town, and Dean Court will be bouncing for what is our featured match in the second part of the evening.

View image in fullscreen Milan fans on Bournemouth pier earlier on Thursday. Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty Images

And, in among all of that, we’ve got Crystal Palace’s trip to Besiktas and one of the great – not a word I use lightly in this context – town centre grounds, plus the linguistic derby of Celtic v Celta, Juventus v Rennes, and form team Brighton’s jaunt to Jablonec in the Conference.

Kick-offs: 5.45pm BST and 8pm BST

Sports.title: Champions League review: PSG take a hit, Man City’s empty seats and teenage hope for Liverpool
Sports.content:
A big week for …

Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday, but the reigning champions lost the best player in last season’s tournament, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This autumn has seen much lobbying for the Ballon d’Or, with the Georgian a popular choice, despite his absence from the World Cup. He is expected to be out for six months, although Rodri’s comeback from serious injury – he was rested by Barcelona on Tuesday until coming off the bench in the 60th minute – shows it can take far longer than that for players to rediscover their highest level.

“Why me?” Kvaratskhelia asked his Instagram followers. The PSG policy of resting players in Ligue 1 to save them for the Champions League failed to protect him. By resting Rodri, Barcelona followed a wider practice among major clubs in European competition of saving stars’ legs for big domestic occasions. Barcelona face Real Madrid this weekend though Lamine Yamal is not being spared; his brilliant goal in Paris made it 10 goals, matched by 10 assists, from 10 matches.

Another heavyweight battle saw Arsenal lose Bukayo Saka to a first-half quad injury in an entertaining 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich. Declan Rice powered in a late equalizer after Harry Kane had put on a show that included a goal and an assist. Does the Ballon d’Or beckon for Kane? The prediction markets suggest so.

Matching Barcelona’s perfect record this season at home and abroad are Manchester City, who continue to thrive amid infamy. A resurgent Phil Foden scored a hat-trick and new signing Allan impressed. The official crowd for their 5-1 defeat of AEK Athens was 40,402, but it looked smaller, and mockery duly descended on the club. There is mitigation for those who stayed away, including high ticket prices for Champions League matches in tough economic times, and a run of five home matches in 17 days. Still, City remain in the crosshairs, and the empty seats raise eyebrows for a club reporting record revenues. Equally, it is fair to point out that Anfield was not full, either, for Liverpool’s 4-3 defeat of Villarreal.

A clean sweep of wins for Serie A, with three of their clubs scoring four goals. Inter let the side down with their 1-0 defeat of Shakhtar Donetsk. Roma defeated Slovan Bratislava 4-0, and Como beat Manchester United 4-1, but the game of the week came in Naples. Scott McTominay scored twice, his first goals since a procedure on a benign heart arrhythmia as Napoli beat Bodø/Glimt 4-3 for their first win of the group stage. “I still need to find my best form, but I am not far away,” said McTominay.

Player of the week

Liverpool were a mess in the first 30 minutes against Villarreal and it was Rio Ngumoha who led the recovery. The 18-year-old played off the right, supplying two assists with his left foot: the long-term replacement for Mohamed Salah may already be at Anfield. Liverpool have nursed Ngumoha along, though this was his fifth start of the season. “Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo [Salah] last year was obviously massive,” Virgil van Dijk said of the teenager.

Club in focus: Como

With traditional Serie A giants Juventus and Milan in the Europa League, Como are enjoying their first season in the Champions League. If Manchester United were dreadful on Wednesday, Como’s rise hit its highest point yet. The club’s success carries echoes of Brighton and Bournemouth’s ascents, although Como’s is even more remarkable. They were a Serie D club in 2008, and the city is now known for something beyond its glorious scenery. Champions League winner Thierry Henry is among the investors in the club as is Como’s coach, Cesc Fàbregas, although the prime financiers are the Indonesian billionaire Hartono brothers.

Jamestown Analytics, the Brighton owner Tony Bloom’s company, has been consulting Como. Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho and Antonio Conte are the elite coaches Fàbregas played under, and he has forged a high-pressing style against Italian orthodoxy. As United labored, they were swarmed by Como’s worker bees. Real Madrid have a buy-back option for Nico Paz, bought by Como in 2024, and the scorer of two fine goals against United. Argentina’s latest Messi replacement is rather beefier than his country’s idol.

As Como deepened Michael Carrick’s plight, thoughts moved to potential replacements. Fàbregas has been mentioned, though United fans will recall the summer of 2013’s unsuccessful chase for him. Had a deal been done, his midfield partner would have been … Carrick.

View image in fullscreen Nico Paz piled misery on Manchester United. Photograph: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock

They said it

Another week, another Manchester United PR crisis. This one involved Carrick hitting back at his players, a rarity in his managerial career. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” Bruno Fernandes said.

Carrick’s riposte: “If you don’t run and you don’t run forward and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win.”

On CBS, Jamie Carragher weighed, saying of Fernandes: “They all think he’s working hard. He’s not. He’s killing the rest of the team doing it.”

The Amazon All or Nothing documentary series currently in production for United’s season will be appointment viewing.

Looking ahead

After two consecutive weeks of action, we have a fortnight off. Will Carrick still be at United by the time they host Roma on 3 November? Aston Villa, who have three wins from three and are second place in the table, have a glamour trip to Barcelona. Real Madrid, another side on three wins, travel to AEK.

After defeat to Inter, Shakhtar’s adopted home, Stamford Bridge, hosts Sporting Lisbon, who this week were on the wrong end of Lask’s first ever group-stage win.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
Sports.content:
For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway. Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle.

Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours?

Sometimes, you simply have to take a deep breath and the plunge. Nobody wants to die wondering. Guimarães knew the Newcastle team was breaking up. Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali had gone to Barcelona and Tottenham. The manager, Eddie Howe, was at the end of the line and he would also leave. Guimarães went through with the £75m transfer and nobody can say it has not worked out so far.

Arsenal felt he would provide a different element for them, different ways of unlocking defences. Plus his trademark work rate and snarl. Guimarães has brought all of that. Already he has made a difference. He even gave a little back to Newcastle when he scored his first Arsenal goal at Sunderland in September. It paved the way for a 2-0 victory. Two Premier League games later, he scored the winner at home against Leeds.

Guimarães almost got another vital goal on Wednesday in the Champions League tie at Bayern Munich only for Manuel Neuer to deny him with an outrageous save. That would have put Arsenal 2-1 up. The game finished 2-2, Arsenal fighting until the end and equalising through Declan Rice in the 82nd minute. Still, it has not been easy for Guimarães and he surely has Arsenal’s visit to Newcastle on 21 November circled in his diary. His greatest hope is that he can build the same relationships at his new club.

“It was not just hard to tell Eddie but to tell the owners and my teammates [about deciding to leave Newcastle],” Guimarães says. “But I think the club went to a new rotation; a lot of players left, as well. The gaffer left. It was tough because my connection with the club was unbelievable. I never felt so loved like the way I was at Newcastle. I hope I can have the same love here at Arsenal.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães says he had sleepless nights contemplating leaving Newcastle for Arsenal. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

“It was hard for me to say bye. I remember when I said bye to the lads, I was crying. They were crying as well because we were a family there. I lost many, many nights of sleep because it was difficult for me, for my family. But sometimes in your life you have to make decisions and in my mind, I needed a new challenge. I wish Newcastle all the best because they were so nice to me. It is just time to move on and I’ve been enjoying my time here at Arsenal, as well.”

Guimarães is enjoying his burgeoning midfield partnership with Rice, not to mention Martin Ødegaard, who tends to be the most advanced of the trio. That said, there is plenty of fluidity between the positions. There is the sense that the manager, Mikel Arteta, is searching for the perfect balance.

“Declan can play – like me – as a No 6, No 8 or No 10,” Guimarães says. “The manager is still trying to get the best version of ourselves. Against Bayern, I played more as a No 6, Declan played more as a No 8. I enjoy playing with him a lot; with Martin, as well. We have been on a good run so far.”

Guimarães’s battles when he was at Newcastle against Rice have been well documented. He said Rice had messaged him as he prepared to sign for Arsenal, saying: “No more fights, now we’re friends.” Guimarães is the player you loathe when he is against you but love when he is in your ranks.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Manuel Neuer keeps out Bruno Guimarães’s header in the Champions League. Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

What was the worst thing Guimarães said to Rice when they were in opposition? “It is difficult to say,” he replies with a smile. “I am like this when I play against teams. When we were playing against each other, I was not nice to him, he was not nice to me! Now we try to help each other on the pitch.”

Guimarães cannot believe how Neuer kept out his close-range header; the 40-year-old goalkeeper clawed the ball up against the crossbar and away. “He pulled off a miracle,” Guimarães says. “I asked him after the game: ‘How did you manage to save that?’ He said: ‘I don’t know. I just saved it!’ He’s unbelievable, one of the best keepers in the world. No matter how old he is, he is top.”

What Guimarães has seen with clarity is the remorselessness of the collective attitude at Arsenal; the insatiable will to win, which comes from Arteta. Next up for them is Everton at home on Saturday. Guimarães knows he is in the right place.

“The mentality of the club has changed a lot and Arteta shows this perfectly,” Guimarães says. “We don’t accept a draw at Bayern. We always want to win. That is the mentality that we go to the training ground with every day. Arteta is always a little bit addicted to videos and the way that he can make us feel better on the pitch. We have a top manager with a top mentality. We want to win everything possible.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane admits wait to learn if he has won Ballon d’Or is ‘very stressful’ for family
Sports.content:
Harry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and constant questions are driving his family to distraction. But the Bayern Munich and England striker accepts the suspense before the big reveal at the London Palladium on Monday night is part of the show.

Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the prestigious individual honour after a prolific run of form. The 33-year-old scored 61 goals for Bayern last season and 12 for England. This time out, he has 10 for Bayern and six for England. He scored from the penalty spot in Wednesday night’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena, although his stand-out moment was the inch-perfect through ball that set up Alphonso Davies to make it 1-1.

Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal is the second-favourite for the Ballon d’Or and Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid is next in the betting.

“I think my wife would prefer to know and my family … it’s very stressful for everyone,” Kane said, when asked whether he would prefer to be told in advance of the ceremony. “I can see why they don’t tell people. They want everyone to go, all the big names, and there will be more people watching it if they don’t know so I can understand why.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“From my point of view, of course I’d love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. But it is their decision, I can’t control that. We’ll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much. I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rumours and stuff flying around so you try to stay away from it.”

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
Sports.content:
Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground it is not the dream start they were aiming for.

As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace.

It cost plenty to acquire Glasner and Delap, which many fans believe should lead to instant results, but that is rarely the case in an industry as complicated as football. For the coach, it is a case of learning the club inside out while influencing performance through an implementation of his carefully choreographed methods. For the striker, he needs to rebuild confidence and that comes via goals.

In Glasner’s first full season at Palace, they won one of their first 13 league matches, but ended comfortably in mid-table and FA Cup winners. It was similar at Eintracht Frankfurt, getting one victory in 10, but going on to win the Europa League.

Learning the Glasner way is not straightforward. Playing three at the back is rarely the norm and nor is having two No 10s, all with the background of Forest losing their best player in Elliot Anderson.

The recruitment was measured, targeting positions that required strengthening and avoiding needless purchases that dogged the club after promotion. Replacing Anderson became a priority, but Glasner felt James McAtee could adapt to a deeper role in midfield alongside the shrewd free signing Xaver Schlager. Ousmane Diomande was a coup in defence and Glasner convinced Daniel Muñoz to follow him from Selhurst Park.

Behind the obvious figures, there is plenty of underlying encouragement for Forest. Based on chances created and conceded, Glasner has had the best start of any Forest manager in the Premier League era. His team rank seventh, according to Opta, for expected goals (xG), but have scored the fewest – five – and are the biggest xG underperformers at -6.2. It is a huge discrepancy, missing out on almost a goal a game. It includes 62 shots at home that have come to nothing and if Glasner wants buy-in from the fans, that needs to change quickly. If every team had scored and conceded the goals measured by xG, Forest would be fourth.

View image in fullscreen Nottingham Forest, and Liam Delap, are yet to score at the City Ground this season. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

It is understandable that Delap is yet to find his feet after a disappointing year at Chelsea and the lack of pre-season set him back. Forest tried to sign him before he went to Stamford Bridge and have great faith in him, but he needs to improve his record of one goal every five league appearances. He is the ideal No 9, possessing pace, power and sharp finishing, but unless he is on peak form, turning that into guaranteed output is not straightforward.

Delap has scored once for Forest, but is putting in the effort through being the front line of defence, relentlessly pressing opposition centre-backs. He has shown plenty of quick thinking, demonstrated by his quick throw-in to set up a goal at Anfield, something almost replicated against Arsenal only for Chris Wood to miss the chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Forest allowed Arsenal a single shot on target last Sunday – it just happened to be deflected in for a winner. Glasner can also point in that match to the absence of his captain, Morgan Gibbs-White, the team’s attacking fulcrum. “It feels very unfair,” Glasner said of the result. “We have to accept we are missing some bits. But the performance in many parts was very good.”

In two full seasons at Selhurst Park, Glasner won two major trophies for a club that had gone almost 120 years without one. He has two European titles and his own distinctive formation and execution, something he has harnessed over 12 years in coaching, so he knows how long it takes to develop the complexities.

The picture looks clearer after almost four months together. The hope at Forest is that the endeavour is rewarded with greater luck, the missing ingredient among well thought-out recruitment led by the chief football officer, George Syrianos, and his team and clever coaching. Syrianos is Glasner’s biggest advocate and told fans the manager would be given time.

Friday will be Glasner’s eighth Premier League match at Forest, three more than Ange Postecoglou was permitted before being sacked this time last year by the owner, Evangelos Marinakis. Glasner, unlike the Australian, can show progress and will be justifiably confident points will come.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca says honest talks have revitalised Foden’s Manchester City form
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has revealed he held heart-to-heart conversations with Phil Foden to help the midfielder back to his best. Foden has struggled over the past two years but has scored four goals in his past two games to give hope he can recapture the form that won him the a Professional Footballers’ Association players’ player of the year award in 2023-24.

City travel to Aston Villa on Saturday lunchtime aiming to continue their perfect Premier League start under Maresca, with Erling Haaland fit after sitting on the bench for Wednesday’s Champions League win over AEK Athens.

“Since we started I sat down with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning,” said Maresca, who knew Foden from a spell as Pep Guardiola’s assistant. “Maybe love is not the right word to use but just to show him how important he is.

“I said many times that I know Phil from years ago so I know how good he is. For different reasons the last few years he was not good enough but again I think when you have more players like Phil available you are a better team because at the end it’s a matter of improving players. If you improve the players you improve the team, so for me it’s my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England. But it’s not just about one game – the season is very long.”

Foden, 26, needs to remain consistent to keep his place in the team, with plenty of competition for the attacking roles, including from Rayan Cherki, who Maresca has described as “one of the best players in Europe”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City’s only competitive defeat under Maresca came against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, and they have seven straight wins in the Premier League to sit three points clear at the top. Maresca is waiting to find out whether Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic and Nico O’Reilly are available after missing the AEK game. “The mood is good, we are happy with our start but we are still hungry for more wins,” Maresca said.

Sports.title: Cathinka Tandberg: ‘Spurs fans hate Arsenal. That’s how it is’
Sports.content:
“It means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday.

“It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.”

“All the Spurs fans hate Arsenal and Arsenal hate Spurs. That’s how it is. You want to show that you’re the best team. Simple as that. You just want to fight for the club, the badge and for the people around you.”

View image in fullscreen Cathinka Tandberg joined Tottenham from the Swedish side Hammarby in the summer of 2025. Photograph: Javier García/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

It has been a significant 13 months for the 22-year-old who made her dream move to London in September 2025. After catching the eye as a goalscorer in the Damallsvenskan at first Linköping and then Hammarby, the Norwegian was signed by Martin Ho on deadline day to bolster the team’s attacking options. She made her mark on her first start, scoring a spectacular 40-yard goal against Everton.

“I settled really well,” she reflects. “I’m really enjoying it and want to push myself forward. It’s been a tough start [to this season] and I haven’t really got what I wanted. But there’s loads of games left. I’m still young. I’m still improving and learning. I just have to trust the process and trust what I’m surrounded by.”

“It’s a big difference from Sweden,” she continues. “You meet World Cup players week in, week out so you have to perform every week if you want results. I feel like my physicality has changed a lot. I’ve got stronger and fitter. Playing under Martin has made me think more away from the goals. I think more about how I play with the ball, how I press and all of those things that I maybe didn’t focus on before … it’s a bit like Harry Kane. The older he gets, he has developed his game as well. He needed to be deeper in the pitch because that’s how they wanted to play and then he has to be better with the ball. That’s a bit how I also need to be. I can’t only just stand in the box. I need to be good everywhere else.”

Spurs have been transformed under Ho and finished fifth last season. However, with success, comes expectation, ambitions that Tandberg clearly shares but with a sense of perspective.

“Tottenham has always been a Champions League club for me,” she says. “But I’m a fan so I can’t really talk for the other players. When I came to the club, I said that I want to get top three. But you also need to be realistic and to see where the team has been before. The transformation that Martin has done in a season is unbelievable. I don’t think anyone else could do that. That tells you everything about him. He’s one of the greatest coaches I’ve worked with and I think everyone that comes here, one of the reasons is because of him. We all trust him and the process.”

View image in fullscreen ‘Tottenham has always been a Champions League club for me. But I’m a fan so I can’t really talk for the other players. When I came to the club, I said that I want to get top three. But you also need to be realistic and to see where the team has been before.’ Cathinka Tandberg’s ambitions for her club are high. Photograph: Leila Coker/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images

That faith is currently being tested. After an unbeaten start, Tottenham have suffered back-to-back defeats, shipping six goals to both London City Lionesses and Chelsea.

“You can call it a dip in form but I still feel like we also showed our qualities in those games,” Tandberg says. “It’s just about ourselves. We maybe need to change our mentality a bit, find that fire and dig a bit deeper when we play those top teams. I feel like maybe it’s good that it’s come because it had to at some point. It’s about how we respond.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

‘We also have to realise where this team has been. Two years ago, it was a relegation club. We need to realise how quickly it has [changed]. But, of course, we have expectations and levels that we want to come to and we know that we can. I feel like we’re working so well … we just have to believe in everyone.”

For Tandberg, putting that right against a struggling Arsenal in front a home crowd would be the perfect tonic. “I’ve always been a passionate player and I’ve been a supporter,” she says. “I play for the supporters because I just enjoy it and I know how it is to be in the stands. I think [that connection] is very important because we have their back and they have ours. To give them something back is important and to show that we see and hear them every time.”

Sports.title: Neil Warnock outlines how Michael Carrick should deal with Bruno Fernandes at Man United
Sports.content:
Neil Warnock outlines how Michael Carrick should deal with Bruno Fernandes at Man United

Michael Carrick must hold a meeting with Bruno Fernandes and start him for Manchester United against Bournemouth on Sunday.

That's the view of legendary manager Neil Warnock, who knows the pair at not currently aligned with each other amid their worrying run of seven winless matches.

4 Fernandes vented his frustrations with Carrick's tactics after they were dispatched 4-1 by Como Credit: Getty

After a bleak 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como, United captain Fernandes took issue with their tactical approach to the match, particularly their decision to not play with man-to-man pressing.

His comments did not reflect well on under-fire head coach Carrick, who explained that when they half-pressed man-to-man during the second half, they conceded.

Carrick also appeared to dig out Fernandes and his commitment on the pitch as he added: "If you don't run, you don't run forward, you don't run back, you aren’t going to win."

Reacting to Fernandes' comments on talkSPORT Breakfast, Gabby Agbonlahor called for the 32-year-old to be dropped when they face Bournemouth at home in the Premier League this weekend.

However, despite having a reputation of being a fierce, no-nonsense manager, former Sheffield United and Crystal Palace boss Warnock thinks Carrick should take a more measured approach to the match.

Carrick must start Fernandes vs Bournemouth

"When things go wrong in a dressing room, players never look in the mirror, they always blame something else," he explained. "Whether it's the pitch, the ball, it used to be the boots and everything else, now it's the manager.

"I just thought it was a disgrace. Fernandes, about a year ago when he started waving his arms, I hated him from a manager's point of view. In fairness, he started playing and looked their best player, I thought, 'He's their best chance'.

"I understand what Gabby's saying about playing the kids, but you can't play the kids on Sunday, and you can't leave Fernandes out.

"He's going to have to have a chat with him and, however much he hates doing it, he'll play Fernandes on Sunday.

"He'll say, 'Come on, we're at home, get back to your way'."

4 Carrick, who currently faces the sack at United, has been told to drop his captain from his starting XI this weekend Credit: Getty

4 However, Warnock has stressed that he cannot drop Fernandes from the team despite his comments Credit: talkSPORT

Warnock then recalled last week's post-match rant from Lisandro Martinez after defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, during which he called out the United board.

"Martinez coming out like that, they're not bothered!" Warnock said. "They've got a club lined up, or they're going to go somewhere else. They're not bothered about the manager, I felt sorry for him (Carrick) last night."

Agbonlahor asked Warnock if he would be able to contain his anger if he was the United manager and heard what Fernandes said in his post-match interview.

"You're going to speak to him but, I'm not being funny, I think if you're captain is onside with you, he wouldn't even think about saying what he said," Warnock responded.

What next for Carrick?

talkSPORT understands that Carrick is still set to hold his pre-match press conference on Friday before the visit of Bournemouth and should be in charge of the team for Sunday's game.

However, United have taken steps to plan for a possible replacement, with former Germany and Bayern Munich boss Julian Nagelsmann being sounded out.

4 Warnock is also worried for Carrick and his future at United, and believes he would be better off with more experience around him Credit: AFP

Meanwhile, Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler has admirers at Old Trafford but would not be interested in taking the job, with Antonio Conte, Eddie Howe, Simone Inzaghi and Cesc Fabregas other options.

"I can't see a way out now for Michael," Warnock said. "I wish I could have worked with Michael.

"He's a lovely lad and he knows what he's doing. I think he just needs a bit of experience there with him as well."

Warnock added: "He's not going to walk away, but the guys at the top... it's almost like he wants to be relieved of his duties, really, he'll be pulling his hair out now.

"When people like Martinez and Fernandes have a go at the tactics, then he knows his time is limited.

"Unfortunately for managers, it's the easy way out, you're not going to get rid of the players."

Sports.title: Jason Cundy makes Man City comparison in explosive rant at Man United
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy has labelled Manchester United a 'car crash of a club', claiming they've swapped places with Manchester City.

His explosive outburst came after Man United fell to a chastening 4-1 Champions League defeat to competition newcomers Como on Wednesday.

2 Man United have lost their last two Champions League games and four of their last seven matches in all competitions Credit: Getty

What did Cundy say about Man United?

Alongside Jamie O'Hara on talkSPORT's Sports Bar, Cundy didn't hold back in his assessment of the current state of United.

"Honestly, watching Man United earlier: wowzers," exclaimed the former Chelsea and Tottenham defender. "What a car crash that club is.

"The thing is with Man United, they're going down the motorway, there's no brakes, and they keep hitting cars.

"Somehow, they're trundling on, and we know how this is going to end: they're going to hit a truck.

"And Carrick is still at the wheel. No brakes.

"For me, this is definitive: Manchester City have swapped places with Man United."

Cundy went on to accuse United of embarrassing English football.

"Man United are disgracing the Premier League in Europe and they're disgracing Manchester," he continued "They are an absolute disgrace."

Discussing Michael Carrick's future amid mounting pressure on the head coach, Cundy said: "He's not the solution, but he's not the problem. I don't know what the solution is.

"You go back to the 90s when Manchester United were the club - not just in England but in Europe, they were one of the best clubs if not the best club for years.

2 Appointed mid-season, Carrick steadied the ship and steered United to third in the Premier League last term, but they've managed a solitary league win so far this time around Credit: Getty

"Manchester City were hanging around, dwindling around mid-table.

"Now, Manchester United have turned into City and City have turned into Man United. That's what's happened. They have literally swapped seats."

Yet another setback for Carrick's United

United fell into further turmoil on Wednesday night as captain Bruno Fernandes hit out at Carrick's tactics post-match.

Fernandes had been hauled off after 66 minutes with United 3-0 down in Italy.

His rant came barely a week after teammate Lisandro Martinez had taken aim at the board for not assembling a squad good enough for the Champions League.

Carrick's days certainly appear to be numbered at Old Trafford, with United winless in seven games heading into Sunday's home Premier League clash against Bournemouth.

talkSPORT understands that former Bayern Munich and Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann is in the frame to take over should Carrick be sacked but that Fabian Hurzeler, currently doing a stellar job at Brighton, would not be interested in the job.

Sports.title: How to follow Manchester United vs Bournemouth on talkSPORT plus team news as Michael Carrick hangs onto job
Sports.content:
How to follow Manchester United vs Bournemouth on talkSPORT plus team news as Michael Carrick hangs onto job

Michael Carrick will be on the touchline for Manchester United this Sunday as his struggling side take on Bournemouth.

Carrick is under huge pressure at Old Trafford but has managed to keep his job heading into the weekend's action.

4 Carrick had to apologise to the Man United fans after another defeat in midweek, but he has managed to keep his job for now Credit: AFP

Man United lost 4-1 to Como on Wednesday on an embarrassing Champions League night that compounded their misery.

The defeat meant that the Red Devils have gone seven matches without a win for the first time in 11 years.

Their horrendous form means Carrick's side are 13th in the Premier League and 20th in the Champions League table.

Carrick apologised to the fans after losing to Como, but his future is hugely up in the air, with ex-Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann sounded out for the job should it become available.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler is also admired by Man United, but talkSPORT understands he would not be interested.

As things stand though, Carrick is going to remain in his post, and he'll be in the Old Trafford dugout on Sunday.

United host Bournemouth in a game they simply must win.

The Cherries won their first game of the season last time out after going six games without a victory to start the campaign.

4 Fernandes criticised Carrick's tactics in his post-match interview after Man United lost yet another game Credit: Getty

Man United vs Bournemouth: What has been said?

Bruno Fernandes ripped into United's tactics after being thrashed by Cesc Fabregas' Como on Wednesday.

In a bombshell interview, he said: "It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence."

When pressed on whether he was insinuated Carrick got his tactics wrong, he replied: "That's on the manager and staff to see, not me.

"Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.

"As you saw with them [Como], the centre-back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to.

"A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide."

Sports.title: Unai Emery to Man United now off the table as Aston Villa boss U-turns over future plans
Sports.content:
Unai Emery to Man United now off the table as Aston Villa boss U-turns over future plans

Unai Emery is capable of succeeding at Manchester United, but Aston Villa remains the perfect fit for him.

That's according to Guillem Balague who revealed to talkSPORT that, despite contemplating a summer exit, the Spaniard is excited for the future at Villa Park.

4 Emery has been eyed by the United hierarchy as they make initial steps to possibly make a new appointment in the dugout Credit: Getty

United are seemingly preparing for life without head coach Michael Carrick after a dismal 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League.

Julian Nagelsmann has been sounded out as a possible replacement, whilst talkSPORT exclusively reported earlier on Thursday that Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler would not be interested in the job.

Emery, who won the Europa League with Villa last season, was part of the recruitment process at United in the summer before they gave Carrick the permanent role.

However, it's understood he would need convincing to leave Villa, as Spanish journalist Balague detailed why the 54-year-old is more than happy to stay put.

Emery set for Villa stay over United move

When asked on White and Jordan if United would be keen on Emery, he said: "You have to take this question from Unai Emery's point of view. This is my opinion, but basically he is where he wants to be.

"He is where he is appreciated, where he has been given everything that is required, including the co-ownership; the owners (V Sports) now co-own his own little club back in Spain (Real Union).

"He has also been given a huge amount of responsibility to take the team as far as he wants to, and he wants to use that responsibility to take the team as far as he can."

Balague joined the show the day after Villa beat Viking FK 3-1 in the Champions League, which maintained their 100 per cent record.

He took the opportunity to praise the impact of Emery's coaching on his team in what is a stark comparison to the United squad of late.

"They all know what they have to do when they go on the pitch. They had players missing but still, once they came on, even (Tyrone) Mings as a left-back, they knew what they had to do, they can play with their eyes closed.

4 Carrick is under the cosh as United head coach having not won any of their last seven matches across all competitions Credit: Getty

4 Balague is confident that Emery would be a successful replacement for Carrick, but has stressed that he is enjoying life at Villa Credit: taklSPORT

"When you follow PSG (Paris Saint-Germain) closely, when you follow Hansi Flick's Barcelona, when you follow Aston Villa

"then you see a team that just look... the players are looking at each other. It's like, 'What are you doing in training, what are you doing with your time?' Players are not listening, it's really annoying."

"Can he do that job? 100 per cent he can," Balague declared on Emery being a hit at United, months after he appeared to come close to ending his tenure at Villa.

Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Youri Tielemans, Emi Martinez and Ezri Konsa were all key to their 2025/26 Europa League triumph, but were then among numerous sales during the summer transfer window.

Villa signed replacements including Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Zion Suzuki, all of whom have impressed, but at one point, Emery considered whether or not he had done all he could.

Was Emery close to leaving Villa?

"There might come a time that Unai Emery will think he's taken Aston Villa as far as he can," Jim White speculated, and Balague replied: "Oh yeah, it was in the summer.

4 Emery is now in his fifth season at Villa and ended their 30-year trophy wait by winning the Europa League Credit: Getty

"He was like, 'That's it. Why does Tielemans go? I don't want him to go. Watkins, does he have to go? Morgan Rogers? Yeah, okay, I get that one'."

However, he explained the U-turn in Emery's thinking: "And then he went like, 'Phew, okay, start over'. And now, he's so excited about having these youngsters coming through.

"They will go up and down, and of course they haven't won in the league at home yet. A lot of other things will happen.

"But the target is, 'Can we go (for the) Champions League? Can we do well in Europe?' At the moment, they're second in the table in the Champions League, three wins in three games."

Sports.title: How to follow Arsenal vs Everton on talkSPORT plus team news for Premier League clash
Sports.content:
How to follow Arsenal vs Everton on talkSPORT plus team news for Premier League clash

Arsenal will look to continue their pursuit of Manchester City at the top of the Premier League against Everton this Saturday.

The Gunners have only lost one of their first seven games, but that is enough to see the off the pace behind unbeaten City.

3 Arsenal come into their clash with Everton after claiming an impressive draw away at Bayern Munich in the Champions League Credit: Getty

Since being thrashed by Brighton in a surprise result, Mikel Arteta's side have bounced back with two league victories.

They have beaten Leeds and Nottingham Forest, as well as coming out on top against Lille in the Champions League.

And Declan Rice's late equaliser saw them pick up an impressive point away at Harry Kane's Bayern Munich on Wednesday.

Next up for Arsenal are Everton, who have actually only lost one game in the Premier League so far this season, winning twice, with four draws.

David Moyes' men are ninth in the table but were beaten at home by Chelsea last time out heading into this tough trip.

Where to watch Arsenal vs Everton

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy still drinks Red Bulls for breakfast and Kyle Walker has a theory
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy still drinks Red Bulls for breakfast and Kyle Walker has a theory

No wonder Jamie Vardy is still lightning fast at 39 years old given he drinks cans of Red Bull for breakfast.

It might not be seen as the best preparation for a modern athlete, but as the saying goes: if ain't broke, don't fix it.



4 Vardy is now at Burnley where he plays alongside Walker and still loves a Red Bull and still drinks it before playing Credit: Getty

Burnley defender Kyle Walker, in his role as talkSPORT Drive host, revealed the secrets to his teammate's success.

"He drinks them... I think it's three or two, even before breakfast, it's ridiculous!

"That's his breakfast, I think, two Red Bulls."

Asked if the striker also swigs them at half-time by his co-host, Andy Goldstein, Walker replied: “He’s constantly got a Red Bull in his hand. It’s ridiculous, it can’t be good for you!



“He’s got to have some sort of deal,” he joked.

“I said, ‘Do you never get comedowns?’ He said, ‘The only one that I did was off a Monster’.

“He used to drink Monsters and then he got a comedown, so he said, ‘I don’t drink them anymore, just Red Bull’.”



Has Vardy always enjoyed a Red Bull?

Vardy, the Leicester City legend who scored 145 Premier League goals and won the 2015/16 title, is famed for love of the energy drink.

He once revealed that he downs a can within 30 seconds on the morning of a 3pm kick-off.



On the day he scored his 100th Premier League goal, Vardy was seen gulping one down moments before coming on as a substitute.

4 Even at the height of his Premier League fame, Vardy was seen guzzling Red Bull before playing Credit: Twitter

4 Walker joked that Vardy can always be seen with a can of Red Bull, but is shocked by just how much he drinks Credit: talkSPORT

4 It has never hindered him and Vardy remains one of the Premier League's great goal scorers Credit: Getty



Now at Championship side Burnley, Vardy is never too far away from a Red Bull as he recently had a can to hand during a pre-match walk.

And whilst many would consider the drink to not fit in with a healthy lifestyle that most footballers stick by, it's something he seems to use for an extra yard of pace on the pitch.

Vardy joined talkSPORT in June and proposed the idea of posing with the drink if he was to ever be given the ultimate honour outside Leicester's King Power Stadium.

"The Red Bull in hand probably would make a good little statue," he said, whilst acknowledging a variety of celebrations that could also make the cut.

Sports.title: Wrexham’s Phil Parkinson automatically becomes third longest-serving manager in English football as EFL boss sacked
Sports.content:
Wrexham’s Phil Parkinson automatically becomes third longest-serving manager in English football as EFL boss sacked

Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson has jumped to third place on the list of English football's longest-serving managers.

It comes after Bromley announced the sacking of Andy Woodman, who had been in charge of the south London club for five-and-a-half years.



2 Andy Woodman was sacked by Bromley despite leading them to League One for the first time in their history Credit: Getty

Who are the longest-serving managers in English football?

Parkinson is now one of only four managers across the Premier League and EFL who have been in their job for five years or more.

Arsenal's title-winning boss Mikel Arteta tops the list having held the reins at the Emirates Stadium since December 2019.

League One Mansfield Town's Nigel Clough has been in post 237 days longer than Parkinson at Wrexham.



League Two Barnet's Dean Brennan is the other current manager in the top four divisions to have passed the five-year mark.

Like Brennan with Barnet, Parkinson guided Wrexham back to the EFL, winning the 2022/23 National League title.



He followed that up with two more promotions as the Red Dragons became the first side ever in the top five tiers to go up three seasons running.

Parkinson currently has Wrexham sitting 14th in the Championship after narrowly missing out on the play-offs last term.



The 58-year-old had been under pressure amid a rocky start to the new campaign, but he responded by overseeing a 4-1 thrashing of Preston at the weekend.

At the other end of the spectrum, seven managers in the 92 are less than 100 days into their tenure.

Michael Duff was the most recent new appointment, taking over at League One Bradford City after Graham Alexander left to become manager of Preston.

Longest serving managers in English football Mikel Arteta (Arsenal) - 6 years, 303 days Nigel Clough (Mansfield) - 5 years, 349 days Phil Parkinson (Wrexham) - 5 years, 112 days Dean Brennan (Barnet) - 5 years, 31 days Paul Cook (Chesterfield) - 4 years, 253 days Richie Wellens (Leyton Orient) - 4 years, 226 days Johnnie Jackson (AFC Wimbledon) - 4 years, 158 days Unai Emery (Aston Villa) - 3 years, 354 days Lee Bell (Crewe) - 3 years, 351 days John Mousinho (Portsmouth) - 3 years, 274 days

2 Michael Duff was the first manager in England's top four divisions to be sacked this season Credit: Getty



Duff's new job came shortly after he was sacked by fellow League One outfit Wycombe Wanderers, who subsequently made 36-year-old Tom Hounsell the fourth-youngest boss in the EFL.

Sacking season underway

Two months into the 2026/27 campaign, sacking season is in full swing.

In addition to Alexander leaving of his own volition, four managers have been dismissed this term.

Woodman is the second in as many days to lose their job after Crawley Town dispensed with the services of Colin Kazim-Richards with the team rock-bottom of League Two.



Former Leeds and Sheffield United boss Kevin Blackwell has since been placed in interim charge.

Bromley, meanwhile, will be led by former captain Byron Webster as they begin the search for Woodman's successor.

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold would have to join a different club from Liverpool to seal Premier League return
Sports.content:
Trent Alexander-Arnold would have to join a different club from Liverpool to seal Premier League return

Trent Alexander-Arnold could return to the Premier League but not by returning to Liverpool.

That's the view of Alexander-Arnold's former England teammate Kyle Walker.



2 Alexander-Arnold has had to get used to warming the Real Madrid bench of late Credit: Getty

What did Walker say about Trent?

Walker co-hosted Wednesday's talkSPORT Drive alongside Andy Goldstein and discussed the right-back's potential destinations amid reports he is considering his Real Madrid future, having endured a somewhat tough time since joining the Spanish giants last year.

"I think everyone knows how I feel about Trent," said Walker. "I think he's an unbelievable player.

"He's probably been unlucky that there was me and Tripps [Kieran Trippier] that were probably more established right-backs in the England set-up.



"Now all of a sudden, he's got Reece James, Tino [Livramento] and Djed [Spence], which is tough competition, but you don't go and play for Real Madrid if you're not a good player."

Asked if he was surprised by Alexander-Arnold's relative lack of game-time at Madrid – he's made only 17 LaLiga starts since the beginning of last season – Walker added: "I am surprised, but I'm not surprised.



"I feel that the way Trent played for Liverpool was very special. I feel some of the things that he did, being a boy of club, loving the club as much as he did and having Mo Salah in front of you helps an enormous amount.

"I played with Riyad [Mahrez at Manchester City]. I probably wouldn't be the player that I am today if Riyad wasn't as good as he was."



Walker, who now plays for Championship side Burnley, also seemed keen to see Alexander-Arnold back in the Premier League.

"Why not?" he continued. "Can he go back to Liverpool with the way that he left [Liverpool fans didn't take kindly to Alexander-Arnold's departure just before his contract expired]? I'm not too sure.

"Do I see him at another club? He's got to go to one of the big ones: Manchester United, Man City."

2 Trent was recalled to the England squad by Thomas Tuchel for the recent internationals, but he'll need regular club football to keep his place Credit: Getty



However, Walker immediately admitted he couldn't see Alexander-Arnold joining Man United, such fierce rivals of Liverpool.

Few players have ever represented both clubs, with Michael Owen the most recent to do so.

Trent's latest Madrid struggles

For now, Alexander-Arnold still has five years left to run on his contract at the Bernabeu.

But he has fallen out of favour with returning head coach Jose Mourinho in recent weeks.



The 28-year-old has been an unused substitute for each of Madrid's last three games, with Fede Valverde – a midfielder by trade – preferred at right-back in each of the last two matches.

And with Netherlands international Denzel Dumfries also joining the club in the summer, Alexander-Arnold could have his work cut out to reclaim his place.

Sports.title: Man United's civil war spills over into the boardroom with chiefs SPLIT over Michael Carrick's replacement: Insiders fear club are 'wasting too much time' as under-fire boss clings on to his job for Bournemouth game
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s problems are piling up with there understood to be growing tensions between director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell. Speaking to a handful of key figures close to the dressing room, each of whom are in regular dialogue with the United hierarchy, Daily Mail Sport has learned that along with disagreements on the pitch between players and manager, there is also growing discontent in the boardroom. Wilcox and Vivell are said to have differing opinions on who should succeed Michael Carrick, should the decision be made to move on to a third manager in 2026. There is some sympathy in the United hierarchy for the position Carrick is in, with nine senior absentees for the Como trip. They too are having to face up to the reality that not enough was done in the summer to strengthen this team to play multiple games a week. Results - which includes just two wins from 11 - are getting worse at an alarming rate and all is not well behind the scenes. Carrick will take charge of United for Sunday’s home match against Bournemouth but potential successors have already been sounded out privately. Michael Carrick is expected to stay in charge of Man United for their match with Bournemouth Director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell are said to have differing opinions on who should succeed Carrick if the decision is made to move him on Vivell is understood to be pushing hard for Julian Nagelsmann to be the leading candidate, with the 39-year-old out of work following a disastrous World Cup in charge of Germany. Chelsea assessed Nagelsmann as a potential manager when Vivell was technical director in west London and his admiration remains. But sources have suggested that Wilcox, who is Vivell’s boss in the chain of command, prefers a Premier League proven manager, with Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery and Antonio Conte, who have all come up on a shortlist, a tick in that category. Hurzeler does not have a release clause in his Brighton contract and so would require enormous compensation. There is well-placed scepticism as to whether any move would even be remotely possible, regardless of how well liked he is inside Old Trafford. Carrick will face the music when he addresses the media on Friday in his pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday’s game against Bournemouth in which he’ll have to address doubts creeping in from players, tensions upstairs among execs and whether he will be able to keep hold of his job. United are refusing to press the panic button and sack Carrick who is now expected to stay in charge for Sunday’s game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at least. United then face Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa before a two-week international break next month. Vivell is understood to be pushing hard for Julian Nagelsmann to be the leading candidate, with the 39-year-old out of work following a disastrous World Cup in charge of Germany Sources have suggested that Wilcox prefers a Premier League proven manager, with Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery and Antonio Conte a tick in that category The fact that Carrick will speak to the media again, less than two days after he tried to explain his team’s shocking performance in the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium, is the strongest signal yet that United are aiming to stand by Carrick for the time being. In-fighting at United is rife right now, not least after captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned the tactics of his manager after the abject 4-1 defeat at the hands of Como. ‘It needs to start at the top,’ one source close to a first team player said. ‘Recruitment guys, manager, the lot need to go.’ Another source said: ‘This needs a strong board to make hard decisions fast. They’ve already wasted too much time.’ United have stressed that Vivell and Wilcox maintain a healthy relationship even in such trying circumstances, but many close to the dressing room are telling a different story. ‘At this club, there’s too much focus on what’s been done in the past, but we’re not those people anymore,’ Fernandes told Sky Italia after the Como defeat. ‘The club and the players need to understand that. Unfortunately for us - especially when it comes to the players - those who join expect to win trophies, win games, and reach the highest level, but unfortunately that's been very difficult at this club in recent years. That's the situation.’
