Sports.title: 'My wife wants to know!': Nervous Harry Kane opens up on Ballon d'Or uncertainty as bookmakers' favourite reveals he has been kept in the dark over award outcome
Sports.content:
'My wife wants to know!': Nervous Harry Kane opens up on Ballon d'Or uncertainty as bookmakers' favourite reveals he has been kept in the dark over award outcome

Harry Kane has opened up on his Ballon d'Or nerves with the England captain insisting he has been kept in the dark as to the outcome of Monday's awards do in London.

The Englishman scored an incredible 61 goals in 51 matches across all competitions last season for German champions Bayern Munich. Bayern also won two domestic cups and reached the Champions League semi-final, losing out to eventual winners, Paris Saint-Germain.

Kane would become the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen, in 2001, if he is crowned the winner on Monday night. However, it is a close race this year with Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe also in contention.

Yamal played a key role in Spain's World Cup success in the United States, and helped Barcelona win LaLiga and the Spanish Super Cup, with 48 goal involvements across all competitions in 58 appearances.

Kane is the bookmakers' favourite to be crowned the world's best on Monday night but the Englishman insists he does not know the outcome of the London Palladium bash.

'They want everyone to go, all the big names there and there will be more people watching it if they don't know, so I can understand why,' he said.

Harry Kane has reiterated he remains in the dark if he has won this year's Ballon d'Or or not

Wife Kate is finding the wait 'stressful' too, according to the Bayern Munich and England star

'From my point of view, of course, I'd love to know to just kind of see and not have to wait throughout the whole night. But it is their decision, I can't control that. We'll have to just enjoy it and try not to stress out too much.

'I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to. There are always rumours flying around and you try to stay away from it.

'Of course I am going to try and enjoy Monday night as much as possible. It is a big occasion so we will have to wait and see.'

Kane added that his wife and family are also finding the agonising wait 'stressful'.

'I think my wife would prefer to know and my family… it's very stressful for everyone.'

Kane was speaking following his goal and assist in Bayern's 2-2 draw with Arsenal on Wednesday night, in the Champions League. He took home the Player of the Match prize following his dazzling display.

The striker insists he is keen to keep his focus on his match this weekend, saying: 'I know we have another important one on Sunday before the event on Monday so that's where my focus is.'

Bayern sit top of the Bundesliga and play Freiburg this weekend.

Sports.title: 'It's a combination of everything!': Youri Tielemans accuses Man United dressing room of lacking effort - as ANOTHER damning Bruno Fernandes interview emerges about living 'in the past' after Como humbling
Sports.content:
'It's a combination of everything!': Youri Tielemans accuses Man United dressing room of lacking effort - as ANOTHER damning Bruno Fernandes interview emerges about living 'in the past' after Como humbling

Youri Tielemans has made the shock admission that there is a lack of effort within the Manchester United dressing room, among other issues, as the fallout of their humbling at Como continues.

Manchester United's winless run in all competitions stretches to seven games now after a thumping 4-1 defeat by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday evening.

The Red Devils started both halves terribly, conceding after two minutes and 49 minutes. This follows last week's 2-0 Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid where they fell behind after just 53 seconds.

Reflecting on United's form, Tielemans conceded post-match on Wednesday that there is worryingly a lack of effort among the squad.

'It's a combination of everything: tactical, technical, effort. We need to try do better at everything,' he told TNT Sports.

That remark came after the Belgium midfielder admitted that he and his team-mates had been outplayed by Como.

"Tonight we were poor at everything."



Youri Tielemans apologises to the Man Utd fans following their heavy defeat at the hands of Como 💬



🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/WxlLLb7vde — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026

Youri Tielemans has admitted that there is a lack of effort within the Man United dressing room

United extended their winless run to seven matches after a 4-1 defeat at Como on Wednesday

'There was a lot said at half-time to try and get back into the game, which didn't happen,' he said of their 1-0 half-time deficit.

'We conceded straight away after half-time, and then you try to do something, and we get outplayed. We got outplayed for most of the game, so it was a very disappointing night.'

The 29-year-old's self-reflection didn't end there. Asked why United were so poor, he said: 'It's everything. You can be good tactically but if the effort isn't there, or the other way round, you have to be good at everything, but tonight we were poor at everything.

'It's the same message as we've had the last few weeks. We can be here and talk about it, but we have to show it on the pitch. We can only apologise to the fans who travelled, the fans who watched us from home and support us. They're disappointed and we're disappointed.

'The only thing we can do is try to show something on the pitch, which we haven't done over the last few weeks.'

This is the second week in a row that Tielemans has fronted up to the media. After Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy for a lack of investment in the summer after losing to Atletico, that question was posed to Tielemans who was one of those summer acquisitions.

The 29-year-old, who joined from Aston Villa for £35million, declined to comment about that outburst.

Carrick's tactics were also questioned by captain Bruno Fernandes in the wake of the defeat by Como.

He said: 'It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.'

Asked if he meant that Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: 'That's on the manager and staff to say, not me.'

When Carrick was told about Fernandes' comments, the United boss gave a pointed response by suggesting that his players weren't willing to run enough.

Bruno Fernandes questioned Michael Carrick's tactics following their 4-1 defeat by Como

Pressure is mounting Man United Michael Carrick head coach after a string of bad results

Fernandes also gave further damning comments in an interview with Italian media post-match.

The Portuguese midfielder, who played in Italy during the early stages of his career, suggested Man United have been living 'in the past'.

'Everyone at the club needs to understand that things aren't the same anymore; we're not in the past, and we have to look to the future,' Fernandes told Sky Sport Italia.

'We have to create something different in the present. At this club, there's too much focus on what's been done in the past, but we're not those people anymore.

'The club and the players need to understand that.

'Unfortunately for us - especially when it comes to the players - those who join expect to win trophies, win games, and reach the highest level, but unfortunately, that's been very difficult at this club in recent years.

'That's the situation.'

Sky Sport Italia's pitchside reporter Pierluigi Bagnulo claimed Man United's press officer had not wanted Fernandes to speak Italian post-match amid fears they 'wouldn't understand his words'.

Tielemans, Fernandes, Carrick and United will look to end their winless run on Sunday afternoon when they host Bournemouth in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Harry Brook's eye-watering double century against Sri Lanka proved he is now the best all-format batsman in the world - this is how he got there, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Harry Brook's eye-watering double century against Sri Lanka proved he is now the best all-format batsman in the world - this is how he got there, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH

If there were any doubt before this morning’s events in Rawalpindi, there can be none now. Harry Brook is the best all-format batsman in the world, and few bowlers appear to know how to handle him.

On Tuesday, it’s true, he was outfoxed by Pakistan left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas, bowled for five by a delivery that gripped and turned, before defeating him on the back foot. There have been moments this year when Brook has felt like his own worst enemy, apparently heading for a century before doing something daft.

But it’s getting to the stage where – like Minhas – the bowler has to produce something special to keep him quiet. If not, he’s going to cause you a world of pain.

The raw numbers of today’s demolition of Sri Lanka are eye-watering in their own right.

A double-century off 114 balls was the quickest in ODI history, beating by three balls Shubman Gill’s blitz for India against West Indies in Guwahati as recently as three weeks ago. His eventual 202 was the highest ODI score in an England shirt, surpassing Ben Stokes’s 182 against New Zealand at The Oval in 2023. And he helped his side to the highest total in Pakistan, beating Pakistan’s own 375 for three against Zimbabwe at Lahore in 2015.

Brook also became only the second player, after West Indies’ Chris Gayle, to possess a triple-century in Tests, a double-century in ODIs, and a single century in T20s.

Harry Brook walks off after his electrifying 202 against Sri Lanka - the first Englishman ever to score a double century in ODI cricket

What took the innings to another level was its 360-degree nonchalance, the idea that no ball was safe, no area of the ground out of reach

But what took the innings to another level was its 360-degree nonchalance, the idea that no ball was safe, no area of the ground out of reach. When Sri Lanka’s bowlers dropped short, he pulled. When they pitched it up, he either scooped, reverse-scooped or went over extra cover.

The eighth of his 10 sixes, an open-faced slice over backward point off Eshan Malinga, was simply ridiculous. Only the pinpoint yorker had any chance of slowing the carnage, and even then you couldn’t be sure.

As Nasser Hussain put it on Sky Sports: ‘That was an innings touched by genius.’ Kumar Sangakkara spoke of ‘batting Nirvana’. The superlatives are drying up.

Brook is making a case that is hard to answer. In Tests, he averages 53, with a strike rate – 86 – that would once have been considered a triumph in one-day cricket. In T20, he averages a very good 36 with a pulsating strike rate of 164; in February, his 50-ball century against Pakistan in Pallekele was arguably the innings of the World Cup.

And now, in ODIs, he is averaging 41 with a strike rate of almost 110. The sense in all three formats, and especially the longer two, is that there is room for improvement.

Who else can challenge him as the world’s best all-format player? Gill himself is in the argument, though he hasn’t played a T20 for India since last December. Then there’s Australia’s Travis Head, who – while Brook was destroying Sri Lanka – fell for 121 as his side failed to save the second Test against South Africa in Gqeberha, losing by an innings and 31 runs to set up a series decider in Cape Town next week.

Head has played some seismic innings on the biggest stages, including 163 to help beat India in the World Test Championship final at the Oval in 2023, followed by a match-winning 137 to break Indian hearts in the World Cup final at Ahmedabad a few months later. Last winter, he tore England apart in the Ashes.

But not even he can boast Brook’s range of strokes and imagination; nor can he quite convey the same sense that, at any given moment, a perfectly respectable delivery is about to disappear to kingdom come. Head is 33 in December, and may have reached his ceiling. Brook is 27, and seems to be getting better.

Shubman Gill is one of the few players who gets close to Brook, but he hasn’t played a T20 for India since last December

Travis Head has played some phenomenal innings in the last few years (pictured at Perth in the recent Ashes) but he does not have Brook's range of strokes or imagination

So dominant was he this morning that other innings, which might usually have grabbed the headlines, ranked only as sideshows. Tom Banton made a powerful run-a-ball 50 before picking out long-off, Joe Root moved past 8,000 ODI runs during his typically unobtrusive 69 off 66, before Will Jacks – the only England player other than Brook to clear the ropes – chipped in with a superb 66 not out off 30 balls.

None, though, could live with Brook, who didn’t allow himself a proper celebration until he lapped Janith Liyanage fine for four in the last over of the innings to bring up his 200. At the other end, Jacks seemed even more excited.

England’s 50-over cricket has been mainly in the doldrums ever since Eoin Morgan’s side lifted the 2019 World Cup. But, under Brook and Brendon McCullum, they are finding their feet.

Tuesday’s defeat by Pakistan showed they are not there yet. Yet if Brook keeps batting like this, no team will relish facing England in next year’s World Cup.

Sports.title: NATHAN SALT ranks Man United's WORST European defeats - after dreadful Como performance sparked latest civil war and left manager Michael Carrick apologising to supporters
Sports.content:
NATHAN SALT ranks Man United's WORST European defeats - after dreadful Como performance sparked latest civil war and left manager Michael Carrick apologising to supporters

Man United were taught a lesson in the rain in Como, delivering a performance that was every bit the men against boys criticism that will fly their way in wake of their 4-1 defeat.

The most damning aspect for United is that this isn’t a one off. Not a one off this season and not a one off in Europe over the years.

Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Ruben Amorim and many more have been shown up in Europe and now Michael Carrick has added himself to the list of infamous defeats.

Como was among the very worst defeats in United’s European history. Abject, devoid of any creativity, and a performance that was miles below the acceptable levels for a Manchester United player.

Daily Mail Sport’s NATHAN SALT picks out six of the most damning defeats in Europe…

Man United were completely outplayed by Como and were humbled 4-1 by the Italian side

United were awful and it was one of the worst European defeats in their illustrious history

Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 Manchester United (May 21, 2025)

Truly terrible. It was a god-awful season under Ruben Amorim and the Europa League final was the final chance to paper over an enormous crack.

They couldn’t in a final performance that was an insult to those who made the arduous trip to Bilbao.

Struggling to think of a single result that triggered as much disappointment and anger in recent seasons than the Bilbao horror show.

United put in a dreadful display to cap a miserable season in the 2025 Europa League final

Como 4-1 Manchester United (October 21, 2026)

A complete and utter aberration.

There was some effort but it ended with a disastrous lack of quality, individual errors, abysmal weather to boot, and the aftermath saw captain Bruno Fernandes openly call out his manager’s tactics.

One of the all-time disaster classes for United.

The Red Devils' night in Como on Tuesday was an absolute disaster class all round

Lille 1-0 Manchester United (November 2, 2005)

Manchester United were already in crisis by the time they headed to France and Ferguson’s charges left in the absolute depths of it after a shock defeat.

Cristiano Ronaldo and Co had just been hammered by Middlesbrough and then put in this sluggish performance that had fans claiming on national radio that United were ‘no longer a high class team’.

Sir Alex Ferguson looks exasperated during United's 1-0 defeat by Lyon back in 2005

Sporting Lisbon 5-0 Manchester United (March 18, 1964)

George Best, Denis Law and Sir Bobby Charlton… and yet Sir Matt Busby’s side were taught a serious footballing lesson.

They went to Lisbon leading 4-1 lead in this Cup Winners’ Cup quarter-final and somehow blew it in epic circumstances.

Sir Matt Busby's United side somehow blew a 4-1 aggregate lead against Sporting in 1964

Videoton 1-0 Manchester United (March 20, 1985)

Ever heard of Videoton? Not many had, especially not when Manchester United lined up against the Hungarians in 1985.

Ron Atkinson’s side were heavy favourites and yet somehow got humiliated in the UEFA Cup quarter-finals by Videoton.

Real Madrid made the final but United were still reeling from this hall of shame loss.

United produced a dismal defensive display in a defeat by Istanbul Basaksehir back in 2020

Istanbul Basaksehir 2-1 Man United (November 4, 2020)

A match that produced arguably the most embarrassing individual moment in the club’s European history.

Demba Ba ran from the halfway line after United botched defending from their own attacking corner and the defending for the second was hardly much better.

This was the start of one of a series of inquests that haunt this club. Really, really bad.

Sports.title: Revealed: Cesc Fabregas told Como players to TAKE MERCY on battered Man United, leaving the score at just 4-1 instead of going for even more
Sports.content:
Revealed: Cesc Fabregas told Como players to TAKE MERCY on battered Man United, leaving the score at just 4-1 instead of going for even more

Cesc Fabregas revealed that he told his players to ease off Manchester United during their Champions League humiliation at the hands of Como in Italy on Wednesday night.

Como were four goals up against Michael Carrick's side when Fabregas ordered his players to conserve energy ahead of Saturday's Serie A clash with Sassuolo.

United scored a late consolation goal through substitute Joshua Zirkzee, and Fabregas admitted that he was angry at himself for not heaping further embarrassment on his opponents.

'I regret the last 10 minutes because I was the one who told the team to slow down the tempo because there's another match and at 4-0 we could manage things a little,' said the former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder.

'I told the players to stop running and stay in the middle and that is something I regret because I'm the first to always push them to fight until the end. Their goal hurt me because we dropped our intensity and dropped our defensive block, but it was my fault.

'I'm very happy with how the players applied everything we tried to do, not only in terms of quality, which was high, but also the way we were pressing relentlessly until the 85th minute.

Cesc Fabregas and his Como players celebrate beating Man United - but he wasn't happy

Fabregas shakes hands with embattled Man United boss Michael Carrick after the game

'We are trying to create a culture at the club, a style of play and an identity. Tonight was another convincing moment for us.'

Como celebrated the greatest result in the club's history, seven years after they were playing in the fourth tier of Italian football.

'I can't lie to you that it (beating United) wasn't pride,' added Fabregas. 'We know the history of our club, how much they have suffered over the last many years. Obviously, I hope that tomorrow all the boys and girls go to school wearing the Como shirt and feel proud.

'I always tell the lads, enjoy yourselves, fight, do everything to make the best career possible for each one of you, because it goes by quickly.

'They made me enjoy myself tonight, but not so much for the win, for the result, because they played like I like my team to play, with conviction, with quality, with a clear head, with aggressiveness, with a fierce pressing.'

Como's star man was Nico Paz who tormented United with two goals and an assist to hand the Premier League club their heaviest defeat in Europe since losing 4-0 to Barcelona in 1994.

'It has been one of the most beautiful nights of my career,' said Paz. 'I'm still young, but I will never forget it. I used to dream of playing in a match like this, and tonight we've gone even further. It's a historic night for Como fans.'

Sports.title: CHRIS WHEELER: Michael Carrick's Man United are a pale imitation of the club's great sides. They were insipid and lifeless in tame Como surrender. How much longer can they sleepwalk through this wretched season?
Sports.content:
As the full-time whistle blew on one of Manchester United’s most embarrassing nights in Europe, Michael Carrick walked over alone to the few away fans still left at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium and held up his hands in apology. They had stood drenched for two hours, battered by the wind and rain that whipped off Lake Como. This has to be the most picturesque venues in the Champions League by some distance, but on a night like this it was downright ugly and so were United. Carrick’s apology was reminiscent of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s farewell game at Watford in November 2021, which also ended in a humbling 4-1 defeat. Solskjaer knew he was a dead man walking that day. If this proves to be Carrick’s last stand, what a lame surrender it was. How much longer can this go on? How much longer can United sleepwalk through this wretched season as Carrick continues to grasp hopelessly for positives? Statistically the fifth worst European defeat in United’s history was also Carrick’s fifth in 11 games this wretched season as they were torn apart by Como and the excellent Nico Paz. Manchester United were completely outplayed by Como as they lost 4-1 to the Italian side The dreadful result heaps further pressure on under-fire Red Devils boss Michael Carrick This was an incredible night for Como, but one of the worst in United's European history This was meant to be the biggest game in Como’s history and they played like it. Cesc Fabregas’ team are a credit to the former Arsenal midfielder and it’s not by chance that they lie fifth in Serie A. But Manchester United coming to town is no longer what it was. This is a pathetic imitation of the teams that have represented this great club down the years. The 700 fans who made the journey to Lombardy stood in one of the areas of this stadium exposed to the elements beneath Giuseppe Terragni’s Monumento ai Caduti that sits at the head of the lake. It means monument to the fallen, and how much further can United keep falling from here? They were insipid. Lifeless. The confidence and self-belief has been sucked out of this team. It’s eight games since they last won, beating Sabah of Azerbaijan in this competition and recording their only clean sheet of the season. Como 4-1 Man United: MATCH FACTS Como 1907 (4-2-3-1): Butez 6; Couto 7 (Smolcic 80, 6), Ramon 7, Kempf 6, Valle 6; Milla 7, Perrone 8 (Dossena 80, 6); Da Cunha 7, Paz 9 (Ricci 80), Baturina 7 (Caqueret 64, 7); Douvikas 8 Goals: Paz (2, 57), Douvikas (49), Ramon (76) Booked: Kempf Manager: Cesc Fabregas 8 Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Dalot 3, De Ligt 3 (Amass 79, 5), Maguire 4, Mazraoui 3; Mount 3, Santos 4 (Baleba 46, 5); Mbeumo 4 (Lacey 86), Tielemans 4, Cunha 3 (Amad 46, 6); Fernandes 4 (Zirkzee 67, 6) Goal: Zirkzee (90+1) Booked: Santos, Baleba, Lacey Manager: Michael Carrick 3 Referee: Sven Jablonski 6 Shortly after the half hour mark, their supporters broke into a chorus of ‘attack, attack, attack’ which is never a good sign for any United manager. From the chance that fell to Diogo Dalot in the opening seconds to Matheus Cunha’s tame effort on the stroke of half-time, they didn’t have another effort on goal in the first half. Yes, Carrick was without nine senior players, forcing him to put Matthijs De Ligt into the starting line-up without playing a minute of football in the last 325 days due to a back injury, and name Jack Fletcher and Tynan Thompson on the bench even though both players had featured in the UEFA Youth League defeat to Como earlier in the day. But that was no excuse for another performance that left you wondering just what these United players are doing on the training pitch all week – and what Carrick is saying to them. If there was concrete evidence that they simply aren’t learning or progressing, it came after two minutes here. A week after United conceded after 50 seconds to Atletico Madrid in Spain, they were behind again. No sooner had Dalot curled an effort wide after mistakenly creating the opportunity for himself by miscontrolling Cunha’s pass than Paz converted a similar chance at the other end. United had been warned about the gifted Argentine, but you wouldn’t have know it by the way Harry Maguire stood off the 22-year-old when he received a pass from Lucas Da Cunha inside the box. Paz looked up, picked his spot and guided the ball beyond Senne Lammens. He was simply too much for United to handle. Andrey Santos was booked for hacking him down with a crude challenge, Cunha resorted to similar tactics, and Lammens was relieved to see the offside flag go up after fouling Como’s No.10 in the box. Carrick made changes at half-time, sending on Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba for Cunha and Santos so that Bryan Mbeumo could play through the middle. He also asked his full-backs, Dalot and Mazraoui, to switch sides. Argentina wonderkid Nico Paz was Como's star as he scored twice and laid on an assist Paz put his side ahead in under two minutes after United's defence mistakenly stood off him United couldn't match Como's intensity and were insipid and error-ridden, which included Carlos Baleba giving the ball away for their second goal United were awful and Carrick even hooked captain Bruno Fernandes in the second half Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation goal in added time but it was barely acknowledged It’s another sign of the growing crisis around Carrick that it only made things worse as United conceded another early goal. Martin Baturina had gone close twice before half-time, so it was no surprise to see him extend Como’s lead. Paz was the architect this time with a fine pass to Baturina who got away from De Ligt and powered a shot past Lammens. United were three down eight minutes later. Baleba gave the ball away to Paz close to halfway and no United player looked like getting near him as he surged downfield and finished clinically. Carrick’s misery was complete in the 76th minute when Jacobo Ramon got the fourth. It was a measure of the brimming confidence in Fabregas’ side that his centre-back felt able to charge forward in open play and meet a left-wing cross from substitute Kaiki Bruno. No-one had tracked Ramon and he beat Lammens with a thumping header. Carrick sent on teenagers Harry Amass and Shea Lacey which felt like a pathetically response to a pathetic performance, even though Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation from close-range in the 91st minute. The damage was done. As Carrick and his players flew home on Wednesday night, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the United board were left with a decision to make about where they go from here.

Sports.title: Como 4-1 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars fare worst in our most damning ratings EVER after Michael Carrick's side sink to new low?
Sports.content:
Como 4-1 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars fare worst in our most damning ratings EVER after Michael Carrick's side sink to new low?

Things went from bad to worse at Manchester United as their 'fresh start' under Michael Carrick began with a disastrous 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Como.

In the pouring rain, United capitulated under the pressure put on by Cesc Fabregas' young guns and they were behind inside two minutes in what was the start of a very long evening.

Anastasios Douvikas got himself on the scoresheet, teed up by man of the match Nico Paz, who scored twice, before Jacobo Ramon compounded United's misery with a fourth.

By the time Joshua Zirkzee held his run to stay onside to score a consolation in stoppage time, there was barely a flicker of a smile on the faces of anyone wearing United white.

At that stage, United's wounded supporters had long left in their droves, furious at a performance that suggests this United group are only heading in one direction: backwards.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT gives his verdict on a truly hapless Manchester United performance in Italy...

Manchester United have a lot of soul searching to do after a shambolic defeat to Como

Nico Paz ran United ragged with a brace and an assist as United's season gets even worse

Manchester United (4-2-3-1)

Senne Lammens – 4

What is he meant to do when those in front of him are so hopeless? The defence was about as solid as a house of cards in a gentle breeze. Genuinely hopeless and as long as that continues, Lammens is on a hiding to nothing.

Diogo Dalot – 3

Wasted a golden opportunity after a deflection fell at his feet in the box, shooting a whisker wide of the post. That proved costly when Como scored less than a minute later. Works hard and was willing at right back, where he started, and left back, where he went at half time. Some at United feel Dalot is unfairly criticised when the chips are down, but he was miles away from the required quality here.

Matthijs de Ligt – 3

His first United appearance in 325 days and there was so much hope that the Dutchman could pick up where he left off. The positive is that he came through it unscathed. By the time he went off, it was a disastrous night for United and De Ligt was far from blameless after losing sight of Douvikas before stumbling as Como made it 2-0.

Harry Maguire – 4

Made a super last-ditch, sliding challenge to deny a second goal but it all proved in vain. Maguire called out the team for not showing enough bravery away to Leeds and this as a response was disastrous.

He was the best of the back-line but that's not saying much. Looks one of very few who can actually handle the pressure and navigate the storm now.

Harry Maguire called out the bravery of this team after Leeds and it didn't have any impact

Noussair Mazraoui – 3

Ran ragged at both left back, where he started, and at right back, where he played in the second half. It was Mazraoui who was at fault for Leeds' equaliser at the weekend and his press to close out in the lead up to Como's second goal was dreadful. Looked like a rabbit in headlights by the time Kaiki, gifted the freedom of Como by Mazraoui, crossed in for the hosts' fourth.

Mason Mount – 3

Has won this competition and has plenty of experience at the level but looked way short of the necessary quality required as this youthful Como team made him look distinctly average. Constantly came out second best in duels.

Andrey Santos – 4

Found himself completely overrun in the middle of the park – he wasn't alone in that – and was hooked at half-time after a rash slide to bring down Nico Paz brought a yellow card. Never got close to the speed of the game. The fact it was only 1-0 when he went off goes in his favour.

Bryan Mbeumo – 4

Has looked best at centre forward and so, naturally, he was deployed wide off the right, a position he doesn't ever seem to thrive in. Made a couple of smart runs but chances were at a premium and he was marginalised.

Bryan Mbeumo was pushed out on to the right and it massively limited what he is good at

Youri Tielemans – 4

Keeps starting matches but this one was one where it was easy to forget he was playing. Totally anonymous.

Matheus Cunha – 3

Another who was totally anonymous. Had one touch in the Como box, didn't create a single chance, and had just one shot off target before he was hooked at half-time alongside Santos. Been in and out of the side of late and this didn't do anything to improve his odds of more starts.

Bruno Fernandes – 4

Shook his head as he was taken off just after an hour into this one-sided contest but the truth is his performances have been way below the levels he has previously shown he can reach and he could have few complaints at coming off.

This false-nine experiment they have used in the past two games isn't yielding successful results.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 2

Spoke about a 'fresh start' after the draw at Leeds and then saw his side get totally dominated by a quicker, hungrier and better coached team. This was alarming mostly because United never looked remotely threatening, never mind threatening to pull off a positive result.

Michael Carrick is going to be under enormous pressure now as he bids to keep his job

SUBS

Amad (for Matheus Cunha, 46min) – 6

The brightest player in a United shirt. Looked to actually make stuff happen, and it was his ball in to Zirkzee that led to the late consolation.

Carlos Baleba (for Andrey Santos, 46) – 5

Catastrophic error to concede possession to Nico Paz as he broke to score a third. Did at least add some physicality that is severely lacking in this team. United cannot start matches going forward without him.

Joshua Zirkzee (for Bruno Fernandes, 67)

Scored in what was basically the only positive on a sobering night. Ended his drought.

Harry Amass (for Matthijs de Ligt, 79)

Shea Lacey (for Bryan Mbeumo, 86)

Como (4-2-3-1)

Butez 6; Couto 7, Ramon 7, Kempf 6, Valle 6; Milla 7, Perrone 8; Da Cunha 7, Paz 9 (Ricci 80), Baturina 7 (Caqueret 64, 7); Douvikas 8

Goals: Paz (2, 57), Douvikas (49), Ramon (76)

Manager: Cesc Fabregas 8

Sports.title: 'I knew Man Utd were sacking me at half-time before I apologised like Michael Carrick'
Sports.content:
'I knew Man Utd were sacking me at half-time before I apologised like Michael Carrick'

Former Manchester United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer reflected on when he knew his reign was coming to an end

View 2 Images Former Manchester United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer reflected on the end of his reign at the club (Image: Glyn KIRK / AFP via Getty Images)

Ole Gunnar Solskjaer knew his time as Manchester United manager was over at half-time during his final match as boss. While Michael Carrick is expected to remain in charge for United’s next game after their dismal defeat by Como, Solskjaer was aware that his reign was over as the club headed to a 4-1 loss against Watford in November 2021.

‌



‌



The former United striker was in charge of the Red Devils for almost three years. Similar to Carrick, the 53-year-old was initially a temporary fix before being appointed manager permanently.

‌



Last season, Carrick enjoyed success as he guided United to third in the table, but his tenure hit a low on Wednesday with a humbling 4-1 defeat by Como in the Champions League. The United boss has won just two of 11 games so far this term and his side are winless in seven.

‌



The 45-year-old apologetically raised his hands to travelling United supporters after full-time in Como. Despite the defeat, Carrick is set to take charge against Bournemouth on Sunday. However, Solskjaer knew he would not be given a similar reprieve after seeing his side fall short for the first 45 minutes against Watford in 2021, with United 2-0 down at the interval.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“Nobody told me, but I knew at half-time against Watford,” United icon Solskjaer recalled to The Athletic in 2023. “We didn’t look like a Man United team; the players weren’t running for each other.

“At half-time, I told the players it was probably going to be the last time we worked together and to play with pride. We almost turned it around, until Harry Maguire got sent off.”

‌



In the immediate aftermath, Solskjaer was quick to apologise to United supporters for his team’s display. "I feel for the fans. I feel the same as the fans,” he said at the time. “We’re embarrassed losing the way we do. We are in a very bad run and bad situation. But that is part of football.

“I know they will support the team and the players on the pitch every single day. Sometimes you have to say sorry and that was a sorry for the performance.”

‌



View 2 Images United boss Michael Carrick worked alongside Solskjaer during his tenure (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

Solskjaer was sacked by United the day after his team’s 4-1 defeat at Vicarage Road. Carrick, who was part of the Norwegian’s coaching staff throughout his reign, sent a similar message to supporters as he reeled from the loss to Como.

‌



“I have to apologise to the supporters,” Carrick said. “I went over to the end and I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more, with the position that I'm in and what I value this football club. For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. It wasn't a good performance at all.”

The United boss added: “We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure.”

Article continues below

Carrick will hope his side can produce a positive response against Bournemouth as his job comes under increasing scrutiny. United will aim to end their winless run on Sunday, with the club preparing to host the Cherries at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Meet the double Winter Olympic champion in BBC SPOTY battle with Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Meet the double Winter Olympic champion in BBC SPOTY battle with Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham

Team GB hero Matt Weston has opened up about his journey from almost quitting sport to finding himself a front runner for BBC Sports Personality of the Year after winning two gold medals at the Winter Olympics

View 5 Images Winter Olympics star Matt Weston is eyeing up the Sports Personality of the Year (Image: Getty Images)

Matt Weston has admitted it would be "insane" if he became the first Winter Olympian in more than 40 years to win the BBC Sports Personality of the Year.

‌



‌



Weston, 29, is the fourth favourite with the bookmakers to pick up the SPOTY prize after winning two gold medals at the 2026 Milano Cortina Games back in February.

‌



The Surrey-born superstar won both the individual and mixed team skeleton events, becoming only the second Team GB athlete to secure two Winter Olympic gold medals, after Lizzy Yarnold.

‌



He set four course records as he raced to his individual victory, finishing 0.88 seconds ahead of Germany's Axel Jungk. Realising his Olympic dream was an emotional and unforgettable moment, but there was more to come.

Just two days later, Weston celebrated alongside Tabitha Stoecker after clinching mixed team gold in thrilling fashion, running a final time of 1:59:36, 0.17 seconds ahead of Germany's Susanne Kreher and Jungk, and setting a new track record in the process.

It wrapped up a historic and record-breaking Winter Olympic Games for Weston and his achievements have not gone unnoticed. Indeed, as well as being given the freedom of his hometown, Crowborough, and an honorary doctor degree at the University of Kent, he is among the frontrunners to win the most prestigious honour in British sport.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Weston is, at the time of writing, priced at 11/1 with bet365 to claim the SPOTY award in December, with only Amy Hunt (5/6), Josh Kerr (10/3) and Harry Kane (7/2) ahead of him. Jude Bellingham (14/1) and Saffie Osborne (33/1) complete the top six.

‌



View 5 Images Matt Weston posing with his first gold medal at the Milano Cortina Games (Image: Getty Images)

Speaking to The Mirror about the potential of winning SPOTY, Weston said: "I think the honour for me, like you said at the start, there has been so many pinch me moments and so many people that I've met and situations that I've been in that I never thought would be possible.

‌



"I do a sport where we don't get much publicity. When you compare us to footballers and things like that, we're like the 0.1 per cent of the publicity and the time and effort that, well, the viewership that they get. And the fact that my name is up there with some huge athletics and football names, like I'm next to Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham! Just to have my name on these lists that are going out there at the moment, that's an honour in itself for me. I'm really happy with that.

"The thought of winning it? I don't know, I don't know. It would be insane. I've already had some amazing responses from the British public and the support that they have given me. I feel very honoured to be a part of that and feel very grateful. And the fact that there's a chance that the British public could do that for me as well would be honestly insane.

‌



"I'm struggling to find the words, really, of how much that would mean to me. It would mean a lot for not just myself, but my family, my friends, the team as well. The recognition would be me going up there, but actually what it would mean for my teammates, for the coaching staff, for the support staff, for everyone who's been a part of my journey getting me to this point. I think it would mean a lot to be honest."

If Weston came out on top, he would become the first Winter Olympian to win SPOTY since ice dancers Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean, following their iconic gold-winning performance at the Sarajevo Games in 1984.

‌



While he does feel he has the support from the British public heading into SPOTY, he believes the timing of winning the gold medals won't do him "any favours".

View 5 Images Matt Weston celebrates winning gold at the Milano Cortina Games (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I think I do a very unique sport and it was a very unique situation what happened at the Olympics and the response from the public was absolutely crazy," Weston said. "I think I am kind of in a bit of a strong point with that.

"I think the only thing that doesn't do me any favours is that the Olympics was in February and Sports Personality of the Year is in December. So I'm almost as far away as you can be from Sports Personality of the Year, from my achievements.

‌



"But the fact that my name is still up there, I think kind of shocks me sometimes at how much of an impact that might have had on the British public as well as myself. So I think we're in a good position, but like all these things, I never want to believe anything until I'm actually there experiencing it. So I'm keeping my fingers crossed and I'm just saying yes to everything and revelling in kind of what's unfolding in front of me."

Weston's double-gold medal haul in Milano Cortina was even more remarkable when just four years before, he finished 15th in the individual skeleton event at the Beijing Winter Olympics and thought about quitting the sport.

‌



But Weston bounced back to win gold at the World Championships in 2023 and 2025, as well as gold at the European Championships in 2023, giving him huge motivation and confidence to come out on top at the Winter Olympics.

"When I first came back from Beijing, I almost wanted to quit the sport," the two-time world champion added. "It was pretty gutting for me. It was really disappointing. I felt like I'd let myself down, the country down, family, team, all that sort of thing.

‌



View 5 Images Matt Weston's Milano Cortina Games was an iconic one (Image: Getty Images)

"It was, yeah, you kind of want to go to the Games and you want it to be this amazing kind of fairy tale of an experience, which kind of, in a way, it was. I actually loved my time at the Beijing Olympics, just apart from the racing side of things, which is almost the most important part.

‌



"But after I'd given myself some time to kind of decompress and accept what had happened, I kind of used that disappointment and turned it into like a fire to like go, 'this isn't the end of my Olympic journey, this isn't the end of my story within skeleton' that I want to make.

"I want to make something better of it, and I used that as kind of like a fire to give me the motivation and dedication to be able to go out there and make sure that this wasn't going to happen again and that I was going to leave no stone unturned on the way to Milano Cortina."

‌



After suffering disappointment in Beijing and a string of long-term injuries, Weston sought help from a psychologist. He had been struggling with his mental health and wanted to ensure his head was in the "right place to go and perform".

Weston admitted: "I mean, the team, there's certain members of the team that were really there for me, as well as I think in the past few years I've worked with psychologists as well. I've worked with two currently. One's a sports psych and one's a clinical psych. And when I first started working with them, especially like we worked as a team, like a three-way conversation where me as an athlete and me as a person are almost like two different people.

‌



"So we need to have the whole complete package in the best place to be able to go out and perform. It's not just focusing just on sport, it's about life as well, because that can creep into your performance. So we've worked a lot.

"It's been a pretty tough journey to get to this point, but I think a lot of my success and a lot of the consistency which I've had is a result of working with the psychologists and making sure my head is in the right place to go out there and perform. And I think that that made a big difference going into this Games, because there was obviously a lot of pressure on my shoulders going in. I've been world number one for the past three years, so I was able to handle that really well because of the work I've put in with the psychologists."

‌



Back in March, fresh after winning in Milano Cortina, Weston admitted he hasn't thought about whether he will aim for Team GB's outright gold medal record at the 2030 French Alps Games. He is level on two with retired skeleton star Yarnold, who was victorious at Sochi 2014 and PyeongChang 2018.

View 5 Images Matt Weston with Lizzy Yarnold (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But now, Weston has revealed that he does "like the idea" of becoming Team GB’s outright most successful Winter Olympian and has "thought about" it.

"A bit of both, to be honest," Weston continued, when asked if he has thought about the record going into the 2030 Games. "Obviously that's come into my mind, but my main priority this year has been enjoying it. I've put nine years of dedication, hard work and sacrifice into this. So I've missed weddings, funerals, birthdays, and so much important family time. I've really tried to, as much as I can, catch up with that and enjoy the kind of reward from winning the Olympics, which is still really weird for me to say.

‌



"But I have had a thought about, like at the moment, obviously in terms of medal tally, I'm tied with Lizzie Arnold for the overall most successful British Winter Olympian ever, which is, there's a lot of things that I'm saying that are still very crazy for me to say. That kind of doesn't feel real, but there is a lot of temptation for me to go out there and be like, well, actually, like, I quite like winning.

"So I quite like the idea of being Britain's outright most successful [Winter Olympian]. So that is something that definitely is playing on my mind, but at the moment I'm kind of focusing on getting my body fixed, as well as spending time with family, friends and my new wife as well."

Article continues below

While getting married his wife Alex, Weston has spent the last couple of months on the treatment table, having had surgeries on his shoulder and his hip. But, after recovering, he is now focused on the winter season and getting back to competing following his heroics in Milano Cortina.

Sports.title: Diogo Jota's wife recalls heartbreaking moment she learned of Liverpool star's death
Sports.content:
It was just 11 days after Diogo Jota married his childhood sweetheart, Rute Cardoso, that tragedy struck. The Liverpool forward was driving alongside his brother, Andre Silva, to board a ferry that would take him back to the UK for pre-season training after enjoying the summer of his life.

Jota, 28, had lifted the Premier League title at Anfield and the Nations League with Portugal before marrying Rute at a ceremony in Porto, close to where the couple met as teenagers at high school. The ex-Wolves star opted to return to the UK via ferry, having been advised against flying after undergoing minor lung surgery.

Jota and Silva, also a professional footballer, were killed on July 3, 2025 when their hired Lamborghini crashed on a motorway in Zamora, Spain. The brothers' deaths led to an outpouring of grief from the football world and beyond.

A new biography of Diogo Jota from Reach Sport tells the inside story of his life that was so sadly cut short. It contains interviews with his family, team-mates and managers that form part of a richly-detailed book and celebration of the much-loved husband and father of three.

‌



In this extract, from Chapter 1 of the biography, Rute recalls how she learned of Jota's death.

“It was a surprise,” says Rute Cardoso, Diogo Jota’s wife, on his decision to hire a Ferrari then a Lamborghini during the summer of 2025. “Unlike most players, who like fancy cars, jewellery and watches, Diogo was never into that sort of thing. He was happy with the cars we had.”

‌



She continues: “So perhaps because he’d never been particularly into cars, he took that chance to try driving a Ferrari before our wedding. After that, he would also rent a Lamborghini, which he had to drop off in Santander.”

There were several key fixtures in Diogo Jota’s schedule for his break in Portugal: there was his rehabilitation from surgery; there was the wedding of José SA, the Wolves goalkeeper; and, above all, he had his own wedding to Rute Cardoso.

He would fulfil all these engagements. His return journey to Santander was planned for 2-3 July 2025 in the company of his brother, André. Before setting off, Diogo hired the Lamborghini.

As the departure drew closer they went to Rute’s sister’s house, to give their family the chance to say goodbye to Diogo and André. “That way, they had the opportunity to see the damned car and have dinner with us.”

‌



Rute recalls having gone to “put the boys to bed” and, upon coming down to the living room, finding Diogo and André almost ready to leave. To break up the journey, they planned to stop for the night at a hotel in Benavente, in Spain.

“A few minutes after they’d left, I sent Diogo a message saying, ‘Safe journey’. He replied with an emoji, and I told him to keep his eyes on the road."

It was the last message that he replied to.

View 6 Images Diogo Jota married Rute Cardoso 11 days before his death (Image: Instagram/Diogo Jota)

‌



"At our wedding, my bridesmaids and I had organised a surprise for him – a dance. On the night of the accident, at around 22:40, the photographer sent me the video of it, which I forwarded to our group chat. They replied that Diogo looked like someone falling in love for the first time.”

Keen to share the video, Rute sent another message to her husband. “It said: ‘When you stop, I’ve got a video to show you.’ It was delivered, but it was never read.”

Of course, Rute knew that Jota was on the road, so an unread message was no cause for alarm. Everything seemed to be proceeding as planned.

“Meanwhile, an uncle of mine who works in Spain had just returned from a trip. I rang my aunt to tell her I was leaving to join Diogo in Liverpool on Friday, and asked her if they wanted to pop round to our house before then.”

‌



They headed over, entirely oblivious to the important role they would play that night.

“After my aunt and uncle had left, I looked at my watch and thought it was about the time that Diogo and André must have been arriving at the hotel. I sent him another message, just asking, ‘Well?’”

This time a grey tick appeared on the WhatsApp message, but there was no sign of the second tick to confirm that it had been delivered. A concerned Rute sent him “another one, then another one… and none of them were delivered”.

There was something else that she could try in an effort to ease her rising anxiety: a message to André.

‌



“That one wasn’t delivered either.”

Rute began to tremble, fearing that something might have happened to them. She sought comfort in her sister, who pointed out that they might be in an area with poor reception or that their phones might have run out of battery.

But Rute’s fears were already multiplying.

“Ever since my eldest son was born, I’ve become afraid of so many things. The week before, Diogo and I had talked about it – about the fear the children would be left to fend for themselves if anything were to happen to us. When I realised the messages weren’t being delivered, all that pessimism came flooding back.”

‌



As if on autopilot, Rute rang a friend, Catarina, to ask if she had booked Diogo and André room at the hotel in Benavente. Catarina hadn’t, but that she did know the name of the hotel. Straight away, Rute rang the hotel, asking if they had checked in two men who had said they would be arriving late. Two brothers in a green Lamborghini.

The hotel receptionist’s reply was delivered in a completely neutral tone. No, they had not yet arrived.

Bursting with anxiety, Rute rang André’s girlfriend Paula, who told her that she hadn’t spoken to him for a few hours. Rute asked her to try to get hold of him, then continued trying to get to the bottom of the situation herself. She felt like she had to keep trying things out, keep taking action, keep looking for answers. To simply wait seemed impossible.

She phoned a hospital in Benavente, but was told they were unable to provide that sort of information.

‌



Next, she tried to contact the Spanish police, to no avail. Her nerves were starting to overwhelm her. Meanwhile, her sister Lídia had another idea: they could call Uncle Vítor, a lorry driver, who might be able to obtain more information from the police.

“I rang him,” Rute recalls, “explaining that I couldn’t get hold of Diogo and that they hadn’t arrived at the hotel yet. I asked if he could help me.”

On the other end of the line, Vítor asked his niece to bear with him. He fetched another phone with a Spanish number and rang the traffic police, all the while keeping his Portuguese phone connected to the call with his niece.

Then Rute heard her uncle say into the other phone: “Yes, two brothers.”

‌



6 View 6 Images Diogo Jota and Rute Cardoso had three children (Image: Instagram) 6 View 6 Images The couple met at high school in Portugal

Rute felt the strong, unyielding certainty that something had happened. And yet...

“My sister and I were confused. How did they know they were brothers?”

‌



Yes, there might have been an accident; yes, their phones might have been broken; yes, and they would be fine in no time.

“Suddenly, my uncle asked me to put Nuno, my brother-in-law, on the line. At that time of night, in the silence, I could make out every word they were saying. I heard my uncle tell him: ‘The bodies are being taken away’. I think he added ‘to the mortuary’, but that’s when my mind went blank.

"Bodies? My brother-in-law froze. My sister took the phone from him and asked my uncle to speak to her. My main concern was to ring Diogo’s father and tell him: ‘You must come here immediately.’ I rang André’s girlfriend and said the same thing: ‘Paula, come over now.'"

Suddenly, the panic began to strengthen its grip. A need to keep busy also took hold.

‌



“I began to realise that it might be true, even though I wanted to believe it was impossible. According to my watch, I walked 11 kilometres that night, just pacing around the yard at my sister’s house."

Two psychologists from the National Institute of Medical Emergencies had already arrived to support Rute and the rest of the family when Uncle Vítor called again to tell her that there was something important she had to hear.

On the other end of the line was a Spanish police officer who, after confirming that he was speaking to Rute Cardoso and that he had Jota’s ID in his possession, stated the following: “I hereby declare the death of Diogo Jose Teixeira da Silva, born on 4 December 1996.”

View 6 Images Andre Silva and Diogo Jota both played for Porto (Image: FACEBOOK)

‌



Rute took a moment before she let a tear fall. She remained in denial, adamant it could not be true. Her mother and mother-in-law wept with an almost inhuman despondency. Rute kept pacing back and forth, ranting, drawing on her last shreds of strength in a refusal to accept the situation.

She remembered how she used to tease Diogo about how lucky he was and how things always went well for him — personally, professionally, everything.

“I just kept saying to my friend Catarina: ‘This is a joke, it can’t be true. There’s no way in the world this can be true!’”

Time passed. Rute cannot say how long. Minutes that must have felt like a lifetime.

‌



“My sister pulled me closer to her and spoke to my heart. Only then did I begin to accept. To understand.”

View 6 Images Rute Cardoso visited Anfield last year to see the tributes (Image: PA)

With professional detachment, the Spanish police informed Jota’s wife that she would have to go to the mortuary to collect his and his brother’s belongings.

“I told the driver I wanted us to take the same route that they had taken. I imagined that, so many hours on, there would be no traces left, but I wanted to know where it had happened. But when we reached that cursed Kilometre 64, what was left of the car was still there.”

‌



Rute tried to get out of the car, but the rear doors were locked. She found herself banging on the glass from the inside, as if she herself were a frightened little girl. Eventually she rushed towards the scene, but she was stopped by a policeman who told her that she could remain at a distance and avoid etching that horrific image in her mind. Devastated, she agreed.

They proceeded to the mortuary, where Rute’s father was already waiting. She asked to see her husband’s body but was refused permission. She waited in a room and they showed her, on the other side of a small window, Diogo’s body on a stretcher and André’s inside a box. Both had been placed in a bag.

They gave her Jota’s watch, wallet and wedding ring. The bodies were transferred into vans and they all continued the journey to the funeral parlour. Finally, they returned to Portugal.

Rute travelled in the van with Diogo’s body, accompanied by Catarina. Exhausted, she finally fell asleep. Perhaps in a nightmare this would not be true.

‌

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua issues fighting message ahead of Tyson Fury showdown
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua issues fighting message ahead of Tyson Fury showdown

Joshua and Fury will clash in Cardiff on December 11 as they look to settle a long-running rivalry which has been brewing for a decade

View 2 Images Anthony Joshua in his Under Armour campaign

Anthony Joshua has vowed to embrace the pressure ahead of his clash with Tyson Fury.

Joshua and Fury will clash in Cardiff on December 11 as they look to settle a long-running rivalry which has been brewing for a decade. Fury is expected to start as the favourite for the all-British showdown - but Joshua insists he will relish the occasion. The Olympic champion was speaking at the launch of Under Armour's HeatGear and ColdGear Baselayers designed for athletes who embrace pressure rather than shy away from it.

And he said: "Pressure comes with every part of this sport. Every training session, every fight, every expectation. I've learned that you shouldn’t run from it. You have to embrace it and when you've put the work in, pressure becomes something that drives you forward."

View 2 Images

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Meanwhile, Joshua believes the fight's organisers want Fury to win. “I believe that, yeah,” he said last month. “I want to do good, I want to bring it to the UK and do good for people and do the right thing. But if that means that people will then hate me and want to see me fail, then I am going to stomp all over you and raise a war that you are not ready for.

“I want to do good, but if someone hits you, you stab them. If you f*** with me and you want to see me lose, I will f*** you up even more. It’s like that now. That’s just how it is. That’s just my mentality. Now it’s just ‘f*** everyone’ and that’s just it.

“He’ll be trying to get under my skin, 100 per cent. I need to be stoic and calm because it’s nothing personal. I know what sort of person he is.”

Sports.title: Scottie Scheffler's agreement with manager as PGA Tour star loses out on millions
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler's agreement with manager as PGA Tour star loses out on millions

Scottie Scheffler is in a league of his own when it comes to golf, but the World No. 1 may also be missing out on a fortune of earnings off the course

View 3 Images Scottie Scheffler's sponsorship earnings pale in comparison with what he earns in competition (Image: Getty Images)

Scottie Scheffler and his manager Blake Smith are both in agreement when it comes to sponsorships and endorsements. The World No. 1's brilliance on the course has seen him earn close to £37.3million ($50m) in earnings on the PGA Tour.

‌



‌



Off the golf course, he is raking in around £22.37m ($30m) in endorsements and sponsorships, according to Forbes. However, there has always been a feeling in the sport that he could be earning much more.

‌



In context, Rory McIlroy, the current World No. 2, brings in around £41m ($55m) in sponsorships, nearly twice as much as Scheffler. However, the American and his manager are both content with their current arrangement.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

He does not earn money from endorsements from pharmaceutical or healthcare brands, nor does he take any money from drinks brands, automaker or video game deals, according to the Athletic.

In addition, he has also declined deals with betting companies or prediction markets and was one of the few players to turn down a lucrative approach from the Tomorrow Golf League, when so many top players were jumping at the opportunity.

‌



When asked why he has turned down so many different opportunities which could have banked him more money, he said: "It’s not necessarily not wanting to do things.

View 3 Images Scheffler's commercial earnings are much smaller than the likes of McIlroy's (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"It’s just wanting to do things with the right people. You know, there’s always opportunities out there, but what are the right ones?”

Smith is always there for him to listen and scrutinise any and all pitches which come his way. He knows exactly how Scheffler would feel about any approach which comes his way and when he is sure the American would not be interested, he turns them away.

‌



Explaining his thinking behind each and every decision, in a past interview, Scheffler said: "I don’t take the partnerships lightly.

View 3 Images The bulk of Scheffler's earnings have been in competition (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Like I don’t want to just work with people that I don’t enjoy being around. Days like today would be a real pain in the butt if I didn’t enjoy the people that I was with.”

There are many sponsorship deals he is involved in. Like many golfers, he is partnered with Nike, Rolex and TaylorMade.

Article continues below

He has also found room for commercial ventures which interest him, including GolfForever training, sportfishing team Texas Lone Star's Angling Club and many others.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher calls Bruno Fernandes a DISGRACE for 'throwing Michael Carrick under the bus'
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher calls Bruno Fernandes a DISGRACE for 'throwing Michael Carrick under the bus'

Jamie Carragher has launched a scathing attack on Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, branding the Portuguese a 'disgrace' for his post-match comments following the club's 4-1 defeat to Como

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher criticised Bruno Fernandes after his post-match remarks

Jamie Carragher has unleashed scathing criticism of Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes - labelling the Portuguese midfielder a 'disgrace.' The former Liverpool defender defended embattled head coach Michael Carrick and commended the 45-year-old for responding to the skipper following their 4-1 hammering at the hands of Como.

‌



‌



Carragher suggested that Fernandes' explosive remarks came after he was left 'embarrassed' by his 66th-minute substitution during their humiliation in Northern Italy. Nico Paz shone brightest as his double inspired Cesc Fabregas' side to a memorable victory and intensified the scrutiny on the Premier League-winning midfielder.

‌



The United skipper joined Lisandro Martinez in delivering a shock statement during post-match media appearances. Fernandes directed criticism towards Carrick, pinning responsibility for the loss on Ruben Amorim's successor.

‌



Man Utd news: Lewis Hall transfer twist as Antonio Conte conditions emerge READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

In an impassioned outburst, the footballer-turned-pundit speaking on CBS Sports accused Fernandes of 'killing' his teammates and being the reason for United's inability to press collectively. He said: "No (not a good look). We said Lisandro Martinez was bang out of order last week for calling out the hierarchy and for Bruno Fernandes to do that is a disgrace really.

"When you think about last season he got Player of the Season, that was off the back of Michael Carrick becoming manager, he wouldn't have got that without Michael Carrick because he got put back in his rightful position and went on to have a fantastic season because he's a talented footballer."

‌



"But in terms of attitude, the way he goes about things, is not right at all. He's reacted like that because he's been brought off and he's been embarrassed by the manager because he's been brought off. When he talks about pressing, man-to-man or zonal, for years, Bruno Fernandes has meant Manchester United can't press.

"Because he does things for the crowd, I commentate on games and he runs all over and plays like a kid in the schoolyard, he plays for the supporters, it looks like he's working hard, he's not, he's killing the team doing it. He's not playing in a successful era for Manchester United.

‌



Carragher continued: "Years ago, there was a captain called Bryan Robson, one of the greatest players to ever play for Man United because he played for the club, he didn't throw the manager or the players under the bus.

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes questioned Man United's coaching staff's decision

‌



"He kept fighting for Manchester United and watching him throw his arms up every week in a game is an absolute disgrace, calling the manager out considering how he's performed this season on the pitch.

"Awful attitude and not what a Manchester United captain should do."

‌



Carragher acknowledged that a change in the dugout is required at Old Trafford following the loss, which extended their winless run to seven matches. During his post-match media briefing, Carrick hit back at Fernandes by suggesting that 'if you don't run forward and back, you aren't going to win.'

The response earned praise for Carrick, with Carragher emerging as an unexpected supporter as he confessed to feeling sympathy for the manager.

‌



"Isn't it funny, how many managers has Bruno Fernandes had? So every single manager doesn't have a philosophy? How many managers are we on now? Five?" said the former Liverpool man.

‌



"It's an easy thing to say, Fabregas is the best new thing in managerial teams but Man United is rotten from top to bottom. Not just the manager, the whole club, who has got the answers?

"We comment on it all the time. Are we ever right really? No one else seems to. There's no doubt the manager needs to be changed now, this can't go on for a club of this stature but I'm glad Michael Carrick come out and said that about Michael Carrick. They don't run.

‌



"What he did last season, no one proclaims Michael Carrick is one of the greatest managers in Europe but what he did was come in and helped his own football club, he was out of work, come in and done amazing, the only reason they're in the Champions League is because of Carrick.

"He got them in there, the reason they got another £100m to £150m, no one thought they'd be there. I feel sorry for him a little bit. It's not working out and it needs to be changed.

Article continues below

"I'm delighted he brought him off and a pop back because that what they need some of them players."
