Sports.title: Jack Catterall Refuses To Move For Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall refuses to move out of Teofimo Lopez’s way, rejecting any payment to surrender his place in the WBA welterweight title queue as their October 22 negotiation deadline arrives.

His message leaves little room for bargaining. Catterall wants the fight he was promised, while Lopez seeks permission to bypass him for a unification against WBC champion Ryan Garcia.

“NO there isn’t an amount of money you can give me to step aside end of discussion,” Catterall posted on X. “I want what i deserve I want what I signed up for and I want to become a world champion and I won’t except any fucking offer to move out the way.”

Teofimo’s team has requested an exception from the WBA to pursue Garcia. Catterall can refuse to cooperate, but the sanctioning body still controls whether its order produces a fight or another delay.

That is where Catterall has reason to worry. The WBA also ordered Jaime Munguia to defend against Bektemir Melikuziev, yet Munguia is scheduled to face little-known Nikita Zon on October 31 instead. The organization has stated that it did not approve that matchup and is reviewing the situation. Bek is still waiting for his ordered opportunity.

Issuing an order does little for a mandatory challenger if the champion continues arranging other fights. The WBA’s response to Munguia has yet to put Bek in the ring with him. Catterall needs more than another statement confirming his position.

Eddie Hearn wants Teofimo to fight Catterall or vacate the belt. If Teofimo prefers the Ryan Garcia payday, Catterall shouldn’t have to put his career on hold to accommodate him.

Catterall won’t move. Now the WBA needs to decide whether Lopez must honor the order or gets to choose another opponent while keeping the title.

Even a promise that the Teofimo-Ryan winner must fight Catterall offers little protection. A lucrative immediate rematch could push him aside again. And if the WBA finally enforces its order, the winner could simply vacate and keep the WBC belt. Catterall would be left without the fight or any compensation for waiting—the same position another promise was supposed to prevent.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Believes He Can Beat Dalton Smith Easily
Sports.content:
Alberto Puello expects to have an easy night at Dalton Smith’s expense this Saturday in Sheffield. The Dominican challenger does not rate the local belt-holder anywhere near his hardest fights, making it clear that Smith will quickly realize finding a target against him is nothing like teeing off on Subriel Matias.

Puello is counting on his slick defense, ring smarts, and footwork to carry the night. In his eyes, Smith had it easy against a flat-footed brawler like Matias, but trying to pin down an awkward southpaw who refuses to stand in the pocket is going to give the champion fits from the opening bell.

“With my experience, hitting him without getting hit, and my skills, I think I can beat him easily,” Puello said to Fight Wire ahead of their October 24 fight in Sheffield.

When asked if Smith is the toughest test of his career, Puello laughed it off with a quick “Not at all.” He pointed right to Gary Antuanne Russell as a far rougher night, and even put Matias above Smith on the danger scale.

“He beat Subriel Matias, of course, but I also think Subriel Matias is a little more difficult than him,” Puello said.

That take is bound to stir up plenty of noise considering Smith stopped Matias. But Puello is looking strictly at styles. Teeing off on an aggressive slugger who marches straight into range is night and day compared to trying to catch a slick technician who makes you swing at fresh air all night.

“I’m a boxer with plenty of defense. I know how to move around the ring. Subriel Matias only has one way of fighting: going forward, taking punches and throwing them. I know how to hit without getting hit.”

Smith will have to work for every opening instead of banking on a sitting target to stay in punching range. If Puello sticks and moves, the local champion could burn serious fuel chasing a ghost all night instead of enjoying the pocket exchanges he had against Matias.

Puello also expects the roaring Sheffield arena to work against Smith. The champion will feel the heat to put on a show and satisfy his hometown crowd, while Puello can relax, stay patient, and stick to the blueprint without any outside pressure.

He is not just planning to scrape by on the cards, either. Puello made it clear his camp has him ready to take a clean twelve-round decision or jump on a stoppage the second Smith gets reckless and leaves an opening.

We already know how the boxing community will treat Smith if he loses to Puello. It will be merciless. The second the final bell sounds, skeptics will point out that the undefeated record was built on domestic fodder and that Matias was simply a flat-footed slugger tailor-made for Smith to counter.

The defeat would leave Smith’s promoter, Eddie Hearn, standing in the ring, needing to tell the fans what went wrong, and likely talking about a rematch.

Sports.title: Fired On His Day Off: Bradley Shreds Shakur Stevenson Over Lost Zuffa Contract
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley pulled no punches on his channel when breaking down how Shakur Stevenson lost his Zuffa Boxing contract. According to Bradley, Shakur fumbled massive money because he failed to deliver the one matchup the promotion actually cared about: Devin Haney.

“Shakur and his team, they thought that they was going to pull off a lick,” Bradley said on Into the Storm. “They was just like, ‘Oh yeah, we got these stupid people up here. They don’t know nothing about boxing.’”

Bradley believes Shakur and his handlers completely misread the room, assuming they were dealing with naive outsiders whom they could easily manipulate. In reality, Zuffa’s willingness to spend fifteen million dollars per fight was meant strictly for marquee events, not hand-picked opposition like Gary Antuanne Russell.

“The fight that Zuffa wanted was Haney-Shakur. Period,” Bradley said.

He also mocked how readily Zuffa allowed Shakur to leave his contract, imagining the company responding, “We good.”

“How big of a damn diva you got to be to get released on your contract?” Bradley asked.

Bradley highlighted the absurdity of the split, pointing out how rare it is for a fighter to get released from a massive deal without ever stepping into the ring. He called out Shakur’s team for managing his career poorly, arguing that letting an eight-figure bag slip away was inexcusable.

While Bradley noted that prolonged weight squabbles and promotional moves damaged the negotiations on both sides, he laid the ultimate fault on Shakur’s reluctance to take real risks.

“All this was done because you afraid to lose that O,” he said. “It’s about protecting that damn O, bro.”

Now planning to launch his own promotional outfit, Shakur faces a stark reality. Finding financial backers willing to offer that caliber of purse without top-tier opponents is nearly impossible. As Bradley put it, someone has to put up the money, and Zuffa was ready to do that, but Shakur was unwilling to fight the opponent required to earn it.

When an entity like Zuffa comes into boxing with massive venture backing, they aren’t paying a fighter $15 million a fight out of altruism—they are paying for immediate, marquee box-office events to establish their footprint.

Shakur made three miscalculated moves. For starters, treating Silicon Valley/UFC money like naive marks. Bradley’s phrase that they thought they could “pull off a lick” was dead-on.

Shakur’s camp operated like they could sign the deal, dictate terms from high above, and then demand eight-figure checks to fight safe stylistic matchups like Gary Antuanne Russell. They forgot that Zuffa’s entire business model is built on rigid control, star matchups, and high returns.

Then he got dragged into prolonged posturing over weight. The nine-month negotiation saga over whether they’d fight at 144, 145, or 147 pounds drained every ounce of momentum. By letting the fight stall over a couple of pounds, and then throwing Keyshawn Davis into the mandatory picture as an artificial wedge, they gave Devin and Bill Haney the opening to outmaneuver them entirely and do their own business with DAZN.

Prioritizing the “0” over generational exposure: At 27 or 28, in the prime of his physical career, Shakur had a direct pipeline to beat Haney, fight Ryan Garcia, and cement himself as the premier American star of this era. Instead, the hyper-defensive mindset inside the ring mirrored his mindset outside of it: risk minimization at all costs.

Getting released from an eight-figure contract without ever throwing a single punch under the banner, literally getting “fired on your day off” while only doing a broadcast stint, is almost unheard of at that level of boxing.

Betting on yourself only works if the market is willing to pay what you think you’re worth. Now Shakur is left trying to build his own promotional company in a landscape where broadcast money is tightening, and network buyers aren’t handing out $15 million paydays for sparring sessions.

Sports.title: Arnold Barboza Hints At Devin Haney Title Shot
Sports.content:
Arnold Barboza Jr. dropped word on social media that a massive welterweight title opportunity just landed in his lap on short notice. While he confirmed that 147 pounds is locked in with a belt on the line, he kept the identity of his opponent quiet for now.

Speculation immediately involved Devin Haney after Haney’s anticipated matchup with Shakur Stevenson fell apart. Barboza’s remarks point to a fast-developing opening, even if ink has not officially met paper yet.

“I got some news today. It’s a blessing. I don’t know how real it is, but it sounds pretty real. It might be a big fight sooner than expected,” Barboza said on social media. “I’ll be stepping in at the last minute on some s***, but I don’t know where it’s going to be at, but it’s soon.”

The tight calendar creates the biggest hurdle. Barboza appears fully ready to sign before even knowing the host city, but world championship bouts offer zero room for entering camp cold. Securing an unexpected offer represents one hurdle; having the necessary weeks to dial in a precise tactical blueprint presents an entirely separate challenge.

If Haney ends up standing across the ring, Barboza faces an elite defensive technician. Taking on Haney demands an answer for his distance control, lead hand control, and inside tie ups. Simply tracking him across the canvas without cutting the ring effectively will turn the contest into a frustrating chase.

“A lot sooner than expected. Not no next year fight. A couple of weeks soon. Yeah, I’m fighting at 147. Yeah, it’ll be for a belt. We got to go for legacy,” Barboza said.

Teofimo Lopez also figures heavily into Barboza’s long-range calculations. Barboza sees capturing a 147-pound crown as his quickest ticket to securing a second chance against Lopez after coming up short in their junior welterweight clash.

“It’s not a rematch with Teo. Not yet. I got to win this belt to rematch him,” Barboza admitted.

Holding a world title strap provides massive leverage at the negotiating table. The immediate task requires transforming the sudden opening into an executed contract, setting up a targeted training block, and verifying the sanctioning body timeline.

Sports.title: DAZN Team May Call Canelo-Mbilli From London
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli could fight in Riyadh on October 31, with DAZN’s broadcast team following the action from a studio in London. The potential arrangement adds another question to a card already approaching under difficult circumstances.

Dan Rafael reports that the team is likely to call the event remotely if it goes ahead. His report leaves both points conditional: the card proceeding and the commentators working outside Saudi Arabia.

“Per sources, if #CaneloMbilli goes forward Oct. 31 in Riyadh, the likelihood is that the DAZN broadcast team will not be ringside and will call the card remotely from a studio in London,” Rafael wrote on X.

DAZN’s likely move speaks for itself. Calling one of the year’s biggest fights from television monitors thousands of miles away suggests the broadcast team wants no part of the danger in Riyadh. Promotional talk about the event going ahead cannot erase the attacks on the city’s international airport.

It also creates an awkward contrast. Commentators would work from the safety of a London studio, while Canelo, Mbilli and the undercard fighters would be expected to fly to Riyadh, attend media events and fight. If the risk is enough to keep the broadcast team away, the fighters have every reason to question why they should be there.

The background explains everything. Dan Rafael reported earlier on missile strikes and drone activity aimed at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, even while noting Canelo planned to go ahead anyway. Those strikes turned travel safety and the host city into the dominant story leading up to the bout.

A London crew can watch the live monitors, but calling an event off a monitor is never the same. Commentators lose their direct line of sight between broadcast angles. They miss corner chaos, subtle crowd shifts, and whatever happens outside the camera frame, leaving them watching the exact same feed fans see on their couches.

That is a massive drop in quality for a pay-per-view centered on the sport’s biggest earner. Calling action from ringside lets commentators catch real impacts, subtle cornerman instructions, and shifts in body language that cameras and boom mics miss entirely.

Canelo is penciled in to challenge Mbilli for the WBC super middleweight title. The sanctioning body still lists October 31 in Riyadh on DAZN.

The card needs an official word on how the broadcast will work. Rafael’s reporting suggests fight week will look bizarre, even if both guys walk to the ring on schedule.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis Calls Sebastian Fundora Too Small
Sports.content:
Jaron Ennis laughed off Sebastian Fundora’s knockout claims, calling the towering champion “too small” to back up his words. Ennis is eyeing Fundora down the line, but he’s making sure business with Josh Kelly gets handled first.

That comment flips the script on Fundora. Opponents usually spend training camp obsessing over his massive reach, but Ennis seems far more eager to exploit openings than worry about incoming fire.

“He too small. He not big enough,” Ennis said to YSM Sports Media when told about Fundora’s knockout comments. “But we focused on Josh Kelly, and that’s the main focus, main target right now. We’ll talk about him later on.”

Ennis kept a close eye on Fundora’s clash with Ermal Hadribeaj, scouting for future business rather than just watching for fun.

“Definitely watching to pick him apart,” Ennis said. “Just to see what he got, and it’s what I’ve been knew.”

Fundora didn’t dial back his confidence at the post-fight presser either. When reporters brought up potential bouts with Ennis or Vergil Ortiz Jr., he insisted he’d halt both.

“If it was those guys, I’d still knock them out,” Fundora said. “These guys can’t hurt me.”

That confidence would face a different examination against Ennis. Choosing to fight inside is one thing against Hadribeaj; giving Ennis opportunities at close range would require Fundora to account for his speed and combinations.

Ennis even took a jab at the Hadribeaj stoppage, arguing the challenger beat the count right as the bell sounded. Regardless, he made it clear he wanted Fundora looking sharp so there are zero asterisks later.

“I don’t want nobody to say nothing,” Ennis said. “No excuses.”

Kelly is the obstacle between that talk and a possible Fundora fight. Ennis described him as a “sharp” and “smart” fighter. Beating him must come before Ennis can turn his confidence against Fundora into something more substantial.

Ennis is spotting the exact same tactical flaw everyone else saw against Hadribeaj: Fundora simply cannot resist fighting like a phone booth brawler. Calling a 6’6″ fighter with an 86-inch reach “too small” sounds bizarre on the surface, but Ennis is talking about physical density and ring presence, not height.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Claims Floyd Mayweather Title Fight Agreement
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia claims he and Floyd Mayweather have agreed to fight for the WBC welterweight title, putting a championship label on a matchup that looks more like a celebrity event than serious business at 147.

The selling point is obvious: Garcia gets a chance to put the first loss on Mayweather’s professional record. Whether beating a 49-year-old version of Floyd would prove much about Ryan’s ability is another question.

“Trust me at first I thought this was bull***,” Garcia posted on X. “But it’s real Floyd and I agree to a fight.”

Garcia added: “147 for the WBC welterweight championship of the world. 50-0 vs The current champ.”

That is Garcia announcing an agreement. His post does not provide a date, venue, or broadcaster, and it does not establish that the WBC has approved Mayweather as a title challenger. Those details still need to follow before this can be treated as a confirmed championship fight.

As a commercial idea, it is easy to understand. Mayweather’s undefeated record gives the promotion something to sell beyond the usual exhibition routine. Ryan would be chasing the “0,” while Floyd would be selling the possibility that he can still beat a much younger champion.

As a title defense, it is a circus.

Mayweather’s reputation was earned against elite fighters over a long career. That reputation does not tell us what he can do at 49 against a current welterweight champion. Putting his record on the line would make the result official, but it would not turn back the clock.

Garcia would also leave himself open to an obvious criticism. Beat Floyd, and he has beaten a retired great approaching 50. Struggle with him, and the questions about Ryan become considerably louder.

There will be people willing to buy it. Two famous names and the possibility of Mayweather finally losing are enough to draw attention beyond boxing’s regular audience.

That is the appeal Garcia is selling. The WBC belt adds decoration, but the attraction is celebrity, money, and a famous unbeaten record.

Sanctioning this as an official WBC welterweight title defense would make a complete joke of the belt and freeze out actual contenders at 147. If two massive names want an unsanctioned exhibition to generate huge pay-per-view numbers, boxing fans understand the drill.

Celebrity events happen all the time now. Slapping an authentic world championship onto it crosses the line from entertainment into parody. Mayweather turns 50 next February and has not fought in a sanctioned professional bout since 2017. He is not ranked by the WBC.

Handing him an immediate shot at a real crown purely because of his fame insults every active fighter grinding through eliminators for a mandatory spot. For Garcia, putting the belt up brings zero boxing credit. If he blows out a 49-year-old retired legend, nobody takes it seriously as a legitimate championship victory.

If he looks bad or gets touched up by Floyd, critics will tear him apart. Keeping it as an exhibition protects the credibility of the sanctioning body, keeps the division moving, and lets fans enjoy the spectacle for what it really is. Turning it into an official title fight cheapens the entire sport.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Could Fight Four Times In 2027
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma could box four times in 2027, with promoter Frank Warren targeting a January return to give the heavyweight an early start on a busy year.

Warren wants at least three appearances, though fitting in a fourth will depend on the opposition. No opponent or venue has been announced for Itauma’s next fight.

“I would like him to have a minimum of three fights, maybe four if we can fit them in, depending on the opposition as well, of course,” Warren told BoxNation.

That last qualification leaves room for the schedule to change. Four fights would give Itauma regular work, but the value of that activity will come from who Warren puts in front of him. An opponent who makes him solve different problems could provide more than another quick finish.

Warren expects to reveal the next step shortly.

“I think we’ll be sometime next week, towards the end of next week, announcing something, but he’ll be fighting very early next year, probably in January,” he said.

January remains a target rather than a confirmed booking. Still, getting Itauma out that early would leave Warren enough room to spread three more appearances across the remainder of 2027, provided the fights and recovery periods allow it.

The opponent announcement will tell us more about the ambition behind that schedule. Warren offered no names and made no commitment to a world title fight during this interview. His comments were about getting Itauma into the ring regularly.

There is also a practical balance to find. As the opposition improves, fights can require longer preparation and leave less room for a quick turnaround. Warren’s preference for three, with four possible, gives him flexibility without committing Itauma to dates before the opponents are secured.

A busy calendar is a reasonable starting point. The next question is whether those appearances move Itauma closer to the heavyweights he eventually needs to beat.

Ghana News.title: CSA and NITA order government institutions to fix critical PHP vulnerabilities within seven days
Ghana News.content:
The Cyber Security Authority (CSA) and the National Information Technology Agency (NITA) have directed government institutions to address two critical vulnerabilities in PHP within seven days, warning that the flaws could allow attackers to take control of affected servers without a username or password.

In a joint cybersecurity alert on Thursday, October 22, the agencies urged government institutions, businesses, website owners, hosting providers and operators of Critical Information Infrastructure to treat the threat as urgent and implement available security fixes.

The vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and referred to as “PHP2Shell”, affect PHP, a programming language widely used to run websites and online services.

Successful exploitation could expose sensitive information, disrupt digital services and allow attackers to launch further attacks against an organisation’s network.

Security fixes available

The agencies said the PHP Project had released fixes in versions 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12.

Affected organisations have been advised to install the appropriate patched release, upgrade to a later supported version or apply a vendor package confirmed to contain the fixes.

They cautioned that updating website themes or plugins alone would not resolve vulnerabilities in the underlying PHP software.

Seven-day deadline for government institutions

Under the directive, all government institutions are required to take action within seven days and report the remedial measures taken to the CSA and NITA.

Heads of institutions have been instructed to ensure that their information and communications technology (ICT) teams and service providers act urgently to identify and secure affected systems.

NITA will coordinate technical support for government digital assets and services, while the CSA will oversee cybersecurity incident reporting and response.

Institutions are also expected to maintain an up-to-date inventory of their digital assets and nominate responsible officers to support remediation and coordination under NITA’s Government Digital Assurance Programme (GovDAP).

Five steps to protect digital systems

The agencies have outlined five key measures for affected organisations.

First, they should identify all websites, web applications and servers running PHP, including those managed by external service providers, prioritising internet-facing systems and essential public services.

Second, they must apply the relevant security updates, follow vendor instructions, restart affected services where necessary and verify that the patches are working.

Third, systems that cannot be updated immediately should be temporarily taken offline until they can be secured. Temporary protective measures should not replace permanent patching.

Fourth, organisations should investigate possible compromises by reviewing system logs, unusual processes, unexpected administrator accounts and unauthorised changes to website files. Suspected compromised systems should be isolated and evidence preserved.

Finally, website owners should obtain written confirmation from hosting providers, developers and system administrators that affected systems have been identified and patched.

Public warned against fraudulent security updates

The CSA and NITA have also cautioned the public against suspicious messages requesting downloads of purported “PHP security updates”, passwords or payment details.

Website owners have been advised to obtain security updates only through official software sources or verified service providers.

Where to report incidents

Organisations and individuals who suspect a cybersecurity incident or system compromise can contact the CSA through the following channels:

Call or SMS: 292

292 Email: report@csa.gov.gh

For government digital services coordination and GovDAP enquiries, NITA can be contacted on:

Email: govdap@nita.gov.gh

govdap@nita.gov.gh Telephone: 055 249 9661

The agencies have urged all affected organisations to act immediately to protect sensitive information, maintain the availability of essential digital services and prevent further compromise of their systems.

Ghana News.title: Speculations about Asiedu Nketia’s presidential bid deepen as he skips NDC chairmanship contest
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has confirmed that its incumbent National Chairman, Johnson Asiedu Nketia, did not pick nomination forms to contest the party’s upcoming national executive elections.

The party’s Director of Elections and IT, Mahdi Gibril, said Asiedu Nketiah, popularly known as “General Mosquito”, had not picked forms by the close of nominations and had not indicated an intention to contest.

“These are those I know that did not pick. In any case, they did not indicate to us that they will pick,” Mr Gibril said.

Although Asiedu Nketia has not formally declared a presidential bid, his decision not to seek another term as national chairman comes amid speculation about whether he intends to contest the NDC’s presidential primary ahead of the 2028 general elections.

In August 2026, Asiedu Nketia was asked whether he had ruled out contesting the 2028 presidential election. He responded emphatically: “No, No, No!”

“I have never ruled any position out in my life. I'm not ruling any position out,” he said at the time, listing the presidency among the positions he could consider.

He also argued that ambition was essential in politics.

“Ambition is a very useful thing in politics. If you are a politician and you have no ambition, you are in the wrong profession,” he said.

His comments have continued to fuel speculation about his political plans, although he has not formally announced a presidential campaign.

The NDC closed the picking of nomination forms for its 2026 National Executive Elections at 5 pm5pm on Wednesday, October 21.

According to a statement signed by the Spokesperson for the Congress Elections Committee, Dr Peter Boamah Otokunor, a total of 137 prospective aspirants picked forms to contest 14 national executive positions.

The figures include five aspirants for National Chairman, 19 for National Vice Chairman, two for General Secretary and 11 for Deputy General Secretary.

With nominations closed, the process will move to the filing of completed forms, scheduled for November 7 to 9, ahead of the National Delegates Congress on December 19, 2026.

Among the prominent figures linked to the National Chairman race is former chairman Samuel Ofosu-Ampofo, whose supporters purchased nomination forms on his behalf.

Former Local Government Minister Akwasi Opong-Fosu, who declared his intention to contest in August 2026, and Ambassador Alhaji Said Sinare have also been associated with the race.

Asiedu Nketiah has served as NDC National Chairman since December 2022, when he defeated Ofosu-Ampofo at the party’s 10th National Delegates Congress.

His decision not to seek re-election leaves the chairmanship open as the party prepares to elect new national executives.

The NDC’s national executive elections will determine the party’s leadership as it prepares for the 2028 general elections.

The next stages include the filing of completed nomination forms and campaigning ahead of the December 19 congress.

While Asiedu Nketiah’s decision not to contest the chairmanship has renewed attention on his political future, the party has not disclosed his reasons for opting out, and he has yet to formally declare a bid for the presidency.

Ghana News.title: NAIMOS to launch Operation Greenshield at Atiwa Forest Reserve to combat illegal mining
Ghana News.content:
The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) is planning a new forest protection operation, dubbed Operation Greenshield, beginning with the Atiwa Forest Reserve, as part of efforts to curb illegal mining.

The Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K. S. Appiah, said the operation would target illegal mining in priority areas, prevent miners from returning to cleared sites and establish a system for the long-term protection of forest reserves.

Addressing the media on the fight against illegal mining, he explained that Operation Greenshield would involve clearing affected areas, securing them against renewed encroachment and eventually handing over responsibility for routine protection to the relevant state agencies.

“We also plan to conduct Operation Greenshield. Operation Greenshield is our planned forest protection intervention that will commence with the Atiwa Forest Reserve,” he said.

According to Colonel Appiah, the intervention aims to disrupt illegal mining in priority areas, deny renewed access, and create the conditions for sustained protection of this strategic watershed.

Colonel Appiah outlined a three-stage approach to the planned operation, comprising clearing and disrupting illegal mining activities, holding and stabilising affected areas, and eventually transitioning responsibility to the relevant authorities.

“The concept for Atiwa follows three stages. We'll clear and disrupt, hold and stabilise, and transition and hand over,” he said.

Under the plan, specially trained personnel will conduct operations to disrupt illegal mining activities in targeted parts of the reserve.

The initial phase will focus on clearing priority hotspots and preventing illegal miners from continuing their activities. This will be followed by sustained patrols and surveillance to ensure that those areas are not occupied again.

The final stage will involve transferring responsibility for routine protection to the Forestry Commission, allowing its guards to take over the ongoing monitoring and protection of the reserve.

Colonel Appiah said the intended outcome was to ensure that priority areas were not only cleared but also secured against renewed illegal mining.

“The intended outcome is a reserve in which priority hotspots have been cleared and stabilised, with routine protection progressively transferred to Forestry Commission guards,” he said.

He added that protecting the Atiwa Forest Reserve would strengthen efforts to safeguard water sources and restore areas affected by illegal mining.

The operations director said a key principle behind Operation Greenshield was to ensure that NAIMOS could move on to other priority areas after completing its enforcement duties.

He explained that the secretariat was not expected to remain permanently in every area where it conducted operations. Instead, the relevant agencies would take over to ensure that cleared forest reserves, watersheds and river systems remained protected.

“Our enforcement, after enforcement, we cannot remain permanently in those areas,” he said.

Colonel Appiah said the operation was therefore designed to create a transition to permanent, agency-led protection rather than rely indefinitely on temporary enforcement deployments.

“So we should be able to transition to other agencies to take over the task of monitoring and preventing illegal miners from encroaching onto declared areas,” he said.

The handover is expected to allow NAIMOS to redirect its personnel and resources to other locations while the responsible agencies maintain a presence in areas already secured.

The approach also places emphasis on preventing illegal miners from returning after enforcement teams have withdrawn, a key challenge in sustaining the gains made during anti-galamsey operations.

Colonel Appiah said maintaining the effectiveness of NAIMOS operations would require continued investment in logistics, mobility, communications and support for personnel deployed in the field.

He said that the scale of the task, combined with the difficult terrain in some operational areas, made reliable transport and communication systems essential.

“Going forward, we need to sustain our operational effectiveness. The scale and terrain of the task require sustained mobility, service-level boots, reliable communication, and effective support to deployed personnel,” he said.

He also mentioned the need for equipment to recover and secure machinery seized during operations against illegal mining.

According to him, the recovery and proper handling of heavy equipment are necessary to ensure that seized machines do not find their way back into illegal mining activities.

“Heavy equipment recovery is necessary to secure seized machines and prevent it from returning to illegal operations,” he said.

Colonel Appiah said the government, through the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, had committed to providing the funding and logistical support required to sustain NAIMOS operations.

“The government, through the Ministry of Land and Natural Resources, has committed to providing the needed logistics support and funding to sustain NAIMOS operations,” he said.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod cites US$130m FX sale as cedi records weeks of appreciation
Ghana News.content:
GoldBod CEO, Sammy Gyamfi

The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has cited a US$130 million spot foreign exchange sale at GH¢11.60 per dollar as part of efforts to support the cedi and strengthen stability on the foreign exchange market.

In a Facebook post on Thursday, October 22, the Board said its interventions were helping to improve dollar liquidity at a time when the cedi had recorded more than three consecutive weeks of appreciation against the US dollar on the interbank market.

GoldBod said the interventions were intended to ease pressure on the local currency by increasing the supply of foreign exchange to the market.

As part of its October 2026 programme, the Board plans to supply US$1 billion to authorised commercial banks and provide an additional US$500 million to the Bank of Ghana for reserve accumulation.

The planned US$1.5 billion supply forms part of GoldBod’s broader foreign exchange intervention programme, which it says is aimed at supporting the recovery and stability of the Ghana cedi.

The Board said its efforts remained focused on foreign exchange market stability and contributing to Ghana’s wider economic recovery.

Ghana News.title: NDC will not shield Obuasi SHTS headmaster over sexual abuse allegations – Fifi Kwetey
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) says it will not shield the suspended headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, over allegations of sexual abuse, insisting that law enforcement agencies must conduct an independent and thorough investigation.

Speaking at a press conference at the party’s headquarters on Thursday, October 22, 2026, General Secretary Fifi Kwetey said the party would not interfere in the investigation and wanted the truth to be established.

“We do not endorse any such conduct, and we want the law enforcement to do an independent job. We are sure they will, and this party would not in any way interfere,” he said.

Mr Kwetey said the party would accept the outcome of the investigation, adding that the headmaster would face the consequences if found guilty.

“We want the truth to be brought out. On the back of the truth, the country would have clear assurance that as a party and as government, we do not cover anybody. If he's found guilty, he'll pay the price. If he's not guilty, we'll be happy for him,” he stated.

The NDC General Secretary also addressed questions about the party’s initial position that the headmaster should withdraw, followed by its subsequent call for him to be given the opportunity to clear his name in line with the presumption of innocence.

He explained that the party did not have access to the full details of investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s report when it first took a position on the matter.

“The party unfortunately did not have access to Manasseh's comprehensive disclosure as at Monday on his radio program. Manasseh aired his video and his tapes the evening of that day,” he said.

Mr Kwetey said the party reconsidered its position after reviewing the material aired by the journalist.

“Soon after watching those tapes comprehensively, it was clear that our earlier decision needed to be changed. And that actually is what saw the change of the decision as you saw happen on Tuesday even before midday,” he added.

Mr Kwetey also condemned remarks allegedly made by an NDC communication officer in Amasaman while defending the situation.

He said the comments did not represent the party’s position on sexual abuse and related offences.

"One of our own, unfortunately, a communication officer, in his attempt to want to defend, said things that absolutely must be condemned—that absolutely have nothing to do with this party," he said.

The General Secretary reiterated that the NDC did not endorse rape, sexual misconduct or sexual abuse, regardless of who was involved.

He said the communicator had apologised and that the party expected the apology to be clearly communicated.

“So any officer who may have spoken clearly is not speaking on behalf of this party. Personal responsibility is his. I think he's had the decency of apologizing, and we expect that the apology will be loud. The party endorses no such communication at any time,” he said.

The NDC’s comments come amid growing public concern over allegations of sexual abuse at Obuasi SHTS, with the number of students reported to have made allegations rising to 16.

The headmaster remains suspended by the Ghana Education Service pending the outcome of investigations.

The police have forwarded the case docket to the Attorney-General’s Office for study and advice. The review is expected to inform decisions on the next steps, including whether criminal charges should be pursued.

Investigations by the Ghana Education Service and the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service are also ongoing.

Ghana News.title: NYA organises breast cancer screening for staff and community members
Ghana News.content:
The National Youth Authority (NYA), led by its Chief Executive Officer, Osman Ayariga, has organised a breast cancer screening exercise to promote early detection and raise awareness about the disease among its staff and members of the surrounding community.

The exercise was held at the forecourt of the Authority on Thursday, October 22, 2026, with staff participating fully in the screening.

Community members also joined the exercise, extending the initiative’s reach beyond the institution and providing an opportunity for more people to access breast health checks.

The initiative forms part of efforts to encourage preventive healthcare and highlight the importance of regular screening in the early detection of breast cancer.

Early detection can improve treatment outcomes, making awareness creation and access to screening important components of the fight against the disease.

The participation of NYA staff and community members underscored the importance of collective action in promoting health and well-being.

By opening the exercise to members of the public, the Authority helped encourage greater awareness of breast cancer and the need for individuals to take proactive steps towards protecting their health.

The exercise also highlighted the role public institutions can play in supporting health education and preventive healthcare initiatives.

Through the screening, the NYA reaffirmed the importance of creating awareness about breast cancer and encouraging early checks as part of broader efforts to promote healthier communities.

Ghana News.title: Lapaz driver remanded over alleged sale of 70 suspected unregistered drug tablets
Ghana News.content:
An Accra Circuit Court has remanded a 38-year-old driver into police custody for allegedly offering 70 tablets of suspected unregistered Royal Tapentadol 250 mg for sale.

‎‎Fatawu Yakubu, a resident of Lapaz, Accra, has been charged with offering unregistered drugs for sale.

‎‎The prosecution told the court that the complainants were police officers attached to the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) Special Operations Team at the Police Headquarters in Accra.

‎‎The court did not take his plea. He is expected to reappear on November 3, 2026.

‎‎‎The prosecution said that on October 15, 2026, at about 1400 hours, the officers conducted an operation at Nii Bio Town Junction, Lapaz, to clamp down on illicit drug peddlers and users.

‎‎During the operation, Yakubu was arrested at a game centre.

‎‎A search conducted on him allegedly revealed 70 tablets of Royal Tapentadol 250 mg suspected to be unregistered.

‎‎‎The prosecution said the exhibits were being forwarded to the Police Forensic Science Laboratory for analysis and a report.

Ghana News.title: We’re mining actively; it’s untrue that we’re only treating existing stockpiles – Damang Gold Manager in charge of mining
Ghana News.content:
Damang Gold Mine Ltd’s Manager in charge of Mining, Frank Dankyi Agyei, has dismissed claims that the mine is relying solely on existing stockpiles for its operations, insisting that active mining is ongoing at multiple pits.

Speaking to Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen host, Philip Osei Bonsu, Mr Agyei said the company had deployed heavy-duty mining equipment to the Amoanda and Juno pits, with plans to extend operations to the Rex pits.

“We are actively mining here, as you can see. Claims that we are only treating existing stockpiles are absolutely false,” he said.

He explained that the Amoanda Pit was undergoing a major cutback to consolidate several previously separate mining areas into one larger pit.

The project incorporates the former Tometo East Pit, Amoanda Pit 4 and Amoanda Pits 2 and 3, which he said had previously operated as smaller, isolated pits. The expanded Amoanda Pit is expected to have a strike length of approximately 1.8 kilometres.

Mr Agyei said two Liebherr 9400 excavators were being used for active mining at Amoanda, alongside a Hitachi EX2000 excavator and a Kattega excavator.

He added that at least four excavators were operating at the pit, while five had been deployed to support active mining at the Juno pits.

The equipment at Juno includes 9350 excavators numbered 88 and 89, excavator 99, a Hitachi EX870 excavator numbered 105, excavator 114 and a Pulse excavator numbered 83.

According to him, the deployment of the equipment demonstrates that the mine is continuing to extract ore rather than depending exclusively on material mined previously.

He also disclosed the scale of investment in the mine’s machinery, saying a Liebherr 9400 excavator could cost about €9 million on the market.

Mr Agyei further said the mine had approximately 50 haul trucks, each costing around €4.5 million, highlighting the substantial financial commitment involved in sustaining its operations.

He said the company was working to revitalise the project and had plans to expand active mining to the Rex pits.

The Damang Mine, formerly operated by Gold Fields Ghana Limited, was officially handed over to Engineers and Planners in April 2026, following the company’s successful bid for the concession.

The handover ceremony took place at the mine site on Saturday, April 18, 2026, where the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, performed the symbolic transfer.

This was after Gold Fields' lease expired, and the government placed the concession under competitive tender supervised by the Minerals Commission.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: From the streets to the ballot box: Serbia’s students hope for election win
World.content:
Share From the streets to the ballot box: Serbian students movement wants ‘mafia’ on social media

It all began on the streets.

A student-led movement has emerged as the most serious challenger to the long rule of the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) and its leader, Aleksandar Vucic, ahead of Sunday’s election.

Over the past two years, many citizens, teachers, professors and other experts have joined the students, a protest group that has evolved into a political movement: “Student List–Students Win” (Studentska lista–Studenti pobeđuju).

The catalyst came after the collapse of a concrete canopy at the renovated Novi Sad railway station on November 1, 2024. Sixteen people were killed in the tragedy, which triggered public outrage over alleged corruption and raised questions about construction safety, the quality of renovation work, and government oversight. Students who led protests have sought a fundamental overhaul of a system they deem rotten.

‘Serbia belongs to people, not to criminals’

Kosta Golubovic, a law student at the University of Novi Sad, has been involved since day one.

“Change is clearly necessary. The state must belong to its people, not to the mafia and criminals,” he told Al Jazeera.

“The way they treat the judiciary, the catastrophic conditions at the local level, mayors resorting to violence, dying villages – along with dubious privatisations, money laundering, the erosion of every single institution, police being replaced by thugs, and an education system vanishing before our eyes… these are some of the reasons why change is needed,” said Golubovic.

Demonstrations transformed into the biggest protest movement in Serbia in years, joined by tens of thousands.



The students have not called for the overthrow of Vucic. But their persistence created one of the biggest threats to the president’s long grip on power.

Vucic became prime minister in 2014. In 2017, he was elected president, a traditionally ceremonial role that he has bolstered by maintaining influence over his SNS party.

‘Vucic is afraid of us’

Opposition parties and rights watchdogs accuse Vucic and his SNS party of bribing voters, stifling media freedom, violence against opponents, and ties with organised crime.

Vucic and his allies deny these allegations. But Serbia’s rating on Transparency International’s global corruption index has worsened gradually in recent years.

“Vucic is clearly afraid of us – it’s obvious. He knows that, for the first time in 16 years, the SNS is no longer the most popular political option in the country,” Golubovic said.

The students’ efficiency is down in part to its structure.

The old student parliament at the University of Belgrade has been replaced with plenums – daily assemblies where each group votes on its course of action. Working groups focus on strategy, donations, and security. Universities in different cities coordinate so demands remain broadly aligned.

This is why the students say they do things differently. One rule is to be leaderless, making it harder for authorities to disrupt the protests. Also, demonstrations must be peaceful, and any debris has to be cleaned up. Third, all decisions must be made democratically during hour-long plenary sessions in their university faculties.

“Even though the authorities mobilised criminal groups against the students and citizens participating in the protests, the students have remained focused on their goal: to oust a government they view as authoritarian and deeply corrupt,” said Natasa Kandic, a Serbian peace activist, sociologist, and founder of the Humanitarian Law Center (HLC) in Belgrade.

“For the first time in Serbia, they have managed to lead protests entirely without violence,” she said. “The video clips we see daily represent a new culture – one defined by irony, laughter, and the deliberate disregard for primitivism and political depravity.”

‘Serious and comprehensive plan’

State-affiliated media have maligned the students. Some Serbian authorities claimed that the group has no programme, and Vucic labelled them as “terrorists”. But their leaders, experts from different fields, claim that they have a plan.

The platform is officially titled the “Student Plan” and is divided into three sections. There are 11 points.



Ilija Srdanovic, a cardiologist and the lead candidate and ballot holder for the Student List, explained that the platform deliberately avoids setting fixed, precise deadlines for the proposed changes. He argued that such timelines can only be determined once contributors have gained insight into the “full current state of affairs”.

“[We plan] many things – too many to list – but the goal is to change the system,” said Srdanovic in a brief call to Al Jazeera.

During debates, the establishment of a special prosecutorial police unit, a law on the origin of assets, transitional justice and the renovation of rural medical clinics are some frequent themes.

Could this be implemented in the case of a victory? Kandic is sceptical.

“The student movement doesn’t possess a transformative potential – the capacity to drive social change, break with the past, and alter a political climate where convicted war criminals are celebrated, Kosovo is treated as part of Serbia, and politicians from neighboring countries are branded as enemies,” he said.

World.title: Fatal Custody
World.content:
Hope Hooton and Kellie Elliott feared their children were not safe with their fathers. Hope sought protection after her husband threatened suicide and later experienced a psychiatric crisis. Kellie documented years of domestic violence and abuse. Yet both fathers had unsupervised time with their children, whom they later killed.

Through the stories of these two mothers, Fault Lines investigates how evidence of danger can be missed, dismissed or fail to reach family courts at all. The film examines the push for equal custody, the failure to treat violence against a parent as a risk to children and the changes advocates say could prevent other families from suffering the same losses.

World.title: Rising costs and tight budgets strain Americans ahead of midterm elections
World.content:
Stacy Eichel, an empty nester in Florida, spent years balancing two jobs. One was in healthcare; the other was her own venture: a small business making custom-branded merchandise for corporate clients, such as coffee mugs and T-shirts that companies hand out at conferences and holiday parties.

For Eichel, the business was more than a paycheque. It was a side hustle for a woman who couldn’t sit still, who was always hungry for the next opportunity. It was the kind of business that thrived when companies had a little extra to spend on small branded trinkets to make an otherwise mundane corporate conference something memorable.

In September 2025, Eichel lost her job in marketing for a healthcare company after a merger. Suddenly, the business she had run on the side had to shoulder more of the burden of supporting her. Yet just as she needed it to provide more, the market for her products was shrinking.

Faced with uncertainty over trade policy and tariffs, alongside the growing use of artificial intelligence across the economy, companies have been tightening their spending. Custom-branded merchandise was becoming one more expense they could do without.

“The economy is such that fewer people are buying custom-branded swag because it’s more of a luxury item. When they have extra money in the budget, that’s what they’ll use it for, but now their budgets are very tight,” Eichel, who has cut back on her expenses, told Al Jazeera.

Eichel’s experience reflects a broader strain in the US labour market, where a paycheque does not necessarily translate into financial security. The headline unemployment rate captures people actively looking for work, but it does not tell the whole story of people who are working fewer hours than they want or juggling jobs that do not provide enough income.



The Department of Labor documents this through what is called the U-6 rate, a broader measure of unemployment and underemployment. It stands at an elevated 7.6 percent. While that’s down from 8.1 percent a year ago, having a job does not necessarily mean Americans are getting ahead financially.

The U-6 measure includes people who are working part-time because they cannot find full-time jobs, as well as those who want to work but have stopped looking for a job recently.

Wallet strains

Even people who are employed full-time are finding that their earnings do not stretch as far as they once did. An estimated 4.5 million Americans were working part-time because they could not find full-time work. Meanwhile, nine million Americans held multiple jobs, accounting for 5.5 percent of all employed workers, according to the most recent jobs report.

“Underemployment is one of the most misunderstood economic problems in America because it doesn’t always look like unemployment. It looks like a college graduate working retail despite having a degree, a former executive accepting a position paying half their previous salary, or a parent working two jobs because neither provides enough hours, benefits or income to support their family,” Tara Furiani, a workforce strategist based in Richmond, Virginia, told Al Jazeera.

Average hourly wages rose 3 percent over the past year, while consumer prices increased 3.7 percent, according to the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report released by the US Labor Department.

That means prices have risen faster than wages, leaving many workers with less purchasing power. Overall, prices rose 0.6 percent from the previous month, while average hourly wages increased by just 0.1 percent, adding to the financial pressure on households like Eichel’s.

Eichel has cut back on expenses and scaled down some of her usual spending, including dining out and takeout, and dropped her cable service.

“I never used to think before ordering in, and now we cook everything,” Eichel said.

With the midterm elections approaching, the cost of living is becoming a greater concern for voters. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found that the cost of living was the most important issue for voters, leading the next-closest issue by a double-digit margin, at 47 percent compared with 22 percent for “democratic norms and values”.

A separate Washington Post–ABC News–Ipsos poll found that voters trust Democrats over Republicans to handle the economy, 40 percent to 33 percent, marking the first time in 12 years that Democrats have held an advantage on the issue.



This comes as 44 percent of Americans said they had struggled to pay for at least one basic necessity over the past year, including transportation, rent or mortgage payments, medical care and food, according to a Pew Research Center poll released earlier this month.

Twenty percent of respondents said they had received food from a food bank or pantry over the past year.

Joshua Teicher, a New York City-based video producer in the advertising industry, said work began drying up after the COVID-19 pandemic, with opportunities dwindling further in recent years as companies tightened their budgets. Even the slow trickle of work has nearly dried up entirely.

Teicher told Al Jazeera that his financial circumstances have changed so significantly that he is now on Medicaid, government-subsidised healthcare for people in lower-income brackets. He said he is struggling to afford prescriptions and food.

“I’m having to go into my savings. Specifically, sometimes I don’t want to get a second cup of coffee because it’s like five bucks for an espresso or something like that. It’s also been harder to eat healthy. Grocery shopping, apples are just ridiculous. I find myself walking a couple of extra blocks to a cheaper store because they have cheaper apples, those sorts of things,” Teicher said.

He told Al Jazeera that his tight budget also prevents him from affording the knee surgery he needs. Cartilage in both knees has worn down. He was able to undergo surgery on his right knee to correct the problem, but cannot afford the same procedure on his left. As a result, one leg is now slightly longer than the other.

Petrol prices are another expense weighing on consumers. The average price for a gallon of gasoline (3.78 litres) on Monday was $4.29, according to the American Automobile Association (AAA), which tracks fuel prices daily. By comparison, the average price was $2.98 when the US and Israel first struck Iran in late February, leading to ongoing disruptions in the global market.

Market pressures

Even for Americans who have jobs, finding a better-paying position can be difficult. Although some industries have continued to add jobs, uncertainty about economic policy has contributed to what economists call a “low-hire, low-fire” labour market.

Employers are pulling back on hiring even as layoffs remain relatively low. The latest Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) from the Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that job openings and the number of workers quitting their jobs were largely unchanged.

“I have seen highly qualified people who have not been able to find a job for 12-18 months,” Babak Hafezi, a professor of international business at American University, told Al Jazeera.

With fewer opportunities available, workers who already have jobs may be reluctant to leave them, even if they are unhappy or want higher pay. Those looking for work face more competition for available positions, while people who are already employed may have less leverage to negotiate better salaries. That can make it harder for workers to improve their financial situations as everyday expenses continue to rise. This is leading some people who already work full-time to add on part-time jobs.



“We have people come in all the time who are teachers looking for a part-time job, or who are in other fields asking, ‘Do you know anyone hiring part-time? I just need 15–20 hours a week to make ends meet.’ At what point does this end?” Debbie Louis, who owns a coffee shop in Brooklyn, New York, told Al Jazeera.

Although industries such as hospitality and healthcare have added jobs over the last year, Hafezi said that growth could slow or reverse over the next year. He pointed to the potential impact of the Big Beautiful tax legislation, which could reduce funding for programmes that support rural hospitals, as well as immigration policies that have discouraged international travel to the US over the past year, hitting businesses that benefit from those revenues.

At the same time, US consumers are also dealing with the reality of reduced purchasing power.

“Tariffs and economic pressures from high inflation are affecting Americans’ purchasing power. As prices increase, unit consumption decreases [they buy less as] their paycheques don’t go as far,” Hafezi said.

“This ultimately leads Americans to feel poorer and less able to consume. That is the environment that many Americans in the ‘K-shaped’ economy are in.”

In a so-called K-shaped economy, wealthier US consumers continue to prosper while lower- and middle-income households fall behind. The Conference Board’s most recent consumer confidence report found that higher-income households, often supported by investment gains and greater financial reserves, are more optimistic than those in other income brackets.

“Ahead of the midterms, policymakers and employers should be examining not simply how many Americans are working, but whether available employment provides adequate wages, sufficient hours, predictable schedules, benefits and genuine opportunities for advancement. Because a paycheque and economic security are, again, not the same thing,” Furiani, the workforce strategist, added.

World.title: Carney, Erdogan launch ‘strong and resilient’ Canada-Turkiye partnership
World.content:
On trade, investment and innovation, leaders will work towards conclusion of a Canada-Turkiye Free Trade Agreement.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan have announced the launch of a Canada-Turkiye Strategic Partnership, backed by a three-year action plan.
