“In an increasingly complex global security environment, rising geopolitical uncertainties, and evolving humanitarian challenges, a strong and resilient Canada-Turkiye partnership is essential, providing a foundation to mitigate shared threats and capitalise on new opportunities,” said a statement by the two leaders on Thursday.

This comes as Carney is on a two-day visit to Turkiye, seeking to forge a new partnership as Canada looks to reduce its dependence on the United States.

The partnership’s three-year action plan rests on four pillars: trade and investment; defence and security; energy; and ties between people, the statement said.

On trade, investment and innovation, the two leaders agreed to “work toward successful conclusion of a Canada-Turkiye Free Trade Agreement”, it said. They will also expand bilateral trade and investments in priority sectors, including energy supply, defence production, aerospace, and artificial intelligence (AI).

On defence and security, the leaders “underlined their intent to deepen bilateral and multilateral cooperation”. They also agreed to “strengthen cooperation in support of peace and security in the Euro-Atlantic region and beyond including Ukraine, South Caucasus, and the Middle East, in particular Gaza”.

Meanwhile, energy ministers from both countries will work on areas such as liquefied natural gas, nuclear energy and critical minerals.



‘Launching a new era’

Speaking to reporters in Ankara alongside Carney on Thursday, Erdogan said the two countries “hope to increase our trade volume, which currently stands at around $3bn, to $5bn initially and then to $10bn through the steps we will take”.

He said the two sides had agreed to begin free trade agreement negotiations before the end of the year to boost trade and investment, adding that elevating Turkiye-Canada relations to the level of a strategic partnership would not be merely a symbolic step on paper.

“We have today overcome the disconnect that had persisted between Turkiye and Canada for many years. Now, we are launching a new era between Turkiye and Canada,” he said.

Canadian and Turkish leaders will convene next month in Ankara for the first round of trade talks, the joint statement said.

Carney is on the first bilateral visit by a Canadian prime minister to Turkiye, although he travelled to Ankara in July to attend the NATO summit.

He was scheduled to meet Erdogan and other officials before travelling to Istanbul for talks with Turkish business groups as the two countries seek to deepen trade ties.

The Canadian prime minister has sought to diversify partnerships and reduce reliance on the US amid an escalating trade war with US President Donald Trump, marked by US tariffs on Canadian goods, followed by retaliatory measures from Canada, as well as Trump’s statements questioning Canadian sovereignty.

World.title: Netanyahu promises Iran regime change: Can Israel topple Tehran government?
World.content:
Israel can inflict devastating damage on Iran, but analysts question its ability to overthrow Tehran’s government.

Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that overthrowing Iran’s government remains Israel’s “primary objective”, as he faces declining support in the polls before national elections next week.

His remarks came after conversations with United States President Donald Trump on Sunday and a visit to Israel by Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth. But Netanyahu offered no indication that Washington had agreed to join another offensive against Iran, let alone a campaign to bring down Iran’s leadership.

While Israel has the firepower to inflict serious damage on Iran, analysts told Al Jazeera, it lacks a clear strategy for translating military gains into the overthrow of Iran’s government. Air strikes alone are unlikely to achieve that objective, while a ground invasion would demand a far greater military commitment, they said.

A renewed offensive would also mean confronting a state that has already survived two rounds of attacks and retains the means to retaliate – both against Israel and its Gulf neighbours who are hosting US military assets. US backing, meanwhile, remains uncertain, with experts questioning Washington’s appetite for renewed fighting as it is yet to find a credible prospect of forcing Iran’s government to surrender to its demands.

Does Israel have the firepower?

Israel’s ability to attack Iran is not in doubt, experts say. Urban Coningham, a research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), told Al Jazeera that its offensive weapons stockpiles, and “aerial refuelling” capabilities give it a substantial advantage. “Israel could again establish air superiority and strike Iranian targets,” he said.



But while Israel can inflict serious damage, analysts are sceptical that it can accomplish regime change.

Netanyahu has portrayed Iran’s leaders as a major threat since his first term as prime minister in 1996. Addressing the US Congress that July, he said, “The most dangerous of these regimes is Iran, that has wed a cruel despotism to a fanatic militancy.”

Nearly 30 years later, US participation in the June 2025 war, and again in the campaign launched on February 28 this year, delivered the military intervention Netanyahu had long sought. The overthrow of Iran’s government, however, did not follow. Netanyahu himself acknowledged the limits of airpower in March, saying, “You can’t do it only from the air.”

“There has to be a ground component, as well,” he added, without explaining what that would involve.

Caglar Kurc, an assistant professor at Abdullah Gul University in Kayseri, Turkiye, said bombing could weaken Iran’s military but not necessarily eliminate its ability to fight back. “Airpower can degrade military capabilities but cannot fully destroy offensive capabilities,” he told Al Jazeera. “Well-hidden systems would survive.”

Overthrowing the government, Kurc said, would require a willingness to deploy troops and remain on the ground for years. Israel can also no longer assume that covert methods used in earlier attacks would prove equally effective again.

Coningham described intelligence assets as “use and burn” because deploying these methods risks exposing networks that Iranian security services will investigate and disrupt.

Israel still has “human intelligence assets on the ground”, he said, while “cyberattacks” could also form part of another campaign. But using those capabilities risks revealing and sacrificing them, making the prospect of a tangible military gain an important consideration.

Covert operations and cyberattacks, in his assessment, do not offer a clear route to overthrowing Iran’s government. Coningham was similarly sceptical that Kurdish or Baloch armed groups could provide the ground force needed to challenge the state. In March, the Trump administration was said to be actively discussing providing arms to opposition Kurdish groups, according to CNN, which cited Kurdish and US officials. But this never progressed.

“Kurdish groups lacked the military capabilities to take on the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC),” he said.

Iran can still retaliate

Iran also does not need to match Israel aircraft-for-aircraft to make another offensive very costly, experts say.



Sidharth Kaushal, a senior research fellow at RUSI, told Al Jazeera that the “Iranians likely retain sizeable stocks of missiles,” even if damage to their targeting systems may constrain their effectiveness.

“The actual antiship missile stockpiles likely remain large, both because they are comparatively easy to make, and Iran has in-housed much of the production of older Chinese ASCMs, and Iran’s southern mountains provide natural shelters against air attack,” Kaushal said.

Coningham said that, for Israel, sustaining its defences would be more difficult, with previous exchanges having drawn down interceptor stocks.

Repeated attacks also impose a financial burden, as Israel will be intercepting relatively inexpensive Iranian drones with far more costly defensive weapons. Over a prolonged exchange, that imbalance could place further pressure on Israel’s interceptor supplies, while Iran retains the capacity to mass-produce more cheap weapons for a lot longer.

Would Washington join another attack?

Analysts consider this unlikely, pointing to diverging political interests between Tel Aviv and Washington, with Trump facing pressure to avoid renewed escalation before the US midterm elections.

The Financial Times reported this week that an Israeli proposal for renewed strikes had failed to secure Trump’s approval, although it suggested disagreement about immediate action rather than Washington ruling out future attacks altogether.

Without Trump’s participation, Coningham said, Israel would lack US capabilities for striking deeply buried facilities. These include the 30,000-pound GBU-57 bunker-busting bombs that US B-2 bombers dropped on Iran’s Fordow and Natanz nuclear facilities in June 2025. Designed to penetrate deeply buried targets, the weapons gave Washington an offensive capability Israel could not match on its own.

Coningham also suggested that, if Israel were to attack without US support, Iran might concentrate its retaliation on Israeli territory while avoiding US targets and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz.

Such an approach would seek to punish Israel without drawing Washington directly into the fighting, potentially further isolating a country already widely ostracised by the international community amid its genocide in Gaza.

But analysts say the central obstacle that could ultimately prevent Israel from attacking Iran is the gap between its ability to destroy military targets and its capacity to force political change within Iran.

“You cannot change a regime unless you are prepared to deploy troops and stay in the country for some years. Israel cannot control Iran. The United States would not engage in another regime change, which could take decades,” Kurc added.

World.title: Germany arrests Ukrainian man accused of spying for Russia
World.content:
Military has raised the threat level of ​Russian sabotage against German troops and facilities.

A Ukrainian national has been arrested in Germany on suspicion of spying for Russia, German authorities have said.

Germany’s federal prosecutors confirmed in a statement on Thursday that the man, identified as Vadym Y, was arrested in the state of Brandenburg 85km (53 miles) west of Berlin.

Prosecutors said the suspect had been in touch with the Russian secret service via an intermediary since at least July 2025.

The suspect had gathered military intelligence on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition and explosives, as well as military personnel and defence installations at locations designed to secure NATO’s eastern flank, prosecutors added.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who is currently meeting with regional leaders in Montenegro for the EU-Western Balkans Summit, said he was “not surprised” by the news of a suspected Russian spy.

The arrest comes after German authorities blamed Russia for drone attacks that officials said are part of Moscow’s “shadow war” on the country.

Germany’s armed forces on Wednesday raised the threat level of Russian sabotage against their troops and facilities to “significant” for the first time – the ‌second-highest level on their internal threat scale, German news reports noted.

The move followed the discovery in mid-September of a crashed drone carrying high explosives near the Wunstorf ⁠airbase in Lower Saxony, German news sites WDR and Sueddeutsche Zeitung reported.

The drone resembled another unmanned aircraft – also laden with explosives – used in a failed attack at Leipzig/Halle airport in August. Unlike the Leipzig incident, which authorities said targeted civilian cargo aircraft, investigators believe the Wunstorf drone targeted military aircraft, according to an internal military document seen by German media.



The report also noted a pattern of suspected Russian reconnaissance across Germany, including drones flown over a missile defence site in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, and a camouflaged camera found filming a strategically important railway station in Minden, in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia.

Martin Jaeger, head of Germany’s BND spy service, told lawmakers this month that Russia’s undeclared “shadow war” against Germany and its allies was escalating further and has “taken on a new, more dangerous character”.

“Germany is at risk of being drawn into a violent conflict with Russia,” he told an intelligence oversight committee at Germany’s parliament, the Bundestag.

Moscow denied involvement and has maintained it is not involved in sabotage or hybrid attacks on European nations.

World.title: Ilhan Omar home raid, Haines attack: Inside rise in violence on officials
World.content:
US Congresswoman Ilhan Omar has her home raided; Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs following an attack.

United States Congresswoman Ilhan Omar has been forced to move out of her Washington, DC residence because of safety concerns after her home was raided, amid growing threats of violence against politicians.

Last week, US federal agents searched Omar’s home with what a Justice Department spokesperson described as a “judicially authorised search warrant”, adding that the raid was part of an “ongoing federal criminal investigation”.

According to NBC News, which cited one person familiar with the matter, charges against Omar may include conspiracy and making false statements in her immigration paperwork.

For years, Somalia-born Omar, who is Muslim, has been the target of right-wing conspiracy theories about her immigration status, including allegations that she had married her brother.

The Minnesota congresswoman has repeatedly denied the allegations as “disgusting lies”.

She has drawn the particular ire of US President Donald Trump, who views her as a thorn in his side and has threatened to deport her.

Omar came to the US in 1995 at age 12 and was naturalised as a US citizen in 2000. Since January 2019, she has served as a congressional representative for the state of Minnesota.

But on Wednesday, she told the US news outlet MS NOW that following the raid on her Washington apartment, she could no longer live there.

“Because our address has been public and with the death threats that I deal with, it’s no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids visiting off and on, having people track them,” she said.



The raid on Omar’s home comes as violent attacks on politicians have grown more frequent.

She, herself, has been physically assaulted. In January this year, Omar was sprayed with an unknown substance by an assailant while calling for the abolition of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency at a town hall meeting in Minneapolis.

On Monday this week, Australian independent MP Helen Haines, who has championed climate action and advocated for improved working conditions as a lawmaker, was hit by a car outside her electorate office, resulting in the amputation of both of her legs.

Australian police said it was a “targeted attack” and warned of growing “online extremism” and recorded a rise in abuse, threats and intimidation targeting lawmakers.

‘Dangerous escalation’

The violent attack on Haines was particularly shocking. Her attacker, identified as Brendan Nugent, 43, allegedly drove past her before turning his car around and veering towards Haines, pinning her against her car.

Australia’s Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said the driver then reversed before ramming her again.

Sofia Collignon, a reader in comparative politics and director of the Mile End Institute of Research at Queen Mary University London, said instances of physical violence, such as the attack on Haines, are still “relatively rare in terms of numbers”.

“It’s very upsetting to see that more and more people in public life are paying a very high price for doing something that is a public good,” Collignon told Al Jazeera.

Abuse online often comes before physical attacks, however.

She said that women – and, in particular, women of colour in politics – are facing high levels of abuse on social media, and this is taking a worrying toll.

“We are seeing from research that this is having an effect on how they [women] behave in politics, or whether they change the way that they campaign, change the type of issues that they advocate or sometimes completely refrain from participating on social media,” she said.

According to a 2023 report by the Centre for Economic Policy Research (CEPR), which assessed 12 years of data on attacks against Italian politicians, “marginally elected women are approximately three times more likely to experience an attack” than marginally elected men.

The Princeton School of Public and International Affairs Bridging the Gap initiative, which tracks political violence in the US, found that there has been a “dangerous escalation in the political violence risk environment in the US, including a series of high-profile assassinations and aggressive federal immigration operations”, in 2025



“Incidents of threats and harassment spiked, and leading community safety practitioners reported that the demand for de-escalation support surged to new heights,” it added.

In the case of Omar, Trump has repeatedly targeted the congresswoman since his first term of office over her Somali origins.

He has called her a “sick person”, an “extremist”, and “garbage”, among other inflammatory language.

Other Muslim or progressive congresswomen have also been subjected to Trump’s rhetoric. In February, he wrote in a post on his Truth Social platform that Omar and Palestinian American congresswoman Rashida Tlaib should be sent “back from where they came from”.

But Trump himself has also contended with political violence. In 2024, during his campaign rally, Trump was shot in the ear by a spectator attending the rally.

Then, Trump ally Charlie Kirk was killed in 2025 by a man named Tyler Robinson, who said he had carried out the attack because he had “enough of his [Kirk’s] hatred”.

‘Fierce political polarisation’ to blame

Online threats of attacks on politicians have led to real-life killings for some time.

In 2016, British MP Jo Cox was killed in her constituency while campaigning to remain in the European Union ahead of the referendum by a man named Thomas Mair, who had shouted: “This is for Britain.”

In 2021, Conservative British MP David Amess was killed by a man named Ali Harbi Ali, who claimed that he had targeted the representative over his vote for air strikes on Syria.

In 2026, former Conservative MP and spokesperson for the far-right Reform UK party, Ann Widdecombe, was killed by a man named Joshua Kerry, who has been charged with engaging in conduct in preparation for “acts of terrorism”, including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

Collignon said she believes social media has “lowered the bar” for bad-faith actors to threaten politicians, which explains the increase in the volume of threats.

“For example, what people consider to be acceptable ways of referring to politicians or to talk to them are more and more aggressive. They can find it acceptable to use more aggressive terms, partly because of the polarisation in politics,” she said.

“It’s not an issue that we observed only on the right or on the left, but we observe it very often on the fringes of the spectrum. They find that it is acceptable to use unacceptable language or behaviour in the pursuit of their political goals. So that means intimidating a politician is something that they kind of condone.”

According to an Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) 2026 annual report, local officials faced a “persistent and evolving threat of violence in 2025” in an analysis of 2,653 incidents of violence that targeted local officials globally.

The data show that the recorded incidents worldwide have spread from 88 countries and territories in 2025 to 97 in 2024.

“Over the past five years, ACLED records at least 13,900 incidents in 138 countries and territories,” said the report. “Local officials often become lightning rods for broader societal grievances. Large-scale protest movements in recent years have directed their frustration and anger at local authorities, viewed as the nerve endings of a failing or corrupt state.



“Especially in Europe and the United States, a pernicious mix of fierce political polarisation and unchecked competition for political dominance exposes politicians, and especially local elected officials, to a growing trend of harassment, abuse and violence.”

Moreover, a 2026 report by the Inter-Parliamentary Union, a global international organisation of national parliaments, revealed that of the 519 parliamentarians who participated in research across five national case studies and joined a global survey, 71 percent of all respondents reported having “experienced violence by the public, whether online, offline or both”.

“Violence is heavily concentrated online, with between 65 percent and 77 percent of MPs across the case studies reporting online abuse,” it found.

However, Collignon said the line between online threats of violence and being physically assaulted has become increasingly blurred.

“Let’s say that I check my social media accounts at home, a place where I should feel safe,” she said. “But then, if my phone is showing me constant abuse, threats of violence, very nasty behaviour, then I am receiving all of these attacks in my living room.

“We currently are operating in a space where lines are blurry, and I think we shouldn’t be thinking about online violence as something that just happens in the digital sphere. It’s something that has consequences for the individual in their daily lives, and the way in which they are involved in politics.”

World.title: FIFA’s Infantino made to wait on Asian support as chief coy at AFC session
World.content:
‘We’re not against anyone and we’re not in favour of anyone,’ says AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa.

Share FIFA’s Infantino made to wait on Asian support as chief coy at AFC session on social media

The president of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) gave no hint about the body’s support — or opposition — to the re-election of Gianni Infantino as FIFA president.

The votes of the AFC’s 47 members could be critical when Infantino seeks his fourth term as the head of global football’s governing body in an election in March. Infantino faces strong opposition in Europe, and has staunch support in Africa — and Asia could provide the swing votes.

Opposition candidates have until November 18 to file. So far, none have

“For people who try to divide us, this is not going to happen,” AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa said on Thursday in a brief address to close a two-day session in Tokyo.

He gave no indication that the AFC as a body would take a position on Infantino.

That differed from just over two months ago, when the AFC joined the football governing bodies in North and Central America and Europe in saying Infantino committed a “fundamental breach of trust”.

Recent reports and his short talk on Thursday indicate Sheikh Salman may have moderated his views. Asia appears split. Qatar, the host of the 2022 World Cup, has come out in support of Infantino while Jordan has declared its opposition.

“We’re not against anyone and we’re not in favour of anyone,” Sheikh Salman said.

“We’re always going to express our feelings and try to do what’s best and what’s right for football. Not just in Asia.”

Meetings closed to media

Recent AFC meetings in a five-star hotel in Tokyo were closed to the media. The conference was shown on the football confederation’s YouTube channel, and presentations were orchestrated without reporters present.



Infantino seldom speaks with the media. He has been travelling and electioneering in Asia, but did not appear publicly at the seminars in Tokyo. During the week, FIFA’s media office promoted his presence in Bhutan and Bangladesh, which have small federations that each have one vote — the same as powerful football nations such as Spain and France.

Infantino apologised last week in Zurich to FIFA’s 37-member ruling council — which he chairs — for “mistakes” he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2bn selloff plan for the World Cup.

An Associated Press tally shows 87 of the 211 federations have indicated support for Infantino, either in individual comments or by endorsing statements of support by their regional confederations.

Sheikh Salman made passing reference to the turmoil in the Middle East and its effect on football in the region.

“We know that the world is changing and football, I think, gets affected as well from what’s happening,” he said, “whether it’s political, economic, or whatever it is.

“People are following the news, what’s happening in the Middle East. It’s important for us.”

Asian Cup in Saudi on track

The Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January is going ahead despite deadly attacks in the country by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, said Muhammed Q Alghamdi, a spokesman for the organising committee. There is a rising fear of an escalation in hostilities.

The Asian Cup is set for January 7 to February 5, with 24 teams playing matches in three cites — Riyadh, Jeddah, and Khobar. Reports suggest it may be too late to seek an alternative venue.

“I’d like to start by acknowledging that we are monitoring the regional developments and we’re working closely with our counterparts at the AFC to make sure we can provide an exceptional tournament,” Alghamdi said.

“I stand before you now, and I am pleased to say that daily life is ongoing in Saudi Arabia. Our job is to be ready, and we will be ready.”

World.title: Police investigate Married at First Sight Australia after 'inappropriate' allegations
World.content:
Married at First Sight Australia is facing fresh controversy after police launched an investigation into the hit reality TV show.

New South Wales Police told BBC News that inquiries had taken place "following a report of inappropriate content being shared".

Channel Nine, which broadcasts Married at First Sight Australia, confirmed that it was "aware of a police investigation" involving the show's production company.

It is the latest blow for the show, after a BBC News investigation earlier this year into MAFS Australia revealed cast members said they had not been told their partners had previous drug and violence convictions.

Those revelations led to a warning from Australia's media watchdog, which called them "serious and disturbing".

The British version of Married at First Sight, known to many as MAFS UK, was separately plunged into crisis in May after BBC Panorama reported rape allegations from two female cast members - allegations the men involved have denied.

MAFS UK is made by a different production company to the Australian version.

World.title: At least four dead after storm brings flooding to southern France
World.content:
At least four people have died in France, and one other has been injured, after flooding caused by Storm Adam.

The storm triggered widespread flooding across southern France on Tuesday, inundating streets and disrupting transport.

The deaths included two women aged 86 and 26 who were found drowned in a cellar in the Bouches-du-RhÃ´ne region.

Corsica was also hit by severe weather. Local media reported that a 4x4 vehicle was swept away by floodwaters on Tuesday - one of the occupants escaped through a window, but another man was found dead. Authorities have not released further details about the fourth death.

In the towns of MouriÃ¨s and Saint-Martin-de-Crau, between Montpellier and Marseille, dozens of residents were accommodated in emergency shelters after the floods hit. Officials said one person had been injured in that area.

Roads and train lines âin â the area were also disrupted, Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot wrote in a post âon X.

"The water has risen to unprecedented levels," Jacques Witkowski, prefect of the Bouches-du-RhÃ´ne department, said in a statement on Wednesday.

Witkowski expressed "a thought for all those who are in distress", adding: "We are mobilised at an exceptional level to resolve several issues."

World.title: French weekend protests to be limited to union demos only, says Macron
World.content:
Only authorised union protests will be allowed in French towns and cities on Saturday, President Emmanuel Macron has said, after demonstrations across the country turned violent last weekend.

Speaking as some cities including Lyon and Nice imposed complete bans, Macron said "illegitimate" protests would not be allowed but unions would be offered alternative routes so that businesses could be protected.

Big demonstrations against the high cost of living and school conditions were overshadowed last Saturday by riots and looting that saw business and historic buildings destroyed.

Interior Minister Jean-Didier Berger said police deployments would be increased by 20% compared to last weekend, after the government was accused of being blindsided by the scale of the unrest.

France's justice minister said on Thursday that 217 people had been jailed over last weekend's disorder after being convicted in fast-track trials, with that number expected to rise.

GÃ©rald Darmanin said 2,700 people had been arrested across France and more than 1,000 have appeared in court.

Half of those detained had no prior criminal record, he said, according to Le Figaro newspaper.

Macron met intelligence services and ministers on Thursday, to prepare for the next national day of protests on Saturday.

"The general recommendation is that there should be no demonstrations. Those who want to continue to demonstrate, when they are trade union organisations, will have alternative routes proposed by the prefects," the French president announced. "When they're not union organisations, wherever possible, they'll be banned."

He attacked what he called "political and even seditious acts organised by far-left groups that aim to bring down the Republic".

Curfews were imposed in several cities in the aftermath of the weekend rioting, and Macron said the government wanted a return to calm.

The gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement was behind many of last weekend's protests and Paris authorities have said several of their proposed marches have been banned.

In Lyon, France's third-biggest city, regional authorities have imposed a blanket ban on demonstrations.

"In light of the mobilisation that is circulating and in view of the events of 17 October, the prefect has decided to prohibit by decree any demonstration in the city of Lyon this Saturday," the RhÃ´ne prefecture said in a statement.

Similar announcements have been made in Toulon on the south coast, the centre of Rouen in the north-west, and Grenoble in the east.

Partial curfews variously restricting the movement of young people and gatherings have been in place this week in cities including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon in the south as well as Lille and other towns in the north.

Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu promised a "massive" deployment of police officers this week to deal with any unrest this weekend, but some officers have told French media they are not trained to deal with large crowds.

World.title: Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya
World.content:
Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian â have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi.

Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year.

No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed.

The Austrian and Swiss governments have both confirmed the release of their citizens.

The Swiss government said Abbt was free and on her way back to Switzerland, while Austria said Gretzmacher had been released after "intensive diplomatic efforts".

"We are all very relieved that Eva G. is free again after more than 21 months... For many months, we worked closely, discreetly, and in a spirit of trust with our regional, European, and international partners. These joint efforts have paid off," Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger said in a statement.

World.title: Teacher in Oregon shooting said she pretended to be dead to survive
World.content:
Some readers may find this article distressing.

A 54-year-old teacher who survived a mass shooting at an Oregon elementary school said she pretended to be dead so the gunman would not shoot her again.

Becky Drury, a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School, said in a statement shared with US media that as she tried to shut her classroom door, the gunman shot her and she fell to the floor.

"I did the only thing I could do, which was to pretend to be dead in the hope he would not shoot me again," Drury said.

The attacker - who has been identified as a 16-year-old former student at the school - killed three students and a teacher before a parent from the school fatally shot him.

In her first remarks since the 15 October shooting in Bend, Oregon, Drury said that she went to see what was happening outside the special-education classroom, and after spotting the shooter, she tried to shut the door.

The attacker still managed to shoot her, so she could not help any of the children in the classroom.

"Lying on the floor, I saw that my left hand was almost completely severed from the gunshot, and my other arm was also severely injured," she said. "I could not get up, defend myself, or protect anyone else."

Drury suffered serious but not life-threatening harm from the shooting, which killed five-year-old Rhoam Summer, an eight and eleven-year-old, and 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert.

Police have said another teacher - who has not been named - attempted to disarm the gunman by throwing her mobile phone. She was not injured.

A father of two other children who had followed the suspect into the school then shot and killed the attacker, who officials named as Griffin J John II.

Reports had emerged that another teacher threw herself on top of a student to protect the child during the shooting, but Drury said she wanted to clear the record about what happened on 15 October.

"I know there has been contradictory reporting about my actions that day, but the truth is I was shot before I had any chance to act," she said in her statement.

Police have not yet shared a motive for the suspect, who officials say was a special-education needs student at Silver Rail.

Drury said what happened in the classroom was "unimaginable".

"[L]ike so many in this community, my heart is broken for everyone affected by this tragedy," she said.

World.title: Two killed in Houthi attack on airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, authorities say
World.content:
Yemen's Houthi movement has said it carried out an attack on an airport in eastern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday evening, which Saudi authorities said killed two people and injured eight others.

The Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation identified those killed at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam as a Saudi citizen and an Indian resident.

It did not say what type of attack occurred, but the Iran-backed Houthis said on Thursday that the airport was one of the sites they had targeted with drones and missiles over the previous 48 hours.

Two more people were killed on Wednesday morning by debris from a drone that was intercepted elsewhere in Eastern Province, the Saudi energy ministry said.

The drone was intercepted as it attempted to target a processing facility owned by Saudi Arabia's state oil company Aramco in the Shaybah oil field, where a contractor's vehicle was set ablaze, according to the ministry.

It identified the dead as residents from the Philippines and Nepal.

The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, did not claim the attack on the oil field.

In addition to Dammam's airport, he said they had targeted the Saudi defence ministry's headquarters building in the capital, Riyadh, an Aramco facility in the Red Sea city of Yanbu, and Abha International Airport in the south of the country.

The Saudi-led coalition supporting the Yemeni government in its war against the Houthis said four drones were intercepted over Eastern Province on Wednesday night, and that another four were intercepted over the provinces of Riyadh and Medina on Thursday.

At least 21 people have now been killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi airports since the start of October, according to Saudi authorities.

One missile strike on Riyadh's international airport on 10 October killed 13 people and injured 308 others â the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.

World.title: Ilhan Omar says 'bizarre' pre-dawn raid on her home is forcing her to move out
World.content:
Minnesota Representative Ilhan Omar has said she can no longer live in her Washington DC home after it was searched by federal agents last week, fearing her address has been exposed after the raid.

"With the death threats that I deal with, it's not, it's no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids," she told MS NOW, external.

In Omar's first public interview since the pre-dawn search of her home, she detailed how Homeland Security Investigations agents seized over a dozen items, including cell phones and notebooks, as part of an investigation.

The government has not said what crime Omar is accused of but that the raid was "part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation".

The search follows multiple comments from officials that cast doubt on Omar's US citizenship, which she received in 2000 after her arrival from Kenya.

More than a dozen subpoenas have also been issued to members of Omar's family, as part of the investigation, and it was reported that her personal computers and passport were among the items that were seized.

Recalling the hourslong raid of her home with MS NOW, Omar said: "It obviously did freak all of us out."

Omar said agents began "pounding on the doors" of her home at around 06:00 EDT (11:00 BST) on 12 October, startling her and her husband, who were both in bed.

"We were screaming," she said, as the couple ran downstairs to see what was happening, calling the incident "so bizarre".

The Minnesota Democrat estimated that between15 to 25 agents encircled her home, all of whom she said "conducted themselves in a decent way".

Agents presented Omar with a warrant at the door after she asked for one.

She then watched from the couch as agents spent roughly five hours going from room to room, Omar said, leaving with a total of 17 items, including multiple cellphones, notebooks, and her husband's camera from the 1960s.

The BBC contacted the Justice Department for comment after being referred by the DHS.

Omar again criticised the government's investigation, suggesting that it was meant to be intimidating.

Immediately following the raid last week, she posted a statement online where she called it "an outrageous abuse of power" and "weaponisation of federal law enforcement to target political enemies".

Former President Barack Obama has also blasted the federal probe, saying in a lengthy statement that it was "so appalling".

Omar, who has represented Minnesota since 2018, has long been a target of President Donald Trump's, who has repeatedly suggested she "go back" to Somalia.

He has denied any involvement in her investigation, saying it has "nothing to do with me".

At an Ohio rally in October, Trump referred to the search of her home, saying: "I don't know what they're doing with it, but I can tell you this: she's a disaster."

The congresswoman, however, rejected the president's response, arguing that "he's got everything to do with it".

"You know, this goes back to 2019 when he was screaming about the fact that, you know, I, I need to be sent back, I need to be deported."

World.title: YouTuber arrested after popular Indian finance influencer's suicide
World.content:
A 27-year-old finance influencer's suicide in India has been mired in allegations of cyberbullying and started a conversation around who should give financial advice to investors.

V Harish - who ran a hugely popular Instagram account called "Finance with Harish" - was found dead on Tuesday morning at his home near Chennai, capital of the southern state of Tamil Nadu.

His suicide came just weeks after his account was disabled by Meta after complaints of irregularities.

In a complaint lodged with the police, his father J Vinayagam has alleged that his son took his life because of online harassment by Jason Samuel, a YouTuber and CEO of tech-centric venture studio Zemuria.

Police arrested Samuel on Thursday under suspicion of trying to "extort money from Harish" and posting "defamatory videos against him on social media".

BBC Tamil has not been able to reach him for comment. Earlier, he denied wrongdoing in a post on X.

The case has brought into focus the growing influence of financial content creators in India, where millions of first-time investors increasingly turn to social media for market advice.

World.title: Cost of Living: Abiodun to cut food prices, expand bus fleet
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has announced plans to introduce a government-backed bulk food purchase scheme to reduce the cost of essential commodities, while promising to expand the state’s mass transit fleet to ease transportation challenges facing workers and other residents.

Abiodun disclosed this during a stakeholders’ meeting with organised labour representatives from the Ijebu axis in Ijebu-Ode, where he reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to workers’ welfare and policies aimed at improving the living conditions of residents.

The proposed bulk purchase scheme, which will be implemented through the planned Gateway Trading Corporation, is designed to enable residents to access essential food items and household commodities at more affordable prices through government-supported purchasing arrangements.

The governor said the initiative was conceived in response to the rising cost of living and followed a suggestion by the state Chairman of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Hameed Ademola-Benco.

He explained that bulk purchasing would enable the government to negotiate more favourable prices for essential commodities, thereby providing economic relief to households facing rising food costs.

According to him, the initiative could also stimulate competition in the open market, as traders may be encouraged to review their prices in response to the availability of essential goods at lower rates through the government-backed platform.

Abiodun assured the labour leaders that his administration would work towards making the scheme operational, stressing that government policies must address the practical economic challenges confronting workers and other residents.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

On transportation, the governor promised to increase the number of mass transit buses available to government workers and members of the public.

He said the planned expansion was in response to concerns raised by organised labour over the need for more buses to ease daily commuting, reduce transportation costs and improve the movement of workers and residents across the state.

Abiodun explained that improving public transportation remained an important part of efforts to enhance workers’ welfare and reduce the financial pressures associated with daily travel.

The governor also addressed concerns raised by the labour representatives over leave allowance and the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), assuring them that the issues were receiving the necessary attention.

On education, Abiodun described teachers as indispensable to the growth and development of Ogun State, noting that their responsibilities extended beyond classroom instruction to character formation, discipline and the preparation of young people for responsible leadership.

He said the quality of education in any society depended largely on the competence and commitment of its teachers, adding that their influence played a significant role in shaping the future of individuals and the nation.

Reflecting on his personal experience, the governor said quality teaching and proper upbringing had helped shape his values and contributed to his journey in life.

He disclosed that his administration had constructed and renovated about 1,600 classrooms, employed hundreds of teachers over the past seven years and introduced reforms aimed at improving teaching and learning in public schools.

Abiodun commended Ogun teachers for their performance, which he said had earned them recognition and awards at national and international levels.

He also applauded students from the state for their achievements in academic competitions and educational assessments, describing their performance as a reflection of the efforts of the government, teachers, parents and other stakeholders to sustain high educational standards.

The governor said the meeting was convened to appreciate organised labour for its support since the inception of his administration and to provide an opportunity for constructive engagement on issues affecting workers and the wider public.

He commended the labour leaders for their contributions and suggestions, stressing that regular consultations with stakeholders were essential to developing policies that addressed the needs of the people.

In their separate remarks, the Ogun State NLC Chairman, Comrade Hameed Ademola-Benco; the state Chairman of the Trade Union Congress (TUC), Comrade Akeem Lasisi; and the state Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Comrade Sewakanu Noah, alongside other labour leaders, commended the governor for what they described as development across various sectors of the state.

The labour leaders acknowledged the administration’s payment of salaries and allowances, regular promotions and settlement of outstanding gratuities and pensions.

They, however, called for a review of the Contributory Pension Scheme, the establishment of a Ministry of Labour Affairs and increased subventions to tertiary institutions.

The labour leaders also pledged their support for candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections, expressing confidence in the party’s leadership.

They said they needed “someone who will serve with dignity, beautiful at heart and beautiful in character.”

World.title: Reps consider bill to ban compulsory multi-year advance rent in FCT
World.content:
The House of Representatives on Thursday passed for first reading a bill seeking to regulate advance rent payments and prohibit landlords in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) from compulsorily demanding more than one year’s rent in advance.

The Federal Capital Territory Advance Rent Regulation and Tenants’ Protection Bill, 2026 (HB.2839), sponsored by Paul Nnamchi (APC, Enugu), with Ahmed Doro (PDP, Katsina) as co-sponsor, also seeks to establish a regulatory authority to protect tenants and landlords from unlawful rental practices.

The bill proposes that landlords, estate agents, property managers or anyone acting on behalf of a landlord must not demand, receive or compel a tenant to pay more than 12 months’ rent in advance as a condition for granting, renewing or continuing a tenancy.

It also seeks to prevent landlords and agents from circumventing the proposed restriction through additional charges, compulsory service charges, artificial renewal of tenancy agreements or other arrangements designed to force tenants to pay more than a year’s rent upfront.

The bill, a copy of which was obtained by PREMIUM TIMES, says the proposed law would apply to both residential and commercial tenancies in the FCT.

Under the proposed legislation, tenants could voluntarily pay more than 12 months’ rent in advance, but only where the offer is initiated by the tenant and is not imposed as a condition by the landlord.

“A landlord, estate agent, property manager or other person acting on behalf of a landlord shall not demand, receive or compel a tenant to pay more than twelve months’ rent in advance as a condition…”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The bill further requires that such payments be made without coercion, discrimination, threats or retaliation and that the agreement be documented in writing.

Proposed FCT rent authority

The legislation proposes the establishment of the Federal Capital Territory Rent Regulation and Tenants’ Protection Authority to administer and enforce the law.

The authority would be empowered to receive and investigate complaints, monitor landlords, estate agents and property managers, issue compliance notices, facilitate mediation and order refunds where unlawful rent payments have been made.

It would also maintain a public register of letting agents where registration is required, establish complaint offices and electronic reporting channels across the FCT, including satellite towns, and publish periodic reports on rental practices and enforcement outcomes.

The proposed authority would also be able to order a landlord or agent to refund an unlawful payment within 30 days where it determines that rent was received in violation of the law.

A person who knowingly demands or receives more than the permitted advance rent could face a fine of between ₦500,000 and ₦5 million, while a body corporate could be fined between ₦5 million and ₦20 million.

The court could additionally order a refund, compensation for proven loss or payment of lawful costs.

The bill also seeks to prohibit unlawful eviction practices, including threats or violence, disconnection of essential services, removal or destruction of a tenant’s property, changing locks without lawful authority and other forms of self-help.

However, the proposed law preserves the rights of landlords to recover rent lawfully due and recover possession of their property through due process.

Rising rents in Abuja

The proposed legislation comes amid persistent concerns over the cost of renting accommodation in Abuja.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in July 2025 that residents across the FCT were struggling with rising rents and arbitrary increases in rent, agency fees, agreement fees and caution fees.

Residents disclosed that the rising cost of accommodation was forcing some people to leave their homes and neighbourhoods for cheaper areas, sometimes with poorer infrastructure and longer commuting distances.

The proposed bill is therefore targeting one of the major pressures confronting tenants: the requirement to raise large sums at once before securing or retaining accommodation.

Meanwhile, in 2022, a similar bill sponsored by a former senator for Kogi West, Smart Adeyemi, scaled second reading at the Senate.

The bill sought to regulate the mode of payment of rent in the FCT by cutting down advance payment of rent from one or two years by tenants to three months and subsequent monthly payments.

The problem is not peculiar to Abuja.

In Lagos, where the cost of accommodation has also become a major concern, the state government introduced the Lagos State Tenancy and Recovery of Premises Bill, 2025, which sought, among other things, to limit advance rent, regulate estate agents and provide mechanisms for tenants to challenge unfair rent increases.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the Lagos proposal sought to prevent landlords from demanding more than one year’s rent from new tenants, while sitting tenants on periodic payment arrangements could not be forced to pay more than three months in advance.

The Lagos proposal also sought to address excessive agency fees, illegal eviction tactics and prolonged disputes between landlords and tenants.

World.title: Alleged Murder: Court warns defence against delay in trial of four IPOB members
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja, on Wednesday warned defence counsel against delay in the trial of four suspected members of the outlawed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) charged with kidnapping and killing of an officer of the State Security Service (SSS).

Justice Joyce Abdulmalik gave the warming after two lawyers, Kelvin Ekwe and Geoffrey Uwadiegwu, who appeared for the defendants, made an application for adjournment.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the defendants are Michael Okafor, alias Onyechimeleze; Chinedu Chukwudozie, alias Kante; Chibunna Olisa; and Chigozie Olisa, alias Ability.

They were arraigned before Justice Abdulmalik on 28 September on a six-count charge of terrorism and kidnapping.

The prosecution alleged that the defendants conspired to commit acts of terrorism and were involved in the abduction of Ekpenyong Owoh, while he was travelling from Port Harcourt in Rivers to Awka.

They were further accused of taking the operative hostage and killing him.

The suspects were also accused of belonging to the proscribed IPOB and its armed wing, the Eastern Security Network, as well as involvement in activities allegedly linked to terrorism.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In addition, the prosecution alleged that the suspects were involved in the unlawful possession of firearms, including an AK-47 rifle, and pump-action gun, in connection with the alleged offences.

The charges followed investigations into the circumstances surrounding the abduction and killing of the officer and the alleged activities of the defendants.

The defendants, however, pleaded not guilty to the charge.

The court session

When the case was called on Wednesday, Munirat Oladunjoye, who represented the prosecution, informed the court that the matter was fixed for trial following the defendants’ denial of the allegations.

She told the court that the prosecution applied to shield the identity of their witnesses pursuant to Section 232(3)(b) of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA), 2015.

Ms Oladunjoye, therefore, prayed the court for an order granting the permission to mask their witnesses, and conceal their names.

But Mr Ekwe, lawyer to the 1st and 2nd defendants, disagreed with Ms Oladunjoye’s oral application. He argued that such application was uncalled for.

Mr Ekwe submitted that there was no evidence to support the prosecution’s claims that if the witnesses were not masked, it will prejudice the prosecution’s case.

Besides, he argued, the application should be formally filed for them to respond appropriately and to guard against ambush.

Justice Abdulmalik then asked Mr Ekwe to cite a law to back his argument that the prosecution must file a formal application to make such request.

Responding, the lawyer said he relied on Section 36 of the 1999 Constitution.

Ms Oladunjoye also countered Mr Ekwe’s submission.

In a ruling, the judge agreed with the SSS lawyer’s submission.

Justice Abdulmalik held that in the light that the case being a terrorism matter, it would not serve the interest of justice to expose the identity of the witnesses in the case.

The judge, who directed the trial to begin and the witness to be code-named as “AB”, ordered that anyone who runs afoul of Section 232(5) of ACJA will be liable to one year jail term.

However, Mr Uwadiegwu, counsel to the 3rd and 4th defendants, informed the court that he was only coming into the matter for the first time and that he would need more time to study the case file.

Mr Ekwe also told the court that he was just served with the video evidence by the prosecution, insisting that he was not ready to go on with the trial.

The prosecution counsel responded that though Mr Ekwe was just being served with the video evidence, the video clip would not be used in the day’s trial.

She prayed the court to allow the matter to proceed.

Besides, Ms Oladunjoye argued that Mr Ekwe’s absence on 6 October caused an adjournment.

Dissatisfied, Messrs Ekwe and Uwadiegwu stood up simultaneously to address the court on why the matter must be adjourned.

This prompted the judge to caution them against unruly behaviour in her court.

“I run my court in line with international best practice, and that is why people say I am strict.

READ ALSO: Court dismisses suit seeking registration of new political party

“So, when I run my court, there should be 99.9 per cent compliance according to international best practice,” she said.

Justice Abdulmalik said she would not have listed the case for hearing because there were many pre-election cases in the docket of the court.

She added that she had at least nine judgements to write in respect of pre-election matters which must be delivered before 9 November.

The judge, however, said that she saw the case as very crucial and which should be determined expeditiously.

Having listened to the parties, Justice Abdulmalik agreed to give a short adjournment. She, however, warned against any act that could delay the trial.

The judge consequently adjourned the matter until 28 October for commencement of trial.

World.title: Election Campaigns: FRSC bars officers from escorting politicians
World.content:
The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has barred its personnel from escorting politicians during campaigns for the 2027 general elections.

Abimbola Owolabi, zonal commanding officer, RS6, gave the directive during her maiden visit to the Cross River Command in Calabar on Wednesday.

Ms Owolabi said patrol vehicles and sirens must not be used for political activities or private engagements, including weddings and funeral processions.

She directed officers deployed to campaign venues to focus exclusively on traffic management to prevent congestion and road crashes.

The zonal head warned personnel against leading political convoys or providing escorts for politicians, stressing that official vehicles must not be used for unauthorised purposes.

She urged officers to intensify public education on road safety, noting that sustained awareness campaigns could reduce crashes and help achieve zero fatalities.

Ms Owolabi also warned against extortion, corruption and other unprofessional conduct, urging personnel to protect the corps’ reputation through accountability.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Misconduct by patrol operators and other personnel undermines public confidence in the corps. Officers must be extremely accountable across operational units,” she said.

She advised officers to prioritise their safety during enforcement operations and avoid unnecessary confrontations that could lead to assaults, injuries or damage to their uniforms.

Ms Owolabi urged personnel to exercise professionalism and discretion when dealing with motorists, particularly in volatile situations that could escalate into violence.

She called for stronger partnerships with private operators to ensure broken-down vehicles were promptly removed from highways and traffic obstructions cleared.

The zonal commander also stressed the need for prompt emergency response, effective rescue operations and intensified patrols to reduce road crashes and fatalities.

“I urge FRSC personnel to maintain high standards of service delivery, process official correspondence carefully and ensure requests for operational support are properly documented,” she said.

She encouraged officers to prioritise their health and utilise the National Health Insurance Scheme, noting that good health was essential for effective service delivery.

Ms Owolabi also appealed to the wives of FRSC personnel under the Road Safety Officers’ Wives Association to support their husbands in discharging their duties effectively and safeguarding lives.

(NAN)

World.title: Nigeria has 500 epidemiologists, govt should let them lead Ebola response, expert says
World.content:
A senior field epidemiologist, Peter Adewuyi, has called on the Nigerian government to put the country’s trained epidemiologists at the forefront of efforts to contain the confirmed Ebola case, saying Nigeria has about 500 specialists capable of supporting the response.

Mr Adewuyi, who led contact tracing during Nigeria’s 2014 Ebola outbreak, said the country should rely on its existing public health expertise rather than depend on foreign epidemiologists to manage the outbreak.

“We have about 500 epidemiologists in the country and the government should just allow them to do their work,” he said during an interview on ARISE TV Morning Show on Thursday.

His comments came two days after Nigeria confirmed an imported Ebola case in a woman in the Federal Capital Territory, raising concerns about the risk of further transmission and the capacity of the country’s surveillance system to detect infections early.

The World Health Organisation said the patient’s symptoms began on 7 October, four days after her arrival in Nigeria. She sought treatment at a private health facility in Abuja on 11 October, and laboratory tests confirmed the infection on 20 October.

The patient is receiving treatment in isolation, while health authorities have identified 44 contacts and are monitoring them for possible symptoms.

Mr Adewuyi said the response to the case had begun early but stressed that the time taken to detect the infection was a concern.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He cited the “717” surveillance performance indicator, which he said requires suspected cases to be detected within seven days, reported within one day and followed by a response within seven days.

“We are supposed to detect within seven days, report within a day and then respond within seven days. Response is okay, reporting is okay, but the detection took about eight to nine days and that is the fear as far as the response that we are given right now,” he said.

‘Local expertise should lead response’

Mr Adewuyi said Nigeria did not need foreign epidemiologists to lead its response, pointing to the pool of trained professionals already available in the country. “Nigeria does not need people to come from outside,” he said.

He cited the African Field Epidemiology Network, which he said was supporting the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention to deploy more epidemiologists to the field.

He also pointed to the Nigeria’s Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response system, which is designed to track diseases from health facilities and local government areas through state authorities to the national level.

He said the system provides a structure for identifying and reporting infections and coordinating responses across the country.

Contact tracing

The epidemiologist stressed that contact tracing must cover everyone who may have been exposed to the infected woman before her diagnosis, including health workers and other people who entered the facilities where she received treatment.

“So in this case, all the people that treated this person from day one till the time she was diagnosed, all of these people are contacts. Whether the person that came to sweep the room, whether the person that came to make the bed, every one of them,” he said.

He warned that the number of identified contacts could increase as investigations progressed, calling on anyone who might have been exposed to provide accurate information to health authorities.

Contact tracing is a critical part of Ebola containment because it enables health officials to identify potentially exposed people, monitor them for symptoms and isolate suspected cases promptly.

Nigeria’s 2014 experience

Nigeria successfully contained its 2014 Ebola outbreak after an infected traveller from Liberia arrived in Lagos. The country recorded 19 laboratory-confirmed cases and one probable case, with eight deaths.

The WHO declared Nigeria free of Ebola transmission on 20 October 2014, after 42 days without a new case.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the federal government had strengthened its Ebola preparedness before the latest case was confirmed, following outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and other African countries.

The latest case is as a result of the ongoing regional outbreak of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease, a strain for which no licensed vaccine has been approved specifically.

The federal government has activated its response arrangements, while the WHO and other partners are supporting efforts to contain the infection and prevent further transmission.

World.title: Edo Queens accept CAF decision, vow to fight for Women’s Champions League spot
World.content:
Edo Queens have accepted the Confederation of African Football’s (CAF) decision to resume the outstanding extra time of their disputed WAFU-B final against Ghanaian champions Ampem Darkoa Ladies in Cairo, Egypt, on 29 October, insisting that their ambition to secure a place in the CAF Women’s Champions League remains unchanged.

The Nigerian champions confirmed their position in an official statement released on Thursday following the conclusion of an appeal process that saw CAF uphold its decision to annul Edo Queens’ penalty shootout victory and order the final to continue from extra time.

The dispute dates back to 5 September, when Edo Queens faced Ampem Darkoa in the WAFU-B qualifying final at the 4th of August Stadium in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.

The encounter ended 2-2 after regulation time, but instead of proceeding to the required two 15-minute periods of extra time, the match went straight to a penalty shootout, which Edo Queens won 4-1.

The result initially appeared to have secured the Nigerian side the WAFU-B title and the zone’s ticket to the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League. However, Ampem Darkoa, through the Ghana Football Association, protested the decision to proceed directly to penalties, arguing that the competition regulations required extra time to be played before a shootout could determine the winner.

CAF’s Organising Committee for Women’s Football subsequently annulled the penalty shootout result and ordered the match to resume from the beginning of extra time, with the score remaining 2-2.

The decision sparked a response from the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), which appealed on behalf of Edo Queens, arguing that the Nigerian club should not be penalised for an error committed by the match officials.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The NFF maintained that Edo Queens had neither requested nor caused the omission of extra time but had simply followed the instructions of the officials appointed to oversee the final.

However, the CAF Appeal Board, in its ruling of 16 October, upheld the earlier decision, confirming that the 4-1 penalty shootout victory had no sporting effect and that the match must resume from the 2-2 scoreline at the start of extra time.

The continuation will consist of two 15-minute periods, with a fresh penalty shootout to determine the winner if the teams remain level after the additional 30 minutes. CAF also directed that different match officials be appointed for the resumption.

Following the unsuccessful appeal, Edo Queens said the club had decided to accept CAF’s position after consultations with its board, the Edo State Government and the NFF.

While admitting that the outcome was not what the club had hoped for, the Nigerian champions stressed that their decision to proceed with the match was driven by the need to settle the contest on the pitch and give both teams the opportunity to determine the outcome through football.

The club also expressed appreciation to the Edo State Government and the NFF for their support and commitment throughout the appeal process, acknowledging their efforts to defend its interests during the dispute.

Edo Queens further thanked their loyal supporters and members of the media who stood by the team, describing their encouragement, solidarity and belief as a tremendous source of strength during a difficult period.

Despite the disappointment surrounding CAF’s ruling, the club insisted that its focus had now shifted to the decisive encounter in Cairo, where the players and technical crew will have another opportunity to secure the WAFU-B ticket to the continental competition.

“Our mission remains unchanged: to fight, to win and to secure our place in the CAF Women’s Champions League,” the statement read.

The club acknowledged the disappointment that the outcome of the appeal might cause among supporters but maintained that it was determined to move forward with courage, discipline, resilience and an unwavering commitment to its badge.

Edo Queens also assured the people of Edo State and their fans that the players and technical crew remained focused, determined and ready to give everything within their power to emerge victorious when the outstanding portion of the final resumes in Egypt.

With the WAFU-B qualification ticket still undecided, the Nigerian side called on its supporters to continue standing behind the team, urging them to keep believing in the Queens and demonstrating the love and solidarity that have accompanied the club throughout its campaign.

The club emphasised that the backing of its fans would remain invaluable as the players prepare for what promises to be a decisive test of their resolve against Ampem Darkoa.

Reaffirming its identity beyond the football pitch, Edo Queens described itself as a symbol of the strength, ambition and fighting spirit of the Edo people, promising to carry those values into the encounter in Cairo.

The statement ended with a rallying message to supporters as the club prepares for the resumption of the final.

“Together, we will fight. Together, we will believe. Together, we will pursue victory and the dream of playing in the CAF Women’s Champions League.”

The winner of the resumed final will represent WAFU-B at the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League, scheduled to take place in Egypt from 1-5 November.

For Edo Queens, the task is now clear: put the disappointment of the appeal behind them, return to the pitch against Ampem Darkoa and fight to reclaim the continental opportunity they initially believed they had secured in Ouagadougou.

World.title: MacArthur President urges Africa to move from AI talk to action
World.content:
John Palfrey, president of the MacArthur Foundation, has urged African countries to translate their artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions into practical solutions, calling for greater investment in digital skills and technologies that improve healthcare, inclusion and economic opportunities.

“It is a matter of putting the right skills in the hands of the right young people and then believing in them that they can shape this future,” Mr Palfrey said.

He spoke during a fireside chat titled “Positioning Africa in the Global AI Order: Capital, Talent, and Trust” at the BUILD 2026 Conference in Abuja.

The two-day conference, held from 21 to 22 October, is hosted by the Nigeria AI Collective. The event focuses on the infrastructure, investment, governance and partnerships needed to advance AI development in Africa.

Speaking about technical talent, Mr Palfrey said Nigeria has a growing population of young people interested in technology, but many lack the skills and opportunities to participate meaningfully in the emerging AI economy.

Citing research conducted in Nigeria, he estimated that fewer than 10 per cent of young people had the skills needed to take advantage of these opportunities.

He commended the Three Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme of the federal government, describing it as an important initiative supported by the MacArthur Foundation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Palfrey said government, philanthropy and the private sector have important roles to play in connecting young people with opportunities. He also highlighted the foundation’s Nigeria Next initiative and partnerships with organisations including the Ford Foundation and Luminate as avenues for bringing capital and ideas into Nigeria’s AI ecosystem.

Responding to concerns about critical thinking in an era of increasing dependence on tools such as ChatGPT, Mr Palfrey cautioned against introducing AI into every aspect of human activity.

He argued that human judgment, lived experience and critical thinking remained essential, particularly in fields such as healthcare, where understanding the circumstances of different communities could lead to important discoveries.

Mr Palfrey also expressed optimism about Africa’s opportunity to influence global AI development, stressing that the continent still had time to shape how the technology evolves.

“There’s urgency, though, to go from talk to build,” he said.

He urged governments, investors and technology developers to focus on measurable outcomes, including improved healthcare, disability inclusion, gender equity and the preservation of lesser-spoken African languages.

Mr Palfrey also highlighted the potential of concessional financing and philanthropic investment to support infrastructure and locally developed AI solutions.

He said investments in connectivity, computing infrastructure and digital tools should be accompanied by efforts to strengthen digital skills and improve people’s livelihoods.

“It’s one thing to lay the fibre. It’s one thing to have access to the tools. But is that actually that smartphone in the pocket of that young person helping them lead a better life, have greater opportunity, thrive in the global ecosystem?” he asked.

World.title: Tinubu commissions section of Kano-Kaduna highway
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday commissioned Section III of the Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano expressway, stretching across Kaduna and Kano states.

Represented at the ceremony by Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf, the president highlighted the project’s role as a vital transport artery linking Kano, Kaduna, and other key commercial regions across the country.

The completion of Section III is expected to significantly improve driving conditions, mitigate hazards caused by deteriorated road surfaces, and substantially reduce accidents and casualties along the heavily trafficked corridor.

Delivering the president’s address, Governor Yusuf commended the federal administration for prioritising strategic infrastructure aimed at boosting transportation, trade, and regional economic integration across northern Nigeria.

He emphasised that durable road networks remain essential for connecting communities, facilitating the seamless flow of goods, and fostering a competitive business environment.

“The Kano–Zaria corridor is of paramount strategic importance due to Kano’s position as the primary commercial hub serving multiple northern states,” Governor Yusuf noted.

He added that sustained investment in transport infrastructure would boost agricultural value chains, broaden market access, and unlock new economic opportunities for transport operators and small businesses.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Advocating closer intergovernmental alignment, the governor urged the federal government to maintain momentum on high-impact road construction and rehabilitation across Kano State to handle heavy commercial tonnage.

The Kano State Government also appealed to motorists travelling the newly completed highway to observe speed limits, avoid reckless overtaking, and strictly comply with traffic regulations to protect lives and property.

About the road project

The comprehensive reconstruction of the 375 km Abuja–Kaduna–Zaria–Kano Dual Carriageway was awarded in late 2017, and flag-off operations officially began in 2018 under former President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration.

Executed by Julius Berger Nigeria Plc, the project was designed to rebuild one of Nigeria’s busiest arterial roads, which had suffered decades of neglect and severe deterioration.

Initially funded through budgetary allocations and later backed by the Presidential Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) (managed by the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority – NSIA).

The multi-billion naira project faced delays due to security concerns along the corridor, funding bottlenecks, right-of-way issues, and scope adjustments (transitioning from asphalt repairs to full cold-in-place recycling and thick asphalt concrete pavement for durability).

To optimise execution, the highway was divided into three main sections: Section I: Abuja – Kaduna (165 km), which is still under construction, section II: Kaduna – Zaria (73.4 km) completed, section III: Zaria – Kano (137 km / Kaduna–Kano stretch) completed under President Tinubu.

World.title: Explainer: What if BVAS fails in 2027 election?
World.content:
File image of a BVAS in use.

By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA

As Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections, public trust in election technology remains a major talking point. But building on lessons from past polls, the Professor Joash Amupitan-led Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has clarified the operational guidelines and legal frameworks governing technical glitches, specifically involving the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, and the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV.

Read Also:

*Who won Lagos in 2023?

*Presidential Election: Tinubu got 517,341 Kano votes in 2023; can he win it in 2027?

So, here is a breakdown of what INEC’s plan entails and what happens if BVAS experiences a technical failure during polling.

1. Local glitches won’t stop overall results

The failure of BVAS in specific polling units will not halt voting, collation, or announcement of results in unaffected areas.

2. Impact Assessment

Collation of results will continue unless the uncollected votes from the affected polling units are significant enough to alter the overall outcome.

3. 24-Hour Reschedule Provision

Under the Electoral Act, if a malfunctioning BVAS cannot be repaired or replaced, voting in that specific unit is postponed to the next day.

4. Hardware & Power Upgrades

INEC said it has procured 57,000 additional BVAS devices and is replacing unit batteries to tackle hardware and power failures.

5. Field Support Teams (RATECH)

Dedicated technical teams will be deployed across Registration Areas for immediate on-site intervention.

6. Upgrades & Technical Prevention Strategy

To mitigate risks before election day, INEC is addressing hardware, battery life, and transmission bottlenecks:

7. 57,000 New BVAS Units

Additional devices are being deployed to serve as active inventory and quick-response backups across polling zones.

8. Battery Replacement

Recognizing power loss as a main cause of past delays, INEC is upgrading built-in batteries to sustain operations throughout polling hours.

9. IReV Platform Optimizations

Software enhancements are underway on the IReV portal to ensure seamless uploading and transmission of polling unit result sheets (eEC8A).

10. On-Ground Troubleshooting: The RATECH Framework

When a BVAS unit fails, polling staff do not immediately cancel voting. INEC utilizes Registration Area Technical Support teams RATECH.

Legal and Operational Scenarios: Step-by-Step;

Scenario A: Localized Technical Failure

Rule: If BVAS fails to transmit results in a single polling unit or cluster of units, elections in unaffected polling units, wards, and local governments proceed as scheduled.

Impact: The failure does not trigger a nationwide or state-wide pause.

Scenario B: Unresolvable Technical Failure on Polling Day
