Rule: In accordance with the provisions of the Electoral Act, if a BVAS device cannot be fixed or swapped by RATECH on election day, polling in that specific unit is suspended and rescheduled for the following day.

Scenario C: Collation vs. Margin of Lead

Rule: When collation reaches the constituency, LG, or national level, election officers evaluate whether the total registered voters in the affected/delayed polling units can mathematically alter the winner.

Outcome

If the combined votes in the affected units will not alter the winner, collation proceeds and a winner is declared.

However, if the affected votes could alter the winner, declaration is withheld until supplementary voting takes place.

Conclusion

INEC’s stance for 2027 emphasizes contingency management over disruption. Therefore, while technology remains central to voter accreditation and result transparency, localized tech failures are expected to be contained via fast-swap backups, RATECH field teams, or localized 24-hour election postponements — ensuring the broader democratic process is not brought to a standstill.

Note

RATECH stands for Registration Area Technical Support.

A “Registration Area” is an electoral ward.

RATECH consists of specialized Information and Communications Technology (ICT) personnel and trained ad-hoc technical staff deployed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Their main duties include:

On-the-Ground Troubleshooting

They are stationed at ward level (Registration Area Centers) specifically to respond when election devices—such as the BVAS (Bimodal Voter Accreditation System)—experience technical glitches.

Hardware & Software Support

Furthermore, if a BVAS unit freezes, experiences battery drain, fails to authenticate voters (via fingerprint or facial recognition), or struggles to upload results to the IReV (INEC Result Viewing Portal), RATECH officers are called in to fix or replace the device on-site.

Direct Communication Link

Also, they maintain a direct line of communication with Polling Officers at the polling units to ensure rapid intervention so that voting and result transmission are not unnecessarily delayed.

Vanguard News

World.title: France records first human death linked to Shamonda virus
World.content:
— Authorities say patient was severely immunocompromised, no public health risk identified

France has reported the death of a severely immunocompromised patient infected with Shamonda virus, marking the first recorded human case of the virus.

The death was announced on Thursday in a statement by the French ministries responsible for health and agriculture, according to Agence France-Presse (AFP).

The ministries described the infection as “an exceptional case involving a severely immunocompromised patient”.

The patient, who died in early October, was believed to have contracted the virus through the bite of a midge in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating among animals during the spring and summer.

French authorities said clinical, biological and epidemiological investigations were ongoing, adding that no risk to the general public had been identified at the time of the announcement.

“Despite circulating in Africa and Asia for several decades, the Shamonda virus has never previously been detected in humans,” the statement said.

It added that the neurological complications observed in the patient before his death were very likely linked to the infection.

About Shamonda virus

According to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Shamonda virus is a vector-borne pathogen belonging to the Orthobunyavirus group. It is transmitted to animals by small biting insects.

The virus was first isolated from cattle in Nigeria in 1965 and was subsequently identified in other parts of Africa and Asia in the early 2000s.

In Europe, clinical signs of the virus in animals were reported from June 2026 and identified in late July, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC).

The ECDC said the virus had been detected in farm animals in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and Switzerland, as well as Jersey.

The agency said it was working with French authorities and European partners to investigate the potential public health implications of the first reported human infection.

World.title: Ebola: Africa CDC says Nigerian patient was born in Uganda
World.content:
— Kaseya seeks travel history to trace source of infection

The Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), Jean Kaseya, has urged the woman diagnosed with Ebola in Nigeria to disclose her full travel history, saying she was born in Uganda but the source of her infection remains unknown.

Kaseya made the appeal during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief, saying the woman had travelled to Uganda, where she spent several days before her husband joined her.

He said the couple returned to Abuja on October 3, adding that authorities were investigating whether she contracted the virus in Uganda or another location.

The Federal Government confirmed Nigeria’s first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease on October 20, after laboratory tests detected the virus in a woman who had recently arrived in the country.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, said the patient had been admitted to a private hospital in the Federal Capital Territory, where she received treatment before the diagnosis was confirmed.

On October 21, Olajumoke Babatunde, Director of Public Health Laboratory Services at the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), disclosed that the patient was a diplomat whose condition had deteriorated to multi-organ failure.

Kaseya said authorities needed to establish whether the woman had travelled to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), had contact with anyone from the country or visited areas outside Kampala during her stay in Uganda.

“I am talking to Ugandan, DRC and Nigerian authorities, that the person we know today without any doubt, that this is a Ugandan-born person who went to Uganda and she was there for some days and the husband flew to join her in Uganda,” he said.

He appealed to the patient to cooperate with health authorities, saying her account of her movements could help investigators identify where the infection occurred.

“What we want is collaboration from this lady. She has to tell us, to disclose to the authorities; I need this information, Nigeria needs this information because we need also to support Uganda,” Kaseya said.

He said the investigation was necessary to establish whether transmission occurred in Uganda or the virus was acquired elsewhere.

“What we know is that the lady came from Uganda, but what we don’t know is whether it is a transmission from Uganda, Kampala, or a transmission that came from another place,” he said.

Uganda disputes link to outbreak

Uganda’s Ministry of Health had reportedly described the patient as Nigerian, saying she travelled to eastern DRC for business before transiting through Uganda in early October.

Charles Olaro, Uganda’s Director-General of Health Services, said the woman did not develop symptoms while in Uganda but became ill after arriving in Nigeria.

Ugandan authorities also said the country had no confirmed active Ebola cases at the time of their statement, insisting that the patient’s passage through Uganda did not establish where she contracted the virus.

“Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation,” Olaro said.

The conflicting accounts underscore the need for further epidemiological investigations to establish the patient’s movements, possible exposure and the source of infection.

Africa CDC warns against blame

Kaseya urged African leaders to avoid politicising the outbreak or blaming individual countries, warning that accusations and isolation could undermine efforts to contain the virus.

“My plea is clear to all leaders: we cannot play politics with this outbreak; we cannot point fingers; we cannot play isolation; we all need to come together to save our continent,” he said.

He called for cooperation among Nigeria, Uganda and the DRC, stressing the importance of information-sharing and a coordinated response to prevent further transmission.

World.title: Ebola: Enugu intensifies surveillance across 17 LGAs
World.content:
— State reactivates emergency operations centre, places response teams on standby

By Anayo Okoli

ENUGU — The Enugu State Government has intensified disease surveillance across its 17 local government areas and reactivated its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre following reports of an Ebola case in Nigeria.

The state Commissioner for Health, Prof. George O. Ugwu, disclosed this while assuring residents that no case of Ebola Virus Disease had been confirmed in the state.

“Let me begin by reassuring the people of Enugu State that there is currently no confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease in Enugu State,” he said.

Ugwu explained that the government had strengthened its preparedness measures in collaboration with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, airport authorities and other relevant partners.

He said Enugu’s position as a major travel and commercial hub, particularly through the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, made it necessary to strengthen disease surveillance and response mechanisms.

According to him, the administration of Governor Peter Mbah considers the health security of residents a priority and is taking precautionary measures without creating unnecessary panic.

The commissioner said surveillance had been intensified across the 17 local government areas, while coordination with relevant agencies and monitoring around the international airport had also been reinforced.

He added that the State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre had been reactivated to coordinate preparedness and response, with rapid response teams and technical personnel on standby.

“I call on all public and private health facilities across the state to remain on heightened alert and maintain a high index of suspicion for suspected cases, particularly among persons with relevant travel or exposure history,” Ugwu said.

He urged healthcare providers to promptly isolate suspected cases and immediately report them to the appropriate Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO) or the state emergency operations centre.

The commissioner also called on health workers to maintain strict infection prevention and control measures, use appropriate personal protective equipment and report suspected infections through established channels.

He stressed that early detection and prompt notification were critical to preventing transmission, assuring health workers that the government would continue to provide the necessary support and guidance to protect them and ensure an effective response.

Ugwu urged residents to remain calm and observe preventive measures, including proper hand hygiene, avoiding contact with the body fluids of sick persons, seeking prompt medical attention when necessary and reporting suspected cases to the appropriate health authorities.

He cautioned against rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation, urging residents to rely on information from the Enugu State Ministry of Health, the NCDC and other recognised health authorities.

The commissioner said the state government would continue to collaborate with national authorities and other partners to strengthen preparedness, surveillance and response.

“I reassure the public that there is currently no confirmed case of Ebola in Enugu State. I urge everyone to remain calm, observe preventive measures, report suspected cases promptly and rely on verified information,” he said.

World.title: Sowore, Basiru clash over 2027 campaign, past activism
World.content:
Omoyele Sowore and Ajibola Basiru

By Ayobami Okerinde

The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ajibola Basiru, and presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, have traded words as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general election.

The exchange started after the AAC requested the venue for the inauguration of its Presidential Campaign Council on November 11, 2026, alongside food, drinks and logistical support for 5,000 participants, citing equal treatment of political parties.

Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, Basiru questioned Sowore’s political relevance, challenging him to win a seat in a state House of Assembly before expecting to be taken seriously.

“Sowore is a skit maker. Let him struggle to even get a seat in the House of Assembly as a politician, and then people will begin to take him seriously,” Basiru said.

He also claimed that rejected ballot papers received more votes than the AAC in the 2023 general elections.

‘‘The struggle for freedom is not comedy’ — Sowore fires back at Basiru

Responding in a post on X on Wednesday, Sowore recalled his history with Basiru during the struggle against military rule in the 1990s, accusing the APC official of abandoning the democratic ideals they once defended.

Sowore shared a photograph of the pair taken in 1998, when he led the Congress of Progressive Youths, and said he received Basiru at the University of Lagos after his expulsion from the University of Ilorin in 1992.

He claimed that he and other activists, including Kunle Adegoke, popularly known as K-Rad, helped Basiru secure an opportunity to return to university and study law.

“The struggle for justice, democracy, freedom and the preservation of human dignity is neither skit-making nor comedy. Ajibola knows this because he was once part of that struggle and benefited from the solidarity of those who refused to surrender to military tyranny.

“It is unfortunate that he has become so carried away by the fleeting privileges of his current political position that he now ridicules the very struggle that helped shape his own future.”

Sowore added that political appointments were temporary, stating that President Tinubu’s administration would eventually leave office, just as previous military regimes had.

Basiru denies Sowore’s claim, says he gained UNILAG admission on merit

In a response posted on X on Thursday, Basiru rejected Sowore’s account, saying the two had no relationship before he gained admission to the University of Lagos to study law.

“I did not have any relationship with you before I got admitted to the University of Lagos. In fact, I got 310 in my UTME exam to gain admission to the University of Lagos and that was the best score for all applicants to the law faculty the year of my admission.”

He insisted that his admission was based on merit and maintained his description of Sowore as a comedian, questioning whether the AAC candidate believed he could win the presidency.

Basiru also accused Sowore of misleading young people by presenting himself as a revolutionary and freedom fighter.

“Leave your sanctimonious harangue to the unsuspecting young people you are lying to that you are a revolutionary or freedom fighter,” he concluded.

World.title: Bundibugyo Ebola: Early detection, isolation key to containing Nigeria’s outbreak – Expert
World.content:
By Sola Ogundipe

Nigeria must prioritise early detection, immediate isolation, rigorous contact tracing and quality supportive care to contain the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus, a medical scientist has said.

Adegboro, who is the incoming Chairman of the Rapid Response Committee of the Academy of Medical Sciences, Nigeria, warned that the absence of an approved vaccine or specific treatment does not make the disease uncontrollable, saying Nigeria’s immediate response should be guided by evidence-based public health measures rather than expectations of premature mass vaccination with an experimental vaccine.

In an interview, he told Vanguard that Nigeria does not need to embark on experimental vaccination at this stage, given the reported single index case and the ongoing monitoring of identified contacts.

Adegboro said the government, through the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), should ensure that suspected cases are identified quickly and tested without delay.

He explained that although a vaccine specifically targeting the Bundibugyo strain remains experimental, patients can still benefit from prompt diagnosis, careful clinical management and measures designed to prevent infection among healthcare workers, caregivers and other contacts.

“Although there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo virus disease, this does not mean that the disease is untreatable or uncontrollable. Early diagnosis, effective isolation, high quality supportive care and rigorous infection prevention can save lives and limit transmission,” he said.

The expert’s recommendations come amid concerns about Nigeria’s ability to prevent a localised Ebola infection from developing into a wider outbreak in a country characterised by extensive domestic and international travel, densely populated urban centres and substantial movement across land borders.

He said Nigeria had valuable public health assets, including disease surveillance networks, laboratory expertise and experience coordinating responses to infectious disease outbreaks. However, their effectiveness must be assessed against current operational realities.

On the country’s preparedness to detect, isolate and manage suspected cases, particularly those with major transport links and high population movement, he said Nigeria has important public health assets.

“But we must distinguish between having preparedness structures on paper and demonstrating that they can function effectively under pressure. Nigeria has valuable experience from the 2014 Ebola outbreak, which it successfully contained through case identification, contact tracing, infection prevention and coordinated emergency response.

“We also have established national and subnational disease surveillance structures, laboratory expertise and experience managing other infectious disease emergencies. These are important advantages.

“However, we should not automatically conclude that Nigeria is fully prepared simply because it contained an earlier outbreak. Our preparedness must be tested against the realities of today’s Nigeria: extensive domestic and international travel, high population density in major cities, substantial informal movement across land borders, uneven healthcare infrastructure and the possibility that patients may initially present to facilities without adequate infection prevention capacity,” he remarked.

On international assistance, Adegboro said Nigeria should work closely with the World Health Organisation, WHO, and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention to strengthen its technical and operational response.

He said lessons from previous Bundibugyo outbreaks in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo reinforced the importance of technical cooperation that would strengthen Nigeria’s domestic capacity rather than create long term dependence on external deployments.

Such support, he indicated, should reinforce surveillance, laboratory diagnosis, infection prevention and control, clinical management and the ability of response teams to trace and monitor contacts.

For Nigeria, he argued, the immediate priority should be to interrupt transmission through rapid identification of suspected cases, safe isolation, laboratory confirmation, contact tracing and strict infection prevention measures.

Ultimately, the expert said, the country’s ability to contain the index case and prevent additional infections will depend on how effectively these measures are implemented across the health system.

“The central challenge is not simply whether Nigeria has the technical capacity to respond, but whether that capacity can be deployed quickly, consistently and effectively enough to stop the virus from spreading,” he stated

World.title: Bandits kill driver, two passengers on Sokoto road
World.content:
Stock image.

— Police confirm three deaths in attack on Marnona-Isa route

By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — Suspected bandits have killed a driver and two passengers after attacking a vehicle conveying commuters along the Marnona-Isa Road in Sokoto State.

The attack occurred on Wednesday evening at Kunawa village in Goronyo Local Government Area, when the assailants reportedly intercepted the vehicle travelling from Sokoto metropolis towards Isa Local Government Area and opened fire on its occupants.

The Sokoto State Police Command confirmed the incident through its spokesperson, DSP Ahmed Rufai.

“A driver and two others were killed by bandits at Kunawa village, Goronyo Local Government Area, along the Marnona-Isa Road,” Rufai said.

The identities of the deceased had yet to be officially disclosed at the time of filing this report. The police spokesperson also did not provide details about the number of assailants involved or any arrests made in connection with the attack.

There were unconfirmed reports that some passengers travelling along the route might have been among the 3,000 people reportedly recruited by the Sokoto State Government and invited for further screening and collection of their documents.

However, there was no official confirmation that any of the victims belonged to the group.

The killings have heightened concerns over the safety of motorists and passengers travelling between Sokoto metropolis and other parts of the state, particularly along routes passing through isolated communities.

The attack also underscores the risks faced by residents whose daily activities, official engagements and other commitments require them to travel between communities.

The police had yet to release further information on possible security operations linked to the incident as of the time of filing this report.

The latest killings come amid persistent concerns over banditry in parts of Sokoto State, where attacks on communities and travellers have threatened lives, disrupted movement and heightened fears among residents.

The incident is likely to renew calls for stronger security measures, including improved patrols and better protection for commuters along vulnerable highways.

World.title: Ebola: Enugu intensifies surveillance across 17 LGAs
World.content:
— State reactivates emergency operations centre, places response teams on standby

By Anayo Okoli

ENUGU — The Enugu State Government says it has intensified disease surveillance across its 17 local government areas and reactivated its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre following reports of an Ebola case in Nigeria.

The state Commissioner for Health, Prof. George O. Ugwu, who disclosed this, said no case of Ebola Virus Disease had been confirmed in Enugu State.

“Let me begin by reassuring the people of Enugu State that there is currently no confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease in Enugu State,” he said.

Ugwu explained that the government had strengthened preparedness measures in collaboration with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, airport authorities and other relevant partners.

He said Enugu’s position as a major travel and commercial hub, particularly through the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, made heightened surveillance and preparedness necessary.

According to him, the administration of Governor Peter Mbah considers public health security a priority and is taking precautionary measures without creating unnecessary panic.

The commissioner said surveillance had been intensified across the 17 local government areas, while coordination with relevant agencies and monitoring around the international airport had also been strengthened.

He added that the state’s Public Health Emergency Operations Centre had been reactivated to coordinate preparedness and response, with rapid response teams and technical personnel placed on standby.

Ugwu urged public and private health facilities across the state to remain on high alert and maintain a high index of suspicion for suspected cases, particularly among people with relevant travel or exposure histories.

He advised healthcare providers to promptly isolate suspected cases and report them immediately to the appropriate Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO) or the state emergency operations centre.

The commissioner also urged health workers to adhere strictly to infection prevention and control protocols, use appropriate personal protective equipment and report suspected infections through established channels.

He stressed that early detection and prompt notification were critical to preventing transmission, assuring health workers that the government would continue to provide the support and guidance needed to protect them and ensure an effective response.

Ugwu urged residents to remain calm and observe preventive measures, including proper hand hygiene, avoiding contact with the body fluids of sick persons, seeking prompt medical attention when necessary and reporting suspected cases to health authorities.

He cautioned against rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation, urging residents to rely on information from the Enugu State Ministry of Health, the NCDC and other recognised health authorities.

The commissioner said the state government would continue to work with national authorities and other partners to strengthen disease preparedness, surveillance and response.

“I reassure the public that there is currently no confirmed case of Ebola in Enugu State. I urge everyone to remain calm, observe preventive measures, report suspected cases promptly and rely on verified information,” he said.

World.title: Tinubu: We’ll Use Nigeria’s Gas Resources To Create Jobs and Boost Export Earnings
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Thursday reaffirmed his determination to unlock Nigeria’s gas resources to power industries, improve electricity supply, create jobs and boost export earnings.

He said this amid indigenous engineering firm, Lee Engineering’s achievement of building two compressor stations to enable the Escravos–Lagos Pipeline System to operate at its full capacity of 2.3 billion standard cubic feet of gas per day.

The president spoke while receiving the Founder and Chairman of Lee Engineering Group, Chief Leemon Ikpea, at the State House, Abuja.

Tinubu reaffirmed his administration’s Nigeria First policy and urged international oil companies operating in the country to give competent Nigerian engineering and manufacturing firms greater opportunities to participate in major energy projects.

Lee Engineering is handling the Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) of two midline compressor stations in Edo State.

Although the pipeline’s designed capacity was increased from 1.1 billion to 2.3 billion standard cubic feet of gas per day under the ELPS II expansion, the compressor stations are needed to raise operating pressure and enable the pipeline to deliver at its full capacity.

The project is expected to strengthen gas transportation to power plants and industries along that corridor, support increased gas supplies to neighbouring West African countries through the West African Gas Pipeline, and create opportunities for additional export revenue.

The president, who said Nigeria First must translate into more contracts for capable Nigerian firms, greater use of locally manufactured equipment and more skilled jobs for Nigerians, encouraged international oil companies to build stronger partnerships with indigenous engineering companies that have demonstrated the capacity to deliver complex projects.

He also pointed to his administration’s 2024 executive orders and presidential directives on local content compliance, contracting costs, and approval timelines as measures to attract investment, cut delays and expand opportunities for Nigerian businesses.

Earlier, Ikpea commended the president’s Nigeria First policy and disclosed that Lee Engineering’s fabrication yard in Warri, Delta State, is manufacturing some components for the compressor stations and houses some of the most advanced fabrication equipment in the industry.

According to him, Nigerian companies have invested heavily in modern equipment, technology and skilled personnel and can now undertake complex EPC projects previously handled by foreign contractors, keeping more jobs, expertise and economic value within Nigeria.

World.title: NBTE Proposes N1.5bn Per Polytechnic to Produce One Local Product
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The National Board for Technical Education (NBTE) has proposed giving between N1 billion and N1.5 billion to each polytechnic to establish production lines under its One Product, One Polytechnic (1P1P) initiative.

Director-General of NBTE, Prof. Idris Bugaje, disclosed this at a strategic session in Abuja organised by the Raw Materials Research and Development Council (RMRDC) with the World Association of Industrial and Technological Research Organisations (WAITRO), tertiary institutions and private sector stakeholders.

Bugaje said under 1P1P, every polytechnic must manufacture at least one product locally, noting that Nigeria should not be importing simple items like wheelbarrows.

He said Nigeria’s heavy dependence on foreign technology and imports shows a weak link between technical education and industry.

“Nigerian researchers are not talking to the industry,” he said, urging researchers to involve manufacturers and end-users from the start to ensure research solves real market problems.

Bugaje said polytechnics and TVET institutions need greater attention because they produce the skilled manpower for manufacturing and infrastructure.

He cited the engagement of thousands of Indian technicians during construction of the Dangote Refinery as proof of Nigeria’s technical manpower gap.

He called for industry-led curriculum reviews, modern labs and workshops, and stronger partnerships where companies provide practical training and equipment to polytechnics.

He also said NBTE is pushing amendments to the Polytechnic Act to allow polytechnics award Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) Honours degrees while retaining the National Diploma pathway, to end the HND/BSc dichotomy.

WAITRO Secretary-General, Dr. Benjin Luo, said the academia must connect with industry to accelerate technology transfer and commercialisation.

Luo, who also represents China’s National Innovation Centre for Excellence, said WAITRO has over 200 member organisations globally.

He said researchers often lack market insights to commercialise findings, while businesses cannot afford own research units, adding that his organisations can translate industry needs into university research and bring innovations to market.

He said Nigeria has the population, market and raw materials to attract technology and investment.

RMRDC Director-General, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, said Nigeria must bridge research-industry gap to maximise value from its natural resources and research investments, adding that the council is pursuing international partnerships for technology transfer and commercialisation.

TETFund representative, Dr. Conforto-Chamberlain, said the Fund is now prioritizing research that produces commercially viable products, not just publications, through centres of excellence.

Dr. Ike Willie Nwobu called for stronger collaboration between tertiary institutions and RMRDC to improve practical training, criticising lack of hands-on experience among mechanical engineering and agronomy graduates.

He said students should not graduate without exposure to farms, livestock and workshops, just as medical students require teaching hospitals.

Stakeholders called for stronger collaboration among government, researchers, polytechnics and businesses to convert technical education and research into local production and industrial growth.

World.title: FG, Stakeholders Seek Promotion of Self Care in Tackling Public Health Challenges
World.content:
*PHCs to play key role, says SFH

Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The Federal Government has said there is need to imbibe the practice of Self-care as part of measures to address several public health emergencies including infectious diseases outbreak.

At the same time, the Society for Family Health said there is a strong link between Self-care and the primary healthcare with sustainable financing, responsible use of technology, and meaningful community participation in advancing universal health coverage.

Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr. Iziaq Salako, stated this in Abuja on Wednesday at the inaugural National Self-Care Conference with theme “Self-care Puts Your Health in Your Hands: Test, Track, Thrive.”

The minister said self-care is important in prevention and control of infectious diseases, including Ebola Virus Disease currently being contained following index case reported on Monday.

“I use this opportunity to call on Nigerian public to observe self-care like hygiene, appropriate disinfection and cooperate fully with public health officials to contain reported Ebola index case,” he said.

Salako said the theme captures fundamental principle of modern healthcare underscoring imperative of empowering people with knowledge, skills and tools to own their health.

“Self-care extends healthcare beyond hospitals and clinics into our homes, workplaces and communities. It encompasses health promotion, disease and complication prevention, appropriate self-testing and responsible management of well-being. However, self-care does not replace professional healthcare nor absolve government of responsibility to provide accessible, affordable and quality services,” he said.

He said government will continue to promote investment in health facilities, skilled personnel, essential medicines and functional referral systems, adding that self-care is opportunity to strengthen primary healthcare, advance UHC and improve outcomes through prevention, maternal health support, management of non-communicable diseases and extension of information to underserved communities.

Salako explained that while Test allows individuals to know health status, with screening and approved self-testing helping early identification of hypertension, diabetes and other risks, Track requires consistent monitoring of blood pressure, blood glucose, physical activity and medication adherence guided by reliable information and linked to professional care.

He said that Thrive is ultimate goal of healthier individuals, stronger families and resilient communities.

The Minister said the benefits require integrating self-care into PHC, training workers, strengthening community education, improving access to quality-assured products and protecting public from unsafe practices, leveraging digital communication and AI.

He called on states to integrate evidence-based self-care into policies, professionals to guide safe use, partners to support financing and capacity, private sector to prioritize quality and affordability, and traditional and religious leaders, civil society and media to build trust.

Earlier, Group Director, Population, Health and Community Systems, SFH Donor-Funded Portfolio Directorate, Pharm. Emeka Okafor, said conference speaks directly to future of health by enabling people take more informed role in own care.

He said Society for Family Health experience shows care becomes more effective when it responds to how people actually live, making decisions at homes, pharmacies, communities and through phones.

Okafor said opportunity is to turn ambition into commitments with stronger links between self-care and primary healthcare, sustainable financing, responsible use of technology and meaningful community participation.

He said that SFH looks forward to the time when more Nigerians can understand their health, act early and access support when they need it.

In her remarks, the Special Adviser to the President on Health, Dr. Salma Anas Ibrahim said that Federal government laying special emphasis on Self Care as a means of further improving national health outcome and attaining the target of universal health coverage.

Highpoint of the event saw minister being presented with an investiture as “The National Self Care Ambassador” by Dr. Salma Anas Ibrahim.

World.title: NAPharm Proposes 10-point Plan to Strengthen Ebola Preparedness
World.content:
Uchechukwu Nnaike

The Nigeria Academy of Pharmacy (NAPharm), has called on the federal government to strengthen Nigeria’s preparedness for Ebola Virus Disease and other emerging infectious diseases through a coordinated national epidemic-readiness framework.

The academy said preparedness measures should be institutionalised, regularly assessed and made functional across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

In a statement signed by the President and Chairman of the Governing Council, Prof. Lere Baale, the academy said the country must move beyond outbreak awareness to measurable national readiness.

The call follows the academy’s policy report titled ‘From Awareness to Readiness: Strengthening Nigeria’s Preparedness for Ebola and Emerging Infectious Disease Emergencies’.

The report draws on discussions at its national webinar on Ebola Preparedness held on August 20, 2026, and the work of its multidisciplinary Task Group on Ebola Virus Disease Resurgence, chaired by Prof. Fola Tayo.

Baale stated that Nigeria’s success in containing Ebola in 2014 should serve as a foundation for stronger preparedness rather than a reason for complacency.

“Nigeria demonstrated extraordinary leadership, professional competence and national coordination in containing Ebola in 2014. However, yesterday’s success does not automatically guarantee tomorrow’s preparedness.

“Our responsibility is to ensure that the capabilities that protected Nigeria in 2014 are institutionalised, continuously strengthened and demonstrably functional across the country,” he said.

The stressed that epidemic preparedness should no longer be treated as an emergency intervention activated only when an outbreak threatens the country. It proposed a continuous national system built around seven interconnected capabilities: anticipate, prevent, detect, respond, recover, learn and improve.

It added that the approach would strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to manage Ebola, Lassa fever, cholera and other emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases.

It commended the federal government, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention for existing preparedness measures, including surveillance, laboratory readiness, infection prevention and control, point-of-entry monitoring, intergovernmental coordination and public communication.

It however said that further action is needed to ensure that existing systems remain functional and effective.

The academy outlined10 priority actions for urgent policy consideration and implementation: Nationwide epidemic-readiness audit; mandatory epidemic simulation exercises; community pharmacy surveillance integration; diagnostic and laboratory turnaround standards; strategic emergency health-commodity reserves.

Others are: multidisciplinary epidemic-readiness teams; healthcare worker protection framework; risk communication and misinformation management; survivor rehabilitation and reintegration; and annual national epidemic preparedness scorecard.

It identified community pharmacies as an important component of Nigeria’s proposed early-warning system for infectious disease threats, adding that community pharmacists are often among the first healthcare professionals consulted by people experiencing fever, weakness and other symptoms that may resemble common infections.

“Under the proposed NCDC–PCN–NAPHARM Community Pharmacy Sentinel Surveillance Pilot, participating pharmacists would receive appropriate case definitions, surveillance protocols, referral pathways and reporting procedures,” it said.

The academy noted that the initiative would not authorise pharmacists to diagnose Ebola, but would strengthen their role in recognising possible warning signs and notifying the appropriate public health authorities. It summarised the proposed approach as: “Recognise. Protect. Refer. Report.”

The academy also stressed the need to protect healthcare workers to sustain an effective epidemic response.

It added that doctors, pharmacists, nurses, medical laboratory professionals, community health practitioners, rehabilitation professionals and other frontline personnel should receive continuous preparedness training, appropriate protective equipment and institutional support.

According to the academy, effective preparedness requires collaboration across professional boundaries and healthcare institutions.

It therefore recommended multidisciplinary readiness teams, coordinated training and periodic simulation exercises reflecting real-life outbreak scenarios.

Beyond the 10 priority actions, the academy proposed an immediate 90-day implementation framework to support government consideration.

The proposed activities include a national functional-readiness audit, laboratory referral mapping, an inventory of emergency health commodities, a community pharmacy surveillance pilot, healthcare worker preparedness programmes and the development of a national epidemic-readiness scorecard.

Longer-term recommendations include preparedness education, stronger surveillance networks, improved supply chain visibility, One Health collaboration and annual public reporting on epidemic readiness.

The academy said that preparedness funding should be tied to measurable outcomes, verified operational capabilities and corrective action rather than procurement alone.

It expressed readiness to collaborate with the NCDC, the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, state health authorities, professional regulatory bodies, healthcare associations, academic institutions, pharmaceutical manufacturers, development partners and community organisations.

It added that the proposed collaboration would support surveillance, pharmaceutical supply security, professional training, public communication, policy research and preparedness measurement without duplicating the statutory responsibilities of existing public health institutions.

The academy urged Nigerians to remain vigilant without panic, rely on verified public health information, disclose relevant travel and exposure histories to healthcare professionals, seek medical attention promptly and avoid spreading rumours or stigmatising suspected patients.

It said that public trust, responsible communication and community cooperation are essential to successful epidemic preparedness.

Baale said Nigeria must translate its experience in containing Ebola in 2014 into lasting institutional capacity.

“Our greatest tribute to the healthcare professionals and institutions that protected Nigeria in 2014 is to build a stronger, more resilient and permanently prepared healthcare system. We must not wait for the first imported case to discover whether our surveillance systems, laboratories, emergency supplies, healthcare workforce, and response structures are ready,” he said.

“Preparedness is not panic. Preparedness is foresight, competence, coordination and national responsibility. Above all, preparedness saves lives.”

The academy reaffirmed its commitment to advancing pharmaceutical sciences, strengthening interprofessional collaboration, supporting evidence-based public health policy and contributing to a more resilient Nigerian healthcare system.

World.title: Popoola: Africa Must Connect Capital to Build Business Champions
World.content:
Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX Group) has called for a more integrated approach to capital formation across Africa, connecting businesses with appropriate sources of financing at every stage of their growth to build globally competitive enterprises.

Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, Temi Popoola, made the call at the Financial Times Africa Summit 2026 in London on Wednesday, October 21, during a panel session titled ‘Building African Champions – The Investment Case for Scaling SMEs.’

Popoola noted that capital markets have traditionally focused on large, mature companies ready to list, while promising businesses often require several rounds of financing before they can access public markets.

“Historically, we have taken a sort of a top-down approach to look for big companies ready to go public,” he said, explaining that businesses typically progress from founder funding and support from friends and family to venture capital, private investment and, ultimately, public-market financing.

He observed that the growing availability of private capital, alongside fewer new listings and an increase in delistings across several markets, underscores the need for a more connected capital formation ecosystem. Rather than waiting for businesses to mature before engaging with them, capital market institutions must find ways to support promising enterprises earlier in their development.

This requires stronger connections between public markets and the broader investment landscape, including private equity, venture capital and institutional investors. Such linkages can help businesses access financing as they grow while creating potential exit opportunities for private investors through public listings.

Popoola also highlighted family-owned enterprises, describing them as “hidden champions” that could make significant contributions to African capital markets if supported to scale and access appropriate sources of capital.

He identified receivables and invoice financing as another way capital markets can help ease funding constraints facing smaller businesses. By enabling companies to leverage invoices, receivables and purchase orders linked to larger corporate customers, these financing structures can help SMEs unlock working capital and sustain growth.

In Nigeria, the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) Growth Board provides small-cap and growth-oriented companies with a pathway to raise long-term capital through the public market, supported by more flexible listing requirements.

The Exchange is also working with institutions such as the Bank of Industry (BoI) to strengthen SME investment readiness through targeted engagements, capacity building and greater awareness of capital market financing opportunities. These efforts support the development of a stronger pipeline of businesses capable of accessing public markets as they grow.

Popoola’s remarks underscores the importance of a connected financing ecosystem in enabling promising African businesses to transition into established enterprises, attract institutional investment and expand beyond their domestic markets.

Achieving this requires collaboration across public and private capital providers, supported by capital markets equipped to facilitate sustainable business growth and broader economic development.

The Financial Times Africa Summit 2026 brought together business and financial sector leaders to examine investment opportunities and the conditions required to support Africa’s next generation of business champions.

World.title: BAS Finance: SME Lending Requires Better Risk Assessment, Not Just More Capital
World.content:
* Firm disburses N55bn to over 120 businesses in nine months, expands invoice-backed financing

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Managing Director of BAS Finance, Adnan Kayode, has said that expanding access to credit for Nigerian small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs) requires better risk assessment and a deeper understanding of businesses’ transactions rather than an exclusive reliance on conventional collateral.

Kayode said lenders could improve access to financing by assessing verifiable invoices, buyers and delivery records to determine the repayment capacity of businesses that might otherwise struggle to secure credit from traditional banks.

He spoke as BAS Finance emerged SME Lender of the Year at the 2026 BusinessDay Banking and Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards held on October 9 at The Civic Centre, Lagos.

The company’s sister subsidiary, BAS Capital, also won the SME Investment Bank of the Year award, recognising its role in structuring and raising capital for businesses seeking to expand beyond conventional borrowing.

Explaining the company’s lending philosophy, in a statement on Thursday in Abuja, Kayode said the challenge facing many businesses was not necessarily the absence of viable commercial opportunities but the difficulty of satisfying the requirements through which financial institutions assess creditworthiness.

“Lending to a small business well is an underwriting problem before it is a capital problem,” he said.

“If you can see the invoice, the buyer and the delivery record, you are not taking the risk the market thinks you are taking. What we have built is the ability to see those things quickly enough for the financing to still be useful.”

BAS Finance said it disbursed N55 billion to more than 120 businesses over nine months, with an average transaction size of N2 billion and a median disbursement period of seven days.

The company focuses on financing businesses that fall outside conventional banking criteria, particularly through arrangements linked to receivables and productive assets.

Its approach places emphasis on identifiable commercial transactions and repayment sources, offering an alternative for businesses whose financing applications may be constrained by collateral requirements or lengthy approval processes.

Through Zuvy Technologies, acquired by BAS Group in 2025, BAS Finance has also expanded its invoice-backed financing services to suppliers of large corporate organisations.

The model enables suppliers to seek financing against invoices arising from completed or verifiable transactions, potentially easing the pressure on working capital while they await payment from corporate buyers.

Kayode’s position highlights a broader challenge in Nigeria’s SME financing market, where the cost of borrowing is only one of several obstacles confronting business owners seeking formal credit.

Lengthy application procedures, collateral requirements and difficulties demonstrating creditworthiness have also constrained access to financing, particularly for enterprises with limited fixed assets but identifiable customers and commercial transactions.

Estimates of Nigeria’s SME financing gap vary according to the methodology used. However, a figure of approximately N13 trillion was presented at the 2025 Annual Directors Conference of the Chartered Institute of Directors, underscoring the scale of the challenge.

Micro, small and medium enterprises account for a substantial share of economic activity and employment, yet many continue to face difficulties obtaining financing suited to their operational needs.

BAS Group’s position is that addressing the challenge requires lenders and investment institutions to match financing instruments to businesses’ circumstances, rather than treating every funding request as a conventional loan application.

Group Chief Executive Officer, Abdulateef Hussein, said businesses required different forms of capital depending on their activities and stages of development.

“The question is not only whether capital exists. It is whether anyone has done the work of matching it to the business in front of them,” Hussein said.

He explained that a manufacturer seeking funds to fulfil a confirmed order might require short-term working capital, while a company pursuing an acquisition or major expansion might need structured growth capital.

“Most of what gets called a funding gap is a translation failure,” he added.

The group’s approach combines lending with investment banking and capital-raising services through its subsidiaries.

While BAS Finance provides working capital and transaction-linked financing, BAS Capital advises companies that have outgrown conventional lending but remain below the threshold that typically attracts larger investment banking institutions.

BAS Capital’s Managing Director, Yinka Adetuberu, said many growing businesses needed financial institutions willing to undertake the structuring required to attract institutional and development finance investors.

“The companies we work with are not short of ambition or of a market. They are short of someone willing to do the structuring work at their size,” Adetuberu said.

The company reported closing more than 25 transactions valued at over N50 billion in 2026.

The recognition of both subsidiaries at the BAFI Awards highlights the two financing approaches pursued by the group: providing credit to businesses with identifiable commercial transactions and structuring investment capital for companies seeking to finance their next stage of growth.

Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Abuja, BAS Group operates across lending, investment banking, wealth and asset management, insurance and financial technology.

Its subsidiaries include BAS Finance, BAS Capital, BAS Wealth, BAS Financial Services, BAS Technologies, ALLY Healthcare and ALLY Microinsurance.

The group said the latest recognition marked the second consecutive year its companies had received awards at the BAFI ceremony. BAS Capital was previously named Emerging Investment Bank of the Year.

World.title: Gov Otu Presents N987.8bn 2027 Budget
World.content:
Cross River State Governor, Bassey Otu, yesterday presented a proposed N987.8 billion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly, christening it the ‘Budget of Consolidation and Renewed Hope’, and reaffirming his administration’s commitment to sustainable development, fiscal discipline, and inclusive economic growth.

Presenting the estimates in Calabar, Otu described the budget as more than an aggregation of figures, characterising it as “a solemn and sacred pact laden with the trust, expectation and aspiration of the people for their improved livelihoods.”

He said its successful implementation would depend on prudent resource management, accountability and disciplined public expenditure, underscoring his administration’s determination to translate its social contract with the people into tangible improvements in their living conditions.

The proposed budget, valued at precisely N987,808,089,235.92, represents an increase of approximately 2.57 per cent over the 2026 budget.

Capital expenditure accounts for N708.43 billion, representing 71.72 per cent of the total provision, while recurrent expenditure stands at N279.38 billion, or 28.28 per cent. The substantial capital allocation, according to the governor, reflects the government’s determination to prioritise infrastructure, human capital development and productive investments capable of stimulating economic activity.

Otu explained that the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and Fiscal Strategy Paper provided the foundation for the estimates, adding that the budget would sustain ongoing programmes while opening new pathways for investment, employment creation and improved public services.

“The imperative of this exercise underscores our collective resolve to chart a sustainable course for the growth and development of our state,” he declared.

Addressing concerns surrounding the state’s debt profile, the governor maintained that his administration had refrained from obtaining fresh domestic and external loans since assuming office in 2023. Citing verifiable indices from the National Bureau of Statistics and the Debt Management Office, he said Cross River remained among the few states that had not contracted new loans during the period. He attributed the state’s existing debt burden to obligations inherited from previous administrations, explaining that debt servicing had constrained the pace at which available resources could be deployed to development projects.

He further clarified that the naira value of external debt had been affected by currency devaluation and foreign-exchange liberalisation.

“I cannot, and will never mortgage the future of our children with unsustainable loans,” Otu declared, pledging to strengthen internally generated revenue, maximise federal allocations and attract development assistance and private-sector investment to finance the state’s development priorities.

Reviewing the performance of the 2026 budget, the governor acknowledged the pressures of exchange-rate volatility, rising operational costs, supply-chain disruptions and inherited debt obligations. He disclosed that the administration had collaborated with the legislature to enact a supplementary budget, raising the spending framework to N963.07 billion to accommodate urgent interventions and counterpart-funding requirements.

Among the achievements highlighted was the delivery of more than 608 kilometres of interconnected road projects across the three senatorial districts, including the Nsan–Oban Road in Akamkpa, the Adiabo–Ikoneto Road in Odukpani and the Yahe–Ebo–Wanakade Road in Yala.

He also reported progress in rural electrification through solar streetlights, mini-grids and network rehabilitation, describing the interventions as essential to reopening economic corridors, improving mobility and restoring commercial activity in underserved communities.

Agriculture featured prominently in the governor’s account of the administration’s economic transformation agenda. Otu disclosed that more than 20,000 bags of fertiliser had been distributed to 8,000 farmers, while over one million improved oil-palm, cowpea and cocoa seedlings had been provided to farmers across the state. He also highlighted the establishment of a 50,000-hectare rice project and support for more than 5,300 livestock farmers, alongside loans, grants and agricultural machinery for smallholder and large-scale producers.

According to him, an N18 billion offtake arrangement had helped advance the state’s agricultural initiatives, while the cash-crop revolution was strengthening the productive capacity of farmers.

“There is no food security without agriculture,” he asserted, adding that the government intended to become Nigeria’s leading cocoa and oil-palm-producing state through expanded cultivation, mechanisation, agro-allied industries and private-sector partnerships.

On healthcare, education and public-sector welfare, Otu outlined interventions designed to improve access, strengthen institutions and enhance service delivery. He cited the renovation and rehabilitation of hospitals, the establishment of medical oxygen plants in Calabar and Ogoja in partnership with UNICEF, and the upgrading of state-owned Schools of Nursing and Midwifery to accreditation standards. He also highlighted a reported 95 per cent routine immunisation coverage, implementation of the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure for medical workers and an increase in the retirement age of health workers from 60 to 65 years.

In education, he said the state had deployed more than N17 billion in Universal Basic Education Commission intervention funds, supported classroom construction and rehabilitation, paid WAEC examination fees for 43,694 Cross River State indigenes and approved the promotion of more than 14,000 teaching and non-teaching staff.

The government, he added, was targeting a literacy rate of 98 per cent from the current estimated 80.7 per cent, while strengthening technical and vocational education to equip young people with employable and entrepreneurial skills.

The 2027 estimates also assign prominent roles to aviation, transportation, maritime development and tourism in the state’s economic diversification strategy. The governor disclosed the integration of a new Bombardier CRJ regional jet into the state’s aviation assets, bringing the fleet to five aircraft, alongside accelerated construction work at the Obudu International Passenger and Cargo Airport. He further highlighted the acquisition of 730 electric vehicles, comprising inter-city and metropolitan buses, tricycles and motorcycles, to reduce commuting costs and support cleaner transportation. On the maritime front, he said the Bakassi Deep Seaport had secured the federal government’s approval and Certificate of Compliance, and was awaiting the commencement of construction, with anticipated private investment of approximately $3.5 billion.

He also cited the federal government’s formal re-accreditation of Cross River as a littoral state, describing it as a strategic development for the state’s maritime ambitions. “Our overall target in this sector is to transform our aviation business model into a highly profitable and self-sustaining revenue asset for the state,” he said.

Infrastructure receives the largest explicitly listed sectoral allocation of N246.1 billion, followed by education with N99.6 billion, health with N85.4 billion, agriculture with N28.2 billion and aviation with N21.8 billion. Other provisions include N20.2 billion for the House of Assembly, N19.1 billion for the judiciary, N16.6 billion for power and N11.3 billion for tourism. The governor said the budget would continue to align with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, ensuring continuity in unfinished projects and directing resources towards the state’s strategic priorities.

He pledged continued investment in forest conservation and the green economy, judicial infrastructure, security and youth empowerment.

In education, the governor reaffirmed the policy of free and compulsory education from primary to junior secondary school, alongside the payment of WAEC fees for public-school students. On the judiciary, he promised adequate funding for ongoing court projects and further improvements in the working conditions of judicial officers, while urging the institution to pursue reforms that would strengthen public confidence in justice delivery.

Concluding his presentation, Otu pledged to sustain a government that is responsive to the needs of citizens, prudent in the management of public resources and accountable to the electorate. He emphasised the importance of harmonious relations among the executive, legislature and judiciary, describing institutional cooperation as indispensable to peace, stability and shared prosperity. The governor formally sought the Assembly’s consideration and timely passage of the proposed N987.8 billion Appropriation Bill, expressing confidence that its implementation would accelerate economic growth and improve the welfare of Cross Riverians.

World.title: APC Deploys Diaspora Network to Fight Anti-Tinubu Narratives
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress (APC) has unveiled an international mobilisation and media offensive to defend President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, counter negative narratives about his administration, and rally support for his re-election in 2027, targeting Nigerians living across major countries in Africa, Europe, Asia, the Middle East and North America.

Under the plan, the party intends to activate its overseas chapters, deploy coordinated digital advocacy, establish a rapid-response mechanism to challenge misinformation, mobilise diaspora funding and encourage voter participation at home as it seeks to shape public perception of Tinubu’s first term ahead of the presidential election.

The Director of the PBAT/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) Directorate of Diaspora Mobilisation, Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, unveiled the strategy at a press briefing in Abuja, describing Nigerians abroad as an influential constituency whose financial contributions, professional expertise and international networks could be harnessed to support the administration.

The initiative signals the APC’s determination to make the diaspora an organised component of its re-election campaign, using Nigerians’ connections with relatives, communities and professional networks abroad to communicate the government’s position on its economic reforms and development agenda.

Dabiri-Erewa said the directorate would not limit its mobilisation to party members, but would also reach out to Nigerians abroad who were willing to participate in the campaign.

“Nigerians abroad are not outsiders. They are stakeholders. They are our doctors, nurses, engineers, students, traders, innovators and community leaders, who send over $20 billion annually back home in remittances,” she said.

She identified the mobilisation of APC diaspora chapters in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, South Africa, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, France, Germany, Australia, Turkey, India and Kazakhstan as a priority, alongside engagement with diaspora associations and community leaders.

At the centre of the strategy is a digital advocacy campaign tagged: ‘Operation Tell Your Story’, through which supporters would receive short videos, infographics and other communication materials promoting the administration’s policies and achievements.

The campaign would address the foreign exchange reforms, foreign reserves, support for small businesses, housing programmes and opportunities for students, while seeking to counter claims the directorate considers misleading.

Dabiri-Erewa also announced plans for a rapid-response hub to provide data, fact-check claims and promote what she described as credible information about Nigeria’s investment climate, economic stabilisation and prospects under Tinubu.

“Our directorate will serve as a rapid-response hub in case of misinformation about Nigeria and the administration. We will provide credible data, fact-check and positive narratives about Nigeria’s investment climate, stabilisation of the economy and the future under President Tinubu,” she said.

The move comes amid continuing public debate over the administration’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange system, which have had significant implications for households and businesses.

Dabiri-Erewa acknowledged the hardship associated with the subsidy removal but defended the policy as a necessary intervention to address structural weaknesses in the economy.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has decided not to manage our feelings, but to fix the system. And it takes a bold leader to do that,” she said.

She argued that Nigerians living abroad could help explain the rationale behind the reforms to their families and communities, particularly because of their understanding of the challenges associated with the previous foreign exchange arrangements.

However, the directorate’s strategy will face the challenge of persuading voters at home that the administration’s policies are delivering sufficient benefits to justify the economic sacrifices they have experienced. The effectiveness of the campaign will therefore depend not only on the reach of its messaging but also on the credibility of its claims and the administration’s record against measurable economic outcomes.

Beyond digital advocacy, the APC plans to mobilise diaspora contributions through structured fundraising platforms to finance campaign activities, voter education materials, town hall meetings and grassroots mobilisation.

Dabiri-Erewa said the proposed fundraising arrangements would emphasise transparency and accountability, but did not disclose the amount the directorate hopes to raise or provide details of the proposed platforms.

The fourth strand of the strategy would focus on voter education and homecoming mobilisation, with diaspora Nigerians encouraged to remind eligible relatives and community members to register, collect their Permanent Voter Cards and participate in the election.

The directorate also intends to use its overseas networks to encourage Nigerians abroad to return home, engage their communities and take part in the political process.

In a related appeal, Dabiri-Erewa called on the National Assembly to consider constitutional amendments that would allow Nigerians living abroad to vote in Nigerian elections.

She acknowledged that diaspora voting remained a subject of debate but expressed hope that lawmakers would address the issue, potentially expanding the formal participation of Nigerians abroad in the country’s electoral process.

Dabiri-Erewa, who also heads the Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NiDCOM), said the commission had established a portal for registering Nigerians living outside the country and put the estimated diaspora population at more than 17 million.

She also urged Nigerians to monitor how state and local governments utilise increased allocations following the removal of the petrol subsidy, arguing that greater public revenue should be accompanied by accountability in spending.

Other members of the directorate backed the administration’s economic policies, acknowledging the hardship associated with the reforms while arguing that the intended benefits would take time to materialise. They highlighted investment, skills transfer, business partnerships and collaboration with government institutions as additional ways Diaspora Nigerians could contribute to national development.

Dabiri-Erewa urged the media to support the directorate’s communication efforts, saying the campaign would focus on continuity, national development and Tinubu’s stated ambition to move Nigeria from reforms to prosperity.

With the 2027 election approaching, the APC’s strategy places diaspora mobilisation, digital communication and the battle over the interpretation of the administration’s economic record at the heart of its re-election effort. Whether the initiative translates into broader electoral support will ultimately depend on how Nigerians judge the government’s performance and whether the campaign can substantiate its claims with credible evidence.

World.title: Meet the three Orlando Pirates youngsters nicknamed “Messi”
World.content:
Orlando Pirates’ Jacob Serman, Khumoetsile Van Schalkwyk and Ofentse Moeletsi share a rather special nickname. It is from none other than the greatest ever football player Lionel Messi.

To make it more exciting, Serman, Van Schalkwyk and Moeletsi play for different dvisions within Buccaneers youth.

THREE ORLANDO PIRATES YOUNGSTERS NICKNAMED MESSI

Jacob Serman



Formerly with SuperSport United, Serman is an exciting attacking midfielder and winger who has also turned out for rivals Kaizer Chiefs.

The left-footed youngster won multiple Under-13 and Under-14 Gauteng Development League titles before making the high-profile move to their Soweto rivals.

A elegant technician has reportedly trained with the club’s DStv Diski Challenge squad.



Khumoetsile Van Schalkwyk

Van Schalkwyk, meanwhile, is a versatile winger capable of playing on either flank. Capable of being the next Relebohile Mofokeng, he is originally from Stella, he developed through regional sides including Masokolara FC, SACOV FC and Sol Plaatje FC before joining the North West University Soccer Institute.

Wearing the number 23 shirt, Van Schalkwyk has earned recognition for his football intelligence and long-range shooting ability. He is part of the Pirates DStv Diski Challenge team.



Ofentse Moeletsi

Moeletsi completes the trio. The 21-year-old attacker first attracted attention while playing for Highlands Park’s Under-19 team, where his ability to beat defenders on either wing caught the eye.

He later featured in the DStv Diski Challenge setup at Sekhukhune United before moving to Orlando Pirates. Moeletsi has featured in the club’s ABC Motsepe League and DStv Diski Challenge structures.



NEXT GENERATION OF TALENT

The nickname Messi is associated with exceptional dribbling, creativity and football intelligence, qualities that have helped make Lionel Messi one of the greatest players of his generation.

Although the nickname alone does not guarantee success, Serman, Van Schalkwyk and Moeletsi have opportunities to develop their talents within one of South Africa’s biggest football clubs.

World.title: Irvin Khoza and Orlando Pirates fans react to Ncikazi’s departure
World.content:
Orlando Pirates chairman Dr Irvin Khoza has reacted following the departure of long-serving assistant coach Mandla Ncikazi.

After days of speculation, the Buccaneers confirmed that the 57-year-old will be leaving the club to take up the Head Coach position at a team in the Premier Soccer League.

“The move follows discussions with management this morning in which Mr Ncikazi expressed his wish to pursue the opportunity to lead a team again. The Club has given him its blessing to do so,” the club said in a statement.



Pirates chairman Irvin Khoza thanked Ncikazi and acknowledged his ambition to return to head coaching.

“Mandla leaves with our gratitude and our blessing. His contribution to Orlando Pirates has been evident throughout his time with us. We respect his wish to pursue this new opportunity and wish him success as he takes on a new responsibility,” said Dr Khoza.

Pirates fans praise Ncikazi following his departure

Many Orlando Pirates fans took to social media to thank the departed coach.



@malalaveve wrote: “He was there during the rainy days.”

@mr_shimmy wrote: “Farewell coach Mandla. You served the team with dedication and determination. All the best in your new role.

@kanyane23 wrote: “Farewell taMindlo. Thank you for serving the Ghost with professionalism throughout.”



With Ncikazi having left Pirates, it is believed he will return to Golden Arrows as head coach. He departs the club with nine trophies as part of the Bucs technical team, where he served mostly as an assistant coach.

World.title: Joburg water WARNING: Don’t drink tap water
World.content:
Johannesburg Water has warned residents in parts of Bezuidenhout Valley not to use tap water until safety tests confirm it is safe. Image: Pexels

Johannesburg Water has warned residents in parts of Bezuidenhout Valley not to use tap water until further notice amid concerns over its safety.

The warning follows damage to a water pipeline at the corner of 6th Street and 8th Avenue.

Although crews completed repairs on Wednesday night, 21 October, the utility has yet to confirm whether the water is safe for consumption.



JOHANNESBURG WATER ISSUES WARNING

According to a report, the pipeline was damaged when a tree stump fell onto it during excavation work.

A contractor was replacing a sewer pipe when the incident occurred.

Johannesburg Water subsequently isolated the affected section of the network and began testing water samples to establish whether the supply meets drinking water quality standards.



“Residents in the affected areas are advised not to use the water until further notice,” the utility said.

The warning affects sections of 8th Avenue at its intersections with:

4th Street

5th Street

6th Street

7th Street

Residents have been urged to avoid using tap water until Johannesburg Water confirms that it is safe.



WHEN WILL WATER BE RESTORED?

Johannesburg Water said the affected supply would remain isolated until laboratory tests confirmed that the water met the required safety standards.

Alternative water supplies will remain available to affected residents while the restriction is in place.

The utility has not announced a specific time for the restoration of normal supply.



It said residents would receive an update once laboratory clearance had been obtained.

HOW TO REPORT WATER PROBLEMS

Residents experiencing water-related problems can contact Johannesburg Water through the following channels:

Customer service: 0860 056 2874

0860 056 2874 Alternative number: 010 061 4470

010 061 4470 Email: fault@jwater.co.za

Residents are advised to monitor official Johannesburg Water communication channels for further updates before resuming normal water use.

World.title: Earthquake strikes Namibia
World.content:
A magnitude 4.9 earthquake struck north-western Namibia on Wednesday night, with an aftershock recorded on Thursday morning. Image: Facebook / EarthquakeTodayOrg

A magnitude 4.9 earthquake struck north-western Namibia on Wednesday night, with an aftershock recorded on Thursday morning.

The earthquake was recorded at 22:34 on 21 October in the Kamanjab area of the Kunene Region, according to Namibia’s Ministry of Industries, Mines and Energy.

The ministry confirmed the event on Thursday, saying it had been detected by six stations in the Namibian Seismological Network and two regional stations belonging to South Africa’s Seismological Network.



The United States Geological Survey (USGS), meanwhile, placed the earthquake’s epicentre about 68km north-north-west of Khorixas, at a depth of 10km

Aftershock recorded on Thursday morning

A subsequent tremor was recorded at approximately 08:08 on Thursday, measuring magnitude 3.2, according to a report by the Namibian website.

The initial earthquake’s magnitude of 4.9 is generally classified as light to moderate. The extent of shaking can vary depending on distance from the epicentre, depth and local ground conditions.

The reports cited did not confirm any deaths, injuries or structural damage resulting from the earthquake.

Residents urged to take precautions

Following the tremor and aftershock, the ministry advised residents to take precautions in the event of further seismic activity.

People indoors during an earthquake should move outside to a clear area if it is safe to do so, or seek shelter beneath a sturdy table if they cannot leave safely.



Those outdoors should move away from buildings, trees and power lines. Residents were also advised to stay away from windows and watch for falling objects.

World.title: Mandla Ncikazi’s trophy cabinet with Orlando Pirates
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have officially announced the departure of Abdeslam Ouaddou‘s assistant Mandla Ncikazi.

Ncikazi had been linked with a possible exit following his absence from the bench for a number of games now.

Ouaddou had attributed Ncikazi’s absence to a surgery that the coach recently had, but the writing was always on the wall.



Subsequent to that, reports surfaced that Golden Arrows were interested in taking Ncikazi back following a series of poor results under the tutelage of Pitso Dladla.

Dladla, though, has maintained that he is still in charge of Arrows and that he still has backing of the management.

Now, Ncikazi, who held different coaching positions, including that of a co-coach alongside Fadlu Davids in 2021, will be take up a coaching role at an unnamed PSL club.

ORLANDO PIRATES TRANSFER NEWS: MANDLA NCIKAZI’S TROPHIES

During his stint as co-coach, Ncikazi won the CAF Confederation Cup silver medal with Pirates after losing to RS Berkane in the final.

He recently also got a silver medal with Pirates as they lost 2-0 to Mamelodi Sundowns in the MTN8 final.

However, Ncikazi leaves with EIGHT major trophies under two different coaches.



His first major trophy was the 2022 MTN8 under the leadership of Jose Riveiro, and it was followed by the 2023 Nedbank Cup.

Overall, Ncikazi won FIVE trophies in three seasons with Riveiro and won THREE, including last season’s league title.
