World.title: Zambia Politics Explained, Who Holds Power in 2026
World.content:
ZAMBIA · POLITICS

Key Facts — The country Zambia is a landlocked southern African republic of about 21.9 million people, according to the World Bank’s 2025 estimate. A directly elected president is both head of state and head of government.

— Who holds power President Hakainde Hichilema of the United Party for National Development (UPND) took the oath for a second term on 1 September 2026. Mutale Nalumango remains vice-president.

— The vote The electoral commission declared Hichilema the winner on 18 August 2026 with 60.5% of the vote against 37.8% for Brian Mundubile. Turnout was about 57%.

— Parliament The new National Assembly has 226 elected seats, 40 proportional-representation seats and up to 11 presidential nominees. Hichilema’s party holds a large majority.

— The cabinet News Diggers reported on 22 October 2026 that only four ministers had been appointed since the August election: finance, foreign affairs, health and the green economy.

— The opposition Mundubile and 17 others are held as treason suspects and are seeking bail in the High Court. Ezra Tembo is the recognised Leader of the Opposition in parliament.

— Still open The remaining cabinet posts, the treason case, a lawsuit over the August court closures and a new IMF programme are all unresolved as of 22 October 2026.

Zambia politics in October 2026 rests on President Hakainde Hichilema, who won a second term in August and commands a large majority in parliament. His copper-exporting country is negotiating a US$1.472 billion IMF programme while prosecuting its main opposition leader for treason.

This guide to Zambia names who holds power and what remains unsettled.

Scene from President Hakainde Hichilema’s second inauguration at National Heroes Stadium, Lusaka, 1 September 2026. (Photo: THE ONE PEOPLE, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas across Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. × Best for expats Cost of living Safest places Easy visas Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

How Zambia Politics Works

Zambia is a presidential republic, and its constitution makes the president head of state, head of government and commander-in-chief. Zambians fill that office in a general election every five years, on the second Thursday of August.

A candidate needs more than half of the valid votes to win outright; otherwise the top two go to a runoff within 37 days. A person who has twice held the presidency is not eligible to stand again, which means Hichilema cannot run in 2031.

The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ), the independent body that runs elections, counted 8,786,300 registered voters in 226 constituencies. Its chairperson is Mwangala Zaloumis, and its chief electoral officer is Brown Kasaro.

Zambia politics in 2026 was shaped by late rule changes. Constitutional Amendment Act No. 13 of 2025 added seats and a proportional tier months before polling, says the Institute for Security Studies (ISS).

Observer missions from the European Union, the Southern African Development Community and the African Union raised concerns about those late changes, the ISS reports. The Zambia explainer covers the country’s wider background.

The President and His Inner Circle

Hakainde Hichilema leads the UPND and has held the presidency since 2021. The ECZ declared him re-elected on 18 August 2026 with about 60.5% of the vote, according to the Institute for Security Studies.

He was sworn in at National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka on 1 September 2026. Vice-President Mutale Nalumango, his running mate, kept her post and was still in office in mid-October 2026.

On 9 October 2026 Hichilema opened the new parliament with the Grow Zambia Agenda, a five-year plan to more than double the economy. Its yearly targets include 3 million tonnes of copper and US$1 billion in beef exports, according to Mwebantu, a Zambian news outlet.

The State House Team

On 22 October 2026 State House re-appointed seven presidential advisers, using powers in Article 92 of the constitution. Bradford Machila is principal private secretary, and Christopher Mundia advises on legal affairs.

Levy Ngoma covers political affairs, Jito Kayumba finance and investments, and Dr Pamela Nakamba economic affairs. Dr Lawrence Mwananyanda handles projects and national security, Joseph Lungu handles policy compliance, and Clayson Hamasaka speaks for State House.

File photo: President Hakainde Hichilema speaking at a meeting with US Vice President Kamala Harris. (Photo: Office of the US Vice President, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

The Cabinet and Key Ministers

On 14 September 2026 Hichilema swore in the first four ministers of his second term. Situmbeko Musokotwane returned as Minister of Finance and National Planning, and Mulambo Haimbe became Minister of Foreign Affairs.

Gilbert Siame took the Ministry of Green Economy and Environment, and Professor Roma Chilengi became Minister of Health. Hichilema told them to deliver results under the Grow Zambia Agenda and to respect collective responsibility, according to Mwebantu.

As of 22 October 2026 no further ministers had been named, and several posts were vacant, News Diggers reported. State House says government continues to function, and State House spokesman Clayson Hamasaka says it has not delayed the appointments.

The cabinet by law includes the president, the vice-president, the ministers and the attorney-general. Mulilo Kabesha is attorney-general, the government’s chief legal adviser, and Gilbert Phiri is director of public prosecutions, the chief prosecutor.

File photo: President Hakainde Hichilema with his first cabinet, 22 September 2021. (Photo: Chalo Chatu, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

Parliament and the Ruling Party’s Majority

Zambia’s National Assembly is the law-making body. The new house has 226 elected members, up from 156, plus 40 proportional seats for women, youth and people with disabilities.

The president may also nominate up to 11 members.

By 24 August 2026 the ISS counted 138 UPND constituency wins and 60 for the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP), Mundubile’s party.

Only two of the 13 parties that contested qualified for the proportional seats, the ECZ says. The NRPUP submitted only eight names, so the commission gave the unfilled seats to the UPND.

The UPND received 32 of the 40 proportional seats, News Diggers reported. Zaloumis denied favouritism on 15 October 2026.

Nelly Mutti, a Lusaka lawyer and the first woman to hold the post, was re-elected unopposed as Speaker on 2 October 2026.

The Opposition and the Treason Case

Brian Mundubile, the NRPUP candidate, led the Tonse Alliance, which inherited many strongholds of the former ruling Patriotic Front, according to the ISS. On 20 October 2026 Speaker Mutti recognised NRPUP president Ezra Tembo as Leader of the Opposition.

She named Milenge member Chonde as party whip and Paul Lungu as deputy whip. A dispute inside the party followed after Stephen Kampyongo, the member for Shiwang’andu, said fellow members had elected him instead, News Diggers reported.

On 14 August 2026, the day after the vote, security forces raided a property in Lusaka, and former transport minister Mutotwe Kafwaya was shot dead. Eleven people were arrested on suspicion of holding military-grade weapons for an armed insurrection, which Mundubile denies.

Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 others are held as treason suspects at Mukobeko prison in Kabwe.

They have asked the High Court for constitutional bail, News Diggers reported on 20 October 2026.

On 22 October 2026 the state and the defence agreed to add Director of Public Prosecutions Gilbert Phiri to the bail case. The accused have not been tried and are presumed innocent.

Courts, Security Forces and the Electoral Commission

Chief Justice Mumba Malila heads the judiciary, and Professor Margaret Munalula presides over the Constitutional Court, which settles election and constitutional disputes. In August 2026 that court ruled the Auditor General’s appointment unconstitutional because of his age, News Diggers reported.

Between 24 and 27 August 2026 the government closed the Constitutional Court, the Supreme Court and other court premises, citing security concerns.

Rights lawyer Linda Kasonde then emailed an election petition to the chief justice, who called the method highly irregular, African Arguments reported from her account.

The Chapter One Foundation has asked the Constitutional Court to declare the closures unlawful, and African Arguments reported no ruling by 9 October 2026. Human Rights Watch called the closures a denial of access to justice.

Lieutenant General Geoffrey Zyeele commands the Zambia Army, and Maambo Hamaundu is permanent secretary at the Defence Ministry, News Diggers reported on 16 October 2026. In June 2026 civil society groups argued that the army has no mandate to keep internal order.

The Zambia Police Service answers to an inspector general. On 4 October 2026 News Diggers reported, citing police sources, that Hichilema had dismissed Deputy Inspector General Charity Munganga.

Provinces, Chiefs and Local Councils

Zambia has 10 provinces and 116 districts, and the president appoints a provincial minister from among members of parliament to run each province’s administration. The constitution provides no elected governors, so provincial power flows from State House.

Voters elect councillors, and mayors and council chairpersons stood in the same August 2026 vote, the ECZ says.

The constitution also creates a House of Chiefs with five traditional leaders from each province. The House advises the National Assembly on development and decides matters of customary law, though it holds no executive power.

Rising Figures to Watch

Hichilema cannot seek a third term, so Zambia politics will turn to who shapes the UPND after 2031.

Roma Chilengi, health minister, said on 6 October 2026 that a US$1.5 billion health agreement with the United States had been revised to drop a specimen-sharing clause, according to Mwebantu.

Situmbeko Musokotwane, finance minister, announced the staff-level IMF deal on 9 October 2026 and is the government’s main voice on debt and growth.

Ezra Tembo leads the opposition benches, and Chonde is his party whip.

Nelly Mutti, speaker since 2021, decides who counts as opposition leader and was re-elected unopposed on 2 October 2026.

What It Means for US Readers

Zambia politics now offers Washington a re-elected government that controls parliament. Zambia and the United States have agreed a revised text of a US$1.5 billion health agreement, Mwebantu reported on 6 October 2026.

Zambia is also seeking a 36-month IMF programme worth US$1.472 billion that needs board approval, according to Mwebantu. The IMF projects 5.6% growth for 2026, and annual inflation was 6.1% in September 2026, the Zambia Statistics Agency says.

The ISS says Hichilema begins his last term with a stronger mandate and fewer institutional checks. Copper is central to the Grow Zambia Agenda, which sets a target of 3 million tonnes a year.

For regional context see the neighbours guide and the election result.

File photo, December 2022: President Hakainde Hichilema with then US President Joe Biden and Jill Biden at the White House during the US-Africa Leaders Summit. (Photo: US Department of State, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

What Is Not Known

No date has been given for filling the remaining ministerial posts,. The identity of the full cabinet will shape how fast policy moves.

The High Court bail hearing for Mundubile and the 17 others is continuing, and no trial date is known. The Constitutional Court had not ruled on the Chapter One Foundation’s challenge to the court closures by 9 October 2026.

The IMF board has not approved the new programme, and the Tonse Alliance’s secretary-general has threatened legal action over the proportional seats. Who will lead the UPND after Hichilema’s last term is also unknown, and Zambia politics offers no clear answer yet.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is the president of Zambia in 2026?

Hakainde Hichilema of the UPND is president, and Zambia politics now centres on him. He was sworn in for a second five-year term on 1 September 2026.

Who is the vice-president of Zambia?

Mutale Nalumango is vice-president and was Hichilema’s running mate in 2026. Under the constitution she is also leader of government business in parliament.

How strong is the ruling party in parliament?

The UPND holds a large majority in the 277-seat National Assembly, with 138 constituency wins counted by the ISS as of 24 August 2026. The ECZ also gave it 32 of the 40 proportional seats.

Who leads the opposition in Zambia politics?

Ezra Tembo of the NRPUP was recognised as Leader of the Opposition on 20 October 2026. Brian Mundubile, the party’s presidential candidate, is in custody facing a treason charge.

Has the full Zambian cabinet been named?

No. News Diggers reported on 22 October 2026 that only four ministers had been appointed: Musokotwane, Haimbe, Siame and Chilengi.

Can Hichilema run again in 2031?

No. The constitution bars anyone who has twice held the presidency from standing again, so his second term is his last.

World.title: Suriname Politics Explained, Who Holds Power in 2026
World.content:
SURINAME · POLITICS

Key Facts — The country Suriname is a small country on the north coast of South America. It became independent on 25 November 1975 and has run under its current constitution since a 1987 referendum.

— Head of state President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons is head of state and head of government. The National Assembly elected her on 6 July 2025, and she was sworn in on 16 July 2025.

— Parliament The National Assembly has 51 seats, filled at the 25 May 2025 election. The NDP won 18 seats and the VHP 17, with 16 seats for five smaller parties.

— Who governs Six parties share power in Suriname politics: NDP, ABOP, NPS, PL, BEP and A20. Together they hold 34 of 51 seats, exactly the two-thirds needed to elect a president.

— The opposition The VHP, the party that led the previous government, holds all 17 opposition seats as of October 2026.

— Still open A fight over who runs the telecoms regulator TAS reached the president’s office on 21 October 2026 and set coalition parties against each other.

Suriname politics matters to Americans because this small South American country is preparing for new oil and gas income that a six-party coalition will control.

President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons leads that coalition, which holds two-thirds of the 51-seat National Assembly as of October 2026. This guide explains who holds power, how the system works and where it could crack.

The newer National Assembly building in Paramaribo, where the 51 members sit. File photo, 2022. (Photo: Ymnes, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Download the PDF checklist

Suriname Politics Starts With the 1987 Constitution

Suriname’s constitution was adopted by referendum in 1987, after the military coup of 25 February 1980 and a period without any constitution. The preamble of the text published by the National Assembly names that coup.

A constitutional-law lecturer wrote in Starnieuws on 20 October 2026 that the 1987 text restored formal democracy.

The same text, as amended in 1992, calls the National Assembly the highest organ of the state. It also makes the president head of state, head of government and chair of two advisory bodies, the State Council and the Security Council.

The president answers to the Assembly, and both serve five-year terms. The next general election is therefore due in 2030, and Suriname politics will turn on it.

The result is a mixed system that students of Suriname politics still argue about. A Starnieuws column of 20 October 2026 says the label, parliamentary or presidential, matters less than whether the system has worked for the country.

The President and the Vice President

Jennifer Geerlings-Simons is Suriname’s first woman president. The Assembly elected her on 6 July 2025 with no rival candidate, according to International IDEA, an intergovernmental democracy institute.

She was sworn in on 16 July 2025, according to International IDEA.

She also chairs the NDP, the National Democratic Party, according to a Starnieuws column of 20 October 2026. Under the constitution she names and dismisses ministers, leads the armed forces as supreme commander and steers foreign policy.

Gregory Rusland, leader of the National Party of Suriname (NPS), is vice president. The constitution gives him daily charge of the Council of Ministers, the cabinet of all ministers, and makes him answerable to the president.

A Starnieuws column of 20 October 2026 says NDP vice chair Faizal Abdoelgafoer holds an influential post at the president’s cabinet. The column presents him as a possible future NDP leader.

The president’s office was also in the news in late October 2026. On 21 October, Simons said she had not let the head of the telecoms regulator TAS stay on after her term ended on 20 October.

She will sign a successor’s appointment only after an inquiry.

The National Assembly and the Seven Parties

The National Assembly has 51 members, elected for five years. Its member list for 2025 to 2030 names Michael (Ashwin) Adhin of the NDP as chair and Ronnie Brunswijk of the ABOP as vice chair.

The Assembly is in recess every September.

Seven parties hold seats, and the Assembly lists each as a faction with a leader. Seat numbers below come from the Assembly’s own list as of 22 October 2026.

NDP, National Democratic Party: 18 seats. President Simons chairs the party, and Rabindre Parmessar leads its faction in the Assembly.

VHP, Progressive Reform Party: 17 seats, all in opposition. It led the previous government, and Asiskumar Gajadien leads its faction.

ABOP, General Liberation and Development Party: 6 seats. Ronnie Brunswijk is the Assembly’s vice chair, and Dinotha Vorswijk leads the faction.

NPS, National Party of Suriname: 6 seats. Vice President Rusland chairs it, and Jerrel Pawiroredjo leads the faction.

PL, Pertjajah Luhur: 2 seats, with Bronto Somohardjo as faction leader.

BEP, Brotherhood and Unity in Politics: 1 seat, held by faction leader Ronny Asabina.

A20, Alternative 2020: 1 seat, held by faction leader Steven Reyme.

An earlier National Assembly building in Paramaribo. File photo, 2008. (Photo: Mark Ahsmann, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

How the Coalition Holds Together

The NDP, ABOP, NPS, PL, BEP and A20 hold 18, 6, 6, 2, 1 and 1 seats, a total of 34. That is exactly two-thirds of 51, the share the constitution requires to elect the president or vice president in the Assembly.

If no candidate reaches two-thirds after two rounds, the choice goes to the United People’s Assembly. It adds the district and local councils to the National Assembly and decides by simple majority.

The coalition has strains. On 20 October 2026 the ABOP faction walked out of an Assembly meeting in protest after a heated exchange over the TAS dispute, Starnieuws reported.

The ABOP also rejected the letter Minister Raymond Landveld sent to the TAS director, Starnieuws reported on 21 October 2026.

The Ministers Who Run the Government

Ministers sit in the Council of Ministers, which the constitution calls the highest executive body of the government. Each name below appears as the sitting minister in a government or Starnieuws item dated September or October 2026.

The Central Bank of Suriname, shown here on the Waterkant in Paramaribo, is separate from the cabinet, but the finance minister works closely with it.

Finance and Planning: Adelien Wijnerman, who met the French ambassador on 25 September 2026.

Justice and Security: Harish Monorath, who answers for the police and ordered an inquiry on 21 October 2026 into officers who appeared at the TAS building.

Defence: Uraiqit Ramsaran, whose ministry reached a new health-insurance agreement with the state health fund on 16 October 2026.

Interior: Marinus Bee, who received a delegation from the foundation Kids van Amsterdam on 12 October 2026.

Foreign Affairs, International Business and Cooperation: Melvin Bouva, who met Albert Ramdin, secretary-general of the Organization of American States, in Washington on 20 October 2026.

Transport, Communication and Tourism: Raymond Landveld, who ordered the TAS director on 20 October 2026 to hand over her duties.

Regional Development: Miquella Huur, who said on 10 October 2026 she wants a land-rights conference in 2027.

Natural Resources: David Abiamofo, elected an alternate board member of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative on 12 October 2026.

The Central Bank of Suriname on the Waterkant, the waterfront street in Paramaribo. File photo. (Photo: Sharmil2672, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Security Forces, Courts and Prosecutors

The president is supreme commander of the armed forces under Article 100. The Defence Ministry runs the National Army, and the Justice Ministry oversees the Suriname Police Corps.

In October 2026 the two work side by side in the interior. The police corps told everyone staying without permission at Masonia, in the Sipaliwini district, to leave by 8 am on Friday 23 October 2026.

The army may help if they do not.

The courts sit under the Court of Justice, the highest court. The government appoints judges and the Attorney General after the Court’s advice.

Under Article 141, appointments to the Court of Justice and the Attorney General’s post are for life.

Attorney General García Paragsingh, named by Starnieuws on 21 October 2026, leads the public prosecution service. Politicians accused of crimes in office are tried by the Court of Justice after the Assembly impeaches them.

A separate Constitutional Court checks laws against the constitution. Its chair, vice chair and three members serve five-year terms and are appointed by the president from names the Assembly puts forward.

The prosecution service is under political scrutiny in Suriname politics. On 21 October 2026 Bronto Somohardjo of the PL asked the Attorney General for figures on whether suspects of every ethnic background are prosecuted equally.

Districts, Local Councils and the Interior

Suriname is divided into districts, and the districts into smaller units called resorts. Each has an elected council, and together the district and resort councils join the National Assembly in the United People’s Assembly.

The interior is where Suriname politics meets resources. Braganza Marketing Group, a farm company, was waiting in October 2026 for permission to start large farms with Mennonite settlers, Starnieuws reported.

Rooftops of Paramaribo, the capital where the government sits, in a photograph from about 1910 to 1914. (Photo: Rijksmuseum, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Rising Figures and the Next Contests

Party leadership races in Suriname politics have begun, according to a Starnieuws column by Nita Ramcharan on 20 October 2026. The VHP holds a board election in May 2027.

Former minister Armand Achaibersing has put himself forward for the chair, and vice chair Asis Gajadien is also preparing.

In the NDP, leadership elections are not expected until 2029, but talk of a successor to Simons has started. The column names Faizal Abdoelgafoer and Ashwin Adhin as people with ambitions.

Rusland, the NPS chair, has said he remains available if the party wants him.

Constitutional change may shape Suriname politics next. The 1987 constitution turns 40 on 30 September 2027.

A constitutional-law lecturer wrote in Starnieuws on 20 October 2026 that the anniversary is the time for a national review.

Any change to the constitution needs two-thirds of the Assembly, a share the coalition holds exactly. That gives each small coalition party an effective veto.

What It Means for US Readers

Deals in Suriname run through the Council of Ministers, and international agreements need the Assembly’s approval under Article 103. A contract signed by one ministry is therefore not final until the wider government agrees.

The coalition’s two-thirds margin is thin, so in Suriname politics a split among its smaller parties could stall big decisions. The ABOP, with six seats, showed on 20 October 2026 how one partner can strain the coalition.

Foreign Minister Melvin Bouva was in Washington in October 2026 for the US–Caribbean Dialogue and met Albert Ramdin, the OAS secretary-general. Bouva said Suriname wants an assertive diplomacy that attracts lasting investment, Starnieuws reported on 21 October 2026.

For more on the economy and foreign policy, see our guides to who runs Suriname’s economy, Suriname geopolitics and Suriname in South America.

The oil shock and inflation story covers prices, and the full country page is on the Suriname hub.

What Is Not Known

The outcome of the TAS dispute, a test of Suriname politics, is open. The board has gone to court for a quick ruling, and no court decision had been reported by 22 October 2026.

The military‘s current commander and the heads of the Court of Justice and Constitutional Court are not named in this guide. Neither is the current VHP chair.

Party platforms are also left out, because the sources used here describe leaders and seats rather than programmes. How long the six-party coalition lasts until the 2030 election is not known.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is the president of Suriname in 2026?

In Suriname politics the president is Jennifer Geerlings-Simons, who chairs the NDP. The National Assembly elected her on 6 July 2025, and she was sworn in on 16 July 2025.

How is the president of Suriname chosen?

The National Assembly elects the president, and the vote needs two-thirds of its 51 members, which is 34. If no one reaches that after two rounds, the United People’s Assembly decides by simple majority.

Which parties are in the Suriname coalition?

Suriname politics is run by six parties: the NDP, ABOP, NPS, PL, BEP and A20. Together they hold 34 of the 51 seats in the National Assembly as of October 2026.

Who leads the Suriname opposition?

In Suriname politics the VHP is the only opposition party, with 17 seats. Asiskumar Gajadien leads its faction in the Assembly.

Who is the vice president of Suriname?

Gregory Rusland, who chairs the NPS. He runs the Council of Ministers day to day and answers to the president.

When is the next general election in Suriname?

In Suriname politics Assembly members serve five-year terms from the 25 May 2025 election, so the next vote is due in 2030. The constitution allows an extension only in war or other extraordinary circumstances.

World.title: Saint Levant Plays São Paulo on 24 January 2027
World.content:
BRAZIL · CONCERTS

Key Facts — The show Palestinian singer and rapper Saint Levant plays his first concert in Brazil, a single show in São Paulo on his Afandi world tour.

— Date and venue Sunday, 24 January 2027, at Cine Joia in São Paulo’s Liberdade district, a former cinema that reopened as a concert house in 2011 with room for about 1,500 people.

— Gate times Doors open at 6:00 p.m. and the show starts at 8:00 p.m. local time, which is 4:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. US Eastern.

— Tickets Ticketmaster Brasil sells tickets online and at its Shopping Ibirapuera box office, with sales open since Tuesday, 20 October. Current availability is not confirmed.

— Prices Standing-floor tickets cost BRL 410 (about US$82) at full price and BRL 205 (about US$41) at half price for eligible buyers.

— Entry for US visitors US citizens need a Brazilian visa or e-visa approved before travel. The State Department rates Brazil Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them. Want prediction market reports on Brazil? Get yours free, right after you confirm →

Saint Levant brings his Afandi tour to São Paulo for a first Brazil show on Sunday, 24 January 2027. Tickets start at BRL 205 (about US$41).

Saint Levant, the Palestinian singer and rapper born Marwan Abdelhamid, plays his first show in Brazil on Sunday, 24 January 2027. The Saint Levant São Paulo concert is at Cine Joia, with doors at 6:00 p.m. and music at 8:00 p.m.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.0 %, Lula 49.0 % 35 national polls from 20 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

Live Nation Brasil promotes the show, and Ticketmaster Brasil sells tickets from BRL 205 (about US$41). The next day, Monday, 25 January 2027, is São Paulo’s city anniversary holiday, so the show falls on a long weekend.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Who Saint Levant Is

Saint Levant was born in Jerusalem, according to Ahram Online, an Egyptian news site, and the Brazilian site Trambicast. His mother is Franco-Algerian and his father is Serbian-Palestinian, both outlets say.

Ahram Online says he is known for the viral 2022 song Very Few Friends and the 2023 EP From Gaza, With Love. Billboard Brasil says that song is sung in Arabic, English and French.

Trambicast says his album AFANDI draws on Arab music icons such as George Wassouf and Kadim Al Saher. It blends them with contemporary and electronic production.

Billboard Brasil calls the São Paulo date his first show in Brazil, and Trambicast calls it a one-off. Live Nation Brasil lists it as part of the Afandi World Tour.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Brazil expat life Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Date, Time and Venue

Cine Joia is at Praça Carlos Gomes 82 in the Liberdade district, Trambicast says. Live Nation Brasil lists the show for Sunday, 24 January 2027, with doors at 6:00 p.m. and the show at 8:00 p.m.

Brazil has no daylight saving time, and US Eastern is on standard time in January. São Paulo is therefore two hours ahead, so doors are at 4:00 p.m. Eastern and the show is at 6:00 p.m. Eastern.

The age rating is 16 for entry without an adult, Trambicast says. Children aged 5 to 15 may enter with a parent or legal guardian, subject to change by court decision.

Bares SP, a São Paulo listings site, says Cine Joia opened in 1952 as a cinema. It reopened as a concert house on 11 November 2011, and Rolling Stone Brasil also put capacity at about 1,500 then.

The same listing describes a floor, an upper seating level with boxes and a small club room. It was last updated in January 2022, and both accounts are dated, so check capacity and layout with the venue.

Billboard Brasil lists only standing-floor tickets for this show. No seated or box sector is listed in the sources checked.

Tickets and Prices for Saint Levant in São Paulo

Ticketmaster Brasil is the official online seller, and Live Nation Brasil links its Saint Levant page to the sale. Sales opened on Tuesday, 20 October 2026, at 10:00 a.m. online and 11:00 a.m. at the box office.

The box office is at Shopping Ibirapuera, Avenida Ibirapuera 3103, lower floor Jurupis, and charges no service fee. Billboard Brasil and Trambicast both report this.

These are the launch prices. Conversions use open.er-api.com rates of Thursday, 22 October 2026, when US$1 bought BRL 5.02.

Pista (standing floor), full price: BRL 410 (about US$82).

Pista (standing floor), half price for eligible buyers: BRL 205 (about US$41).

Each CPF, the Brazilian taxpayer number, can buy up to six tickets, and no more than two at half price. Buyers can pay in up to three interest-free installments, Billboard Brasil says.

The sources do not say how a foreign visitor without a CPF buys a ticket. They also do not explain how a visitor proves eligibility for half price, so read the Ticketmaster Brasil rules first.

The organizers advise buying only through official channels, Trambicast says. Avoid resale listings, because the sources checked do not vouch for any.

Ticketmaster Brasil could not be opened for this guide, so current availability and fees are not confirmed. The Live Nation Brasil page labels the show new and offers a buy link.

Getting to Cine Joia

Liberdade is a central São Paulo district, and its own metro station, Liberdade, is on the city metro network. The sources checked do not state the walking distance from the station to Cine Joia, so confirm the route before you go.

The show starts at 8:00 p.m. on a Sunday, and the end time is not published. Check Metrô hours for the night, or plan a rideshare home.

The State Department says not to hire informal or unregistered taxis, and to avoid public buses, especially at night. It also advises caution when walking at night.

It warns that thieves on motorcycles or bicycles often target mobile phones. Keep your phone out of sight on the street and agree a meeting point inside the crowd.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

The State Department says US citizens need a Brazilian visa, whatever the purpose of travel, approved before departure. The e-visa application is at brazil.vfsevisa.com, and the passport must be valid on the date of entry.

The e-visa portal strongly advises applying two months before travel, and consular posts may take up to 10 business days. For a 24 January arrival, two months before is about 24 November.

The State Department rates Brazil Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, in an advisory issued on Monday, 31 August 2026. It says any public event, including concerts, can turn violent, so stay alert in crowds.

Emergency numbers are 190 for police, 192 for ambulance and 193 for fire, according to the State Department. The ticket is the main published cost, at about US$41 to US$82.

Monday, 25 January 2027 is a São Paulo municipal holiday, BNews São Paulo says in its 2027 holiday list. Check opening hours for shops and attractions if you stay for the long weekend.

What It Means for You

If you are a US fan, this is the first chance to see Saint Levant in Brazil. Buy a ticket first, and check that you can complete the purchase without a CPF.

If you need a visa, apply before you book flights or hotels. Do not wait until January, because processing can take up to 10 business days.

The holiday on Monday, 25 January 2027 may make flights and hotels busier on that weekend. Compare cancellation terms before you pay.

What Is Not Known

Current ticket availability is not confirmed, because the Ticketmaster page could not be opened. How a foreign visitor without a CPF buys a ticket is also not confirmed.

No opening act, set length or end time has been published. The nearest metro station to Cine Joia and its walking time are also not confirmed.

No second São Paulo date has been announced, and Trambicast calls this a one-off. Prices for later sale phases, if any, have not been published.

What Comes Next

The next fixed date is the concert on Sunday, 24 January 2027, with doors at 6:00 p.m. local time. Watch Ticketmaster Brasil and Live Nation Brasil for stock updates and any opening act.

US visitors should aim to file the e-visa application by about 24 November, the two-month mark the portal advises. Nothing published says the tour will add other Brazilian cities.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where does Saint Levant play in São Paulo?

Saint Levant plays Cine Joia in São Paulo on Sunday, 24 January 2027. Doors open at 6:00 p.m. and the show starts at 8:00 p.m. local time, or 6:00 p.m. US Eastern.

How much are Saint Levant tickets in São Paulo and where do I buy them?

Ticketmaster Brasil sells standing-floor tickets at BRL 410 (about US$82), or BRL 205 (about US$41) at half price. Availability is not confirmed, so check the Ticketmaster page.

Do US citizens need a visa to see Saint Levant in Brazil?

Yes, the State Department says US citizens need a Brazilian visa or e-visa approved before travel. The e-visa portal advises applying two months ahead, so apply by about 24 November.

World.title: International News: Greek students and teachers protest high living costs and demand more education funding
World.content:
International News: Greek students and teachers protest high living costs and demand more education funding

By Zoila Palma: Thousands of students and teachers took to the streets of Athens, Greece, on Wednesday, demanding affordable student housing and increased government investment in education.

Similar demonstrations were held in other Greek cities, including Thessaloniki and Patras, as concerns over the rising cost of living and deteriorating school conditions fueled public protests, AP reports.

Demonstrators carried signs highlighting the financial challenges facing students, with one banner reading, “From Greece to France, give money to education.” Others displayed messages questioning how young people could afford both their education and basic living expenses.

The demonstrations come as protests over housing affordability, rising fuel costs and education funding spread across several European countries, including France, Italy and Albania.

World.title: 21 year old Jamir Arana missing after last being seen on Baymen Avenue
World.content:
21 year old Jamir Arana missing after last being seen on Baymen Avenue

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A Belize City family is asking for the public’s help to find 21 year old Jamir Arana.

Jamir, who has autism, was last seen on Baymen Avenue in Belize City between 1:30pm and 2:00pm on Wednesday, October 21.

At the time, he was wearing a white T shirt, long white pants and a pair of blue Crocs.

His family is urging anyone who has seen him to come forward.

If you have any information on his whereabouts, please call his mother at 614 6039 or the Missing Person Belize page at 610 6094.

World.title: Maya Island Air eyes Punta Gorda route after Tropic Air pullout
World.content:
Maya Island Air eyes Punta Gorda route after Tropic Air pullout

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): There may be hope for air service to Punta Gorda.

Prime Minister John Briceño has confirmed that Maya Island Air has expressed interest in operating a route to the south, after Tropic Air announced it will close its Punta Gorda station on November 1.

Briceño said Tropic Air made a commercial decision because it had been losing money on the route.

“You can’t force a company to run, a private company to be able to continue to run that,” he said.

The Prime Minister said the Government is now in discussions with Maya Island Air’s CEO, and likely with the Belize Airports Authority.

He said he hopes to hear the airline’s terms by this week or early next week to see if it is something the Government can work with.

World.title: Big savings coming to Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware October 26 to 31
World.content:
Big savings coming to Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware October 26 to 31

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): For six days, Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware is putting its customers first.

The store’s Customer Appreciation Sale, running October 26 to 31, is its way of thanking the people who keep coming back, with deals on tools, paint, appliances, power and solar products.

World.title: Missing Belize City man found dead
World.content:
Missing Belize City man found dead

By Zoila Palma: Belize City resident Jamir Arana,21, was reported missing by his family this morning.

Arana has autism and was last seen on Wednesday afternoon in Belize City.

But, reports say that his body was found this morning in the area between Armenia and Belmopan and it appears to be a case of hit and run.

Authorities are on the scene.

World.title: Belizean exporters showcase products at Kaohsiung Food Show 2026 in Taiwan
World.content:
Belizean exporters showcase products at Kaohsiung Food Show 2026 in Taiwan

By Zoila Palma: A delegation of Belizean exporters is representing the country at the Kaohsiung Food Show 2026 in Taiwan, seeking to showcase Belizean specialty products and explore opportunities in international markets.

The delegation includes Oscar Requena, Business Advisor at EXPORTBelize, a unit of BELTRAIDE.

The team is highlighting Belize’s artisanal food products, including specialty honey from Farmed to Perfection, artisanal Mayan chocolate from Che’il Mayan Products, and single-origin chocolate from Ixcacao Maya Belizean Chocolate. The products reflect Belize’s diverse flavors and cultural heritage.

The participation aims to introduce Belizean products to international buyers, establish business connections and create new market opportunities for local exporters. The trade mission also provides an opportunity to strengthen commercial relationships between Belize and Taiwan.

EXPORTBelize acknowledged the support of the Taiwan Embassy in Belize, the Embassy of Belize in Taiwan, TAITRA Global and the Latin American and Caribbean Trade Office in facilitating the mission.

World.title: Forest Department says 2026-2027 logging season now open
World.content:
Forest Department says 2026-2027 logging season now open

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Forest Department has announced the opening of Belize’s 2026–2027 logging season, which runs from October 15, 2026, to June 15, 2027.

The department is reminding prospective loggers to comply with licensing requirements and submit their applications before the established deadline.

Applications for logging licences on private and lease land must be submitted to the respective Forest Department District Offices no later than January 31, 2027.

Applicants are encouraged to use the department’s checklist to ensure that all required information and supporting documents are included.

The department cautions that applications submitted after the deadline will not be accepted or processed. It also reminds loggers that the harvesting and transportation of forest produce must comply with applicable laws, regulations and permit conditions throughout the season.

To ensure compliance, the Forest Department will conduct monitoring and inspections during the logging season.

World.title: International News: President of El Salvador warns gangs in Haiti of stronger military response if missing soldiers not released
World.content:
International News: President of El Salvador warns gangs in Haiti of stronger military response if missing soldiers not released

By Zoila Palma: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele has warned Haitian gangs that they could face a stronger military response if four Salvadoran soldiers who went missing following an ambush in Haiti are not returned alive and unharmed.

The soldiers disappeared on October 18 in the Santo area of Croix-des-Bouquets, northeast of Port-au-Prince, while serving with the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), The Haitian Times report.

Bukele said the four men are aviation technicians assigned to support medical evacuations and save lives, rather than combat personnel.

“To the gang leaders and gang members holding four of our compatriots hostage in Haiti:

The men you kidnapped are not combatants. They are aeronautical technicians who are part of our mission in Haiti, comprised exclusively of pilots and technical personnel, whose primary task is to conduct medical evacuations and save lives, not to fight,” Bukele said.

The soldiers were reportedly abducted while returning from a supermarket, and their vehicle was set on fire during the attack. Their whereabouts and condition remained unknown as search and rescue operations continued on Wednesday.

In a statement posted on X on October 21, Bukele warned the gangs that the ongoing search operation was only a fraction of what could follow if the soldiers were not released. He referenced his government’s crackdown on criminal gangs in El Salvador and urged the kidnappers to return the men safely, warning that further security operations could intensify.

“But I want you to understand something: today’s attack is nothing compared to what will come if you do not return the four to us alive.

And do not mistake our words for an empty threat. We have already eliminated the gangs in El Salvador, and we can eliminate you as well.

You still have time to prevent it,” Bukele added.

Meanwhile, the Haitian government said securing the soldiers’ release was an absolute priority and that all necessary resources were being mobilized.

World.title: Water pressure
World.content:
Addressing a Jamaica Observer Press Club on Wednesday, Water Minister Matthew Samuda (left) acknowledges the public’s concerns about higher water bills, while NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the utility needs sufficient revenue to keep operating.Naphtali Junior

WATER Minister Matthew Samuda and National Water Commission (NWC) officials are defending the utility’s proposed 51 per cent tariff increase, arguing that rising operating costs, ageing infrastructure, and repeated droughts have made higher revenue necessary to maintain and improve water supply.

Speaking at a Jamaica Observer Press Club on Wednesday, Samuda acknowledged the public’s concerns about higher bills, but argued that the country can no longer postpone major repairs to its water system, while NWC Board Chairman Michael Shaw said the utility needs sufficient revenue to keep operating.

“If we could have asked for one per cent and been okay we would have asked for one per cent. No politician on the planet Earth is interested in increasing the cost of living. This is a necessary step to resolve long-standing issues in our water sector,” Samuda said.

He said Jamaica is “in a race against time” to replace ageing infrastructure and improve the reliability of water supplies, warning that the country’s long history of inadequate investment has left the utility facing mounting challenges.

In the meantime, Shaw noted that the NWC needs to be able to meet the public’s expectations while maintaining its daily operations.

“We need to continue the operations from one day to the next. Our citizenry is expecting that when they go home and turn on that tap, there’s water in it. There can’t be any worse feeling. So if you were to measure when you go home and you turn on [the switch] and there’s no light versus turn on and there’s no water, I think it’s a no-brainer, and as such, this tariff is going to right-size our position to ensure that we continue to deliver, as is our commitment to the citizens of Jamaica,” he said.

Samuda said the proposed increase must be viewed against the economic and environmental challenges Jamaica has faced since the last interim tariff adjustment granted in 2019.

He said the COVID-19 pandemic caused significant revenue losses when hotels and other commercial customers shut down, while disruptions to supply chains and rising prices subsequently increased the cost of operating the utility.

He added that droughts in 2022, 2023 and 2025; along with Hurricane Beryl and Tropical Storm Rafael in 2024; alongside Hurricane Melissa last year, further affected the NWC’s operations and revenue.

The minister argued that the utility continued to incur expenses even when drought reduced the amount of water available to sell.

He also pointed to rising energy costs and changes to staff salaries, saying the NWC’s energy costs were now close to 50 per cent higher than in 2019, while salaries had doubled over the same period.

“Nobody plans for three out of your five worst droughts ever during this period. Nobody plans for the worst El Nino in 200 years, which is what this is becoming, and… when we talk about these things people say, ‘El Nino? Whatever.’ But the last time we had an El Nino like this it triggered global famine. This is not a normal weather phenomenon that we are going through,” he added.

Samuda argued that these pressures had been absorbed while the NWC’s tariffs remained unchanged, but said the utility could no longer defer essential repairs to its ageing infrastructure.

He noted that the NWC had never replaced even one per cent of its asset base in a single year during Jamaica’s independent history — a shortfall he said had contributed to the deterioration of pipes and other infrastructure.

He pointed to repeated breaks in a major pipeline at Coral Gardens in Montego Bay, which he said had broken six times in one month and required a $170-million intervention to safeguard the main supply line serving the city.

“The reality is the capital replacement ratio of a utility is not intended to fall below one per cent of total capital replacement being done on an annual basis. In our independent life that has never happened…we’ve never replaced one per cent of the asset base of the water commission in a single year. We’ve never gotten close, and that is the utility standard globally. So what you have happening in the middle of that seven-year period is also the collapse of ageing infrastructure. I should be changing the third generation of those lines now, not the first generation in that way,” he said.

Samuda said the combination of ageing infrastructure, climate-related pressures, and decades of inadequate investment have left Jamaica with urgent work to do.

“Ultimately, it is our responsibility to do now what should have been done a long time ago. We will do it. And we can have confidence that at the back end of our work and our investment in these varying programmes, they will have the confidence; and I assure them in the coming years we’ll have other things to complain about other than potable water in the pipes,” he said.

The proposed 51 per cent increase has not been approved by the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR), which is to review the NWC’s application.

Furthermore, Acting NWC President Kevin Kerr separately told the Jamaica Observer that the application includes a significantly lower proposed increase for the utility’s lowest consumers, but said the details could not yet be released because the OUR had not reviewed the application.

World.title: Gully bank relocation
World.content:
From left: K2 developer Richard Lake; Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness; developer Michael Lake; and Phillip Paulwell, Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal, cut the ribbon to the development. At back is Delano Seiveright, state minister in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce.(Photo: Andrew Holness on X)

AN initiative by the Government to relocate people whose houses are situated on gully banks, and who are often affected by adverse weather events, is to be piloted in four communities across the Corporate Area.

The disclosure was made by Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness on Wednesday, during his address at the official opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony of the K2 housing development in downtown Kingston.

Although the timeline of the pilot’s execution was not disclosed, Holness said the project will facilitate the construction of new abodes for people who will be relocated, or the provision of grants for them to source other spaces to call home.

One of the communities of concern mentioned by Holness was the flood-prone Burger Gully, situated in the Kingston Eastern constituency.

“We will be selecting maybe four communities across the Corporate Area to start the pilot project to have persons who are living on the gully banks, particularly those that are at risk of an epiphenomenal weather event, to help them to move from the gully banks. We cannot continue this unsafe practice… that must come to an end,” Holness said.

Member of Parliament for Kingston Eastern and Port Royal Phillip Paulwell, who was also at the function, had disclosed in August that close to 150 residents of Burger Gully had signalled their willingness to relocate.

The flooding of the gully, an informal settlement also called 17 1/2 Mountain View Avenue, has been an ongoing problem, but worsened last year as sections of the gully which runs through the community were damaged by flood waters.

At that time, Paulwell said lands were identified in the communities of Mountain View and Rockfort to facilitate the relocation exercise, but a response was being awaited from minister with responsibility for works Robert Morgan.

Holness maintained Wednesday that the issue of communities which are currently irregularly settled “must come to an end”, but underscored that “the success of any government policy is dependent upon the government’s ability… to do what it says it’s going to do”.

“In my own constituency I have demonstrated to the people there how the Government can effectively do a relocation. In the best circumstances, relocation is always disruptive. In the best circumstances, persons are going to feel traumatised by relocation. No one wants to have their house uprooted, their furniture taken and destroyed. Nobody wants to have to move from where they have made their life,” said Holness, who is Member of Parliament for St Andrew West Central.

According to Holness, the National Works Agency will also test a programme that will reclaim the reservations [of buildings] 20 feet away from the gullies in Kingston.

“Whenever I speak like this, immediately everybody starts to get worried [that,] ‘Boy, the Government going to come throw me off [my land].’ That’s not what the Government wants to do. The Government has a right in law to, for the public good, have persons relocate. But the relocation must be done in such a way that the people who are relocated are made no worse off,” Holness said.

The K2 development, located in Bournemouth Gardens, Kingston 2, is a 10-storey residence featuring 119 units. It was developed by Sherbourne Limited, led by Michael and Richard Lake.

World.title: Mental Chung sees The Psychic Realm
World.content:
An animator/graphic designer by profession, Mental Chung wanted to express that creativity when he launched his music career eight years ago.

He called his sound Reggae Barque, which can be heard on The Psychic Realm, the St Ann artiste’s first album.

Released on October 10, it contains six songs which Mental Chung produced for his Art Creed Records.

“The songs come from new age spiritual concepts surrounding the hidden forces and ones guiding us in life,” he reasoned. “I went for a more mainstream, youthful sound that has elements of reggae, soul and dancehall.”

Quinting Pink Pinch is the only song from the project released to date. The Psychic Realm’s songs are driven by ethereal beats conjured by Stephen Dajure and Aye Psycho.

Their rhythms complement what Mental Chung describes as “playful, militant and thought-provoking” music.

Born Reinardo Chung, he got his creative start as an animator almost 20 years ago with Bad Influence, an eight-minute, dancehall-inspired film released in 2010. It won an award at the Reggae Film Festival which was held in May 2011 in Kingston.

Mental Chung’s stocks rose even more with the Dutty Bwoy series, which was driven by his love for dancehall culture. It has animated cameos by stars like Bounty Killer, Beenie Man, and Usain Bolt.

Lead, Blaze It, and Talk Back are some of the songs that announced Mental Chung’s music career.

— Howard Campbell

World.title: FID wins big
World.content:
.

THE Financial Investigations Division (FID), in its capacity as Jamaica’s assets recovery agency under the Proceeds of Crime Act (POCA), has secured a Pecuniary Penalty Order of $62 million against businessman Ou Yongjia, following his convictions for unauthorised use of a trademark and misleading and deceptive conduct.

The order was made by consent in the Home Circuit Court of the Supreme Court on October 2, 2026, pursuant to Section 5(3)(b) of POCA.

As the initial sum payable under the order, Yongjia agreed to forfeit $20 million held in bank accounts that were restrained by the Supreme Court on March 18, 2025. He will pay the balance of $42 million to the FID in monthly instalments commencing February 2, 2027.

The matter began on February 11, 2021, when police executed a special warrant at a business premises owned and operated by Yongjia.

Officers seized 2,840 pairs of counterfeit slippers bearing the trademark designs of three popular brands, two invoice books, and $829,000 in cash. Based on the selling prices recorded in the seized invoice books, the FID estimated the value of the counterfeit slippers at $1.3 million.

Yongjia was charged on March 4, 2021. On December 7, 2022 he pleaded guilty in the Corporate Area Parish Court (Criminal Division) to one count of misleading and deceptive conduct, contrary to Section 28(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, and three counts of unauthorised use of a trademark, contrary to Section 69(1)(b) of the Trade Marks Act.

He was fined $375,000 on each count, or nine months’ imprisonment in default, a total of $1.5 million, which was paid on the same day. A separate charge of possession of criminal property was withdrawn by the prosecution.

Following the convictions the matter was committed to the Home Circuit Court so the FID could pursue a Pecuniary Penalty Order or Forfeiture Order under Section 5 of POCA. The FID subsequently filed its application in 2023. By virtue of his convictions Yongjia was deemed, under Section 6(1)(a) of POCA, to have a criminal lifestyle, from which he obtained a benefit.

The FID’s financial investigators examined records relating to four bank accounts held by Yongjia and his business between 2019 and 2024, including records obtained under a Production and Inspection Order. This was followed by a sworn statement of information filed with the court on March 11, 2025. The $62-million sum was agreed between the parties, and Yongjia consented to the order being made without a benefit hearing, and waived his right to challenge or appeal the FID’s application.

Under the consent agreement, interest will accrue at five per cent per annum on any instalment not paid by its due date, and the bailiff of the Supreme Court is authorised to seize and sell chattels owned by Yongjia, without further order of the court, to satisfy any sums left unpaid.

The agreement also provides that failure to comply with the payment schedule is an offence, punishable on conviction before a parish court judge by imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, and that any reversion to or future participation in criminal conduct would permit the FID to pursue the full amount of the assessed benefit.

The court’s order carries a penal notice and gives the FID liberty to apply to enforce its terms.

FID’s Principal Director of Financial Crimes Investigations Keith Darien said the outcome reflects the careful work of its investigators who followed the financial trail connected to the case and presented a clear, evidence-based picture to the court.

“It also reflects the importance of our collaboration with law enforcement partners. The FID remains committed to ensuring that those who profit from unlawful conduct do not keep the benefit,” he said.

Added FID Senior Director of Legal Services Courtney Smith: “Jamaica’s asset recovery framework continues to mature through the restraint, seizure and confiscation of criminal property, advancing the broader objectives of punishment, deterrence and rehabilitation. This outcome demonstrates our commitment to depriving offenders of criminal benefits, encouraging lawful conduct, and ensuring that crime does not pay.”

A Pecuniary Penalty Order requires a person to pay a sum of money in respect of benefits obtained from criminal conduct. Asset recovery under POCA is a lawful, court-supervised process, and the FID said it will continue to take lawful steps, where the evidence supports it, to remove the benefit from crime and protect Jamaica’s financial system from criminal abuse.

World.title: HANDLE WITH CARE
World.content:
Vitel Lawes of West Indies bowls during the ICC Under-19 Men’s Cricket World Cup Super Six match against Ireland at HP Oval in Windhoek, Namibia, on January 25, 2026. (Photo: ICC/Getty Images)

FORMER West Indies all-rounder Carlos Brathwaite believes the coaching staff must ensure Jamaican teenager Vitel Lawes continues to develop, after his recent struggles against India.

Lawes recently returned from the Windies’ white-ball tour of India where he played in the three-match One-Day International (ODI) series.

The 19-year-old came to prominence during the Under-19 World Cup earlier this year and made his senior international debut against New Zealand in July. He took eight wickets in the five-match series, which the Windies lost 3-2, including best figures of 3-39 in the third ODI.

However, Lawes went wicketless in the second and third ODIs against India, conceding 127 runs across the two matches as the Windies lost the series 2-1.

Several Caribbean fans criticised his performances and questioned whether he was ready for international cricket.

Former West Indies fast bowler and cricket commentator Ian Bishop, who covered the series, defended the young Jamaican.

“I’ll say it again: We have to be patient with Vitel Lawes and manage the youth better,” he said on X. “We keep rushing the kid into scenarios he isn’t ready for. Please give him time to grow and get his reps in. He is 19 years old, not 29 years old.”

Brathwaite, who helped the West Indies win the T20 World Cup in 2016, is concerned about the support Lawes will receive as he gains experience at the international level.

“A part of me is happy he’s getting the opportunities and that we’re backing a young player, but for me now the follow-up is how do we support that young player,” he said on The Super Over podcast.

“The challenge I found that West Indies cricket has had is not necessarily finding talent — [because] finding talent has always been quite easy for us — I think the difficulty for West Indies is honing that talent.” Brathwaite believes Head Coach Daren Sammy and his staff must find ways to help Lawes improve, especially with fewer opportunities for young players to gain experience in first class cricket because of Cricket West Indies’ (CWI) financial difficulties.

“You look to three first class games this season and no Super 50, [so] where does a Vitel Lawes now go at a level below international cricket and learn his game? He would have had lots of things that he would have done well and be happy with, and there’ll be a lot more things that he probably was unhappy with coming out of India, things he can work on, but where does he work on those things?” Brathwaite asked.

“Does he work on those things in a random pitch somewhere in Jamaica where the pressure is off and the spotlights are off as well? Or do we throw him in at first class level, 50-over level, T20 level? What is the level between CPL and international cricket? So, my challenge to the powers that be in West Indies cricket is to see what Vital Lawes has done well, see the challenges he’s had, and now give him an opportunity to be able to learn at the level below so he can have a quicker bounce back and not be like a Jewel Andrew a couple years later, flirting between the doldrums and — I don’t want to say failure — but not hitting the heights that we expected of him two years ago.”

Sammy said in September that the team would remain patient with Lawes because of his ability as a wrist spinner.

“Vitel, to me, is a find for us. What we saw in him that caused him to debut against New Zealand was all part of the planning and the processes we put in place. You’ve heard me for years talking about a wrist spinner in the West Indies team, and Vitel came in and immediately had an impact on the bowling unit for us,” he said.

“He’s still got a long way to go but we will continue with his development through either playing games or the specific work we’ve put in place for him. He’s worked really well with Nikita Miller and Ravi Rampaul. We’ll continue creating those opportunities for him and, hopefully, he can continue to grow. A little bit fast-tracked, but we’re pleased with what he’s done so far.”
