World.title: Iran's Balochistan border region sees growing unrest
World.content:
Violence is on the rise in Iran's border region with Afghanistan and Pakistan. The Iran war could shift the strategic balance for militant groups operating in the area.

Recent weeks have seen renewed attacks, assassinations and armed clashes in the southeastern province bordering Pakistan and Afghanistan. The incidents occurred in the provincial capital of Zahedan, as well as smaller border towns.

The border region of Iran, Pakistan and Afghanistan is home to the Baloch ethnic minority. The region on either side of the Iran-Pakistan border is among the most economically disadvantaged of the wider area.

The Pakistani province of Balochistan is economically underdeveloped, despite having large reserves of natural gas, gold and copper.

The situation is similarly dire in the Iranian province of Sistan and Baluchistan, which is predominantly inhabited by Sunni Baluchis. It is one of the poorest regions in the country and marked by underdeveloped infrastructure, limited educational opportunities and water supply shortages.

Significantly less information is available about the situation of the Baloch in Afghanistan.

Armed groups sense security gaps

Various Baloch groups are active in Iran and Pakistan, some of whom seek Balochistan independence. Yet to date, there is no evidence of coordinated cross-border cooperation among these organizations.

In December 2025, several Baloch opposition groups in Iran united under the umbrella of the Popular Fighters Front. Observers see this as an attempt to more closely integrate their political and military activities.

This coalition, which formed before the outbreak of the Iran war, could try to exploit security gaps created by the current situation, Iranian journalist Mehdi Nakhl Ahmadi told DW.

Ahmadi, who lives in Italy, has been covering the situation of the Baloch people for years. He said the new security situation could allow armed groups to expand their operations.

Struggling with poverty, suffering marginalization

Ahmadi said there are structural reasons for Baloch dissatisfaction. "The Islamic Republic's security policy toward ethnic and religious regions has widened the gap in economic development between these regions and other parts of the country in recent decades," he said.

He added that the rising number of attacks points to a shift in dynamics, as do increased coordination and changes in the way recent operations have been carried out.

Among the victims of recent clashes were members of Iran's Revolutionary Guards, the Basij militia, armed individuals, and a Sunni cleric.

A source within Iran, who is familiar with the situation of the Baloch people, yet whose identity we cannot disclose security for reasons, attributed some of the armed violence to political, economic and religious discontent.

Discrimination in employment, education, regional development and religious matters contribute to the tension, the source said.

Hidden executions surge in Iran during US-Israeli war To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

That's why the armed conflict should not be viewed in isolation, the Iranian source explained. Clergy, academics and other social leaders had been trying for years to peacefully voice their demands for better social policies and greater investment in the region, the source said.

The fact that these efforts were largely unsuccessful had led to a growing willingness among some to resort to more radical measures.

"The high number of executions in recent decades is another factor that fuels discontent," said the source. Most documented executions in the province, meanwhile, are related to drug offenses.

Although Baluchis make only up an estimated 2–6% of the Iranian population, they are significantly overrepresented among those put to death. Iran Human Rights reports that Baluchis accounted for 9% of all recorded executions in 2025. In previous years, that figure was 11% (2024) and 20% (2023), respectively.

For many people who live in this economically disadvantaged region, smuggling opium into Iran, and fuel out of the country, are one of the few ways to earn a living. This, in turn, has contributed to a continued military and security presence at the border.

It is not, meanwhile, known whether armed groups in southeastern Iran are being supported from abroad.

For many people in the region, fuel smuggling across the Iran-Pakistan border is one of the few ways to make a living Image: Abdula Ghani Kakar/DW

Violence has also escalated in the Pakistani province of Balochistan. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , 131 armed attacks were recorded there in September, up from 89 in August.

In addition to the separatist movement, which has been active for years, the Pakistani Taliban (TTP) are also expanding their operations. This had led to strategically important transportation links between Iran and Pakistan coming under growing pressure.

Still, it cannot be said with certainty whether the recent uptick in violence in Iran's Sistan and Baluchistan province stems from security gaps resulting from the Iran war.

The growing number of attacks does, however, suggests that the security situation in the already fragile border region continues to deteriorate.

Additional reporting by Morad Rahmati.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
World.content:
As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

A few days ago, three Russian aerial bombs struck a residential neighborhood on the outskirts of Sloviansk. One hit a five-story apartment building, injuring seven people. Along with neighboring Kramatorsk, Sloviansk is one of the last major towns in the eastern Ukrainian region of Donetsk still under Ukrainian control. Since summer, the city has been a combat zone.

In a courtyard surrounded by damaged apartment blocks, a dusty carpet hangs over the metal frame of a swing set. Tetjana, a pensioner who lives in the building across the street, has brought it out of her rubble-strewn apartment to clean it. She was in her kitchen when the bombs struck.

"The bomb hit the second floor, and a woman who lived on the fourth floor was screaming," she tells DW. "They managed to rescue her before that entire section of the building collapsed," she adds.

Despite being offered the opportunity to evacuate, Tetjana has yet to leave Sloviansk. "I don't know where I would go," she says. Rent can cost up to €400 ($449) a month. Tetjana's pension is the equivalent of just €67 ($75) a month. Even with monthly relocation assistance of about €40 ($45), she could not make ends meet. "I couldn't live on that. Nowhere!"

Meanwhile, electricity and water are still available in her neighborhood, but the gas supply has been cut off. "We'll get through this," Tetjana says hopefully. "Everything will be OK. That's what I tell everyone. I want that so much."

People who want to evacuate are not allowed to bring their pets Image: Hanna Sokolova-Stekh/DW

Residents reluctant to evacuate without pets

Days after the attack, the few residents remaining in the damaged buildings were still clearing out their apartments. But another attack hit as they worked. This time, the bombs struck a building housing a state-run emergency assistance center and the Red Cross. While firefighters put out the blaze, rescue workers and volunteers retrieved belongings left inside and cleared away broken glass. Eight people were injured in the attack.

"I was on the balcony when there was a deafening bang. It felt as if someone had hit me over the head," says Natalja, describing one of the recent attacks. The pensioner comes to this part of the city to care for her twin sister. "She can no longer get around. Today, I couldn't bring her bread, only crispbread," she tells DW. Although shops and a few stalls remain at the burned-out market, bread is not available every day.

Volunteers help clear the debris and retrieve belongings from a resilience center after a Russian bomb struck the building in Sloviansk Image: Hanna Sokolova-Stekh/DW

"I tried to persuade my sister to leave. I would go to a nursing home and she would go to a hospital. But her dog is sick, and I have one, too," Natalja says, noting that pets are not allowed during evacuations. "I can't leave my sister behind. She is worried and angry with me, as if everything were my fault. I have no strength left."

Natalja slowly sets off for home, "so I can get there before dark." The city center is nearly 4 kilometers (2.5 miles) away. Public transportation has been suspended since 30 people were killed in an attack on two buses in neighboring Kramatorsk.

Natalja cares for her twin sister who refuses to leave as she would have to leave her dog behind Image: Hanna Sokolova-Stekh/DW

"We're used to living under fire"

The center of Sloviansk is heavily damaged. Few people are out on the streets, though a handful of shops remain open. Of the city's 100,000 residents, about 20,000 remain, most of them elderly people who are unable to leave.

Vasyl, a pensioner, is from the village of Mayaky, north of Sloviansk. A neighbor drove him into the city center, where he sat down for lunch in a cafe. "We're used to living under fire by now," he says. "But it's a bad habit. We should have broken it long ago."

Vasyl wants peace for his homeland. But he rejects Russian President Vladimir Putin's demand that the part of the Donetsk region under Ukrainian control be handed over to Moscow.

Life has almost come to a standstill in Sloviansk and only few shops and market stalls remain open Image: Hanna Sokolova-Stekh/DW

Two elderly women talk on a street covered with nets to protect against drones. "I can't remember the last time I slept through the night," says Iryna, a pensioner. "It's terrible, but I have nowhere to go. I'm supposed to leave my two cats behind, but I love them so much. They're all I have."

"We can only hide, trembling, and pray to God that everything will be all right," Iryna continues. "When I have to go to the market, I don't know if I'll make it there alive."

Russian drones attacked the central market several weeks ago, injuring at least three people. Since then, fewer vendors and customers have been coming to the market.

The constant buzz of drones and the fear of Russian attacks keeps people from sleeping through the night Image: Hanna Sokolova-Stekh/DW

"We dream of staying here"

Valeriya sells women's underwear. With kindergartens closed, she has to bring her 5-year-old daughter Sofia to work. Their neighborhood in Sloviansk is not yet subject to the mandatory evacuation of families with children.

"We're used to this life by now. We were evacuated in 2022, but later returned. Now we're waiting to be evacuated again," Valeriya says.

Sofia races through the market aisles with her friend Anya, who is a year older. Anya's mother is a soldier defending her hometown. Her grandmother, Tetjana, sits nearby selling men's clothing. She, too, has to look after her granddaughter while working.

Sofia, 5, and Anya, 6, play at Sloviansk central market as their kindergartens are closed due to the war Image: Hanna Sokolova-Stekh/DW

Tetjana has started shipping her belongings to the Dnipropetrovsk region, where she hopes to start a new life. She is sending them while the post office is still open. "It hurts to see our Ukraine being destroyed," she says, fighting back tears. "Who will rebuild our cities?"

She hopes to return one day. But the fate of Bakhmut weighs on her mind. "Look at Bakhmut. There are no houses left. I'm counting on our boys to hold our cities, even though it's very difficult." Bakhmut, about 50 kilometers (31 miles) from Sloviansk, fell to Russian forces in 2023 after months of heavy fighting.

The women see little hope for a ceasefire. "Putin won't want one. And our younger generation will ask us what we fought for in the first place," Tetjana says. She believes Russia must withdraw from Ukrainian territory.

Drones buzz overhead as gunfire echoes across the market. "It's hard for our boys to shoot them down," Tetjana says. "But they're doing their best."

World.title: Germany arrests Ukrainian man suspected of spying for Russia
World.content:
The suspect is thought to have gathered defense-related information on the production of tanks and munitions, as well as details about NATO's eastern flank.

Police in the German state of Brandenburg have arrested a Ukrainian man on suspicion of spying for Russia, the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office in Karlsruhe said Thursday.

The man, identified only as Vadym Y. by prosecutors, is suspected of having used his connections to European defense firms to gather information that he then allegedly passed on to a Russian spy agency.

What do we know about the alleged espionage in Germany?

Prosecutors said he had been in touch with a middleman since July 2025. They said he had been gathering intelligence in connection with the Russian full-scale invasion of Ukraine from Germany.

This information reportedly included "details regarding the production of armored vehicles, ammunition and explosives, as well as information on personnel and military facilities at locations intended to secure NATO's eastern flank."

Germany has been on high alert for acts of sabotage in recent months, especially since an explosive-laden drone was discovered near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig airport. Berlin said Moscow was behind the attempted attack.

Germany gives spy agencies expanded powers To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Why is Germany worried about Russia's 'hybrid' war?

Germany is one of the biggest military and political supporters of Ukraine, especially following an increasingly friendly US stance toward Russia under President Donald Trump.

This seems to have put Germany in Russia's crosshairs as part of what has been called a "hybrid" campaign of espionage, sabotage and other disruptions.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he was not surprised by the arrest, adding that there would be more such cases ⁠in ​the future.

Besides the incident at Leipzig airport, there have been numerous cases of people being arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia. Moscow has denied all allegations.

This has led Germany to give increased powers to its own spying agency, the BND.

The agency's chief, Martin Jaeger, told German lawmakers earlier in October that the Russian "shadow war" is escalating and has "taken on a new, more dangerous character."

"Germany is at risk of being drawn into a violent conflict with Russia," he told a hearing of parliament's intelligence oversight committee in Berlin.

World.title: Álvarez de Toledo y Sémper serán los números dos y tres de Feijóo en la lista por Madrid
World.content:
Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo y Borja Sémper, las dos almas del PP, ocuparán las dos posiciones más destacadas de la lista de Madrid al Congreso, la que encabeza Alberto Núñez Feijóo. La diputada madrileña será la número dos tras el líder del PP, mientras que el parlamentario vasco irá como el número tres, el mismo en el que concurrió en las pasadas elecciones generales de 2023. Es Álvarez de Toledo la novedad y quien escala en la lista, porque en las últimas iba en el puesto seis, coincidiendo con el ascenso de los perfiles más duros en el PP para competir con Vox.

Álvarez de Toledo (Madrid, 1974) era la apuesta del PP de Isabel Díaz Ayuso, como publicó EL PAÍS, para acompañar a Feijóo como número dos. La decisión ha sido de Génova, pero los territorios hacen sus propuestas para las listas y la diputada era la preferida por los populares madrileños, donde creen que tiene mucho tirón electoral en la derecha y que por eso puede hacer campaña por sí sola en Madrid, con independencia de Ayuso. Álvarez de Toledo, cercana a Ayuso, ha protagonizado ya en los últimos días varios actos de campaña no solo en Madrid, sino por todo el país. “Felicidades, Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo, número dos de la lista por Madrid al Congreso de los Diputados, acompañando a Feijóo en esta apasionante aventura”, ha escrito Ayuso en la red social X. Solo la ha felicitado a ella. El PP de Madrid es crítico con Sémper, considerado por este sector como demasiado blando. La presidenta madrileña mantiene una cruzada contra los “tibios”, aunque nunca ha precisado a quiénes se refiere.

Álvarez de Toledo es doctora en Historia por la Universidad de Oxford y ejerció durante un año como portavoz parlamentaria del PP en el Congreso, hasta que Pablo Casado la destituyó porque consideraba que ejercía como verso libre. Ella misma ha contado la historia de su defenestración como portavoz en Políticamente Indeseable (Penguin), donde escribe: “Me mueven las causas no completamente perdidas, pero sí en grave riesgo de perderse: la épica. Y si no soy un genio gestionando equipos, mucho menos facciones. Sin embargo, las altas instancias de Génova decretaron que yo era un sujeto bajo sospecha. Un peligroso foco de poder paralelo. Una rival. Y así Teodoro García Egea pudo ir avanzando, como uno de esos rulos o apisonadoras que utilizamos los toledanos para convertir nuestros pedregales en praderas, hacia su objetivo final: limitar al máximo mi autoridad, influencia y margen de maniobra. Desgastarme ante la opinión pública. Convertirme en un bonito florero. Solo me quedó mi voz. Y no siempre”.

La diputada del PP Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo, en el Congreso en septiembre. Víctor Lerena (EFE)

Feijóo ha elegido como número dos a una política con la que ha tenido diferencias estratégicas y de estilo desde mucho antes de llegar a la presidencia nacional del PP. Álvarez de Toledo ha despertado siempre recelos en los sectores más moderados del PP, a los que pertenecía, cuando era el presidente de la Xunta de Galicia el propio Feijóo, que llegó a discrepar de que Casado la eligiera como portavoz en 2019. “El tiempo dará y quitará razones si son buenos o malos nombramientos”, dijo entonces el presidente del PP gallego con escaso entusiasmo cuando fue nombrada. Un año después, las discrepancias se revelaron públicas, cuando Feijóo criticó con una dureza inusual las palabras desde la tribuna del Congreso de los Diputados de Álvarez de Toledo, que había llamado “hijo de terrorista” a Pablo Iglesias. Feijóo acusó entonces a su compañera de partido de haber “perdido los papeles”.

Poco a poco, con la llegada de Feijóo a Madrid, Álvarez de Toledo fue ganando posiciones en la dirección y en el grupo parlamentario como uno de los principales arietes del PP contra el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez. Feijóo la incluyó en el comité ejecutivo y la nombró portavoz adjunta en el Congreso, donde siempre intervenía en las sesiones de control con discursos de verbo afilado.

El presidente del Partido Popular, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, junto a la portavoz adjunta en la cámara, Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo, en el Congreso en 2025. FERNANDO VILLAR (EFE)

El líder del PP se ha terminado rodeando de perfiles duros en esta campaña, donde necesita competir con un Vox al alza. La evolución es clara. En 2023, su número dos fue la exdirigente de Ciudadanos Marta Rivera de la Cruz, que poco después renunció a su escaño para centrarse en la concejalía de Cultura del Ayuntamiento de Madrid. Ahora, además de a Álvarez de Toledo en Madrid, ha situado al alcalde de Badalona, Xavier García Albiol, como número uno por Barcelona. Algunos dirigentes populares describen la evolución de Feijóo y de su núcleo gallego, que en la Xunta representaban el ala moderada del PP, como una reacción a la forma de ejercer la política de Sánchez. “Se han hecho de derechas”, ironiza un miembro del PP.

Génova ha explicado el nombramiento de Álvarez de Toledo y de Sémper como dos y tres de la lista por Madrid con el argumento de que “el Partido Popular es un proyecto amplio en el que caben todas las sensibilidades”. “No somos el PSOE. Somos una formación abierta donde los matices y los acentos no incomodan a nadie, sino que enriquecen a todos. Las diferencias en el PP no se combaten, se respetan. Y Feijóo es un candidato en el que pueden confluir españoles de diferente signo y condición. Como siempre dijimos, la España sin muros”, afirma el partido en un breve comunicado.

Borja Sémper comparece en rueda de prensa en la sede del Partido Popular en Madrid, el 24 de agosto de 2026. Víctor Sainz

Con Borja Sémper (Irún, 1976), licenciado en Derecho y representante del ala más templada del PP, Álvarez de Toledo también ha protagonizado desavenencias en el pasado, en el mismo periodo en el que ejerció como portavoz parlamentaria del PP. Entonces, Sémper llegó a exigirle una rectificación pública por calificar de “tibia” su política contra el nacionalismo vasco. “Mientras algunas caminaban sobre mullidas alfombras, otros nos jugábamos la vida”, se quejó el parlamentario vasco en referencia a su ahora compañera de lista. Sémper actúa ahora como portavoz adjunto en la campaña, pero a diferencia de las elecciones de 2023, cuando lo hizo en solitario, ejerce conjuntamente con Ester Muñoz, otro de los perfiles duros aupados por Génova en esta etapa, en la que algunos miembros de la dirección popular observan al político vasco algo “incómodo”. Sémper volvió a la política de la mano de Feijóo, después de haberla abandonado en 2020, bajo el liderazgo de Pablo Casado. “Un partido no es una secta”, dijo en su marcha.

El PP no oculta las diferencias de perfil de Álvarez de Toledo y de Sémper, y las reivindica como ejemplo de que junto a Feijóo caben las distintas sensibilidades del partido. Ambos “representan formas distintas de entender España y ambos han atravesado por diferentes etapas en el PP”, afirman fuentes de Génova en el comunicado enviado a los medios. “Por eso, estamos muy orgullosos de que los dos sientan que el Partido Popular de Alberto Núñez Feijóo sea su casa y además decidan dar la cara por sus ideas encabezando, junto al candidato a la Presidencia del Gobierno, la lista de Madrid en los puestos 2 y 3″.

World.title: Mi vecina es morosa y ocupa la vivienda de su madre fallecida. ¿A quién reclamamos la deuda?
World.content:
Pregunta. Tenemos una vecina morosa que acumula una deuda de más de 6.000 euros. Los propietarios murieron y la casa está habitada por la hija y la familia de esta. No se adjudicaron la herencia. La hija y los dos hijos mayores de edad trabajan, mientras que el el marido cobra una pensión no contributiva. ¿Cómo podríamos cobrar la deuda? ¿Se podría hacer alguna anotación de la deuda en la finca? F.J. Callejón

Respuesta. Cuando los propietarios de la vivienda han fallecido y los herederos no han aceptado ni rechazado la herencia, los bienes forman una herencia yacente. Las reclamaciones judiciales por impago de cuotas comunitarias deben dirigirse contra la herencia yacente y los herederos desconocidos o potenciales.

Respecto a la ocupación de la vivienda por parte de la hija con su familia, con carácter general, el Tribunal Supremo y las Audiencias Provinciales determinan que no se puede condenar al pago de cuotas comunitarias a un heredero si no se acredita que ha aceptado la herencia, bien de forma expresa o tácitamente. El uso de la vivienda puede ser indicio de aceptación tácita de la herencia, pero esto debe ser valorado y declarado en el procedimiento judicial correspondiente. Por ejemplo, la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid considera que el uso y disfrute de los bienes de la herencia podría constituir un acto de aceptación tácita de la misma (artículo 999 del Código Civil). Si formalmente no se considera aceptada la herencia, la deuda recae sobre la herencia yacente (el patrimonio del fallecido que aún no tiene titular adjudicado). Si se considera aceptada la herencia, entonces el heredero responde de las deudas de la comunidad de forma solidaria con su propio patrimonio.

Respecto a la anotación de la deuda sobre la finca, no se trata de una cuestión sencilla. Para que el Registro de la Propiedad y el juzgado permita una anotación preventiva de embargo sobre los bienes, es necesario acreditar el título sucesorio e identificar quiénes son los herederos concretos titulares de esos derechos.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: El kiwi redescubre su lado gastro: todas las posibilidades de una fruta cargada de nutrientes
World.content:
Del clásico bol de desayuno a los carpaccios más elaborados, la iniciativa #1ZespriAlDía propone nuevas maneras de incorporar el kiwi a nuestra rutina y exprimir sus beneficios

Exótico por fuera, nutritivo por dentro. El kiwi llegó a la cumbre de Hollywood, convirtiéndose en un fetiche gastro de la élite de Los Ángeles. En cuanto cruzó la frontera en los setenta, los chefs y bartenders de la ciudad cayeron rendidos ante este fruto de aspecto psicodélico y notas cítricas, utilizándolo para darle un toque de excentricidad a pasteles y cócteles. En una cultura obsesionada con la belleza y el bienestar, sus credenciales nutricionales terminaron de blindar su estatus: en ese corazón tierno había un tesoro de bajas calorías y una alta concentración de fibra, potasio y antioxidantes.

“Sin que existan los superalimentos, tal y como se venden a veces, el kiwi es una fruta muy particular, ligeramente superior a otras”, defiende Aitor Sánchez, miembro del Panel de Expertos Nutricionales de Zespri, que más allá de sus beneficios, destaca su comodidad para incorporarlo en nuestra rutina. “Es un alimento fácil de transportar, con una buena duración en el frutero y fácil de repartir por raciones y por persona. Incluso la pega de que necesitamos pelarlo se puede combatir fácilmente si decidimos partirlo y comerlo con cuchara”. Hay quienes se lo comen incluso con la piel.

Juan Alejos. Cortesía de Zespri

¿Por qué este detalle es más importante de lo que creemos? En España se da una realidad muy curiosa: según los datos del I Estudio de la FEN, nueve de cada diez españoles se preocupan bastante por su alimentación, pero el II Radar SaluDiable revela que solo el 28% consigue mantener hábitos saludables en su día a día. Una brecha a la que hay que sumarle el ruido de las redes sociales, donde el bienestar es el territorio que más tendencias cuestionables y bulos genera. “Se ha puesto de moda hablar de anécdotas: ayuno, microbiota, glucemias… sin que sean la verdaderas preocupaciones y prioridades para la salud. La gente necesita mensajes aplicables, no más carga mental”, subraya Sánchez. De ahí la importancia de incorporar gestos sencillos que nos hagan pasar de la intención al hábito.

De contar calorías a pensar en nutrientes

Uno de los grandes mitos que existen sobre la alimentación es que comer mejor exige grandes sacrificios. Para los expertos, la clave no está ni en las restricciones ni en el recuento de calorías, sino en sopesar la densidad nutricional: qué nos aporta y en qué cantidad. “Más sedentaria es la rutina de una población, su dieta tiene menos margen para incluir nutrientes extra”, señala el experto. En otras palabras, cuando pasamos buena parte del día sentados frente a un ordenador, el margen calórico se reduce y elegir bien lo que comemos cobra todavía más importancia. Lo mejor es priorizar alimentos que nutran, sacien y, sobre todo, que nos gusten.

Los kiwis Zespri™, en este aspecto, son un gran aliado. A través de su plataforma Cargados de nutrientes, la marca pone en valor cómo solo una pieza de fruta puede marcar la diferencia. Cada variedad, aporta algo diferente. El kiwi amarillo Zespri™ SunGold™ es una opción para quienes prefieren los sabores dulces. Su pulpa dorada y sus matices tropicales esconden un alto contenido en vitamina C (152 mg por cada 100 gramos), un nutriente que favorece el funcionamiento normal del sistema inmunitario, participa en la síntesis de tejidos, mientras ayuda a reducir el cansancio y la fatiga. No se le puede pedir más.

Por otro lado, Zespri™ Green™, el kiwi clásico de pulpa verde y sabor refrescante, es conocido por su aporte en fibra, tanto soluble como insoluble, lo que contribuye a su fama en el buen funcionamiento del tránsito intestinal. “También alimenta nuestra microbiota y reduce el tiempo que las sustancias perjudiciales están en nuestro aparato digestivo”, añade Aitor Sánchez, que prefiere centrarse en una de las facetas menos conocidas, sus posibilidades culinarias.

Juan Alejos. Cortesía de Zespri

La sencillez hace al hábito

El kiwi es un habitual en los fruteros españoles, pero todavía no hemos aprendido a sacarle todo el jugo. Para el nutricionista, el desayuno puede ser un buen punto de partida: “si empezamos el hábito de incorporar una pieza de fruta al desayuno notaremos sus beneficios, pero además estaremos desplazando alimentos malsanos que suelen estar a esa hora”. Para cumplir con el conocido propósito #1ZespriAlDía, en la web de la marca encontramos múltiples recetas para disfrutar de esta fruta. Desde boles de avena con kiwi para empezar el día hasta batidos de fruta nutritivos para después de entrenar.

La iniciativa se enmarca en la segunda edición del NutriTour by Zespri, que durante el mes de octubre ha recorrido las oficinas de Madrid para acercar la nutrición a los trabajadores y demostrar que incorporar opciones nutritivas en el día a día puede ser más sencillo de lo que parece. El kiwi es además una fruta muy versátil, que puede disfrutarse solo o incorporarse fácilmente a distintas recetas, desde ensaladas y desayunos hasta platos principales o snacks. Una forma sencilla de aportar variedad a las comidas del día a día, también en la oficina.

World.title: El juez propone juzgar a otros cuatro exjefes de ETA por el atentado mortal de Santa Pola de 2002
World.content:
El juez de la Audiencia Nacional Antonio Piña ha propuesto sentar en el banquillo a cuatro exjefes de ETA por el atentado cometido, el 4 de agosto de 2002, contra la casa cuartel de la Guardia Civil de Santa Pola (Alicante), que dejó dos muertos —uno de ellos, una niña de seis años— y más de medio centenar de heridos. Se trata de Juan Antonio Olarra Guridi, alias Jokin; Ainhoa Múgica Goñi, Olga; María Soledad Iparraguirre Guenechea, Anboto; y Félix Ignacio Esparza Luri, Navarro. Con ellos, ya son seis los exdirigentes de la organización terrorista procesados por este atentado, después de que en agosto de 2024 lo fueran Mikel Albisu Iriarte, Antza y Ramon Sagarzazu Gaztelumendi, Ramontxo. Todos ellos están acusados de los delitos de asesinato, lesiones y daños terroristas.

Esta causa ―por la que ya fueron condenados en 2012 a 843 años de cárcel los dos autores materiales, Óscar Celarain y Andoni Otegi― se reabrió en marzo de 2022 a partir de una querella de la asociación de víctimas Dignidad y Justicia, que lleva años intentando abrir una nueva vía en los tribunales para condenar a los antiguos responsables de ETA como “autores mediatos por dominio” de los atentados cometidos por sus subordinados —una especie de inductores intelectuales de los crímenes, al tener el control absoluto de la banda—. De los cuatro exjefes ahora procesados, tres de ellos ―Olarra, Múgica y Esparza― están en semilibertad después de que el Gobierno vasco les aplicara el artículo 100.2 del Reglamento Penitenciario. A Iparragirre se la ha concedido también, pero la medida ha sido recurrida por la Fiscalía y aún está pendiente que la Audiencia Nacional se pronuncie. Los dos exjefes etarras encausados con anterioridad están en libertad.

En su resolución, el juez Piña señala que, de los informes aportados por la Policía Nacional y la Guardia Civil, así como de las declaraciones que tomó a los cuatro antiguos dirigentes de la organización terrorista el pasado junio, se desprende que, en el momento en el que se cometió el atentado, tanto los ahora procesados como los dos que lo fueron hace dos años formaban parte de la zuba, la dirección de ETA, en la terminología de los terroristas. Según destaca el instructor, los documentos policiales “atribuyen a dichas estructuras directivas la provisión de los medios materiales necesarios para la ejecución del atentado, entre ellos el vehículo sustraído utilizado como coche bomba, las placas de matrícula falsas y el material explosivo, elementos que habrían sido entregados al comando Argala [autor del atentado] ya preparados desde Francia”.

En concreto, el juez sitúa a la pareja formada por Olarra Guridi y Múgica Goñi al frente del aparato militar, denominado internamente como Otsagi y que se encargaba “del control, coordinación y abastecimiento de los comandos operativos”. Por ello, considera que ambos, como responsables de esta estructura, intervinieron “en la obtención, preparación y suministro de los medios materiales empleados” en el atentado. Y detalla que “la estructura bajo su responsabilidad” entregó el vehículo utilizado como coche bomba “previamente acondicionado para su uso en la acción terrorista”.

En el caso de Esparza, el juez lo sitúa en aquellas fechas como “el máximo responsable” del aparato logístico de ETA, denominado Lohi. En su resolución, recuerda que es, precisamente, esta parte de la organización la encargada de “la obtención, almacenamiento, conservación y distribución de los recursos materiales necesarios para la actividad terrorista”, incluido “explosivos, vehículos sustraídos, documentación falsa, matrículas y demás instrumentos utilizados por los comandos operativos”. El magistrado añade que existen indicios de que dicha labor también la realizó para el atentado de Santa Pola.

A la cuarta procesada, Iparraguirre ―que es la pareja de Mikel Antza―, la resolución judicial la sitúa al frente del aparato de finanzas de la banda, o Diba, encargada de “la gestión, administración y distribución de los recursos económicos destinados al mantenimiento y funcionamiento de los distintos aparatos de ETA, incluyendo el aparato militar y el aparato logístico”. “Existen indicios de que, desde dicha posición directiva, [Anboto] participó en la financiación y sostenimiento económico de las estructuras organizativas que hicieron posible la comisión del atentado investigado”, añade el juez. Los dos exjefes de ETA que habían sido procesados con anterioridad también formaban parte de la Zuba. Así, Mikel Antza es señalado como jefe del aparato político de la banda, encargado de fijar la estrategia de la organización. Ramontxo era el máximo dirigente del llamado aparato internacional, órgano encargado de dar cobertura a los etarras huidos a otros países y de entablar relaciones con organizaciones afines.

El de Santa Pola es uno de los 10 sumarios por atentados de ETA que se han reactivado en los últimos años y que han puesto en el foco judicial a más de una veintena de exdirigentes de ETA. Además de por el crimen de la localidad alicantina, la Audiencia Nacional investiga a antiguos jefes de la organización terrorista por el secuestro y muerte en 1997 de Miguel Ángel Blanco; el asesinato en 1995 del concejal popular Gregorio Ordóñez; el ataque contra la T-4 del aeropuerto de Barajas en 2006, con dos muertos; el atentado contra la comisaría de la Ertzaintza de Ondarroa (Bizkaia) en 2008; el atentado de Sangüesa (Navarra) en 2003, que causó la muerte de dos policías; el asesinato del coronel Pedro Antonio Blanco en Madrid; el del fiscal jefe de Andalucía Luis Portero en Granada; el atentado contra el magistrado Francisco Querol, donde perdieron la vida el juez, su chófer y su escolta; y el crimen del concejal del PP Jesús María Pedrosa en Durango (Bizkaia), estos cuatro últimos cometidos en el 2000.

World.title: Más escapadas, más cortas y durante todo el año: el auge de los microviajes como tendencia
World.content:
Huir de las masificaciones, los altos precios y el calor de los meses de verano va ampliando el calendario turístico y consolidando los viajes breves fuera de la temporada alta

Una de las pocas ventajas que Paco y Paloma le ven a las vacaciones en verano es que pueden coincidir con los amigos. En todo lo demás ganan las escapadas fuera de temporada. “Hay menos gente y es todo más barato”, resume esta pareja de treintañeros residente en Madrid, con posibilidad de pedirse días libres fuera de julio y agosto en sus respectivos trabajos. Su tónica en los últimos tiempos ha sido la de hacer dos viajes largos al extranjero (de unas tres semanas sumando ambos), más una serie de desplazamientos cortos con el resto de días de descanso, festivos y los puentes, normalmente en coche, al norte peninsular o por Europa si encuentran un vuelo económico.

Los datos avalan su postura y la tendencia al alza de los microviajes. Más del 70% de los encuestados por Eurostars Hotel Company en 2026 manifestaron su preferencia por las escapadas cortas, frecuentes y con un propósito. Pequeñas aventuras como extensión, y no paréntesis, de la vida cotidiana, con planes sencillos y disfrute inmediato, según establecen los autores del estudio.

Más información Un recorrido musical por Barcelona en cuatro movimientos con Pau Casals

Según la oficina estadística de la Unión Europea, Eurostat, alrededor del 56% de los desplazamientos turísticos de los residentes de la UE en 2023 y 2024 fueron de entre una y tres noches, aunque la cifra incluye el turismo de negocios y de reuniones (MICE). El 70% de las aventuras exprés (entre cuatro y seis días) y los weekend (de uno a tres) de la agencia WeRoad se desarrollan en España y Europa, y van buscando la experiencia: visitar chocolaterías en Ginebra, destilerías en Varsovia, las luces navideñas de la italiana Salerno, el Caminito del Rey en Málaga, auroras boreales en Laponia, rutas en barco en Albania o senderismo en Sierra Nevada.

El estudio Viajar con un propósito: cómo la Generación Z y los millennials están redefiniendo el viaje, elaborado por Expedia Group a partir de 7.000 entrevistas en siete mercados, revela que los jóvenes prefieren viajar fuera de temporada alta, eligen alternativas menos concurridas y apoyan medidas que reduzcan la presión sobre destinos populares.

Iria Caamaño, profesora e investigadora en la Facultad de Turismo de la Universidade da Coruña, comparte la tesis solo a medias. “Hay una aparente contradicción entre buscar lugares poco concurridos y desplazarse a un concierto multitudinario, aunque la diferencia puede estar en cómo se vive. En un concierto, compartir la experiencia con mucha gente puede formar parte de su atractivo; en una ruta de senderismo, esa misma concentración puede entrar en conflicto con la tranquilidad que se busca”, reflexiona. Su conclusión es que estas generaciones no rechazan la presencia de otros, sino la saturación que dificulta disfrutar de la experiencia.

Visitantes cruzando el puente colgante en el Caminito del Rey, Málaga, España. Cavan Images / GETTY IMAGES

Preguntada sobre si las miniescapadas podrían considerarse una manera “natural” de viajar para millennials y Z, Caamaño responde que el saco es demasiado grande y heterogéneo como para generalizar. “Los microviajes encajan con una forma de ocio organizada alrededor de intereses y experiencias concretas”, describe. La posibilidad de practicarlos depende tanto de la edad como de los recursos y del tiempo disponible. “Una persona sin hijos y con flexibilidad puede organizar sus viajes de manera diferente a otra condicionada por el calendario escolar, aunque ambas pertenezcan a la misma generación. Y una persona jubilada también puede realizar varias escapadas fuera de temporada”, apunta. “La cuestión no es solo qué generaciones quieren viajar así, sino quiénes pueden permitírselo”, plantea.

Daniel Martínez, director de Marketing y Eventos de WeRoad, observa que desde 2022 se está produciendo una progresiva reducción en la duración de las propuestas de su agencia, a razón de un día menos por año. Pero no cree que los viajes largos estén desapareciendo entre los jóvenes, que forman el grueso de sus clientes. Sus estancias, en promedio, siguen superando las siete noches. “El viaje largo es en el que centramos nuestro poder adquisitivo, y ya el resto del año jugamos con los puentes”, concreta.

En el calendario español figuran varios de estos paréntesis laborales de tres o cuatro días (dependiendo del año): septiembre en Barcelona, noviembre y mayo en Madrid, febrero en Andalucía, más los nacionales: el del Pilar en octubre, el de Todos los Santos en noviembre, el de la Constitución en diciembre, Semana Santa… “Los viajes de fin de semana y los puentes llevan mucho tiempo formando parte de nuestras prácticas turísticas”, matiza Caamaño, que los considera una práctica consolidada. Sí que se atisban indicios de una mayor distribución de la actividad turística en el pre y el posverano, aunque la experta hablaría más de una ampliación de la temporada que de una sustitución de julio y agosto.

“En España, según las comparativas entre 2019 y 2024, las llegadas internacionales crecieron más en los meses de temporada media y baja que en los de temporada alta. Eso apunta a una desestacionalización relativa, pero no significa necesariamente que haya menos turistas en verano”, puntualiza. Lo que sí parece claro es que comienza a haber más en mayo y en septiembre, incluso en octubre. Los Movimientos Turísticos en Fronteras (Frontur) de los siete primeros meses de 2026 (última estadística del INE) documentan una subida del número de viajeros internacionales del 9,5% en mayo y del 4,6% en julio. Falta por conocer cómo han evolucionado agosto y septiembre.

La Encuesta de Turismo de Residentes (Familitur) arroja un aumento del 2,9% en los viajes que los españoles emprendieron durante el segundo trimestre (abril, mayo y junio) y un descenso del 3,6% en el tercero (julio, agosto y septiembre). Según estimaciones recién publicadas por el INE (no son cifras definitivas), los españoles viajaron un 0,6% menos en julio de este año que en el de 2025. Los altos precios y la masificación explican que, cada vez más, quien puede huye de la temporada alta. “Para mí, claramente, el calor es otro de los factores que están influyendo en las preferencias de viaje”, suma Caamaño.

Septiembre se perfila como ganador en esta evolución del calendario turístico. Es el mes en el que las reservas de WeRoad crecieron un 61,3% entre 2024 y 2025. “Es una manera de romper con la vuelta a la rutina tras el verano y, además, existen un montón de ofertas”, subraya Martínez. En ese sentido, Paco y Paloma valoran como un plus añadido la posibilidad de irse de vacaciones en mitad del año, “y la rotura radical con la rutina” que eso implica. “La sensación de estar de vacaciones a contratemporada es una gozada”, enfatizan.

Unions FNV and CNV have suspended their weekly strikes in regional public transport for two weeks after employers made new commitments on a collective labour agreement, broadcaster NOS reported on Wednesday.

The suspension means Thursday’s planned strike did not go ahead, the unions said in a press release.

The unions announced in early October they would strike one day a week after talks broke down. Staff at operators including Arriva, Keolis and Qbuzz walked out for the first time last week, cancelling many buses and regional trains across the country.

The unions are demanding a 9.5% pay rise over two years and better conditions for older staff.

World.title: Gambling regulator hits illegal casino with record €37m fine
World.content:
The Dutch gambling regulator KSA has issued a record fine of €37 million on a company for running a dozen unlicensed online casinos.

EOD Code SRL, which says it is registered in Costa Rica, offered games to players in the Netherlands through sites including Instantcasino and Skyhills without a Dutch licence, KSA said on Thursday.

KSA inspectors were able to register and gamble on the sites with no measures in place to stop people in the Netherlands using them. Several of the sites had no visible age checks and accepted cryptocurrency and other anonymous payment methods.

The investigation began with Instantcasino and later uncovered 11 more sites run by the same company. The KSA based the fine on an estimate of the company’s Dutch revenue.

Online gambling was legalised in October 2021, with the government arguing a regulated market would draw players away from illegal sites. But the KSA estimated last year that more money goes to unlicensed sites than to legal ones.

In August, radio station BNR found that illegal operators were targeting Facebook and Instagram ads at people on Cruks, the national register that bars them from gambling. The cabinet set out plans in June to ban online gambling advertising and bonuses.

If you are concerned about your own or someone else’s use of alcohol, drugs, or gambling, the Jellinek addiction helpline can be reached on 088 505 1220 or at jellinek.nl. The line is staffed in Dutch and English on weekdays, 1pm to 5pm.

World.title: Airbnb to hosts: no more asking guests to wash the dishes
World.content:
In addition to increasingly strict rules for hosts renting out their homes on Airbnb – including limits on the number of nights, guest caps and permit fees – there are now new rules to abide by: they can’t ask their guests to do the dishes or remove bed sheets.

Airbnb introduced a new policy on house rules earlier this week that will go into effect on November 20, 2026. Among them are what the company considers “reasonable requests”, which Airbnb defines per chore.

“You may not ask guests to wash everything and store the dishes, but you may ask them to put the dishes in the sink,” says the site.

“You may not ask guests to pick up the bed linen or put the laundry in the washing machine, but you may ask them to collect used towels.”

And: “You may not ask guests to take the garbage and dispose of it elsewhere, but you may ask them to separate their residual waste and recyclable waste in the designated waste bins in the accommodation.”

But “reasonable” appears to be a relative term. Airbnb will let hosts, for example, ask guests to put their garbage in animal-resistant containers if there are bears in the area.

“It’s ridiculous,” said one former Airbnb host who doesn’t want to be named. “The rules were changing all the time, getting more restrictive, which made it increasingly hard to make any money at all. I’m glad I got out of it before I can’t tell my guests to clean up after themselves. What’s next? Will we have to provide sunbeds for them?”

According to the booking website, the world’s largest for private stays, landlords already charge their guests a cleaning fee. Making them clean more is unfair, says Airbnb, and leads to guest dissatisfaction.

Airbnb has faced criticism for years in many cities where it operates, with detractors saying it leads to higher rents, less housing for locals and less livable neighbourhoods, especially in smaller cities with huge tourist populations like Amsterdam and Barcelona.

World.title: Get help with careers, homes and more at IamExpat Fair The Hague
World.content:
The IamExpat Fair is returning to the Grote Kerk in The Hague on Saturday November 7 with more exhibitors than ever, three international centres from across South Holland and large sections for families and health.

The IamExpat Fair, now in its 24th edition, provides advice and services of all kinds for the international community, from housing and careers to schooling and leisure, including special offers only available for attendees. Tickets go for €6 online, or €10 at the door.

“We have an exciting lineup of exhibitors and workshops this year in The Hague,” says events manager Claire Leunissen.

“From exhibitors specialised in preparing newcomers for the inburgering exams, to career coaches experienced in advising expats, and stocking the health & leisure section with physical and mental resources, we’re confident that services at the IamExpat Fair will help internationals thrive. ”

Workshops, presentations and centres

Experts will run workshops throughout the day on topics including buying a house and securing a mortgage, job hunting and help with lifestyle and health. Places are limited, so make sure to book your chosen sessions in advance – you can sign up here.

The Hague International Centre will have a large stand, joined by representatives from across the province, including Leiden International Centre and the Rotterdam International Center, to answer practical questions about settling in the region.

Learning Dutch and finding work

For newcomers working toward the inburgering exams, there are resources from Inburgering Online and Easy Dutch, alongside language schools including Language Institute Regina Coeli, and Bart de Pau.

Career stands and coaches include recruitment agency Undutchables and Work & Worth Coaching, while Work in South Holland will explain the state of the labour market across the region’s main industries.

Families and health

The Family & Kids section brings together several international schools, including the International School of The Hague, The British School in the Netherlands, International School Delft and Optimist International School. There is also kids’ area where families can play games together.

The Health & Leisure section is one of the largest at the fair, with exhibitors ranging from mental health services to dentists and chiropractors.

The IamExpat Fair The Hague takes place in the Grote Kerk on Saturday November 7 from 10am to 5pm. Free tickets are available online while they last; after that, entry costs €6 in advance or €10 at the door. The first 1,000 visitors receive a free tote bag.

World.title: Police shut 30 webshops linked to counterfeit pill deaths
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Thirty websites were taken offline and three men arrested earlier this week in connection to sites that sold counterfeit pills that led to the deaths of three people.

The suspects – a 35-year-old man from Kwintsheul, a 39-year-old man from Rotterdam and a 66-year-old male from The Hague – are suspected of “offering, selling and supplying illegal drugs”, including sedatives, sleeping pills and painkillers like oxycodone, which contained extremely potent synthetic opioids known as nitazenes.

Nitazenes can be many times stronger than morphine and more lethal than fentanyl.

Police say the victims bought the prescription-only pills on websites Slaappillen.net or regionapp.net shortly before they died, and are holding the suspects responsible for running them.

Whack-a-mole

Even though Slaappillen.net was taken down last year, police say the men continued to sell the counterfeit drugs through other websites, which kept popping up as soon as others were taken down.

But according to police, this time they not only took the web shops offline, but confiscated the servers they ran on.

“We have taken down the entire technology behind the websites,” Ron van Brussel told NOS. He is responsible for tackling serious organized crime at the National Investigation and Interventions Unit. “This makes it more difficult to make a restart.”

Both the servers and data have been seized for investigation, and more arrests have not been ruled out.

The police searches were carried out in five locations, including homes and a storage box in The Hague. Crypto wallets, cash and valuables were seized.

With this week’s arrests, police say the main players from the group are now in custody. But, they add, the sale of illegal drugs is far from over.

“There are several criminal groups that keep these types of sites online,” said Van Brussel.

World.title: Are you financially fit for your life in the Netherlands?
World.content:
New to the Netherlands or a longer-term resident looking to get your finances organised to make the most of your Dutch life? A little planning, a few local habits and some expert coaching will soon have you in the best financial shape.

The foundation of any fitness plan is the basics, so first of all you need to establish what your monthly costs are likely to be. Alongside your rent or mortgage repayments, you’ll have to pay for health insurance, council taxes, public transport, gas and electricity, and perhaps a gym membership.

“If you are financially fit, you are able to meet all your monthly and annual payments, save some money and live the life you would like to have at that moment,” says Ame Pots, a financial health coach with ABN Amro who helps expats make the most of their money.

What costs can you expect?

ABN Amro is hosting a free webinar on October 28 to explain how to get financially fit in the Netherlands.

You will have to pay for insurance. Health insurance, for example, will cost you upwards of €160 a month from next year, and you will have to pay the first €400 of insured treatment. You can cut the monthly premium by around €25 if you raise your voluntary deductible by €500, but that means you’ll need to increase your savings so you can pay if you do fall ill. If you want supplementary insurance, such as dental coverage or extra physiotherapy, you will pay more.

By the way, the six-week window for changing health insurer kicks off in mid-November, so now might be a good time to start shopping around for a better deal.

You’ll also have to pay your local authority for waste collection and the water board for water usage. How much you pay depends on the size of your home and how many people live there, but between €250 and €450 a year is the norm in most places. If you are a homeowner, you will pay slightly more. These bills often arrive at the same time of year, in the spring, so you’ll need to make sure you have enough savings to cover them as well.

“We rarely use credit cards, and this surprises a lot of people,” Ame says.

Some bills are monthly, others come once a year

If you live in rented accommodation, you may have to pay service costs, which can range from around €50 to over €250 a month if you live in a building with a lift and lots of amenities such as co-working spaces or a gym. The monthly service fee is an estimate, and you will get a final invoice once a year. Rents also go up once a year, usually in July, by a percentage set by the government. For 2027, the increase in the non-rent-controlled sector, where most expats live, will be 4.4%.

You can keep an eye on your gas and electricity bills if you have a smart meter. If you pay too little to cover your usage, you will be invoiced for the extra costs and your monthly payment is likely to increase. If you pay too much, you’ll get the difference back.

“All this means that you need to really plan out your spending over the year,” says ABN Amro expert Ame. “For example, if you have the 30% ruling, will you still be able to meet your payments when it ends in five years’ time?”

Once you understand the costs you face, create a budget that includes fixed spending, savings and fun stuff. Remember to adjust it if your financial situation changes.

Why is banking in the Netherlands different?

“It’s important to explain to new arrivals how the financial system works in the Netherlands, because it may be very different to back home,” says Ame. “For example, we rarely use credit cards, and this surprises a lot of people from countries where they use a credit card as part of their regular spending.”

You’ll need a Dutch bank account for your salary, your rent and pretty much everything else. The Netherlands runs on digital payments, with debit cards, internet payments and payment request apps dominating how the Dutch spend their money.

“If I ask people how much they spend on rent or groceries, they often give a round number – €100 or €200 – but in practice it is more than that,” says Ame. “Once you are aware of what is really happening in your finances, you will understand how much you can actually spend each month.”

How can you improve your financial fitness?

What to know more about how to stay financially fit in the Netherlands. Join ABN Amro’s free webinar on Wednesday, 28 October, 12:00–13:00 CET. Register now

World.title: Afghans washed up on Texel were human smuggling victims
World.content:
Two Afghan men whose body parts washed ashore on Texel in 2023 were victims of a vast human smuggling network led by infamous migrant smuggler Idriss Ghazi Kareem, according to an investigation by regional broadcaster NH and investigative TV programme Zembla.

The Afghan refugees, Samiullah (20) and Ahmad Jan (27), were only identified this summer. They had boarded a rubber dinghy on the night of August 12, 2023, along with 66 others just north of Calais, in an attempt to cross the English Channel. The boat’s engine failed and, after an explosion, the vessel tore apart.

Although 60 men survived, six were declared dead when found. Samiullah and Ahmad Jan, though, had gone missing.

Two months later, a single foot still in a shoe and a torso washed up on Texel. Dutch detective Fetze Venema worked with the Red Cross to identify the remains, including tracking down the relatives of the missing men in Afghanistan for DNA testing.

Idriss Ghazi Kareem

Following the incident, French authorities dismantled a huge human-trafficking network led by Idriss Ghazi Kareem. He was tried with eight others in Paris last year and sentenced to 15 years in prison for, among other things, procuring boats and other equipment for migrants to cross the English Channel.

The court found he earned hundreds of thousands of euros a year from his people-smuggling operations, which he continued to organise from prison.

Kareem had visited the Netherlands several times, including just three days before the fatal accident. The Marechaussee, the military police force responsible for border control, says the country plays a key role in people-smuggling.

“It involves the import, transit, and storage of nautical equipment that is transported to the French coast, where it is then used to ferry migrants across to Great Britain.”

The Marechaussee has not commented on the latest media investigation, saying it “may be part of an ongoing investigation”.

Additional research by NH and Zembla found that at least 26 people, including eight women and two children, have died this year attempting to cross the English Channel in unseaworthy boats.

“Floating coffins”

Much of the equipment – from the rubber boat to its motor and life vests – was substandard. “These rubber boats are not seaworthy and generally originate from China,” national public prosecutor for migration-related crime Petra Hoekstra told Zembla. “They are imported into the Netherlands via Turkey.”

And, he said, the smugglers knew that. “For us, that is an aggravating circumstance. They believe that the money outweighs a human life. And that means they are deliberately placing people in floating coffins.”

World.title: Rotterdam police arrest AI scammers over €400k thefts
World.content:
Police in Rotterdam have rounded up a gang who ran a sophisticated phishing scam using a fake banking app that stole nearly €400,000 from 170 victims.

The gang set up a bogus bank helpdesk service that targeted customers by phone and asked them to download an app that could read the NFC chip on their bank card.

Police arrested the two men behind the operation, a 23-year-old man from Vaassen, and a 25-year-old man from Ede, on October 4. On Tuesday they appeared in court, where a magistrate extended their detention for 90 days.

The fraudsters made the scam more plausible by using AI-generated voices to read out messages telling their victims to check if Google Pay had been installed on their phones by their bank.

When they saw it had not, they were told to press 1, which connected them straight to the fake helpdesk.

The victims were told to install the app and hold their card to their phone, allowing the criminals to download their details. At the same time accomplices would try to hack into the account using the card’s PIN.

Ruben van Well, head of the Rotterdam cybercrime team, said the victims ranged in age from their twenties to their eighties. “We found a lot of young people had been defrauded,” he said. “The victims also came from all over the country.”

Police confiscated hundreds of thousands of euros in cryptocurrency following the arrests and took the fake app and server offline. “We are not ruling out further arrests,” said Van Well.

World.title: Poland and India aim to double trade by 2030 as PMs meet in New Delhi

The prime ministers of Poland and India have, after a meeting in New Delhi, outlined aims to double bilateral trade by 2030 and expand cooperation in mining, shipbuilding, energy, space and defence technologies. Donald Tusk’s visit, the first by a Polish prime minister to India in 16 years, follows the upgrading of bilateral ties between the two countries to a strategic partnership during Narendra Modi’s trip to Poland two years ago, which was the first by an Indian prime minister in almost five decades. During a joint press conference with Tusk on Thursday, Modi said that his Warsaw visit had acted as a catalyst for the Polish-Indian relationship to “gain speed over the last two years”. Tusk added that the two leaders had now reviewed the results of their cooperation so far and outlined priorities for the coming years. They discussed, among other things, ways to deepen economic, investment and technological ties between the two fast-growing economies. Poland’s GDP is set to grow by 3.5% this year, the second-fastest rate in the European Union, while India will see economic growth of 7%. Poland’s economy is also on the verge of becoming the 20th largest in the world, with the country hoping to join the G20. “The economic strength of both countries offers a wealth of opportunities for strategic partnership,” Modi said. Tusk, meanwhile, underlined that “Poland and India are countries that have much in common and nothing that divides them…[with] no conflicting interests or historical grievances.” Poland hopes that the boost to bilateral trade will come from an EU-India trade deal expected to be signed in December. The agreement is designed to eliminate or reduce tariffs on goods accounting for 96.6% of the value of EU exports to the Indian market. Tusk said Poland wanted to capitalise on the opportunities created by the deal, with the ambition of becoming “India’s gateway to Europe”. Modi expressed confidence that Poland’s and India’s “shared goal” of doubling bilateral trade by 2030 “will certainly be achieved”. “Today, trade between Poland and India totals just over $6 billion,” said Poland’s finance minister Andrzej Domański, who joined Tusk on the trip to India. “We want this trade to grow, and the conditions for that are very favourable.” However, “it is no secret that we have a significant trade deficit with India”, Domański added. Last year, Poland exported goods worth €1.4 billion to India, with machinery, mineral products and metals the largest categories. Meanwhile, it imported €4.3 billion, in particular textiles, machinery and metals. The United States wants Poland to become a full member of the G20 "as soon as possible". "Poland’s economic growth, combined with its growing leadership position in the international arena, make it an ideal participant," says the @StateDept https://t.co/OjpWly4FTw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 12, 2026 According to the Polish prime minister’s office, the EU-India agreement could also help increase Polish investment in India, particularly in advanced manufacturing, food processing, biotechnology and mobility. To help facilitate such investments, Tusk travelled with almost 100 Polish business representatives, hoping the visit will help them to enter the large and rapidly growing Indian market. His office described the delegation as the largest of its kind in the history of Polish-Indian relations. Modi said he was “particularly happy” with Tusk’s decision to bring a business delegation and announced plans to strengthen links between startups in both countries, including through technology hackathons for young people. The countries plan to expand cooperation in critical minerals, raw materials and coal gasification, a process that converts coal into gas for energy and industrial use. Shipbuilding, defence, space and advanced technologies are also among the priority sectors. Indians are now the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, followed by Colombians, according to new data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Ukrainians remain by far the largest immigrant group, followed by Belarusians https://t.co/hNiOqmeUfX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2026 The leaders also highlighted historical ties and people-to-people exchanges as a foundation for closer relations. Modi recalled the role of Indian Maharaja Jam Saheb Digvijaysinhji Ranjitsinhji, known in Poland as the “Good Maharaja”, who provided shelter and care to around 1,000 Polish children evacuated from the Soviet Union during the Second World War. “In 2022, Poland helped our Indian students, demonstrating that same spirit of humanity,” added Modi, referring to the support Poland provided to Indian students escaping from Ukraine following Russia’s full-scale invasion. Modi said he hoped that the ongoing Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme, which recently took place for the second time, will “introduce the next generation to this Polish-Indian friendship”. The strengthening of bilateral relations has also come amid a rapid rise in Indian migration to Poland in recent years. This year Indians became the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, numbering around 25,500, up almost 5% in a year. World.title: How will recent scandals affect Polish politics?
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
