World.title: Raihan Vadra’s protest photos spark political row, Congress alleges censorship, BJP hits back - all you need to know
World.content:
Raihan Vadraâs protest photos spark political row

Bikaner House says photographs were inconsistent with its policy

Raihan Vadra questions restrictions on political art

Priyanka Gandhi backs son, Robert Vadra says family will find another venue

Gehlot calls removal of photographs censorship

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BJP targets Gandhi family over exhibition row

NEW DELHI: The Bikaner House Management Society on Thursday defended its request to remove certain photographs from visual artist Raihan Vadraâs exhibition, saying they were âfound to be inconsistentâ with its policy, as the dispute over the removal of images documenting student protests and photographs of the national flag escalated into a political confrontation between the Congress and the BJP.Vadra, son of Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, alleged that the administration asked him to remove 70 of the 105 photographs displayed at his exhibition, No Idea Is Final, in New Delhi. He questioned the restrictions on political expression at an art institution, while several Congress leaders criticised the decision as censorship. The BJP, meanwhile, accused the Gandhi family of using the controversy for political purposes.In a statement on Thursday, the Bikaner House Management Society said certain photographs displayed at the exhibition were found to be inconsistent with its policy and their removal was requested. It added that the photographs considered consistent with its policy continued to be displayed."Bikaner House is a public cultural institution dedicated to the promotion of art and culture.The exhibition and associated activities must comply with Bikaner House Management Society policy," the statement said.The clarification came a day after Vadra alleged that the administration had asked him to remove several photographs documenting protests in Delhi, including images of the national flag, ahead of the exhibition's scheduled opening on Wednesday evening.In an Instagram post on Wednesday, Vadra said, "Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show "No Idea Is Final", which opens this evening at 7 pm. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi.Apparently, the content is "objectionable". They also directed me to remove two photos of the Tiranga. I have refused. I will not take down a picture of the Indian flag."He said the exhibition would proceed with the remaining works and that he would consider another venue if necessary to display the complete collection of protest photographs.Speaking to PTI Videos, Vadra said he had been informed about potential objections to some photographs a day before the exhibition and had asked the management to communicate its concerns in writing."My show, 'No Idea Is Final', was supposed to start at 7 pm yesterday at Bikaner House. Twenty-four hours before the opening, I was approached by the Bikaner House management and told that some of the pictures might be objectionable or against their policy. I said that I did not believe they are, but I am happy to discuss the matter and asked them to get back to me in writing as to what are the objections," he said.According to Vadra, the management did not respond until the following morning, when its team inspected the exhibition. He said he was subsequently told to remove 70 of the 105 photographs."I did not hear from them till 11 am next day when their team came, saw the exhibit and left, they even complimented me on some of the photographs. Then, around 12.30 pm, we received a call from the deputy resident commissioner saying that you have to remove 70 of the 105 photographs in the exhibition because they are against the policy," he said.Vadra said he had already removed some photographs containing overtly political slogans after reviewing the venue's policy and was willing to discuss concerns over images featuring flags and political leaders.The management later insisted that the remaining photographs considered objectionable be removed, he alleged. Vadra said he asked officials to put their objections in writing, particularly regarding the photographs of the national flag."So, we took them down except two photographs of the Indian flag which also they asked me to remove. I said, 'But they are just pictures of the Indian flag. I do not think there is anything in your policy that says photographs of the Indian flag have to be removed'. At that point, I firmly told them to put their demand in writing if they wanted me to remove the photographs of the Indian flag," Vadra said.He alleged that although the management did not provide a written demand, officials removed one of the two photographs while he was away.Vadra questioned the restriction on political expression at an art institution, saying, "I mean, most art is political, right? You cannot function as an artistic institution and then say that political content is not allowed," he said.He also alleged that he had shared a layout of the exhibition with the management a week earlier, but was later told that officials had not been able to review it.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra backed her son on Thursday, expressing support for his decision to stand by his work.In a post on X, she wrote, "When someone with power becomes afraid of the expression of another, he doesn't know it, but he has already lost the very power he is trying to protect. You stand for what is true and everything beautiful will find its way to you. I am proud of you, always will be."Robert Vadra also expressed pride in his son and said the family would find another venue if necessary.Speaking to ANI, he said, "I am very proud of Raihan. He has seen what the whole family goes through and has gone through, and what his father has gone through. So, he is a very strong person, a very strong-headed person. He will find another location, and we will do it at another location.âHe said Raihan had attended the recent protests, documenting them through photographs before deciding to organise an exhibition on the subject. According to Robert Vadra, his son had submitted a PDF of the proposed exhibition to the Bikaner House authorities about a week in advance, but they had not raised concerns about its content.Robert Vadra also questioned whether the decision was linked to the Rajasthan government or resulted from other pressures, adding that his son would not be prevented from showcasing his work.Former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot criticised the BJP government over the controversy, describing the removal of the photographs as an attack on artistic expression and democracy."Bikaner House is a property of the Rajasthan government. This means a young artist's creativity was stifled under the BJP government's watch, which is highly condemnable," Gehlot said in a statement.He alleged that the government was attempting to suppress images reflecting public dissent and demanded an explanation for the removal of the photographs."Suppressing the voice of artists is a direct attack on democracy. This is a clear example of censorship," Gehlot said.Gehlot also praised Vadra for refusing to remove the two photographs featuring the national flag.Congress leader Pawan Khera also questioned the restrictions placed on the exhibition, arguing that artists should be able to express themselves through their work.Speaking to ANI, Khera said, "Raihan Vadra is an artist. We can't understand why this government is against the expression of art by an artist. Every day we see examples of how this government is against the youth voicing their opinions using different mediums, including art," Khera said.The BJP hit back at the Congress over the controversy, with party spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia targeting the Gandhi family and alleging that it was using the episode to pursue its political ambitions.Speaking on the issue, Bhatia said, âCongress' psychophant leaders are saying that he is the future president of Congress. One defective product who has lost 99 elections has not been launched by Sonia mummy. Now Priyanka mummy's mission has come to launch Raihan."Further targeting the Congress leadership, Bhatia alleged that the family was willing to do anything to regain power."This fake Gandhi family wants power every time, and as soon as they are out of power, they will do anything. They can do anything for power. The law will prevail in the country, be it the defective product Rahul Gandhi or the future president of Congress, Raihan Vadra. Priyanka mummy is now on a new mission. After the launch of Rahul Gandhi, Raihan will be launched,â he added.

World.title: 'No political family faced as much injustice': Akhilesh meets jailed Azam Khan, targets BJP
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

chief

on Thursday met jailed party leader

at Rampur district jail and alleged that no political family had faced as much injustice as Khan's family. The meeting comes ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, with the SP discussing its electoral strategy.

According to PTI, Yadav accused the BJP government of pursuing political vendetta against Khan and lodging false cases against him.

"No political family has faced as much injustice as Azam Khan's family," Yadav said while addressing reporters after the hour-long meeting.

Yadav said he had discussed all 403 Assembly constituencies with Khan, along with suggestions received from the party's alliance partners. Asked who would contest from Rampur, he declined to reveal the name, saying, "Why should we reveal that now?"

Khan and his son, Abdullah Azam Khan, were sentenced to seven years in prison by a Rampur court in November 2025 in dual PAN card cases linked to discrepancies in their dates of birth.

Khan has also faced convictions in several other cases, including hate speech and a fake birth certificate case. He has challenged convictions through appeals.

Yadav also accused the BJP government of undermining the Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, an institution associated with Khan, alleging that a conspiracy had been hatched to destroy it.

World.title: ‘Inconsistent with policy’: Bikaner House on removal of photos from Raihan Vadra’s exhibition
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bikaner House Management Society on Thursday said it had requested the removal of certain photographs from Raihan Vadraâs exhibition, âNo Idea Is Finalâ, after finding them inconsistent with its policy.

The statement came after Vadra, son of Congress MP

and businessman Robert Vadra, alleged that the venueâs management had asked him to remove photographs depicting youth movements in Delhi just hours before the exhibitionâs scheduled opening at 7 pm.

In a statement, the society said Bikaner House was a public cultural institution dedicated to promoting art and culture, and that exhibitions held at the venue must comply with its management policy.

"Certain photographs displayed as part of Mr Raihan Vadraâs exhibition, No Idea Is Final', at Bikaner House were found to be inconsistent with the policy of the Bikaner House Management Society. Accordingly, their removal was requested," it said, as quoted by news agency PTI.

"The photographs that are consistent with the Society's policy have continued to be displayed," the statement added.

Speaking to ANI, Vadra said the management had first raised concerns about some images 24 hours before the opening.





He said he had asked officials to identify the photographs so that the matter could be discussed, but was approached again on Thursday afternoon, leaving him with only a few hours to address the issue.

Vadra alleged that he had shared the exhibition layout a week earlier and questioned why the concerns had not been raised sooner. He also said he had requested written explanations for the proposed removals but had not received specific reasons.

World.title: Tirupati MP alleges NDA ‘coercion’ against YSRCP nominees, seeks SEC action
World.content:
Tirupati MP Maddila Gurumoorthy has flayed the ruling NDA government for resorting to threatening the YSRCP candidates in the fray to withdraw their nominations.

The MP even complained to the State Election Commission (SEC) about the series of incidents that amounted to alleged coercion of his party candidates in Kaluvoy mandal of Venkatagiri constituency and termed it as ‘unacceptable’.

“The local TDP MLA K. Ramakrishna openly told his cadres at a meeting held on October 19 to prevent YSRCP candidates from filing nominations. I have submitted the video evidence to the SEC and asked the officials to take action”, he told the media on Thursday. The SEC, in turn, directed the State Director General of Police and the Tirupati District Collector to take action, Mr. Gurumoorthy added.

Meanwhile, the YSRCP Venkatagiri constituency convener Nedurumalli Ram Kumar, who was in the thick of action during the nomination phase, was issued house arrest notice on Thursday. The notice insisted him to stay indoors till the evening of October 23 (Friday).

“When the TDP MLA threatened to break the legs of YSRCP nominees, why are you confining me to my home?” Mr. Ram Kumar asked seeking an explanation.

The notice arrived when he was planning to accompany eight candidates who were filing their nominations for MPTC positions in Venkatagiri mandal.

Meanwhile, Joint Collector R. Govinda Rao inspected the nomination filing process for MPTC elections at Venkatagiri and Balayapalle mandals. He checked the condition of the ballot boxes and the storage mechanism adopted at the centres.

World.title: Vizag Port eyes stake in Mulapeta Port SPV to streamline regional cargo
World.content:
The Visakhapatnam Port Authority (VPA), is exploring a strategic partnership with the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board (APMB) to acquire a 49% equity stake in the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) developing Mulapeta Port in Srikakulam district.

Speaking to The Hindu, a senior VPA official confirmed that discussions were under way between the State government and the Centre. “A final decision is likely to be taken by the end of 2026-27FY,” the official said.

The proposed partnership is aimed to optimise regional cargo distribution along the Andhra Pradesh coast, improve overall operational efficiency, and support Visakhapatnam’s long-term evolution as a major urban and economic centre.

Phased cargo relocation schedule

The arrangement envisages a gradual, phased shifting of bulk commodities—specifically coal, iron ore, and other suitable mineral cargoes—from Visakhapatnam Port to Mulapeta. The execution schedule and extent of relocation are tied directly to the infrastructure readiness, the availability of berths, storage yards, and cargo evacuation facilities at Mulapeta. This phased transition will allow Mulapeta to progressively build its cargo throughput while enabling Visakhapatnam to streamline its cargo profile.

Project scale and capacity

Mulapeta Port is being developed as a greenfield facility by the State government through APMB.

Phase I of Mulapeta Port comprises of four berths—three for general cargo and one for coal— with a planned annual handling capacity of approximately 23.50 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA). The estimated project cost of the first phase in ₹3,670 crore.

Operational and urban advantages

The proposed reallocation of bulk cargo handling is expected to quicken vessel turnaround times, enhance berth utilisation at Visakhapatnam, and advance port modernisation goals.

Furthermore, relieving Visakhapatnam Port of heavy mineral cargo handling directly supports the city’s long-term urban decongestion and environmental objectives. VPA intends to leverage its decades of operational experience and industry relationships to accelerate cargo mobilisation at the greenfield site.

Industrial integration and way forward

Beyond port operations, the roadmap incorporates port-led industrial development through a proposed Special Economic Zone (SEZ) on the adjacent 4,000 acres of salt lands. This integrated ecosystem aims to attract anchor manufacturing units, boost value-added logistics, and stimulate regional employment. Through coordinated maritime and industrial expansion, the partnership seeks to reinforce complementary trade corridors across North Coastal Andhra Pradesh.

World.title: Underage driving, non-adherence to helmet rule back in focus after death of a man in accident in Puducherry
World.content:
The recent death of a 52-year-old person in an accident has once again brought to fore the dangers of motor vehicles being driven by underage children and riding of two-wheelers without wearing a helmet in Puducherry.

Early this month, a family of three travelling in a scooter along Ambedkar Salai near Uppalam was hit by a high-performance sports bike ridden by a minor. Varadaraj, 52, who was riding the scooter sustained head injuries while two others who were travelling with him suffered bruises.

Mr. Varadaraj, after receiving initial treatment at the Puducherry Government General Hospital, was shifted later to a private healthcare facility in Chennai. Despite the efforts of the doctors at the private hospital, he succumbed to his injuries a few days ago. His death has now prompted the police to alter the criminal sections charged against the minor boy from 125(a) and 281 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, to sections 281 and 106(1) of the BNS, 2023.

Police said the rider of the high-end motorcycle was only 17 years of age and was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner when the accident occurred. The minor has been arrayed as the first accused (Juvenile in Conflict with Law) and his mother, the registered owner of the motorcycle, as second accused for allegedly permitting her minor son to ride the vehicle.

“The tragic incident highlights how irresponsible decisions by parents and vehicle owners in allowing their minor wards to ride motor vehicles could result in devastating and irreversible consequences. The accident could have been averted if the minor was not permitted to ride the bike. Further, wearing a protective helmet could have significantly reduced the risk of fatal head injuries and might have saved the victim’s precious life,” Senior Superintendent of Police D. Divya said.

She further said the incident served as a painful reminder that both responsible parental supervision and strict adherence to basic road safety measures were essential to prevent avoidable loss of life. Parents and vehicle owners should recognise that handing over a vehicle to a minor could have grave legal consequences and might result in preventable accidents, permanent disabilities and loss of precious lives, Ms. Divya pointed out.

Concurring with the views of the police officer on the need to follow traffic rules, Additional Professor and Head, Department of Neurosurgery, Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research, Manoranjitha Kumari Mani said adhering to road safety rules for protecting lives was a collective responsibility. Road discipline, adherence to traffic rules, responsible driving and respect for traffic police must become an integral part of commuting culture, she added.

“In India, approximately 19 individuals die every hour due to road traffic injuries, with head injuries accounting for a substantial proportion of these deaths. In Puducherry, data indicate that 15 out of every 100 patients admitted with head injuries die in hospital. In severe cases, even those who survive may never regain their pre-injury functional status. Much of the sufferings could be prevented by wearing a good quality helmet with the chin strip securely fastened, both for rider and pillion rider,” the doctor said.

Advising road users to follow traffic rules for their personal and common good, the SSP said stern action would be initiated against violators. The minors involved in traffic offences would be strictly dealt with under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 and owners of the vehicle would be made liable for the crime in accordance with the law, she added.

World.title: Kerala High Court upholds 10-year jail term for man convicted of raping 73-year-old woman
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has upheld a 10-year prison sentence imposed on a man convicted of raping and molesting a 73-year-old woman in Thrissur in 2022 on the pretext of driving out an “evil spirit”.

Dismissing the appeal filed by Muhammad of Thrissur against his conviction, Justice A. Badharudeen held that the survivor’s testimony alone was enough to establish guilt, despite a 19-day delay in reporting the crime and discrepancies over the date of the incident. The absence of injuries did not discredit her account, the court said, noting that she had waited to consult her children before approaching the police.

The court also cancelled his bail and directed him to surrender before the trial court to serve the sentence.

World.title: Telangana to host three-day Raksha Expo from December 7
World.content:
Telangana government will host Raksha Expo 2026, the inaugural edition of the State-level expo for the aerospace, space, defence and internal security sectors, from December 7 to 9 at the Bharat Future City, near Hyderabad, as part of the Invest Telangana Global Summit 2026.

It is the first such expo being organised by any State and the first in the country to bring space and internal security together with aerospace and defence on one platform. Raksha Expo will serve as a forum to showcase Telangana’s vision for defence sector and support India’s mission to become aatmanirbhar in defence research design and manufacturing capabilities and emerge as a global exporter.

Seeking to highlight how the State must be part of the revolutionary change underway in the defence industry, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said “the nature of conflict is changing. Conventional methods of warfare and statecraft now operate alongside drones and new-age missiles. Telangana must be the centre of this revolution.”

Integral to Telangana Rising vision: CM

He said the State must be the largest contributors to India’s national and internal security. It possessed the advantage and resource to turn this into a reality. The defence, space, aerospace and internal security sectors would be integral to the vision of Telangana Rising 2047 and the goal of building a $1 trillion economy by 2034.

Mr. Revanth Reddy had recently met Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and invited him to inaugurate the expo.

From missiles and fighter aircraft to satellites and secure communications, Hyderabad has powered India’s strategic programmes for decades, said Chief Secretary Sanjay Jaju. It is home to nearly 30% of the country’s defence and aerospace industry. Raksha Expo brings these strengths onto one platform for the first time, and adds space and internal security, because the security challenges of tomorrow cut across all four domains.

“Our experience with iDEX has shown how quickly startups and MSMEs deliver when they are connected directly with users, so this expo is designed for partnerships, not just displays,” he said, inviting manufacturers, innovators and investors from India and across the world to build with Telangana and make the State a trusted pillar of India’s self-reliance in defence.

Focus on domestic production

Recent conflicts around the world have exposed fragile supply chains and shown that national security now depends on dependable domestic production of ammunition, drones, counterdrone systems, secure networks and resilient infrastructure. India’s defence production reached a record ₹1.78 lakh crore in 2025–26, with defence exports touching an all-time high of ₹38,424 crore.

Telangana’s aerospace and defence exports doubled in 2025-26. Aerospace exports alone rose from ₹15,900 crore in 2023–24 to ₹30,742 crore in 2024–25, about 93% growth in one year. The sector is growing at more than 30% a year. The State inland location offers strategic depth for critical research institutions and manufacturing facilities, a natural advantage in an uncertain geopolitical environment, the State government said in a note.

Curtain raiser on Saturday

Raksha Expo 2026 will consist of exhibitions, live technology demonstrations, drone shows and December 9 an air show. A curtain raiser event is planned in the city on October 24 and in Delhi on October 29.

World.title: Death toll in accident involving TNSTC bus rises to three
World.content:
A 46-year-old man, who was hit by a TNSTC bus that went out of control after its driver suffered a cardiac arrest on Wednesday (October 21, 2026), succumbed to injuries on Thursday (October 22, 2026), taking the death toll to three.

The police said that Abbas, a resident of Tipu Sultan Colony near Kuniyamuthur, died without responding to treatment on Thursday.

According to the police, Abbas was hit by the bus when he was sitting on his two-wheeler on the side of the road and talking to a person over the phone. He suffered grievous injuries.

The two others who died in the accident are driver of the bus T. Martin (54) and Noor Muhammed (46), an autorickshaw driver from Kuniyamuthur.

World.title: Girls participation in NCC will motivate others, says Colonel Ravi Vyas
World.content:
The annual training camp of 600 National Cadet Corps (NCC) cadets commenced at Police Training College in Vizianagaram on Thursday. National Cadet Corps Commanding Officer 2 (A) of Girls Battalion Colonel Ravi Vyas said that the active participation of girls in the NCC would motivate and inspire more people to devote their time to serving the society.

Deputy Camp Commandant Major Satyaveni and others were present.

World.title: Is shoot-to-disable the new normal? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far:

The “leg-shot” doctrine appears to have become the new normal in Uttar Pradesh, emerging as a genuine crime-control model that Herbert Packer advocated in 1968, in his work — The Limits of the Criminal Sanction. Between 2017 and 2025, the State Police recorded over 16,000 encounter operations. In about 97% of cases, the accused survived with a bullet wound to the leg. At this scale, the question is no longer whether something unusual happened, but what it means when the unusual becomes routine.

What is Operation Langda?

A motorcycle is intercepted on a highway. The accused attempts to flee. Shots are fired. He is injured, typically in the leg, and taken into custody. This sequence, which now recurs across the State, is now known as “Operation Langda”, or “half-encounters”, from the Hindi word langda (lame), a policing methodology cultivated by the Uttar Pradesh Police since 2017 under its “zero-tolerance” framework. What may initially have appeared as a sporadic enforcement tactic has, over time, acquired the characteristics of a routine practice governed by a dual logic of incapacitation and punishment.

Refined through repetition, encounters have evolved into a recognisable policing pattern marked by targeted leg injury, standardised reporting, official endorsement and overt punitive logic.

How are half-encounters structured?

A study by the Centre for Criminology and Victimology at National Law University Delhi, based on official U.P. Police data and 100 verified encounter cases (January 2025–May 2026), found that these incidents follow a near-identical sequence: intelligence received, suspect intercepted, alleged attempt to flee or fire, police response in self-defence, gunshot to the leg, arrest, and recovery of a locally made pistol. This seven-step sequence is the standardised operational template of Operation Langda, repeated across more than 30 districts over nearly a decade.

What distinguishes the practice is its focus on incapacitation rather than lethality. By visibly disabling accused persons, it functions as both a disciplinary mechanism and an assertion of state authority. The standardised language of police reports further normalises this extra-procedural punishment by presenting it as routine law enforcement. Nearly 80% of 100 cases in the micro-level dataset used either “retaliation” or “self-defence” as the major justificatory framing, no matter what the alleged offence is.

The consistency of this framing across widely different offences suggests a standardised narrative template rather than case-specific accounts. This helps reproduce the practice across districts as a recognisable policing methodology.

In most of the 100 cases examined, media reports reproduced the police version without critical scrutiny. Critical coverage emerged only when direct counter-evidence challenged the official narrative. As a result, these incidents entered the news cycle largely as routine law-and-order events, that functioned as transmission rather than scrutiny.

The emergence of this methodology must be understood against the institutional constraints faced by the Uttar Pradesh Police. Prior to 2017, conviction rates in several categories of violent crimes were below 20%, while investigative capacity lagged far behind caseloads. In this environment, ‘half-encounters’ present a pragmatic alternative.

Crucially, shooting to disable rather than kill makes the practice more legally defensible. The accused survives to be produced in court, the officer can claim self-defence, and the state records an arrest rather than a death. This distinguishes the U.P. model from the typical “fake encounter” tradition of other States. It is also a reason why the practice continues to enjoy official support. State data show declines in crimes such as dacoity and robbery, but these gains do not address concerns over due process and the erosion of the rule of law.

Uttar Pradesh publicly treats encounter statistics as indicators of law-and-order achievements. Through official recognition and accelerated promotions, an exceptional tactic has become an accepted metric of policing performance. The incentive structure is reflected in the data: 2,739 encounter operations were recorded in 2025 alone — the highest annual figure in the dataset.

This official endorsement contrasts sharply with established judicial standards. In People’s Union for Civil Liberties v. State of Maharashtra (2014), the Supreme Court laid down sixteen principles and mandated an independent inquiry in every case. While these remain the legal benchmark, they have not been systematically applied in the State.

In January 2026, the Allahabad High Court observed that “half-encounter” practices had become routine and were often driven by official rewards and promotions. The court reiterated that the power to punish belongs exclusively to the judiciary.

What makes reform so difficult?

The central problem is that “Operation Langda” is ; that it operates as a self-sustaining system. Political endorsement, professional incentives, media transmission and the chronic weaknesses of the criminal justice process do not merely tolerate the practice, they reproduce it. Piecemeal reforms will not be enough. What is most striking is how a practice that sits outside legal norms has, through routine and reward, become part of how the state governs. Any durable reform must dismantle the interlocking incentives and channels that produce it.

G.S. Bajpai is the Vice Chancellor of the National Law University, Delhi. Vibhuti Sharma is an Academic Fellow, NLU Delhi. Views are personal.

World.title: PM vows to bring back progress to KP, assails PTI's 'callousness' during its tenures
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday vowed that the federal government, which now runs Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province.

He made the remarks while chairing a meeting of the apex committee in Peshawar, where he arrived earlier in the day on his first visit to the province since the imposition of governor’s rule and the declaration of emergency on Oct 11.

The meeting, attended by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, reviewed KP’s overall security situation. Federal ministers and newly appointed provincial advisers were also present.

Addressing the committee, PM Shehbaz reiterated that emergency and governor’s rule had to be imposed “under extreme compulsion”.

“I promise that we will leave no stone unturned in bringing back the happiness and era of progress to this province, and in the practical realisation of the wishes, aspirations, and dreams of this province’s people that have been shattered due to the worst actions of recent years,” he said.

The prime minister affirmed that the Centre “will place all possible resources at your feet”.

He added that himself, the Advisory Council led by the governor, the president and the CDF “will ensure that this province, once again, not only matches the other provinces in the race for development, but I would be extremely happy if it moves even further ahead”.

The prime minister regretted that “terrorists were summoned back here” after peace had been established, “washing down all sacrifices down the drain”.

“There can be no greater enmity with the country than not honouring and respecting such sacrifices, not holding them in esteem,” he remarked, highlighting that young soldiers left their homes and families to defend their country.

The premier called for an “all-encompassing analysis as to why this happened”, adding that there was “no worse callousness, criminal negligence, and hostility towards the national interest than this”.

He said: “All issues of the people were pushed aside — whether it is education, healthcare, or protecting the lives and property of the people — and [having] matters with terrorists instead. I believe that no other example can be found of such hostility against the country, in terms of their attitudes, detachment, and callousness.”

PM Shehbaz asserted that 5,000 police vacancies were not filled, Safe City projects were yet to be completed, the capacity of the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) had not been enhanced significantly, and neither were special measures taken regarding police training.

He recalled that all provinces had agreed at the time of the 2010 National Finance Commission Award that KP, being the front-line region in combatting terrorism, needed ample resources.

“From 2010 to today, more than Rs800 billion in funds have either already been provided or are being provided under this,” he stressed.

“However, not only did it resurface, but the weapons needed to counter terrorism, the required capacity, and the trained officers needed were nowhere to be found.”

While saying he would not go into the details, the prime minister emphasised that he had assured the provincial governments of ex-chief ministers Ali Amin Gandapur and Sohail Afridi of the Centre’s full support in the fight against terrorism.

“But nothing was done regarding this,” he regretted, adding that the government could not remain a “silent spectator” when a “party was stooping to such enmity against the country” and the economy and society were being destroyed.

“Therefore, on this occasion we made this one last effort,” the premier said, referring to the province’s interim handover to the federal government under governor’s rule.

Highlighting the Centre’s efforts to stabilise the economy over the past two and a half years, PM Shehbaz remarked, “It wouldn’t have been possible [without] unprecedented partnership between political and military hierarchy.”

He said the federal government could not remain a silent spectator when “terrorists were roaming around dancing in all areas of KP, and were ruling over some areas in the evening, and collecting extortion” at a time when the stabilisation of Pakistan’s economy was being acknowledged globally.

The prime minister recalled the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between the Centre and reiterated that his government was “compelled to make this decision” of imposing governor’s rule.

PM Shehbaz remarked that the province was “shattered with wounds due to the circumstances created in the past several years”.

He highlighted the poor law and order situation over the past six years, recalling that security forces and law enforcement agencies had made sacrifices to establish peace in KP.

The premier said there was corruption of Rs100bn in the clean drinking water of the Cities Improvement Project and Rs37bn in the “infamous looting” in the case of the Kohistan District Accounts Office.

He said that “80,000 people were martyred and the [economy] suffered a loss of several hundred billion dollars. Only then, in 2018, was peace completely restored in this country”.

Describing the province as “very beautiful”, the premier expressed his hope that the government “work hard day and night and speedily make it progress towards development and prosperity”.

“This is the province that is the first extremely strong wall of the homeland,” he noted.

Centre announces Rs160bn uplift funds, other measures

PM Shehbaz later also attended a meeting of the Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) constituted for 12 districts of KP, which face serious security challenges.

The council covers Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper and South Waziristan Lower. It includes 48 elders and prominent personalities from those districts to ensure local representation.

Addressing the ARDC, the prime minister announced that the federal government would provide KP with Rs160bn for development projects.

Furthermore, to address the wheat shortage in the province, he said the Centre would provide KP “as much wheat as is needed” from the storages of Pakistan Agricultural Storage and Services Corporation (Passco).

“However, there should be no hoarding. And whatever price the Centre provides wheat at, the common man should get wheat at that very price,” the premier emphasised.

He went on to assure the ARDC that the federal government will provide “whatever assistance” in operations and resources is needed to fight terrorism. He also said directives have been issued to bolster the CTD and complete Safe City projects.

PM Shehbaz also asserted that any difficulties in the completion of the federal government’s projects in KP will be resolved, adding that the governor-led administration will address problems in provincial projects.

The prime minister appreciated the tribal elders for always supporting Pakistan unequivocally and said the ARDC now had an “immense responsibility”.

Noting the remarks of ARDC Chairman Shaukatullah Khan, PM Shehbaz said: “He stated that development work is zero, corruption is 100 per cent, and terrorism is at its peak. I completely agree with him.”

The premier referred to weaknesses in the police’s performance, stating that arrests in cases of theft and robbery were not made.

Mentioning examples of corruption, such as the Kohistan scandal, he said: “You will feel great pain and sorrow over how the province’s resources were looted. God willing, this will be fully controlled, and every single penny of your development and prosperity will be delivered to your doorstep.”

Police’s vehicle procurement ban relaxed: Kundi

Separately, in a bid to improve the police’s capabilities amid the current law and order situation in the province, Kundi said he has approved the relaxation of the police’s vehicle procurement ban to ensure personnel have the necessary resources.

In a post on X, Kundi said that in line with the prevailing security landscape in the province, he approved the relaxation of the ban.

“Our [KP police] force stands on the front lines to protect the lives and security of our people,” he wrote.

“In the prevailing law and order situation, ensuring that our officers have the vehicles and resources they need is essential to an effective response to security challenges.”

Kundi added that the restrictions would be loosened “within the approved scope and against funds already allocated in the Police Procurement Plan”.

“This will strengthen operational capacity without placing any additional burden on the provincial exchequer,” he noted.

“Supporting our police is not just a responsibility; it is an investment in the safety of our people and the peace of KP.”

In July this year, the KP government had imposed a ban on the procurement of vehicles except for ambulances; earth-moving machinery; fire trucks; tractors; trucks; buses; passenger vans; prisoner vans; motorcycles; water tankers; rescue and recovery vehicles and boats; and mobile laboratory vehicles, according to an order issued by the KP finance department.

“In case of [an] essential requirement, the chief minister, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, may relax the ban on [a] case-to-case basis,” the order, seen by Dawn, read.

Development of merged districts a ‘special priority’

In his address to the apex committee, the KP governor termed establishing peace and stability in KP a “collective priority”, and stressed that it was in the interests of the entire country.

Referring to the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, Kundi said that the peaceful transition showed that the people of the province wanted peace and stability.

“I want to pay tribute to my people who showed restraint despite the turmoil,” he said, asserting there had been no untoward incident in the region following the measures.

On Oct 14, three days after emergency was imposed, a protest demonstration by PTI workers in Khyber’s Bara tehsil turned violent as protesters clashed with police. Injuries to party workers and cops were reported in the incident.

Speaking at the meeting, Kundi also paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives in the war against terrorism, including personnel of the police, army, Frontier Corps, and Federal Constabulary.

“These sacrifices demand a more effective strategy to combat terrorism,” he underscored.

The governor reiterated that the foremost priority of his KP Advisory Council was to restore peace and eliminate terrorism.

Kundi termed the development of the merged districts a “special priority”.

“The people of these regions have paid a heavy price during this fight against terrorism. Now, they deserve better education, health, and economic opportunities,” he declared.

“The federal government’s cooperation in establishing peace and stability in the province is very significant,” the PPP leader highlighted, saying he was keen to play his role in this collective endeavour.

The governor maintained that the people of KP would not have to choose between peace and development. “This is our collective responsibility to provide people with both.”

Kundi declared that the KP Advisory Council would keep playing its role in integrating these merged areas in the circle of national development.

“The public’s trust is the only metric of measuring our success in the war on terror,” he asserted, while reaffirming that the whole network of terrorism would be annihilated, and the facilitators and financiers of terrorists would also be targeted.

“I seek constant support and supervision by the federal government,” he asked, expressing the hope that the Centre would continue its cooperation.

Emergency amid security challenges

The Centre had imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament last week amid protests by the opposition.

Governor Kundi, along with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, had chaired a meeting of the provincial apex committee a day after governor’s rule was imposed.

In the meeting, the governor — who is now in charge of running the province — assured Naqvi he would enforce all policies of the federal government and work together with the security forces for peace and prosperity of the province.

Kundi asserted that under the new set-up, tackling terrorism would be the priority.

Later that day, Kundi, addressing a press conference, called for greater coordination between the Centre and the province, stressing that policies on counterterrorism will “come from Islamabad [..] not Kabul,” in an apparent jibe at the PTI-led KP government, which has been accused of maintaining a “nexus” with terrorist groups by federal ministers.

The Centre’s move to impose governor’s rule and emergency in KP also followed a mobilisation drive and protest march by the PTI and in opposition at the Centre, to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results, with counterterrorism policy being one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their talks.

The PTI said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre denied . It also called for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticised the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objected to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Soon after, the Centre also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP.

Federal ministers have also alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, stating that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

Additional input by Irfan Raza

World.title: Punjab MPA Hina Parvez Butt defends deleted X post on alleged CCD encounter amid criticism
World.content:
Punjab lawmaker Hina Parvez Butt on Thursday defended herself after a social media post by her regarding an alleged encounter by Punjab’s Crime Control Department prompted outrage and criticism.

On Wednesday, a suspect accused of running over a teenage boy who worked for him with his car in a private housing society in Multan, was killed in an alleged encounter in Bahawalpur. The killing of the teenager, Waseem, had sparked anger among the public, with a police officer saying the he had been “subjected to barbarity”.

“This is [Punjab Chief Minister] Maryam Nawaz sahiba’s government; justice is served immediately,” Butt subsequently wrote on X, sharing screengrabs of a TV report regarding the alleged encounter. She later deleted the post after it was widely panned for “celebrating extrajudicial killings”.

In a video statement posted on X on Thursday, Butt said: “I posted a tweet in which I said, ‘This is Maryam Nawaz Sharif sahiba’s government; justice is served immediately’. This was my personal opinion and creating propaganda on this was uncalled for.”

She said that the post was meant to express the “feelings of an ordinary citizen”. She asserted that she did not “blame” the chief minister, the Punjab government or talk about any institution. She said that criticising her for this was “uncalled for”.

She also took exception to remarks by Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, saying that she “respectfully disagreed”.

On Wednesday night, Bokhari had appeared on Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Ke Saath’, where she was asked about Butt’s post.

The Punjab minister said that Butt had a habit of saying things without thinking them through, which caused problems for her and become a “source of embarrassment for the government”.

Referring to the remarks, Butt said: “None of my actions or words have ever harmed or embarrassed the Punjab chief minister or the government. If Azma Bokhari sahiba is feeling embarrassed, that is her personal choice.

“I don’t feel that anyone should be embarrassed [at] anything I tweeted on my social media account. Azma Bokhari is the [Punjab] government’s official spokesperson, so obviously she clarified the government’s policy, which is good. But, I think her remarks on me were unnecessary and uncalled for,” she said.

“So I would again, respectfully, disagree with her,” she said.

Referring to recent incidents involving minors and the youth in the country, she said that their parents should be called on shows and asked how those who subjected their offspring to “savagery” should be treated.

“I believe I have stated public sentiment and what is the people’s voice. Those coming forward to defend the culprits do not meet the families whose children’s bodies are recovered in a bad state. I meet such parents,” he said.

“So any person who has even a bit of humanity in their heart, what will they have felt when they heard about Waseem from Multan?” she asked.

The CCD, established last year, has been criticised by human rights advocates and civil society members for a high number of casualties.

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) alleged earlier this year that the CCD has adopted a “deliberate policy of staged police encounters leading to extrajudicial killings”.

World.title: Direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives on the horizon as PM stresses connectivity
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday announced that he had issued instructions for direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives.

Addressing the Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum, attended by visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, the premier said that once the dignitary returned, a delegation of Pakistani government officials and businessmen would be sent to Malé. He said that the delegation would arrive within the next week or so.

“I want to say that connectivity is very important. We don’t have direct flights from Malé to Islamabad or Karachi, so this air link is very important,” PM Shehbaz said, addressing Muizzu.

“I have already given instructions to our ministry of civil aviation to prepare a quick feasibility [study], be it Pakistan International Airlines, or any other airline in Pakistan, to find the ways and means to take the first flight comprising tourists [and the] business community to Malé,” he announced.

The premier said he had been informed by President Muizzu that he gave instructions “to his airline to work out a quick plan to start flights from [the] Maldives to Pakistan”.

“I have given instructions to our civil aviation department to immediately invite a delegation from [the] Maldives and work out a plan whereby we can start these air flights between the two countries as early as possible,” PM Shehbaz added.

Moreover, the premier highlighted the importance of maritime connectivity, noting that unless there is a reliable direct shipping schedule from Karachi or Gwadar to Male, “we will not be able to meet our targets efficiently and effectively.”

Calling Muizzu a “very sincere friend of Pakistan”, the premier hailed his visit as a “turning point in further strengthening our bilateral, brotherly relations” and a “game-changer in terms of promoting our bilateral trade and investment portfolios”.

“I would like to convey this message to our great entrepreneurs, traders, investors and businessmen from both [the] Maldives and Pakistan,” he added. “Here is an opportunity we can really convert into … a concrete action plan.”

Citing figures provided by Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan, PM Shehbaz said that the trade volume between Islamabad and Malé is approximately $13 million.

“My brother, President Dr Muizzu, on my request, readily agreed to make a firm understanding to increase our bilateral trade from $13m to $200m in the next two years, and now it’s all up to us to make use of this opportunity, do our homework and make full preparation to achieve these targets through joint efforts and very close coordination,” the prime minister stated.

Taking the podium, President Muizzu thanked PM Shehbaz for taking the time to attend the forum and said that his presence was “a testament to the close friendship and our shared commitment to strengthening economic cooperation”.

“It is such a great pleasure for me to be with you today in Islamabad. And particularly to address a gathering of those who drive enterprise, investment, and economic opportunity in our two countries,” he added.

“As we mark 60 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the relationship between the Maldives and Pakistan is rooted in deep fraternal affection, and above all, in the enduring bond of our Islamic faith.”

Muizzu noted that while Islamabad and Male had strong political solidarity and diplomatic trust, their economic relationship had yet to reach its full potential.

“We must now define the ambition of our future,” the Maldivian president said. “The time has come to transform the strength of our friendship into a new era of trade, investment, and shared prosperity, which is why yesterday Prime Minister Sharif and I agreed to enhance our bilateral trade to $200m over the next two years.”

He added, “Beyond the numbers, this ambitious target is investing in our people. We are not only creating new opportunities for businesses on both sides, but also fostering greater regional prosperity and long-term stability.”

Muizzu said Pakistan possessed tremendous potential and that the economies of both nations had “important complementarities”.

“For the Maldives, food security is not merely a commercial consideration. As an island nation, resilient supply chains are a matter of national security, and the scale of our market should not be underestimated,” he explained.

Noting that Pakistan’s agricultural sector already serves the island nation, Muizzu emphasised the need to move beyond a typical buyer and seller relationship into partnerships in cold chain logistics, temperature-controlled storage, modern food processing and climate-adaptive agricultural technology

“But trade requires connectivity. For an island nation, maritime connectivity is an economic lifeline. We must create more efficient corridors through which that trade can move,” he highlighted. “Therefore, I encourage shipping, port and logistics companies from both countries to explore direct and commercially viable connections between Pakistan and the Maldives.”

Muizzu echoed PM Shehbaz and urged the establishment of an air corridor between Pakistan and the Maldives.

“In this regard, I am pleased to announce that Maldivian, our national airline, aims to establish [a] direct air link between Male and Karachi soon,” he announced. “This service will make travel easier for the people of our two countries, creating new opportunities for trade and tourism.”

Stressing the importance of healthcare infrastructure, the Maldivian president highlighted that the country is making significant investments to move from regional tertiary hospitals to modern island-level facilities.

“Our demand for reliable, high-quality and certified medical supplies will therefore continue to grow. We welcome Pakistani pharmaceutical manufacturers and healthcare providers,” Muizzu said.

Furthermore, he invited Pakistan’s construction companies, developers, manufacturers and engineering firms to partner with the Maldives in housing, land reclamation and connectivity projects, as part of Male’s endeavours in infrastructure and urban development.

“Renewable energy is another area of enormous potential. The Maldives spends hundreds of millions of dollars each year importing diesel. For us, therefore, the transition to clean energy is not only a climate imperative, it is an economic and fiscal necessity,” he added.

“My administration has set a target of producing 33 per cent of our national electricity requirement from renewable sources by 2028. That means more than quadrupling more than the amount generated in a five-year period.”

Additionally, the Maldivian president highlighted opportunities in both nations, unlocking the power of the global Islamic economy through Sharia-compliant finance, and halal tourism and products.

“The Maldives is strengthening its financial landscape and institutional frameworks for Islamic finance,” he said. “Together, our financial institutions, regulators, and businesses can explore Sharia-compliant investment instruments, sukuk, Islamic financial services and halal value chains. And these areas are by no means exhaustive.”

More to follow

World.title: ATC replaces state counsel in security breach case after Imaan, Hadi object to appointment
World.content:
RAWALPINDI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Thursday cancelled the appointment of state counsel Taimoor Janjua in a security breach case against lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha, after the accused objected to his past conduct in another case.

Imaan and her husband, Hadi, are facing a jail trial in a 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest.

The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on Oct 7. ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra presides over the proceedings at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail.

Hearing the case on Thursday, Judge Sipra named Atif Mehmood as the replacement for Janjua, who was appointed as the state counsel just a day ago to conduct cross-examination of prosecution witnesses after the lawyer couple’s counsel failed to do so during proceedings.

During the proceedings, Imaan told the court that Janjua had previously been appointed as state counsel in another case involving her, referring to the controversial social media posts case in which they were sentenced in January.

Hadi also raised objections to his conduct, alleging that the lawyer had told people that he had received Rs500,000 and completed cross-examination in a single day.

In response, Janjua challenged the allegation and retorted that the accused should accompany him to a private case outside the court to see whether he performed his professional duties properly.

The exchange prompted defence counsel Advocate Aimal Khan Mandokhail to question the state counsel’s role, asking him whether he was representing the accused or working against them.

The judge also expressed displeasure over Janjua’s conduct and questioned his manner of appearing before the court.

“Has no one ever taught you how to appear in court?” the judge asked the state counsel.

Then, Imaan informed the court that she and Hadi did not need a state counsel as they already had their own lawyers.

Hadi explained that their lawyers were frequently occupied with other cases at the Islamabad High Court (IHC), while the trial court had scheduled daily hearings at Adiala, making it difficult for them to attend every proceeding.

Meanwhile, no prosecution witness could be cross-examined during Thursday’s hearing amid the dispute over the state counsel’s appointment.

The court directed the prosecution witnesses to appear again on Friday and warned the accused that the cross-examination would proceed without further delay.

Addressing Imaan and Hadi, the judge directed them to ensure that their respective lawyers conducted the cross-examination at the next hearing. He added that if their lawyers failed to do so, newly appointed state counsel Mehmood would undertake the exercise.

The court adjourned further proceedings until 9am tomorrow (Friday).

Advocate Janjua had previously been appointed to represent Imaan and Hadi in a controversial social media posts case — a development to which the couple had objected .

He had shown up in an Islamabad district and sessions court during a November hearing after state-appointed Advocate Shakeel Jatt refused to cross-examine the prosecution’s witnesses in the case, saying that he could not “ask questions dictated” to him.

At a December hearing, Hadi had informed the court that a no-confidence application had been filed against Advocate Janjua.

Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest

The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in the controversial social media posts case.

The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

On Sept 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the Supreme Court suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the Islamabad High Court’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision.

However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Imaan and Hadi were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added.

The FIR included sections 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), 341 (wrongful restraint), 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

World.title: Mir Raza murder case: Sindh minister says JIT to be formed as per judicial panel's suggestions
World.content:
Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said on Thursday that a joint investigation team (JIT) would be formed as per the recommendations of the judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances surrounding the murder of Mir Raza Ali.

The 25-year-old businessman and Institute of Business Administration graduate had gone missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS, and his body with gunshot wounds was found a day later in bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar’s locality.

A judicial commission, formed on the Sindh government’s directives after the family accused police of burying the facts, has declared that Ali’s death was a murder and pointed out lapses by the police during the probe.

Speaking to the media in Karachi on Thursday, Lanjar said: “The JIT will be formed under the West Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Irfan Baloch, and the summary has been sent to the chief minister.”

The decision to form a JIT under DIG Baloch was in accordance with the judicial commission’s report, which suggested his appointment.

Submitted to the government on Oct 15, the report by Sindh High Court judge Justice Omar Sial had recommended forming a JIT under the leadership of DIG Baloch to “balance the need for public accountability with preserving Sindh Police morale and reputation”.

The commission had termed the formation of a JIT the “most viable path” to mitigate ongoing reputational damage to the Sindh government.

Lanjar further said that in his recommendations to CM Murad Ali Shah, he has suggested the JIT’s terms of reference (TORs) include presenting a charge sheet after completing the investigation.

However, he added. “It is the prerogative of the court to accept it or not under the circumstances; either it is a murder or suicide.”

In its report, the judicial commission had also recommended integrating senior representatives from the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Pakistan Rangers (Sindh), and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in the JIT to “ensure an impartial, comprehensive, and credible resolution”.

The notification of the JIT’s formation and composition is yet to be issued.

Furthermore, in line with another recommendation of the judicial commission, the home minister said a committee has been formed under the chairmanship of DIG Zulfiqar Ali Larik to take action against any police officers involved in negligence.

The 62-page judicial commission report, authored by Justice Sial, had declared: “This case demonstrates an epic failure by the police in their investigation.”

The commission, which examined 49 witnesses and the available record, determined that police investigation “failed in its most basic duty: to establish the truth”.

Besides making several recommendations regarding the case and police training, it had also listed its observations for certain police officials involved in the investigation, finding “criminal negligence” by three.

Initially, the police built the case around suicide on the basis of the first autopsy , which indicated a bullet entry wound on the chest, and by pointing out business losses and money borrowed by the victim.

Police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed had disputed the findings of the first post-mortem conducted by medico-legal officer Dr Osama Sheikh.

The second post-mortem report termed the findings of the first report “inconsistent” with suicide as the manner of Mir Raza’s death. It said the Exhumation Board was of the unanimous opinion that the death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back.

In August, the provincial government formed the commission, which was tasked with making recommendations for further investigation and forensic analysis or legal/departmental action, and it was required to submit its findings and recommendations to the Sindh government within 30 days.

World.title: President Zardari departs for Germany on 3-day visit to discuss bilateral ties
World.content:
President Asif Ali Zardari departed for Germany on Thursday on a three-day visit to discuss bilateral ties as the two countries are set to mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.

In a statement issued earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) said the president’s visit, scheduled for Oct 22-24, is “part of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and Germany”.

President Zardari “has departed from Lahore for Germany”, the President’s office said on social media on Thursday.

The FO statement highlighted that the visit “holds special significance in the context of the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries being commemorated this year”.

It said the visit reflects the “deep commitment of both countries to further strengthening the partnership”.

During his visit, President Zardari will hold meetings with his German counterpart Frank-Walter Steinmeier, as well as senior leadership and business leaders, with a “particular focus оп economic and trade cooperation”, FO said.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah is also expected to accompany the president on his trip, with the matter being discussed in Murad’s meeting with German Consul General Thomas E. Schultze.

In September, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

During the meeting, Germany appreciated Pakistan’s mediation efforts in regional conflicts, especially in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab while the two sides also agreed to “get negotiations on peace for Ukraine going”, according to the German foreign office.

Meanwhile, in June, a German delegation announced plans to bring about 30 German companies to Pakistan and link local businesses to European markets.

World.title: JI, govt to hold talks on Friday to work out plan for meeting between PM Shehbaz, Naeem
World.content:
Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) has said it will hold talks with the government on Friday regarding its demand to abolish the petroleum levy and on further high-level contacts between them.

The committee-level talks were fixed following a telephonic conversation between JI Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch and Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, according to a press release issued by JI on Thursday.

The JI has been demanding for over two months that the Centre abolish the levies — Rs114 per litre on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel — as the total prices have skyrocketed due to conflicts in the Middle East since March.

Friday’s talks between the two sides’ negotiating committees will take place at Punjab House in Islamabad, where they will also work out a schedule for a proposed meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, the party said.

According to the statement, despite the planned talks, Baloch reiterated his party’s call for countrywide protests tomorrow (Friday).

“JI will hold peaceful protests at district headquarters across the country on Friday to demand the abolition of unjust petroleum levy,” Baloch was quoted as saying.

The party would continue its protests alongside negotiations with the government, he declared.

“The campaign is not about the party’s interests but aimed to secure public relief, reduce unbearable production costs and revive economic activity.”

The party vice chair also called a meeting of the JI negotiating committee in Islamabad ahead of the talks.

According to the JI statement, Iqbal, who heads the government’s negotiating committee, informed Baloch that the meeting had initially been planned for Tuesday or Wednesday but was postponed because of the government’s “urgent engagements”.

Baloch, in the press release, argued that reducing the burden of petroleum levies and payments to independent power producers (IPPs) was essential to easing pressure on households, agriculture, industry, trade and small businesses.

“Such measures could help revive economic activity and create employment opportunities,” he emphasised.

The JI leader claimed governments were often reluctant to give up unjust taxes and rarely acknowledged the role of protest movements in securing public relief.

“Previous relief measures were announced under pressure from public sit-ins and had been implemented through flawed methods that failed to produce a positive impact on the national economy,” Baloch said as per the press release.

He also called on the government and other institutions to acknowledge their mistakes and avoid constitutional measures that could deepen the political crisis.

The JI leader urged all stakeholders to engage in a national dialogue and agree on priorities to steer the country out of its political and economic difficulties.

“JI’s negotiating committee has already identified possible options and available fiscal space within the constraints imposed by the IMF programme and the national budget,” Baloch was quoted as saying.

“The government and the prime minister’s team must now demonstrate the political will to provide relief to the public.”

“If the government failed to meet the party’s demand, JI will proceed with its planned long march from Multan,” he warned, referring to the protest that it had launched towards Islamabad but postponed at PM Shehbaz’s request.

On Aug 16, the JI announced sit-ins in all the provincial capitals of Pakistan against the petroleum levy and had called for a nationwide strike on Sept 3. However, when the day arrived, the two sides agreed to form committees to recommend measures to reduce the levies.

On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

On Sept 22, the JI emir said his party, whose convoy had reached Multan, was postponing its long march at the request of PM Shehbaz, who had assured the other side of a meeting to discuss the matters.

In a press release issued on Wednesday, the JI alleged that the government had made no further contact regarding the planned meeting between Rehman and PM Shehbaz.

World.title: Targeted by Trump, International Criminal Court wins top EU rights prize
World.content:
Facing US sanctions, the International Criminal Court was awarded the European Union’s top rights prize on Thursday, in a show of support that risks upsetting President Donald Trump.

“The European Union is built on respect for multilateralism and international institutions, and this prize recognises the important work of the court in upholding international law and justice,” said European Parliament chief Roberta Metsola, announcing the award.

The ICC thanked the European Parliament for giving it the Sakharov Prize “at a time when the Court and its officials face unprecedented challenges”.

“Against this backdrop, the Sakharov Prize carries particular significance, reaffirming the importance of independent judicial institutions and of those who work to uphold international law,” ICC President Tomoko Akane said.

This month, the United States announced sanctions against the ICC aimed at crippling the day-to-day operations of the court, which tries individuals for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.

Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”, furious that judges have issued an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleged crimes in Gaza.

The win comes after ex-ICC judge Navi Pillay, who also served as UN rights chief, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize this month — a choice Trump slammed as “disgraceful”, arguing the award should have gone to him.

The EU has already thrown its support behind the ICC in the face of the US sanctions — which will come into force in six months — and has said it is “ready to take any necessary measures” to make sure the court can keep working.

“The International Criminal Court must be free to pursue its mission, independently, and without pressure or intimidation,” EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said on social media after the prize was announced.

Brussels is hoping to use the delay before the sanctions are applied to try to talk the US down, but is also eyeing implementing a “blocking statute” to shield the ICC from Washington.

Three finalists

Set up in 1988 and named after Soviet dissident Andrei Sakharov, the EU prize is bestowed annually on individuals or organisations to recognise their fight for human rights or democracy.

The ICC was among three finalists this year, alongside Tanzania opposition leader Tundu Lissu and twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, representing those prosecuted by the Iranian government.

The nominees are put forward by the political groupings in the EU, and the winner is chosen by senior lawmakers. An award ceremony will be held in December.

Lissu, head of Tanzania’s opposition Chadema party, was detained in April 2025. He faces a possible death penalty if convicted of treason for allegedly inciting the public to boycott elections last year.

Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, 21, have respectively been sentenced to death and 36 years in prison for having taken part in anti-government protests in Iran.

Other recent high-profile winners of the Sakharov Prize have been Venezuelan opposition chief Maria Corina Machado, deceased Russian Kremlin critic Alexei Navalny and the people of Ukraine.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility.
